title: BIM Specialist (Electrical Systems Modeling)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>BIM SPECIALIST (ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS MODELING) </strong></p> <p>Building on the rapid advancement of the Starship program, SpaceX is seeking to rapidly develop and retrofit launch infrastructure facilities to support vehicle builds and re-flight refurbishments. We are seeking a Building Information Modeling (BIM) Specialist to lead the modeling, integration and coordination of electrical systems for multi-disciplinary Starship and Super Heavy Booster tooling systems, and facilities infrastructure. This position will serve as a key technical resource, supporting project teams and fostering strong BIM practices throughout the project lifecycle.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Develop, maintain, and upgrade detailed 3D BIM models of electrical systems (power distribution, control systems, data acquisition, wire harnesses, routing, cable management, hardware mounting, and equipment placement) using industry-standard software such as Revit, Navisworks, AutoCAD,or NX</li> <li>Own, draft, redline, and maintain electrical schematics, single-line diagrams, panel layouts and prepare related documentation while coordinating 3D model placement of electrical systems with the system Responsible Engineers</li> <li>Integrate electrical systems with architectural, structural, mechanical, plumbing (MEP), and other disciplines for Starship facilities and production tooling, in a safe, economical, and reliable way. Lead coordination of electrical systems into living facility models, owning end-to-end integration and electrical documentation ownership</li> <li>Generate construction documents, quantity takeoffs, visualizations, and as-built drawings from BIM models to support bidding, procurement, on-site execution, and long-term reliability improvements for electrical infrastructure and production systems</li> <li>Act as a liaison between project stakeholders, internal tooling teams, production leadership, responsible engineers, internal design and construction teams, and third-party consultants throughout the project life cycle</li> <li>Perform clash detection, model coordination, and constructability reviews focused on electrical systems to identify and resolve conflicts early in design and construction phases</li> <li>Support the development and maintenance of SpaceX BIM standards, protocols, and workflows for electrical infrastructure; act as the primary technical resource for electrical BIM issues</li> <li>Lead transition of electrical BIM workflows (including data migration, process documentation, and training); actively drive continuous improvements and optimizations for team processes, quality improvements, faster build times, lower maintenance, project kitting, communication, and feedback loops</li> <li>Support review and interpretation of power system studies, field data, and electromechanical integration; perform daily task prioritization and risk mitigation; participate in cross-functional meetings providing electrical BIM expertise to inform design decisions</li> <li>Perform other related duties as assigned to ensure an efficient and effective work environment</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in architecture, engineering, or construction management; or associates or vocational certification in electrical design, construction drafting, or design technologies</li> <li>1+ years of experience in a 3D drafting or BIM specialist/modeling role</li> <li>1+ years of experience working with electrical systems</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Occupational trade school qualification or experience working in an electrical technical role or in the electrical field</li> <li>Working knowledge of NFPA 70 (National Electrical Code), NFPA 70E, NFPA 79 &amp; UL508A codes</li> <li>Proficiency with BIM tools such as Revit, Navisworks, AutoCAD Electrical, NX, and/or SolidWorks</li> <li>Proficiency in clash detection, federated modeling, interdisciplinary coordination workflows, and constructability reviews for large-scale or high-rise projects</li> <li>Experience drafting and maintaining electrical schematics, single-line diagrams, and as-built drawings with strong ownership of documentation practices and revision control</li> <li>Experience modeling electrical systems in industrial environments</li> <li>Strong written and verbal communication skills</li> <li>Ability to independently drive projects, manage multiple priorities, and succeed in a high-paced team environment with evolving needs</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>This position is based in Starbase, TX and requires being onsite - remote work not considered</li> <li>Must be willing to travel to various SpaceX locations for mission critical projects</li> <li>Flexible to work extended hours and/or weekends to align with residential project deadlines and site operations</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. title: Chemical Process Engineer (Starship Launch Systems)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p></p> <p><strong>CHEMICAL PROCESS ENGINEER (STARSHIP LAUNCH SYSTEMS)</strong></p> <p>The Starship launch team is looking for a highly motivated individual to support launch pad fluid systems design and build with a focus on the implementation of cryogenic propellant processing and generation systems for all Starship launch sites, landing sites, test sites, production facilities, etc. Join the team responsible for launching the largest and most powerful rocket known to man!</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:&nbsp;</strong></p> <ul> <li>Design, build, and operate systems that support critical rocket launches and testing</li> <li>Perform thermofluid analysis and other design tasks associated with gaseous and liquid (including cryogenic liquid) fluid systems</li> <li>Manage the fabrication and installation of fluid systems and other construction projects occurring at the launch and test sites</li> <li>Help SpaceX develop state-of-the-art technologies for all aspects of the production of cryogenic rocket propellants (oxygen and methane)</li> <li>Design, build, and commission air separation, liquefaction, liquified natural gas production, and other cryogenic process equipment</li> <li>Perform balance of plant calculations for cryogenic systems</li> <li>Manage interdisciplinary engineering projects from concept through design, build, and activation</li> <li>Work closely with operational teams, cooperating to ensure system design is well-understood and easy to operate long-term</li> </ul> <p><strong>&nbsp;BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in mechanical, chemical, or aerospace engineering</li> <li>1+ years of hands-on experience working with fluid systems in a professional setting (internships qualify)</li> </ul> <p><strong>&nbsp;PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Advanced degree in mechanical, aerospace, or chemical engineering</li> <li>Degree in chemical engineering</li> <li>Strong working knowledge of fluid dynamics, thermodynamics, and process engineering</li> <li>Demonstrated expertise in designing and operating cryogenic fluid systems</li> <li>Experience in the filtration and distillation of liquid gases, including liquid air and liquid natural gas</li> <li>Experience with cryogenic systems in maritime environments</li> <li>CAD capability for 3D Modeling (NX, SolidWorks, etc.)</li> <li>Knowledge of engineering standards and best practices</li> <li>Knowledge of safety protocols for handling, storage, and transportation of cryogenic propellants in accordance with industry standards</li> <li>Experience operating and troubleshooting control systems required for remote operations</li> <li>Experience commissioning and/or plant operation (liquefied natural gas, air separation unit)</li> <li>Able to work well in an integrated collaborative team environment, including daily interactions with technicians, engineers, and managers</li> <li>Able to prioritize and execute tasks in a high-pressure, fast-paced environment</li> <li>Self-motivated and directed with keen attention to detail</li> <li>Passion for advancing the commercial space industry and human spaceflight</li> <li>Demonstrated ability to lead a team of talented and driven engineers</li> </ul> <p><strong>&nbsp;ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Occasionally exposed to work in extreme outdoor environments - heat, cold, rain</li> <li>Work performed in an environment requiring exposure to fumes, odors, and noise</li> <li>Must be willing to travel to other launch sites in support of build and operational activities and launches; travel requirement is up to 15%</li> <li>Availability to work extended hours and weekends as needed; flexibility is required</li> <li>Stand: Up to 6 hours per day</li> <li>Sit: Up to 6 hours per day</li> <li>Push/Pull: Up to ≤ 50 lbs. (unassisted) 15 minutes or less per day</li> <li>Overhead reach: Up to 3 hours per day</li> <li>Walk: Up to 10 hours per day</li> <li>Lift/Carry: Up to ≤ 25 lbs. (unassisted) 15 minutes or less per day</li> <li>Climb (ladder/stairs): Up to 1 hour per day</li> <li>Kneel/Crouch: Up to 3 hours per day</li> <li>Upper body twist: Up to 3 hours per day</li> <li>Ability to work in temperatures over 80 degrees for 6 hours or greater per day</li> <li>Candidate must be capable of safely working at heights (up to 500ft), in confined spaces, operating heavy equipment and machinery, and performing the physical requirements of the job listed in the job description. Candidate may be required to complete a pre-employment questionnaire and/or physical to confirm these capabilities, which may include a medical history review.</li> </ul> <p></p><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR <a href="https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/?id=ddtc_kb_article_page&amp;sys_id=24d528fddbfc930044f9ff621f961987">here</a>. &nbsp;</li> </ul> <p>SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.</p> <p>Applicants wishing to view a copy of SpaceX’s Affirmative Action Plan for veterans and individuals with disabilities, or applicants requiring reasonable accommodation to the application/interview process should reach out to&nbsp;<a href="mailto:EEOCompliance@spacex.com">EEOCompliance@spacex.com</a><em>.&nbsp;</em></p></div>

title: Construction Supervisor, Fluid Systems
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>CONSTRUCTION SUPERVISOR, FLUID SYSTEMS</strong></p> <p>As a critical member of the Starbase Infrastructure team, you will supervise and lead a group of laborers and contractors to enable the build and activation of infrastructure for a variety of projects.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Oversee the day-to-day site supervision of a fast-paced, high impact construction project including the responsibilities below: <ul> <li>Supervise a team dedicated to construction site logistics/operations, including work schedules, project progress, and resource allocation</li> <li>Plan, implement, and enforce construction site logistics to enable broader project goals and schedule</li> <li>Manage SpaceX construction assets (trailers, portas, rental equipment, etc.)</li> <li>Implement and enforce SpaceX safety policies. Drive the safety culture on the jobsite through contractor and internal partners</li> <li>Daily field coordination and conflict resolution for contractors and internal partners</li> <li>Manage site logistics, including daily deliveries, offloading, inventory, storage, and staging of SpaceX purchased materials</li> <li>Responsible for jobsite cleanliness</li> <li>Create, enforce, and iterate on schedules for workers and subcontractors in conjunction with engineering and project management team</li> <li>Maintain a daily log for the job site’s operations, reporting to management as necessary</li> </ul> </li> <li>Oversee the procurement and execution of specific construction projects as delegated by the engineering &amp; project management team <ul> <li>Provide budgetary costs based upon the preliminary scope of the project</li> <li>Gather proposals from contractors; assign contracts upon receipt of all proposals</li> <li>Develop the final cost and schedule for the sub-project, and implement controls as needed to manage cost, schedule and scope</li> <li>Coordinate project implementation and track project status</li> <li>Coordinate with end user and facilities team for building operations and maintenance</li> <li>Supervise night shift contractors as project work requires</li> </ul> </li> <li>Make changes in the operation as necessary to best meet construction deadlines, triage issues to engineering &amp; project management team as necessary to ensure schedule and quality are adequate</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>High school diploma or equivalency certificate</li> <li>2+ years of professional experience in engineering, construction management, architecture or facilities management</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Field experience in a technical field or in supervising a multi-discipline team of contractors/laborers</li> <li>Previous experience with project management and scheduling software</li> <li>Understanding of multiple disciplines such as civil, structural, mechanical, electrical, piping, geotechnical, and surveying</li> <li>Experience with project management of construction projects including estimating, cost control, schedule, and contractor management</li> <li>Experience reading, reviewing, and approving shop and fabrication drawings</li> <li>Ability to rapidly change roles/responsibilities while maintaining a high sense of urgency in a high-paced, challenging work environment</li> <li>Ability to work independently and in a team, take initiative, and communicate effectively</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Ability to work at elevated heights (200+ feet)</li> <li>Physical effort with lifting and carrying materials or equipment (up to 25 lbs.)</li> <li>Typically exposed to work in extreme outdoor environments – heat, cold, rain</li> <li>Work performed in an environment requiring exposure to fumes, odors, and noise</li> <li>Must be available to work extended hours and weekends when needed based on site operational needs; flexibility required</li> <li>Valid driver’s license</li> <li>Travel may be required based on specific project tasks</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. title: Embedded Software Engineer, OS/Platform (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><div> <p><strong>EMBEDDED SOFTWARE ENGINEER, OS/PLATFORM (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>At SpaceX, we’re leveraging our experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation and is providing fast, reliable internet to 9M+ users worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system – thousands of satellites, consumer receivers that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing, and the software that brings it all together. We’ve only begun to scratch the surface of Starlink’s potential global impact and are looking for best-in-class engineers to help maximize Starlink’s utility for communities and businesses around the globe.</p> <p>As an Embedded Software Engineer on the Starlink program, you will be solving challenges underpinning every aspect of the program’s growth. The areas you could have an impact on could include, but are not limited to:</p> <ul> <li>Bringing up next generation space grade silicon, including in house designed system on chip and peripherals.</li> <li>Develop software from the early stage boot loaders to business logic with an emphasis on deterministic, secure, and performant platform for all of SpaceX Linux based spacecraft and grounds-based components.</li> <li>Infrastructure and tools to enable rapid development and testing of new features for all OS/platform features.</li> </ul> <p>Our software engineers are responsible for the complete lifecycle of the software they create, including development, testing, and support.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Maintain and update in house branches of OSS software such as Linux, Buildroot, and u-boot.</li> <li>Support secureboot and runtime security of all Linux based satellite components.</li> <li>Maintain the spacecraft Ethernet network and connectivity.&nbsp;</li> <li>Develop, deploy and test spacecraft software update process.&nbsp;</li> <li>Support in-house System on Chip and peripheral through the life-cycle of the part.&nbsp;</li> <li>Support OS/Platform specific test infrastructure.&nbsp;</li> <li>Development and support device drivers for third party and in-house components.&nbsp;</li> <li>Be the first software team to receive new satellite components.&nbsp;</li> <li>Interface with Silicon, Electrical, and Application Software Engineers to bring hardware from prototype stage to on on-orbit operations.</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in computer science, engineering, math, or science discipline; OR 2+ years of professional experience in software development in lieu of a degree (internship experience is applicable).</li> <li>Development experience in C, C++, python and/or rust.&nbsp;</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Linux Kernel Up streamed patches preferred.</li> <li>Knowledge of networking and Linux networking stack.&nbsp;</li> <li>Good knowledge of computer architecture and modern secure boot flows.&nbsp;</li> <li>Experience with ARM embedded systems.&nbsp;</li> <li>Deep understanding of testing, continuous integration, build, deployment &amp; continuous monitoring.&nbsp;</li> <li>Creative approach to problem solving, exceptional analytical skills and engineering fundamentals.&nbsp;</li> <li>Strong skills in debugging, performance optimization, and unit testing.&nbsp;</li> <li>Excellent communication skills both written and verbal.</li> <li>Ability to work effectively in a dynamic environment with changing needs and requirements.</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Must be willing to work extended hours and weekends as needed.</li> </ul> </div><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. title: Fluid Systems Engineer, Solar Cell Factory (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>FLUIDS SYSTEMS ENGINEER, SOLAR CELL FACTORY (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>The Solar Cell team is revolutionizing power generation for space applications through advanced solar cell manufacturing. We're scaling production of high-efficiency solar cells to support sustainable energy solutions for Starlink constellations, launch vehicles, and beyond. As a Solar Cell Factory Fluids Engineer, you will design, build, and optimize fluid systems for the delivery of critical gases and chemicals in solar cell fabrication. This role requires a detail-oriented engineer passionate about safe handling of hazardous materials in a high-volume manufacturing environment, ensuring reliable supply to processes like vacuum deposition and etching while minimizing risks and maximizing efficiency in our cutting-edge solar cell factory.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Design, build, and activate fluids systems for the distribution of key gases (e.g. specialty and bulk gases), chemicals (e.g., hydrofluoric acid, solvents) and exhaust systems used in solar cell processes, including tanks, pumps, heat exchangers, gas panels, valves, scrubbers, and abatement systems</li> <li>Cradle-to-grave project ownership including requirement definition, design, justification of key decisions, equipment procurement, build coordination, commissioning and project management throughout</li> <li>Design modular systems capable of being manufactured at scale for future solar production facilities</li> <li>Apply fluids/mechanical engineering skills such as P&amp;ID development, equipment sizing, detailed fluid and thermal analysis, system-level CONOP development, structural analysis, materials and component selection.</li> <li>Perform safety/hazard assessments (ex. FMEAs, HAZOPs) to ensure appropriate hazardous system design, including emergency shutdown CONOPs, redundancy, and general compliance with hazardous material safety standards</li> <li>Design, build, and deploy data acquisition and control systems for fluid facilities control and monitoring</li> <li>Collaborate with process engineers to integrate fluid systems with manufacturing equipment and optimize delivery rates, purity levels, and recovery/recycling of process fluids to support high-yield production</li> <li>Support installation, commissioning, and troubleshooting of fluid systems, working closely with facilities operations, EHS, automation, and procurement teams to resolve issues and implement improvements</li> <li>Ensure regulatory compliance with OSHA, EPA, ASME, NFPA, and SEMI standards for chemical and gas handling in semiconductor-like environments</li> <li>Track system performance metrics (e.g., flow rates, contamination levels, downtime) and contribute to continuous improvement initiatives, such as lean manufacturing and sustainability efforts for fluid reuse</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering, chemical engineering, aerospace engineering, or other engineering discipline</li> <li>1+ years of hands-on build or design experience (internship, club, and competition team experience qualifies)</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Advanced degree in engineering or related field</li> <li>2+ years of experience in fluid systems design, particularly with gases or hazardous chemicals in manufacturing or semiconductor industries</li> <li>2+ years of experience in photovoltaic, semiconductor, or thin-film deposition manufacturing</li> <li>Knowledge of safety protocols for handling pyrophoric materials (e.g., silane) and toxic gases/chemicals (e.g., phosphine, HF)</li> <li>Knowledge of ASME B31.3, SEMI S2/S8 standards and experience with cleanroom HVAC integration for fluid systems</li> <li>Familiarity with cleanroom fluid systems, gas cabinets, scrubbers, and wastewater neutralization for solar cell jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. We are looking for engineers who treat fellow teammates with fairness, respect, and support.</p> <p>Our team is currently creating and evolving systems to enable rapid build and reuse of Starship as well as designing the next generation manufacturing software that will be used in high throughput factories for Starlink. Other applications range from platforms that support concurrent streams of data from many always-on assets to manage the world’s largest satellite constellation to public facing systems where customers can join our Starlink network globally. We work closely with engineers throughout the company to create and update our systems with respect to crewed launches, Starship flights, changes to the Starlink network and much more.</p> <p>Aerospace experience is not required to be successful here - rather we look for smart, motivated, respectful, collaborative engineers who love solving problems and want to make an impact on a super inspiring mission. title: Integration Engineer (Starship)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>INTEGRATION ENGINEER (STARSHIP)</strong></p> <p>As an Integration Engineer you will be responsible for establishing requirements and developing tooling and processes to enable at-rate production of the most powerful rocket ever made. Your role will focus on integration of avionics, propulsion, and structural assemblies, and you will work with both design engineering and technician teams daily. You will be well-positioned to influence overall vehicle architecture, with a focus on design for reliability and manufacturability.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES</strong></p> <ul> <li>Operate as a systems level engineer to collect production requirements then plan and execute the build, integration, and validation of flight hardware to those requirements</li> <li>Design and implement tooling solutions to eliminate assembly error, improve quality, and accelerate build</li> <li>Automate novel processes to ensure repeatability on a large scale production line</li> <li>Prove that a subsystem work center meets cycle time requirements, or own the design change required to meet target cycle time</li> <li>Become a subject matter expert for the build of a vehicle level system like aero control surfaces, propellant feed systems, actuation systems, thermal protection systems, secondary structures, avionics, primary structure, etc.</li> <li>Generate and maintain design for manufacturing requirements for the processes used to build Starships and Super Heavy Boosters</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in an engineering discipline</li> <li>1+ years of hands-on engineering experience (design teams and previous internships qualify)</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS</strong></p> <ul> <li>Master's degree in an engineering discipline</li> <li>1+ year of system level acceptance test exposure</li> <li>2+ years of professional experience in the field of aerospace/mechanical engineering</li> <li>2+ years of experience with GD&amp;T concepts</li> <li>Experience with large steel structure construction (civil, naval, or mechanical)</li> <li>Experience in process development, facility and line layouts, error-proofing, factory optimization, and lean principles</li> <li>Experience with Siemens NX and Teamcenter CAD, PLM, Process Simulate, and other automation systems</li> <li>Prior experience with developing, maintaining and improving welding processes</li> <li>Strong interpersonal and organizational skills</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS</strong></p> <ul> <li>Flight hardware typically is built in tight quarters and physical dexterity is required</li> <li>Ability to perform job duties that require standing, kneeling, crouching, twisting upper body, working in cramped positions in small openings and climbing hand over hand</li> <li>Typically exposed to work in extreme outdoor environments – heat, cold, rain</li> <li>Work performed in an environment requiring exposure to fumes, odors, and noise</li> <li>Schedule varies depending on site operational needs; flexibility required</li> <li>Flexibility to travel to remote build sites, up to 10%</li> <li>Stand: Up to 6 hours per day</li> <li>Sit: Up to 6 hours per day</li> <li>Push/Pull: Up to 50lbs. (unassisted) 30 minutes to 1 hour per day</li> <li>Overhead reach: Up to 1 hour per day</li> <li>Walk: Up to 1 hour per day</li> <li>Lift/Carry: Up to 25lbs. (unassisted) 30 minutes to 1 hour per day</li> <li>Climb (ladder/stairs): Up to 6 hours per day</li> <li>Kneel/Crouch: Up to 6 hours per day</li> <li>Upper body twist: Up to 6 hours per day</li> <li>Ability to work in temperatures over 80 degrees 6 hours or greater per day</li> <li>Candidate must be capable of safely working at heights (up to 500ft), in confined spaces, using an air purifying respirator, operating heavy equipment and machinery, and performing the physical requirements of the job listed in the job description</li> <li>Candidate may be required to complete a pre-employment questionnaire and/or physical to confirm these capabilities, which may include a medical history review</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. title: Integration Engineer, Heatshield (Starship)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>INTEGRATION ENGINEER, HEATSHIELD (STARSHIP)</strong></p> <p>Starship requires a robust Thermal Protection System (TPS) to withstand the extreme heat generated during atmospheric reentry at hypersonic speeds. The thermal hardware team is responsible for the design, analysis, integration, and continuous improvement of Starship's reentry heatshield and structures. As a mechanical engineer, you will drive the development of the next-generation heat shield from concept and detailed mechanical design to thermal-structural modeling, qualification testing, production, integration, flight rationale, and post-flight data-driven optimizations. At Starbase, you will have the opportunity to work in an exciting and dynamic environment, dividing your time between the office and the production floor to ensure the delivery of the best-engineered product and ultimately mission success.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Develop, test, and qualify new or refined thermal protection system solutions for our Starship architecture</li> <li>Own the outcome and set up the end-to-end solutions to thermal challenges from idea to flying hardware</li> <li>Work with production on resolving issues on the floor and on the vehicle with our flight hardware</li> <li>Analyze and troubleshoot post-flight conditions on vehicle heatshields to drive vehicle changes and improvements</li> <li>Coordinate with analysis, avionics, structures, supply chain, and reliability engineers to drive multidisciplinary projects</li> <li>Work with outside vendors, suppliers, and testing resources to bring in new materials, capabilities, or processes</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in material science, mechanical engineering, materials engineering, or aerospace engineering</li> <li>1+ years of engineering experience designing, analyzing, or building mechanical or thermal systems (internship and school projects experience qualify)</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>3+ years of experience working on thermal protection systems</li> <li>Strong fundamentals in aerothermal heating on reentry vehicles</li> <li>Strong fundamentals in the materials and mechanisms by which thermal protection systems operate</li> <li>Hands-on experience with hardware that has had to perform in challenging thermal environments such as rockets, reentry vehicles or other extreme temperature applications</li> <li>Ability to drive open-ended design and development challenges</li> <li>Familiarity and experience with production, installation, qualification, and use of thermal protection system materials</li> <li>Experience using Siemens NX, or similar CAD software</li> <li>Ability to perform basic thermal or mechanical analysis</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Ability to work extended hours and weekends as necessary</li> <li>Ability to travel domestically</li> <li>Ability to pass Air Force background jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>IT SYSTEMS ADMINISTRATOR, LAUNCH</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is looking for a highly skilled and knowledgeable IT Systems Administrator to support the networking, compute administration, and application support needs of our launch environment. This role will be pivotal to the enablement of safe and sustained launch cadence, directly supporting our goals of making humanity a multiplanetary species. Candidate must be comfortable working on mission-critical systems with a sense of urgency appropriate to the responsibilities while maintaining attention to detail and operational excellence.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Augment and deploy new IT infrastructure, including networking, server, and desktop hardware directly supporting mission critical networks across the country.</li> <li>Perform periodic systems upgrades and patches in between critical operations, sometimes on weekends and evenings.</li> <li>Monitor IT services and respond aggressively to incidents to maintain systems performance.</li> <li>Collaborate with cross-functional teams to proactively identify and resolve potential technical issues with systems deployments.</li> <li>Author and maintain documentation for IT systems, from systems overview documents and design drawings to procedures.</li> <li>Leverage automation tools and contribute to IT systems engineering efforts.</li> <li>Ensure that systems are configured and maintained in compliance with industry and cybersecurity standards (e.g. ITAR, ISO, NIST).</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>High school diploma or equivalency certificate.</li> <li>3+ years of experience in IT systems administration.</li> <li>Hands-on experience with Linux or Windows server administration.</li> <li>Experience with enterprise network administration and deployment.</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Working knowledge of network protocols (TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, SNMP, NTP, PTP etc), firewalls administration and cybersecurity technologies.</li> <li>Proficiency in scripting (Bash/Powershell/Python) and automation frameworks (Terraform, Ansible, Puppet).</li> <li>Familiarity with Active Directory and multi-platform authentication/identification environments.</li> <li>Experience with virtualization platforms and tools.</li> <li>Understanding of Layer 1 configuration best practices and multiplexing technologies.</li> <li>Working knowledge, including the ability to setup, configure, upgrade, manage, and troubleshoot, Windows-based systems and services (i.e. SCCM, Active Directory).</li> <li>Exposure to real-time systems and industrial telemetry networks.</li> <li>Experience with configuration management, provisioning, infrastructure as code, and other DevOps concepts and tools.</li> <li>Excellent communications skills with the ability to communicate with internal/external customers, vendors, management etc. in both formal and informal situations.</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Ability to pass Air Force background checks for Cape Canaveral and Vandenberg.</li> <li>Must have valid driver's license.</li> <li>Willing to work extended hours or weekends as necessary.</li> <li>Willing to be on after-hours on-call rotation.</li> <li>Ability to lift up to 30lbs.</li> <li>Ability to work at heights.</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, title: Lead Automation and Controls Engineer, Silicon Technology (Starlink)

Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation, providing fast, reliable internet to millions of users worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system – thousands of satellites, consumer receivers that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing, and the software that brings it all together. We’ve only begun to scratch the surface of Starlink’s potential global impact. As we continue to upgrade and expand the constellation, we’re looking for best-in-class engineers and leaders to join the team.</p> <p>In true SpaceX fashion, Starlink is taking the next step in vertical integration by bringing advanced silicon packaging and assembly in-house for development and manufacturing. We are looking for a hands-on, creative, and driven Lead Automation and Controls Engineer to spearhead the automation for our internal advanced silicon packaging lines. The Lead Engineer will be responsible for architecting and scaling the automation systems that allow for meaningful reduction of both user terminal cost and risk of global supply chain calamities limiting production capability of Starlink. Engineers on this team are curious, love to learn new things, and work effectively in a dynamic environment with changing needs as we strive to deliver high-impact technology on a massive scale.</p> startup.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:&nbsp;</strong></p> <ul> <li>Design and specify mechanical cooling systems for data center facilities: chilled water plants, CRAH/CRAC units, air handling testing</li> <li>Troubleshoot operational issues in existing facilities — water treatment, pump cavitation, control valve failures, capacity shortfalls</li> <li>Support due diligence and technical evaluation for new site selection, including utility water availability and existing mechanical infrastructure condition</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:&nbsp;&nbsp;</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering or related discipline</li> <li>5+ years of experience in mechanical/plumbing design for mission-critical facilities, data centers, or comparable produce mechanical/plumbing construction documents, P&amp;IDs, and equipment schedules</li> <li>Direct data center design or operations experience, ideally at hyperscale or colocation facility scale</li> <li>Experience with liquid cooling technologies: direct-to-chip, rear-door heat exchangers, or immersion cooling systems</li> <li>Familiarity with Uptime Institute Tier standards and ASHRAE TC9.9 data center thermal guidelines</li> <li>Commissioning experience, including functional performance testing (FPT) and&nbsp;integrated systems testing (IST)</li> <li>Experience with water title: Mechanical Engineer, Fluid Systems (Design & Build)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p></p> <p><strong>MECHANICAL ENGINEER, FLUID SYSTEMS (DESIGN &amp; BUILD)</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is looking for engineers to support the development and production testing of Starship/Raptor, Falcon, and Dragon engine and vehicle hardware in McGregor, TX. This is a fast-paced, hands-on, constantly evolving, real-as-it-gets engineering position available for the ambitious. We design, build, activate, modify, and maintain the fluid and mechanical systems that power, restrain, and measure the most powerful high-volume rocket engines in the world. In this dynamic environment, you can expect your engineering skills to be put to the test and the hardware you designed to be built and installed the very same day. From thousands of gallons per minute of cryogens to tens of pounds per second of high-pressure gas, we develop clever solutions to meet the needs of a demanding test program both today and in the future. We have open positions ranging from entry-level to very experienced engineers to add value to the SpaceX mission.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES: </strong></p> <ul> <li>Analyze, design, and build systems that support testing of fully integrated flight vehicles, individual rocket engines, and various rocket components</li> <li>Drive cradle-to-grave ownership of engineering projects through design reviews, decision justifications, equipment procurement, and coordination/participation in the construction of your ideas</li> <li>Work directly with skilled technicians to build your designs and fix real-world problems on the fly</li> <li>Maintain a tight feedback loop with the test operations team to rapidly alter plans as necessary to meet tight testing deadlines critical to company success</li> <li>Operate and troubleshoot equipment to achieve testing objectives, and apply lessons learned to iterate system designs for improved performance and maintenance</li> <li>Evaluate complex engineering needs and arrive at solutions to seemingly impractical problems that support test programs and achieve company objectives</li> <li>Take a hands-on approach to tackling rapidly-emerging field projects that keep the company testing rocket engines and vehicles every single day</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering, aerospace engineering, chemical engineering, or other engineering discipline&nbsp;</li> <li>1+ years of hands-on design or build experience (professional work, internships, clubs, or other engineering activities qualify)</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Strong fundamental understanding and intuition for fluid, structural, or mechanical systems</li> <li>Critical thinking and problem solving in stressful, dynamic situations</li> <li>Positive responses and outcomes to challenges posed by short deadlines</li> <li>Hands-on build—machining, welding, and other fabrication techniques are a plus</li> <li>Creativity to imagine and design for reliability, efficiency, and maintainability from scratch</li> <li>Driven approach to addressing challenges and opportunities—an enthusiastic, self-motivated, positive, can-do attitude</li> <li>Determining the best solution among several options, often balancing cost/schedule/complexity</li> <li>Acute attention to detail, and ability to see interactions with related systems to avoid problems</li> <li>Instrumentation and testing, data review and analysis, verification of models against reality</li> <li>High-pressure or cryogenic fluid systems and components</li> <li>Complex structural or mechanical systems and components</li> <li>Design verification with simplified hand calculations and complex modeling—FEA or CFD is a plus</li> <li>Production of fabrication drawings for parts to be machined or welded</li> <li>Intermediate skill level using CAD—Siemens NX is a plus</li> <li>ASME piping and pressure vessel design</li> <li>Excellent written and verbal communication skills</li> <li>3+ years of engineering design experience in an industrial setting or equivalent</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Ability to work both independently and as part of a team, take individual initiative, and communicate effectively to peers, leadership, and customers</li> <li>Ability to rapidly change roles/responsibilities while maintaining a high sense of urgency in a fast-paced, challenging work environment</li> <li>Willingness to perform other related duties for the purpose of ensuring an efficient and effective work environment</li> <li>Availability to respond to emergencies to support priority projects, missions, and launches</li> <li>Availability to work extended hours and weekends as needed—flexibility is required</li> <li>Ability to perform job duties that require standing, kneeling, crouching, twisting upper body, working in cramped positions in small openings, and climbing hand over hand</li> <li>Ability to lift heavy objects unassisted—up to 25 lbs.</li> <li>Ability to work at elevated heights with proper PPE—up to 300 ft.</li> <li>Ability to work in extreme outdoor environments when needed—heat, cold, wind, rain, etc.</li> <li>Ability to work in environments with exposure to fumes, odors, and noise</li> <li>Working conditions may be in tight quarters—physical dexterity is required</li> </ul> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p></p><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR <a href="https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/?id=ddtc_kb_article_page&amp;sys_id=24d528fddbfc930044f9ff621f961987">here</a>. &nbsp;</li> </ul> <p>SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.</p> <p>Applicants wishing to view a copy of SpaceX’s Affirmative Action Plan for veterans and individuals with disabilities, or applicants requiring reasonable accommodation to the application/interview process should reach out to&nbsp;<a href="mailto:EEOCompliance@spacex.com">EEOCompliance@spacex.com</a><em>.&nbsp;</em></p></div>

title: Power Systems Engineer
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>POWER SYSTEMS ENGINEER</strong></p> <p>As a member of the Construction Projects Team, you will work with engineers across multiple disciplines to design, build, and activate infrastructure that will enable SpaceX to achieve its long-term mission. This team is responsible for the delivery of large capital projects to various internal customer groups across the company. This position is based out of the Bastrop site in the Bastrop, TX area. Travel may accompany this role, and based on business needs, opportunities to work at other SpaceX facilities may occur in the future.</p> <p><strong>&nbsp;RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Lead the project team, consulting engineers and contractors throughout the entirety of the engineering, procurement, construction, and commissioning process for power-specific scope items</li> <li>Develop and issue drawings, design documentation, and reports for aerospace, industrial, and commercial type projects</li> <li>Write, negotiate, and manage construction contracts with subcontractors across multiple disciplines through contract close-out</li> <li>Resolve design and construction conflicts in the field in real-time</li> <li>Coordinate with electrical utility provider for design/engineering to ensure reliable power service to critical site infrastructure</li> <li>Interact with engineers, contractors, vendors, fabricators, and project stakeholders</li> </ul> <p><strong>&nbsp;BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in electrical engineering or electrical engineering technology</li> <li>3+ years of professional experience with the design or build of commercial or industrial power systems</li> </ul> <p><strong>&nbsp;PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Primary experience with electrical and power distribution systems (&lt;600Vac)</li> <li>Working knowledge of delta/wye transformers, switchgear, motor control centers, building lighting, building construction specifications, and facility grounding</li> <li>Experience with critical power infrastructure including UPS systems, backup generators, and automatic transfer switches</li> <li>Experience creating and implementing process/design solutions with minimal impact on business operations</li> <li>Able to quickly assess an issue and assist technicians with troubleshooting and repair</li> <li>Ability to work in a high-concentration, high-stress environment, under possible extended work hours and tight deadlines</li> <li>Acute attention to detail, ability to see interactions with other systems to avoid problems</li> <li>AutoCAD/Revit – beginner to intermediate skill level</li> <li>Familiarity with the National Electric Code, National Fire Protection Association, and International Building Code</li> </ul> <p><strong>&nbsp;ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Perform hands-on work in all environments (heat, cold, rain), in tight quarters or at heights</li> <li>This role requires you to be onsite - hybrid or remote work will not be considered</li> <li>Must be able to work extended hours and weekends as needed</li> <li>Remain focused while working in hazardous environments, while wearing appropriate PPE</li> <li>Must be able to lift up to 25lbs unassisted</li> <li>Travel up to 25%</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR <a href="https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/?id=ddtc_kb_article_page&amp;sys_id=24d528fddbfc930044f9ff621f961987">here</a>. &nbsp;</li> </ul> <p>SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.</p> <p>Applicants wishing to view a copy of SpaceX’s Affirmative Action Plan for veterans and individuals with disabilities, or applicants requiring reasonable accommodation to the application/interview process should reach out to&nbsp;<a href="mailto:EEOCompliance@spacex.com">EEOCompliance@spacex.com</a><em>.&nbsp;</em></p></div>

title: Power Systems Engineer (Starship Avionics)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>POWER SYSTEMS ENGINEER (STARSHIP AVIONICS)</strong></p> <p>The Starship Avionics team supports the mission to revolutionize orbital flight and space travel-opening access for humankind to establish new frontiers in space and ultimately become a multi-planetary species. Our team builds some of the most advanced electronics ever flown in space- at a cost and rate previously considered unthinkable in the space industry. Become a part of this fast moving and world class Avionics team, work with super smart and motivated engineers, and achieve truly audacious goals. If you’re ready for a challenge and would like to help make our civilization multi-planetary then you’ve come to the right place!</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Provide engineering expertise in design, system analysis, and testing of&nbsp;high voltage systems, including lithium-ion batteries, solid state load switches, DC-DC power converters, and power distribution optimization</li> <li>Work on electrical power system and sub-system level design trades and develop requirements</li> <li>Define and perform electrical power system verification testing and analysis</li> <li>Work with multidisciplinary teams of design, test, and production engineers to create new power electronics hardware</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering</li> <li>1+ years of experience with high voltage systems, lithium-ion batteries, solid state load switches, DC-DC power converters, or power distribution (personal projects, research, internships, and extracurricular academic projects qualify)</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Previous experience with DC-DC power converters, electric motors, lithium-ion batteries, or solid state load switches</li> <li>Experience with electric drivetrains in aircraft flight control surfaces, electric vehicle traction systems, or similar applications</li> <li>Experience in modeling, simulation, and testing of electrical power systems&nbsp;</li> <li>Understanding of design for fault tolerance and reliability</li> <li>Familiarity with power supply testing and packaging for harsh environments</li> <li>Experience with in-lab impedance measurement and loop-gain measurement</li> </ul> <p><strong>&nbsp;ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Ability to work extended hours or weekends as needed for mission critical deadlines</li> </ul><div title: Power Systems Engineer (Starship)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>POWER SYSTEMS ENGINEER</strong></p> <p>Join the High Power Engineering team at SpaceX to pioneer the design, build, operation, and maintenance of advanced power generation, transmission, and distribution systems for Starship's launch, production, propellant generation, and the city of Starbase, TX. As a power systems engineer, you'll work with a team to scale high-capacity electrical infrastructure for the world's most powerful rocket, ensuring seamless energy flow for groundbreaking missions. The position is based at Starbase, TX, with potential travel to other SpaceX facilities.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES</strong></p> <ul> <li>Design, build, operate, and maintain the various microgrids that comprise Starbase, TX.</li> <li>Collaborate with cross-functional teams; lead projects; and drive rapid, continuous improvements at Starbase launch sites.</li> <li>Be responsible for infrastructure upgrades to dynamically scale systems for Starship's production rate targets.</li> <li>Create and maintain sitewide power budgets, monitoring, and metering for mission-critical assets to optimize visibility and efficiency.</li> <li>Develop and execute asset strategies for high-power launch and grid infrastructure.</li> <li>Develop standardized designs for launch, propellant generation, and power delivery facilities.</li> <li>Performs detailed design on all aspects of electrical power systems: one-lines, three-lines, control/relaying schematics, wiring diagrams, SCADA, conduit/cable sizing/routing, grounding design, general arrangement, etc.</li> <li>Develops and implements protective relay settings and schemes for high voltage equipment.&nbsp;</li> <li>Maintain organized design and asset documentation for all Starbase launch and power facilities.</li> <li>Ensure compliance with NFPA 70, 70B, 70E, NESC, and IEEE standards, prioritizing safety and engineering excellence.</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, physics, or another engineering discipline.</li> <li>1+ years of experience in power systems design, analysis, and build, with a focus on high-power, high-voltage systems.</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCES</strong></p> <ul> <li>3+ years of professional experience in a similar role.</li> <li>Professional Engineering license or intention to actively seeking PE license.&nbsp;</li> <li>Experience with power systems analysis software and tools: ETAP, SKM, EasyPower, PowerWorld, Matlab, PSCAD, PSEE, Simulink, etc.</li> <li>Experience performing basic load flow, short-circuit, arc-flash, coordination, and transient stability studies.</li> <li>Familiarity with industrial power systems up to 345 kV, including switchgear, transformers, BESS, VFDs, motors, distribution systems, UPS/emergency backups, power generation, relaying, metering, protective devices, and networking.</li> <li>Familiarity with industrial communications protocols and networking: Modbus, IEEE C37.115, IEEE C37.111, DNP3, etc.</li> <li>Experience with CAD software: Revit, AutoCAD, NX, etc.</li> <li>Demonstrated initiative, creative problem-solving, and strong analytical/engineering fundamentals.</li> <li>Excellent written and verbal communication skills.</li> <li>Proven ability to lead teams, work independently, and thrive in dynamic, high-stress environments with tight deadlines.</li> <li>Strong organizational skills to prioritize, schedule, and implement solutions with minimal operational impact.</li> <li>Ability to quickly troubleshoot issues and support technicians hands-on.</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS</strong></p> <ul> <li>Perform hands-on work in all environments (heat, cold, rain), in tight quarters or at heights.</li> <li>Work extended hours and weekends as needed to support launch operations.</li> <li>Remain focused in hazardous environments while wearing appropriate PPE.</li> <li>Lift up to 25 lbs. unassisted.</li> <li>Provide 24/7 on-call support for emergencies.</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. title: Propulsion Engineer, Stage Systems (Starship)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>PROPULSION ENGINEER, STAGE SYSTEMS (STARSHIP)</strong></p> <p>The Stage Responsible Engineer (Stage RE) develops the fluid systems required to enable higher-performance, highly manufacturable interplanetary vehicles. This role develops the design, operation, and performance of the stage propulsion systems on the Starship launch vehicle. The stage propulsion systems include all propellant feed systems, propellant management systems, helium pressurization systems, pneumatic systems, autogenous pressurization systems, differential pressure measurement systems, engine ignition gas supply systems, environmental control systems, and attitude control systems integrated into each stage of the vehicle. The Stage RE owns overall stage&nbsp;propulsion system performance for each vehicle and mission.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Develop and maintain top-level requirements, system design, operation, and performance of the associated components for the systems above</li> <li>Develop and maintain thermal/fluid models of the stage propulsion systems</li> <li>Generate and maintain stage control system timing, valve sequencing, and stage systems mission design; develop CONOPs from conception through flight software configuration, implementation, and execution</li> <li>Support production, test, and launch operations as needed across all SpaceX facilities</li> <li>Review and approve all stage system checkouts and non-conformance dispositions, and perform final vehicle inspections prior to shipment or test</li> <li>Generate and maintain all stage test plans; fully support all stage testing operations (including on-console operations); review stage test data; validate stage system performance; and provide final sign-off on system acceptance prior to shipment to the launch pad</li> <li>Review and approve stage systems launch procedures, final integration instructions, anomaly resolutions, and flight software</li> <li>Fully support all major launch operations, as directed by the launch director</li> <li>Review launch data, validate flight vehicle performance, and lead any stage-related flight anomaly resolutions and corrective actions&nbsp;</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in mechanical, manufacturing, or aerospace engineering</li> <li>1 year of mechanical or fluid system design experience&nbsp;</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Master’s degree in mechanical engineering, aerospace engineering, or another engineering field </li> <li>Strong first principles understanding of thermodynamics, incompressible flow, and compressible flow </li> <li>Proficient knowledge of statics and mechanics of materials </li> <li>Strong critical thinking and problem-solving skills, exceptional attention to detail </li> <li>Experience working with pressurized fluid systems and components, such as pneumatic systems, cryogenic systems, pressure control devices, valves, diffusers, and fittings </li> <li>Experience testing rocket stage or engine propulsion systems </li> <li>Experience with integrated vehicle pad and launch operations </li> <li>Familiarity with common aerospace instrumentation (e.g. pressure transducers, RTDs) </li> <li>Familiarity with basic concepts of control systems </li> <li>Hands-on hardware experience performing fabrication, assembly, and/or testing (can be professional, academic, entrepreneurial, or hobby setting) </li> <li>Demonstrated track record of success in a rapidly growing, changing, and highly technical environment – ability to act and execute in a scrappy, entrepreneurial manner against tight timelines </li> <li>Excellent communication skills (both written and verbal) and ability to succinctly present recommendations to stakeholders, the customers, and management </li> <li>Working knowledge of Python and/or MATLAB </li> <li>Strong desire to mentor and develop direct reports &nbsp;</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Must be willing to work extended hours and weekends as needed </li> <li>Flight hardware typically is built in tight quarters and physical dexterity is required </li> <li>Ability to perform job duties that require standing, kneeling, crouching, twisting upper body, working in cramped positions in small openings and climbing hand over hand </li> <li>Typically exposed to work in extreme outdoor environments – heat, cold, rain </li> <li>Work performed in an environment requiring exposure to fumes, odors, and noise </li> <li>Schedule varies depending on site operational needs; flexibility required </li> <li>Flexibility to travel to remote build sites &nbsp;</li> </ul> <p>&nbsp;</p><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be title: Sales Manager (Global Starlink Enterprise Sales)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>SALES MANAGER (GLOBAL STARLINK ENTERPRISE SALES)</strong></p> <p>The Starlink Enterprise Sales team is hiring a local, results driven Sales Manager to support Starlink’s adoption across North America. Starlink brings an unprecedented opportunity to significantly impact communities, businesses, and governments worldwide. The role requires high personal motivation and self-accountability to drive demand generation, co-sell with resellers, and win deals with mid-market Enterprise accounts.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Internal Responsibilities: <ul> <li>Exceed sales</li> <li>Develop territory strategy</li> <li>Manage activity</li> <li>Maintain CRM</li> <li>Weekly reports</li> <li>Quarterly business reviews</li> </ul> </li> <li>External Responsibilities: <ul> <li>Build pipeline primarily through outbound prospecting</li> <li>Conduct new business meetings</li> <li>Qualify opportunities</li> <li>Communicate value</li> <li>Build relationships</li> <li>Deliver proposals</li> <li>Lead winning sales campaigns</li> <li>Collaborate with resellers and internal teams</li> </ul> </li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree</li> <li>4+ years of enterprise sales experience or 1+ years at SpaceX</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Proven Enterprise sales track record exceeding revenue targets</li> <li>Proven Enterprise vertical experience with one or more of the following <ul> <li>SLED: State and Local Government &amp; title: Site Reliability Engineer, Platform Infrastructure
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>SITE RELIABILITY ENGINEER, PLATFORM INFRASTRUCTURE</strong></p> <p>The application software team is the central nervous system of SpaceX. Manufacturing is how SpaceX turns designs into hardware. The compute, storage, and networking that run our factories must be as reliable as the products we build. This team owns infrastructure supporting Starship, Starlink, Starshield, and Terafab. This position will have a direct impact on factory uptime, throughput, and production scale across programs.</p> <p>The ideal candidate has strong software engineering fundamentals and a passion for infrastructure: reliability, stability, proactive maintenance, and scalability. You understand the system before you change it, solve hard problems, communicate clearly with stakeholders and teammates, and take ownership of work that manufacturing depends on.</p> <p>Aerospace experience is not required. We value smart, motivated, collaborative engineers who treat teammates with fairness, respect, and support, and who want to take full ownership of challenging problems to help make humanity multi-planetary.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Deploy, upgrade, operate, maintain, and scale compute, storage, and networking for manufacturing systems across Starship, Starlink, Starshield, and Terafab</li> <li>Manage infrastructure as code and use observability to provide a complete picture of platform health</li> <li>Design for reliability, stability, and scale; find and remove bottlenecks with measurement and engineering</li> <li>Practice proactive maintenance: capacity planning, lifecycle management, and reducing toil before it becomes an incident</li> <li>Partner with software engineers, manufacturing stakeholders, and site teams to build operable, maintainable systems</li> <li>Improve the full lifecycle—from design through deployment, operation, and continuous refinement</li> <li>Practice sustainable incident response and blameless postmortems</li> <li>Provide high-quality support to manufacturing and engineering users</li> <li>Communicate clearly with stakeholders and teammates</li> <li>Participate in on-call and travel to sites as needed for deployments, incidents, and cross-site reliability</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in computer science, information systems, or an engineering discipline; OR 3+ years of professional experience in SRE or DevOps in lieu of a degree</li> <li>1+ years of software development experience&nbsp;</li> <li>Experience with Linux operating systems</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Experience with compute, storage, and/or networking infrastructure in production</li> <li>Infrastructure as code (Terraform, Ansible, Puppet, or similar)</li> <li>Containers and virtualization (Docker, Kubernetes, vSphere, QEMU, KVM, etc.)</li> <li>Databases and data modeling (Postgres, Clickhouse, etc.)</li> <li>Ability to translate high-level requirements into implementations from first principles</li> <li>Comfort with mission-critical systems and appropriate urgency and care</li> <li>Skillful communication with customers, peers, and management</li> <li>Comfort operating across multiple sites and manufacturing programs</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Must be able to work extended hours and weekends as needed</li> <li>Must be able to travel to different sites (Hawthorne, CA; Redmond, WA; Cape Canaveral, FL; Starbase, TX)</li> <li>Ability to pass Air Force background check for Cape Canaveral&nbsp;</li> <li>This role requires you to be onsite. Remote and/or hybrid work will not be considered&nbsp;</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. title: Sr. Electrical Engineer (Power Systems)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>SR. ELECTRICAL ENGINEER (POWER SYSTEMS)</strong></p> <p>As a member of the Construction Projects team, you will work with engineers across multiple disciplines to design, build, and activate infrastructure that will enable SpaceX to achieve its long-term mission. This team is responsible for the delivery of large capital projects to various internal customer groups across the company. This position is based out of the McGregor Rocket Development Facility. Travel will accompany this role, and based on business needs, opportunities to work at other SpaceX facilities may occur in the future.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Collaborate and grow with the multi-disciplinary SpaceX Construction Projects team by performing (power-specific) engineering, procurement, construction, and commissioning activities for a variety of critical and fast-paced company projects.</li> <li>Develop and issue drawings, design documentation, and reports for aerospace, industrial, and commercial type projects</li> <li>Write, negotiate, and manage construction contracts with subcontractors across multiple disciplines through contract close-out</li> <li>Resolve design and construction conflicts in the field in real-time</li> <li>Coordinate with the electrical utility provider for design/engineering to ensure reliable power service to critical site infrastructure</li> <li>Interact with engineers, contractors, fabricators, and project stakeholders</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in electrical engineering or electrical engineering technology</li> <li>6+ years of professional experience with the design or build of commercial or industrial power systems</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Primary experience with electrical and power distribution systems (&lt;600Vac)</li> <li>Working knowledge of delta/wye transformers, switchgear, motor control centers, building lighting, building construction specifications, and facility grounding</li> <li>Experience with critical power infrastructure, including UPS systems, backup generators, and automatic transfer switches</li> <li>Experience creating and implementing process/design solutions with minimal impact on business operations</li> <li>Ability to quickly assess an issue and assist technicians with troubleshooting and repair</li> <li>Ability to work in a high-concentration, high-stress environment, under possible extended work hours and tight deadlines</li> <li>Acute attention to detail, ability to see interactions with other systems to avoid problems</li> <li>AutoCAD/Revit – beginner to intermediate skill level</li> <li>Familiarity with the National Electric Code, National Fire Protection Association, and International Building Code</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li style="text-align: left;">Perform hands-on work in all environments (heat, cold, rain), in tight quarters or at heights</li> <li
