As part of our infrastructure team, your responsibility will be the proficient installation and management of server, network, and power systems in our data centers, adhering to best practices to ensure optimal performance. The ideal candidate has experience working with various types of hardware architectures and understands the strengths of each. You will also carry out performance-tuning and quality assurance operations on critical infrastructure components to ensure high level of data quality, availability, and security across the enterprise. In fulfilling this role, you will be expected to collaborate with the team to develop and implement strategies for improved data center operations.&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Resolve operational, infrastructure or hardware incidents in multiple data centers.</li> <li>Manage complete lifecycle for data center hardware, including deployment, operation, and decommission.</li> <li>Physically rack and cable data center equipment.</li> <li>Track and logically organize the physical storage of incoming data center equipment.</li> <li>Perform quality assurance testing and resolve recurring issues.</li> <li>Schedule and track hardware maintenance tasks.</li> <li>Update port maps and rack layouts and create operational procedures.</li> <li>Monitor the environmental conditions and power/cooling systems of a data center to ensure they are optimum for servers, switches, storage arrays, and other devices.</li> <li>Run hardware diagnostics and replace failing parts in a timely manner.</li> <li>Upgrade internal system components, including CPUs, memory, and storage.</li> <li>Setup and operate common Linux and Windows servers.</li> <li>Document processes and keep event logs.</li> <li>Work with the purchasing department on the procurement of new data center equipment.</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in a STEM discipline and 1+ year of data center experience; title: Data Engineer (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><h1 style="line-height: 1.2;"><span style="font-size: 10pt;"><strong>DATA ENGINEER (STARLINK)</strong></span></h1> <p style="line-height: 1.2;">At SpaceX, we’re leveraging our experience building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation, delivering fast, reliable internet to more than 10 million users worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate the full stack — satellites, user terminals, and the software that ties it all together.</p> <p style="line-height: 1.2;">As a Data Engineer on the Starlink Enterprise team, you will improve the quality of data flowing into our commercial systems and build the integrations and AI agents that turn that cleaner data into better decisions and faster execution — from pipeline generation through closed revenue and ongoing enablement. You will partner with Enterprise sales, channel and reseller operations, sales ops, and enablement to fix messy inputs, reduce manual cleanup, and ship automations that make go-to-market workflows more reliable.</p> <h2 style="line-height: 1.2;"><span style="font-size: 10pt;"><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></span></h2> <ul> <li>Improve data hygiene and quality across go-to-market systems — identify bad, missing, duplicate, and stale records; implement validation, enrichment, and remediation so higher-quality data enters our system of record, opportunity, partner/reseller, and enablement workflows</li> <li>Raise the quality of inputs to AI agents and analytics so outputs (recommendations, deal status, enablement answers, reporting) are more accurate, trustworthy, and actionable</li> <li>Build integrations across internal tools and external systems so deal, customer, and partner context flows cleanly between sales, channel ops, and operational platforms — reducing manual re-entry and preventing quality issues at the source</li> <li>Develop Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and related interfaces that connect AI assistants (including Grok) to internal and external go-to-market systems, with an emphasis on reliable, well-scoped access to the right data and tools</li> <li>Design, ship, and iterate AI agents that power Starlink Enterprise go-to-market workflows</li> <li>Contribute to AI-powered applications and automations that accelerate lead-to-revenue cycles, working within the additional datasets and systems architecture owned by the team</li> <li>Instrument data quality and agent performance with monitoring and feedback loops — catching regressions early and tying improvements to outcomes (e.g., cleaner pipeline, faster cycle times, higher adoption and trust)</li> <li>Partner closely with sales, sales ops, channel/reseller ops, and enablement to turn recurring data-quality problems and manual processes into durable automations and standards</li> <li>Create reusable tools, checks, and documentation that help the team maintain data quality and extend agents over time</li> </ul> <h2 style="line-height: 1.2;"><span style="font-size: 10pt;"><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></span></h2> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in computer science, data science, physics, mathematics, or another STEM discipline</li> <li>1+ title: Design Reliability Engineer (Crew Starship)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>DESIGN RELIABILITY ENGINEER (CREW STARSHIP)</strong></p> <p>After 50 years, humankind will once again return to surface of the moon using SpaceX’s new vehicle, the Human Landing System (HLS) – this time for good. Leveraging the lessons learned from our flight proven Dragon spacecraft, Falcon and now Starship, HLS will usher in the next era of manned spaceflight and exploration, ultimately allowing us to establish permanent communities on the Moon, Mars, and beyond.</p> <p>The HLS Design Reliability team is responsible for ensuring that flight hardware and concepts-of-operations lead to successful completion of missions while meeting or exceeding both internal and external design requirements. We perform a unique engineering role, evaluating and guiding engineering designs from concept to flight. We facilitate cross-disciplinary action and problem-solving across all SpaceX programs and staff.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:&nbsp;</strong></p> <ul> <li>Develop design criteria, requirements, and verification approaches for new systems.</li> <li>Ensure that the SpaceX design process &amp; design criteria/requirements are being followed for flight, launch, and/or recovery systems, including: <ul> <li>Provide critical peer review and approval of hardware designs during design reviews, and of acceptance and qualification test campaigns.</li> <li>Drive improvements to vehicle design through close integration with hardware teams.</li> <li>Perform verification reviews hardware and systems.</li> </ul> </li> <li>Ensure that the customer design criteria/requirements are addressed for flight systems, including: <ul> <li>Lead spacecraft certification efforts through direct interaction with U.S. Government customers.</li> <li>Tailor and negotiating requirements and verifications to meet program goals.</li> <li>Review vehicle changes to ensure qualification compliance.</li> </ul> </li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in an engineering discipline.</li> <li>1+ years professional experience in fabrication, assembly, and/or testing.</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Master's degree in an engineering discipline.</li> <li>Experience with aircraft, launch vehicles, spacecraft, or other aerospace systems.</li> <li>Experience with aircraft, launch vehicle, or spacecraft requirements and standards.</li> <li>Experience with standards and requirement negotiation.</li> <li>Excellent customer interface skills.</li> <li>Experience with at least one commercial FEA package (NASTRAN, ABAQUS, or ANSYS).</li> <li>Hands on experience with various industry standard manufacturing tools, techniques and processes, including mills, lathes, electronics assembly, composite layup, etc.</li> <li>Scripting and data analysis experience using Visual Basic, Matlab, Python and Excel.</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Must be available to work long hours and weekends as necessary.</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) title: Development Process Technician, Injection Molding (Starlink) - Level 4/5
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>DEVELOPMENT PROCESS TECHNICIAN, INJECTION MOLDING - LEVEL 4/5</strong></p> <p>As a technician, you will be responsible for maintaining daily production uptime of fully automated injection molding machines, including all subsequent post-mold operations. You will support planned and unplanned repairs, modifications, and upgrades of injection molding machines, peripheral equipment in the Injection Molding Starlink program. The goal of the team is to develop new manufacturing methods and qualify processes to be introduced into production.This position also involves the proper documentation of process settings through setup sheets and maintenance of process books and their contents. Other tasks relevant to the technician process include overseeing analyses, participating in work instruction development projects, and training others as necessary. Work area will be on the manufacturing floor running plastic injection molding machines, fixing the machines, setting up/calibrating the machines, operating the machines, and documenting as required. This is a hands-on production job that includes meeting goals for production, quality, inventory of both parts and raw material, and personnel aspects.&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Install, commission and validate intelligent equipment to support injection molding applications</li> <li>Participate in process development of the injection molding process through parameter optimization, DOE experiments, and trials that will lead to a robust process</li> <li>Oversee operator instructions, critical parameters, checklists and training materials for all molding operations, update special equipment service manuals including BOMs, drawings, wiring schematics, recommended needed processes, technical expertise, and tooling for optimization of production runs</li> <li>Update special equipment service manuals including BOMs, drawings, and wiring schematics Recommended needed processes, technical expertise, and tooling for optimization of production runs&nbsp;</li> <li>Work closely with product design engineering teams to define requirements</li> <li>Diagnose equipment failures, collect data to identify root causes and develop sustainable solutions</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>High school diploma or equivalency certificate</li> <li>5+ years plastic injection molding experience in a production environment</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>7+ years plastic injection molding experience in a production environment</li> <li>3+ years experience with highly automated injection molding cells</li> <li>3+ years molding experience with Engel brand machines</li> <li>Experience of multi-shot molding, automated color blending and central material drying system</li> <li>Experience in independently troubleshooting advanced electrical circuits, electronic systems, motors &amp; starters, electrically operated equipment and making successful repairs and modifications</li> <li>Electrical wiring experience and some knowledge of how PLCs, sensors, and other electrical components are wired and work</li> <li>Strong skills in troubleshooting with scientific, Paulson, or RJG processes</li> <li>Able to interpret geometrical tolerances on part drawings</li> <li>Comprehensive knowledge and thorough understanding of robotics and auxiliary equipment used with plastics Injection molding machines</li> <li>Proficient in Microsoft Excel, Office, and Word</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Ability to work the following hours: <ul> <li>Monday to Friday from 5:00AM to 5:30PM</li> </ul> </li> <li>Ability to lift up to 25 Ibs. unassisted</li> <li>Standing/walking for long periods of time</li> <li>Ability to work overtime and weekends when needed to meet critical deadlines</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. title: Development Test Engineer (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>DEVELOPMENT TEST ENGINEER (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is leveraging its experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation and is providing fast, reliable internet to millions of users worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system – thousands of satellites, consumer receivers that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing, and the software that brings it all together. We’ve only begun to scratch the surface of Starlink’s potential global impact. As we continue to upgrade and expand the constellation, we’re looking for best-in-class engineers to join the team.</p> <p>Starlink Development Test is a fast-paced R&amp;D focused group that aims to reduce hardware development time and increase reliability by testing Starlink’s next-generation hardware. Our Test Engineers design, fabricate, and implement test equipment as well as conduct development tests for the new structures, components, mechanisms, and more.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Create test stand concepts, fabrication drawings, wiring schematics, and instrumentation lists</li> <li>Design and analyze structures, fluid systems, and mechanisms</li> <li>Supervise the integration of test stands including fabrication, mechanical assembly and data/control systems</li> <li>Operate test stands with great attention to detail (tests have very little margin for error, so attention to detail is a crucial and essential characteristic of a development test engineer)</li> <li>Develop test requirements with the flight engineering team, develop a design solution that meets or exceeds those requirements, and drive the campaign to closure</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering</li> <li>1+ years of experience in one or more of the following: <ul> <li>Involvement with an extracurricular project team designing and building mechanical structures and/or high-pressure systems</li> <li>Academic research on mechanical structures</li> <li>Professional experience designing and analyzing mechanical structures</li> </ul> </li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Experience with hydraulic, thermal, structural, electromechanical, high pressure, and vacuum systems</li> <li>Experience with basic test instrumentation and control components such as pressure transducers, thermocouples, RTDs, strain gauges, accelerometers, flow meters, load cells, relays, solenoid valves, and encoders</li> <li>Experience with Unigraphics (NX)</li> <li>Experience performing finite element analysis (FEA)</li> <li>Experience with steel and/or aluminum weldment design and analysis</li> <li>Experience with high pressure (up to 30,000 psi) Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>DEVELOPMENT TEST TECHNICIAN - 2ND SHIFT</strong></p> <p>Test technicians for the Starbase Structures team are highly multidisciplinary, and this individual will be tasked with a wide variety of test operations and test equipment fabrication work. The team consists of technicians and engineers working closely together to build mechanical and fluid assemblies, modify and integrate test articles, build data and control systems, and support testing operations.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Build, modify, and troubleshoot new or existing test equipment, ranging from fluid systems, mechanical assemblies, data and control systems, and instrumentation</li> <li>Fabricate high-pressure fluid panels, plumbing, and hydraulic manifolds, including tube fabrication and routing, cleaning, proofing, and activating</li> title: Development Test Technician (Mechanical)

Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>DEVELOPMENT TEST TECHNICIAN (MECHANICAL)</strong></p> <p>Development test technicians get to assemble, troubleshoot, repair, and perform regular maintenance, work on flight and development engines, and support test and build equipment and tooling. Development test technicians support the company by building and maintaining flight-worthy spacecraft engines, components, and associated test equipment, supporting engineering in suggesting and implementing process improvements, and maintaining a clean and safe work environment. These technicians support activities in the engine assembly area, as well as enjoy working outside at the rocket development facility, on our development test (R&amp;D) stands, supporting test operations first-hand. Development test technicians enjoy witnessing the rumbling of rocket engines throughout the day. We work as a highly integrated team and job responsibilities will include helping other programs to ensure the overall success of SpaceX.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Prepare test articles, test stands, and systems for test operations</li> <li>Ensure all test stand-related equipment, systems, and servicing are performed on time, safely, and in a professional manner</li> <li>Perform post-test operations and inspections to ensure flight-worthy hardware</li> <li>Maintain, troubleshoot, and repair equipment and instrumentation as needed</li> <li>Fabricate, repair, and assemble hardware/equipment needed for test operations</li> <li>Collaborate with engineers to develop and document activities</li> <li>Ensure all components and materials are clean and inspected according to applicable standards</li> <li>Operate and maintain hardware, high-pressure systems and pumps, and other ancillary equipment including pneumatic components</li> <li>Obtain and maintain licenses, operator permits, or certifications as required</li> <li>Monitor and maintain a reasonable inventory of cryogenic equipment, pneumatic equipment, fittings, hoses, and other supplies necessary to perform test operations</li> <li>Acquire proper inventory parts and equipment needed for repair or replacement of defective components</li> <li>Process work orders and maintenance tickets</li> <li>Perform a variety of related duties in support of acceptance and development testing, as well as testing site-wide, as needed</li> <li>Develop novel ways site-wide to streamline processes and increase the reliability of testing operations</li> <li>Participate in rigging and crane operations for test equipment and test articles; including hangar bridge cranes and mobile crane lifts</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>High school diploma or equivalency certificate</li> <li>3+ years of experience working with and troubleshooting complex title: Dynamics Engineer (Starship)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>DYNAMICS ENGINEER (STARSHIP)</strong></p> <p>The Starship Dynamics team is responsible for induced vehicle environments, system dynamics and vehicle dynamics on the Starship and HLS vehicles. The dynamics group is focused on defining forcing functions acting on the vehicle, predicting vehicle and system response, and ensuring hardware is qualified for ground testing and flight. The group has a wide range of responsibilities that include structural dynamics, fluid system dynamics, random vibration, engine dynamics and multibody dynamics. Dynamics engineers are expected to have a strong intuition of physics first principles, frequency domain analysis, and a broad range of engineering disciplines, in addition to having solid software and analytical skills.&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Resolve dynamics problems through analysis, test and the use of flight data</li> <li>Build finite element and lumped element models of launch vehicle systems</li> <li>Execute dynamic testing from start-to-finish (pre-test analysis, sensor selection &amp; installation, testing, data analysis, signal processing and model correlation)</li> <li>Own system level analysis and drive hardware modifications or vehicle operations across vehicle engineering teams</li> <li>Perform analyses using commercial and in-house codes as well as write new code</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in an engineering discipline</li> <li>1+ years of experience with structural or fluid dynamics via full-time employment, outside the classroom projects, or lab work</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Hands-on experience either analyzing data or building hardware</li> <li>Experience with frequency-based and/or time-history vibration analysis</li> <li>Experience with vibration, shock, and modal testing (system-identification experience a plus)</li> <li>Experience with data processing and analysis in Python and MATLAB</li> <li>Experience with solving ordinary differential equations</li> <li>Experience with turbomachinery, combustion dynamics, fluid system modeling, or structural-fluid coupling pogo problems</li> <li>Working knowledge of structural analysis and test, including a fundamental understanding of strength, stability and fatigue failure mechanisms</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Position may require extended work hours and weekend work</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>ELECTRICAL DESIGN ENGINEER, GATEWAYS &amp; CUSTOMER HARDWARE (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>Starlink believes in providing fast, reliable internet to serve populations with little or no connectivity. We design, build, launch, and operate the world's largest constellation of satellites, enabling us to operate a global internet network unbounded by traditional ground infrastructure limitations. Starlink also designs, builds, and delivers high-volume consumer hardware that allows users to connect to these satellites within minutes of unboxing, as well as our advanced gateways that we deploy regionally throughout the world. The root of SpaceX’s success so far lies in our mission to keep all engineering and production in-house, which enables a tight feedback loop, nimble decision-making, and speedy deliverables. With millions of daily users worldwide already online, Starlink is truly a game-changer and levels the playing field for those who were previously unconnected.</p> <p>As an Electrical Design Engineer on the Starlink team, you will have complete ownership over the development of millions of customer-facing products and devices that we ship directly to end users (Starlink dishes/user terminals, Wi-Fi routers, etc.). Our customers currently include teachers in the most remote parts of the Amazon, researchers in Antarctica, digital nomads who travel via RV, emergency responders, commercial airlines, cruise lines, and residential users who live in more rural or developing areas. You will be responsible for the design, implementation, and verification of the entire electrical system for these products. You could also be responsible for the design and performance of next-generation gateways - ultimately ensuring that our ground station antenna hardware can withstand the harshest environmental conditions while maintaining reliable communication with millions of users on a global scale. You will interact regularly with partner teams including silicon, software, mechanical, and manufacturing engineering to steer this hardware from initial concept development to full-scale production.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Design, develop, and test highly reliable electronics for communicating with our satellites</li> <li>Partner with software, mechanical, thermal, manufacturing, and production test teams</li> <li>Drive system trades, requirements capture, component selection, analysis, schematic capture, PCB layout, prototyping, hardware bring-up, debugging, documentation, manufacturing, and test of complex electrical designs</li> <li>Get hands-on and support hardware through production, satellite integration, and flight</li> <li>Work closely with engineers from adjacent disciplines (mechanical, thermal, software, test engineering, supply chain, silicon design, etc.) to deliver tightly integrated, high-performance hardware</li> <li>Drive continual improvements to our designs by building physical and digital tools to analyze data collected on orbit and in the lab</li> <li>Challenge assumptions and work to find simple solutions to complex problems</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering or other engineering discipline</li> <li>1+ years of professional experience designing circuits, electronic products, or hardware</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Master’s degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, or similar engineering degree</li> <li>2+ years of professional experience rapidly designing and delivering highly reliable products</li> <li>2+ years of electronic product experience designing hardware from concept through production; strong emphasis on full life cycle development of new hardware products and not small incremental updates to legacy hardware</li> <li>2+ years of experience designing and implementing mixed-signal circuit boards from concept through production using processors, FPGAs, Ethernet, multi-GHz Serdes, DRAM interfaces (DDR4), I2C, SPI, operational amplifiers, analog to digital and digital to analog converters, and power supply components</li> <li>2+ years of professional experience testing, troubleshooting, and debugging electronics</li> <li>Strong understanding of computers and programming languages (Python, C/C++)</li> <li>Demonstrated ability to work in a highly cross-functional role</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Ability to work extended hours or weekends as needed for mission critical deadlines</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. title: Electrical Engineer, Hardware Reliability (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>ELECTRICAL ENGINEER, HARDWARE RELIABILITY (STARLINK)&nbsp;</strong></p> <p>At SpaceX we’re leveraging our experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation and is providing fast, reliable internet to millions of users worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system – thousands of satellites, consumer receivers that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing, and the software that brings it all together. We’ve only begun to scratch the surface of Starlink’s potential global impact and are looking for best-in-class&nbsp;engineers to help maximize Starlink’s utility for communities and businesses around the globe.</p> <p>As an electrical engineer on the Starlink hardware reliability team, you'll sit at the intersection of electrical, firmware, RF, and manufacturing engineering. You will be responsible for hardware failure analysis, root cause, and driving for design and process changes to improve hardware reliability across our various devices. Your focus will be on product launches and field returns. title: Electrical Engineer, PCB (Starlink/Starmind)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>ELECTRICAL&nbsp;ENGINEER, PCB</strong><strong> (STARLINK/STARMIND)</strong>&nbsp;</p> <p>SpaceX is leveraging our experience building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s largest satellite constellation and most advanced broadband internet system. We provide reliable and fast internet to millions of users worldwide, including populations with little or no connectivity, rural communities, aircraft, watercraft, and places where existing services are unreliable, too expensive, or disconnected by natural disasters. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system, thousands of satellites and consumer antennae that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing. The Starlink team is seeking out the best-in-class professionals to maximize Starlink’s potential for communities and businesses around the globe.&nbsp;</p> <p>As an Electrical Test &amp; Manufacturing Engineer on Starlink, you will spearhead state-of-the-art production processes for our printed circuit boards (PCBs). This position is responsible for the development and implementation of all equipment, facilities, tooling, and manufacturing process technologies necessary to scale production to high volumes. You will design and implement advanced manufacturing processes and automation, owning your projects from conception and factory design through machine installation, commissioning, factory ramp, and process optimization. You will design and run large, hands-on process design of experiments (DOE), optimize complex mechanical and chemical process equipment, and interact regularly with senior leadership during critical design phases.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p> <p>Your work will form the backbone for millions of next generation consumer-facing devices that we ship directly to customers and businesses all over the world. From private homes, RVs, planes, or boats, this team plays an instrumental role in leveling the playing field for high-speed connectivity.&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong>&nbsp;</p> <ul> <li>Develop, implement, and maintain new and/or improved manufacturing processes, equipment, technologies, and facilities; examples could include automatic optical inspection, bed-of-nails, and flying probe</li> <li>Analyze production processes and machinery from a first principles, physics-based approach&nbsp;</li> <li>Lead design of experiments (DOE) to establish a stable and robust technicians&nbsp;</li> <li>Solve technical and emergent issues from manufacturing (part quality, machine reliability, process instability, etc.)&nbsp;</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC title: Electrical Engineer, Silicon Reliability Test (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>ELECTRICAL ENGINEER, SILICON RELIABILITY TEST (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>As an electrical engineer on the Starlink silicon reliability team, you'll sit at the intersection of electrical, packaging, semiconductor, and manufacturing engineering. You will be responsible for package-level and wafer-level reliability testing, including HTOL and other accelerated life tests, root cause of silicon and packaging failures, and driving design and process changes to improve microelectronics reliability across Starlink devices. Your focus will be on the qualification of new silicon packages, wafer-level reliability, and supporting high-volume production.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Own package-level (HTOL, LTOL, etc.) and wafer-level (TDDB, ECM, etc.) reliability qualification and testing of new silicon designs and manufacturing technologies for high-volume production</li> <li>Plan, develop, execute, and analyze reliability test campaigns aligned with JEDEC and related standards</li> <li>Develop and procure custom test hardware, fixturing, burn-in boards, and environmental chambers/systems required for package-level and wafer-level reliability testing</li> <li>Design and develop PCBs and electrical interfaces for reliability test fixtures, sockets, and monitoring systems</li> <li>Develop software, automation scripts, and data acquisition tools (e.g., Python) to control test equipment, log telemetry, perform real-time monitoring, and analyze large reliability datasets</li> <li>Perform hands-on debugging and electrical characterization to drive root cause and corrective action of silicon, package, and interconnect failures observed in reliability testing, production, or the field</li> <li>Utilize advanced diagnostic and test tools (oscilloscopes, power supplies, vector network analyzers, custom firmware/scripts, thermal chambers, etc.) to characterize devices under stress and isolate failure mechanisms</li> <li>Run reliability failure investigations, coordinating efforts across silicon design, packaging, manufacturing, and reliability teams, and communicating findings to leadership</li> <li>Analyze reliability data (Weibull, acceleration models, etc.) to predict field performance, document failure modes, and drive design/process improvements for higher yield and reliability</li> <li>Partner with design, packaging, software, test, and manufacturing engineering teams to deliver reliable silicon hardware by informing product design, package selection, process changes, and test coverage</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, electronics engineering, or other engineering discipline</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>1+ years of experience in semiconductor reliability, packaging reliability, consumer electronics, characterization, or test</li> <li>Hands-on experience with HTOL or other accelerated life tests for packages or TDDB, EM, HCI, and other wafer-level tests</li> <li>Experience developing or procuring custom test hardware, burn-in boards, sockets, or fixturing for reliability testing</li> <li>Experience designing PCBs for test fixtures or high-reliability applications</li> <li>Familiarity with title: Electrical Hardware Engineer, AI Satellites (Starmind)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>ELECTRICAL HARDWARE ENGINEER, AI SATELLITES (STARMIND)</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is leveraging its experience deploying and operating the world’s largest satellite constellation to develop Starmind, a new constellation of satellites capturing solar energy in space to power low-cost, high-performance AI compute for Earth. Realizing this vision demands highly reliable, high performance electrical hardware ranging from power electronics, high speed digital systems, mixed signal designs, robust avionics, networking, and custom compute electronics. These systems must operate in the extreme environment of space while delivering the connectivity, control, power distribution, and processing needed for orbital AI inference.</p> <p>We are seeking best-in-class Electrical Hardware Engineers to own the full lifecycle of the electronics that make Starmind possible. You’ll apply deep electrical engineering skill sets at the intersection of power conversion and distribution, high-speed digital communications, analog design, network integration, thermal management, signal integrity, and on-orbit compute to create the hardware backbone for next-generation space-based AI infrastructure.</p> <p>We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system. Your work sits at the intersection of electrical, mechanical, thermal analysis, software, and networking engineering that enables orbital compute capability. Challenges range from high-speed digital communications, analog, network system integration, power electronics, RF/optical devices, and high-performance compute electronics for space. Your work will include everything from system design and schematic capture to PCB layout oversight; as well as hardware troubleshooting to driving requirements for the underlying silicon and complete product production and test. This also includes driving successful business outcomes across interdisciplinary subsystems of the satellite, inclusive of mechanical and software engineering peers among other engineering disciplines. Sub-teams include:</p> <p><strong>Avionics</strong>: The backbone of Starmind satellites are the bus avionics systems which control the vehicle, convert and distribute kilowatts of power, route high-speed vehicle and user/compute traffic, and connect satellites to each other via our state-of-the-art Space Lasers! The team is responsible for the design, development, and ultimate success of these avionics systems from concept to grave.</p> <p><strong>Payload</strong>: The Payload team is responsible for the design of custom AI compute electronics that push the forefront of AI chip performance, interconnectivity, and cluster size. Everything from high-power AI chips to high throughput network switching to high density storage conversion. The team owns the design, development, and ultimate success of this hardware from concept to grave.</p> <p>Your placement on these teams will be determined throughout the interviewing process after factoring in technical fit, expertise, and your personal preference.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES</strong></p> <ul> <li>Rapidly develop high-reliability electronics for satellites and spacecraft.</li> <li>Drive system trades, requirements capture, component selection, analysis, schematic capture, PCB layout, prototyping, hardware bring-up, debugging, documentation, manufacturing, test, and on-orbit performance of complex electrical designs</li> <li>Get hands-on and support hardware through production, satellite integration, and flight</li> <li>Determine layer stackup, perform component package selection, component placement, routing feasibility studies, and signal routing of digital, analog, RF, and power conversion of PCBs</li> <li>Library creation and maintenance</li> <li>Create and release documentation for fabrication of PCBs</li> <li>Collaborate with internal teams and PCB vendors to continually improve design rules, constraints and design for test and manufacture guidelines</li> <li>Work closely with engineers from adjacent disciplines (mechanical, thermal, software, test engineering, supply chain, silicon design, etc.) to deliver tightly integrated, high-performance hardware</li> <li>Challenge assumptions, question requirements, learn from your mistakes, and approach problems with an open mind</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, or physics</li> <li>1+ years of experience designing circuits, electronic products, or hardware (internships/co-ops can apply)</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE</strong></p> <ul> <li>Master’s degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, or similar engineering degree</li> <li>2+ years of professional experience rapidly designing and delivering highly reliable products</li> <li>2+ years of electronic product experience designing hardware from concept through production; strong emphasis on full life-cycle development of new hardware products and not small incremental updates to legacy hardware</li> <li>2+ years of experience designing and implementing mixed-signal circuit boards from concept through production using processors, FPGAs, Ethernet, multi-GHz Serdes, DRAM interfaces (DDR4), I2C, SPI, operational amplifiers, analog to digital and digital to analog converters, and power supply components</li> <li>2+ years of professional experience testing, troubleshooting, and debugging electronics</li> <li>Strong understanding of computers and programming languages (Python, C/C++)</li> <li>Demonstrated ability to work in a highly cross-functional role</li> <li>2+ years working on aerospace systems</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS</strong></p> <ul> <li>Ability to work extended hours or weekends as needed for mission critical deadlines</li> <li>Some travel may occasionally be required</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, title: Electrician, Medium Voltage (Starship)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>ELECTRICIAN, MEDIUM VOLTAGE (STARSHIP)</strong></p> <p>As a Medium Voltage Electrician, you will support the installation, inspection, testing, maintenance, and repair of electrical equipment in substations and power grid facilities to ensure safe, reliable power delivery. This role focuses on basic tasks under direct supervision, working with energized equipment up to 260 volts initially, progressing to higher voltages (above 750 volts) after training. You will assist higher-classified personnel in high- and medium-voltage environments, following strict safety standards. This position combines core responsibilities from substation technician and station electrician roles, emphasizing hands-on learning and team collaboration.<br><br><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Assist in installing, inspecting, maintaining, and repairing substation equipment, including breakers, transformers, switches, relays, buswork, control systems, and batteries.</li> <li>Perform basic routine maintenance on high- and medium-voltage electrical systems, such as cleaning, lubrication, and visual inspections (e.g., checking oil levels, lights, heaters, and connections).</li> <li>Conduct entry-level electrical testing, including using voltmeters, ohmmeters, ammeters, insulation meggers, and assisting with insulation resistance, relay, transformer, and circuit breaker tests.</li> <li>Read and interpret basic electrical drawings, one-line diagrams, schematics, wiring diagrams, and work orders with guidance.</li> <li>Troubleshoot simple electrical, mechanical, and control system issues under supervision.</li> <li>Follow lockout/tagout (LOTO), grounding, clearance procedures, and safety protocols (e.g., PPE, emergency rescue techniques like steel/aerial lift rescue).</li> <li>Assist in station switching, de-energizing equipment, placing grounds, and coordinating with operators, engineers, and utility crews during outages or Operations.</li> <li>Help with physical tasks: digging/backfilling trenches, installing conduit/pipe/cable/wire, uncrating materials, painting structures, climbing ladders/structures (up to 50+ ft), and operating hand/power tools, portable generators, blowers, and pumps.</li> <li>Support emergency responses to outages, faults, and call-outs for prompt service restoration.</li> <li>Document work performed, test results, and observations accurately; maintain records and prepare basic reports.</li> <li>Replace simple components like lamps, switches, outlets, dry cells; assist with oil sampling/handling and signal/communication systems.</li> <li>Participate in training sessions, assist in training others, and become familiar with company safety rules, First Aid.</li> <li>Operate company vehicles and specialized equipment; inspect and store personal protective equipment (PPE).</li> <li>Perform similar or less skilled incidental duties as assigned.</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>High school diploma or equivalency certificate.</li> <li>3+ years of experience working as a licensed electrician.&nbsp;</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Associate degree in electrical, mechanical, industrial maintenance technology.</li> <li>Basic understanding of electrical principles (AC/DC circuits, safety standards).</li> <li>Ability to read basic prints/drawings and use common test tools.</li> <li>Proficiency with hand/power tools and physical tasks (lifting 50+ lbs, working at heights/confined spaces, outdoors in all weather).</li> <li>Strong safety focus, attention to detail, and ability to work independently or in teams.</li> <li>Knowledge of print reading for drawings, manuals, and one-lines.</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Schedule varies depending on site operational needs and flexibility required regarding frequent overtime/weekend support.</li> <li>Ability to work in an environment requiring exposure to fumes, odors, and noise.</li> <li>Ability to rapidly change roles/responsibilities while working in a high-paced, challenging work environment.</li> <li>Stand: Up to 6 hours per day.</li> <li>Sit: Up to 3 hours per day.</li> <li>Push/Pull: Up to 75lbs. (unassisted) 1-2 hours per day.</li> <li>Overhead reach: Up to 3 hours per day.</li> <li>Walk: Up to 3 hours per day.</li> <li>Lift/Carry: Up to 50lbs. Candidate may be required to complete a pre-employment questionnaire and/or physical to confirm these capabilities, which may include a medical history review.</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Perform complex technical assignments involving instrumentation and data acquisition/processing systems</li> <li>Connect and verify pressure electrical panels</li> <li>Lay out, build, test, troubleshoot, repair, and modify developmental and production electrical and electronic units, assemblies, components, parts, equipment, and systems</li> <li>Perform continuity checks, locate and correct wiring errors using measuring instruments such as ohmmeters and sequential continuity checkers</li> <li>Maintain, calibrate, configure, hardware</li> <li>Adjust, calibrate, align, and modify circuitry and components and record effects on unit performance</li> <li>Collaborate with design engineers to troubleshoot failures and issues college program counts)</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Basic knowledge of Wheatstone bridge theory, ability to apply Ohm's law, and an understanding of DC signal conditioning concepts for various types of sensors, including the following: thermocouple types K,&nbsp;S, and E; TC bonding concepts: resistance weld-on and adhesive bond-on types; TC probes title: Embedded Software Engineer (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>EMBEDDED SOFTWARE ENGINEER (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation and is providing fast, reliable internet to millions users worldwide. We design, build, manufacture, and operate all parts of the system including thousands of satellites, hundreds of gateways, and millions of customer kits. Our customers currently include teachers in the most remote parts of the Amazon, researchers in Antarctica, digital nomads who travel via RV, emergency responders, commercial airlines, cruise lines, and residential users who live in more rural or developing areas. While users can get online within minutes almost anywhere in the world, we’ve only begun to scratch the surface of Starlink’s potential. We are looking for best-in-class engineers to help maximize Starlink’s utility for individuals, communities, and businesses. Below are just some of the focus areas for software teams on Starlink:&nbsp;</p> <ul> <li>Develop software running on custom hardware that is deployed to millions of devices around the world</li> <li>Create infrastructure and tools for rapid and reliable deployment of our code to our customers no matter where they are</li> <li>Write software for Starlink’s custom phased array and modem silicon</li> <li>Radically improve the user experience of satellite internet</li> <li>Develop a telemetry system that scales to millions of devices with trillions of data points</li> <li>Build robust systems that are resistant to adversarial attacks</li> </ul> <p>Our software engineers are responsible for the complete lifecycle of the software they create, including development, testing, and support.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Design and implement highly available, fault-tolerant consumer devices and gateways that operate for long periods of time with minimal maintenance for millions of users</li> <li>Participate in architecture, design, and code reviews</li> <li>Develop prototypes to prove out key design concepts and quantify technical constraints</li> <li>Work with the Starlink factory to manufacture devices in-house</li> <li>Write quality Linux based software for common processors and microcontrollers (e.g. ARM, RISC V, etc.)</li> <li>Develop systems that allow for test execution across multiple environments such as virtualized hardware or real hardware-in-the-loop simulations</li> <li>Invent new tools that enable more frequent and reliable software deployment, test execution, and data analysis as part of a continuous integration and release system</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in computer science, engineering, math, or a STEM discipline and 1+ years of professional experience in software engineering; This includes one of the largest PCB manufacturing lines in North America and soon to be one of the largest solar cell manufacturing facilities in the world. title: Environmental Health & Safety Engineer
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH &amp; SAFETY ENGINEER</strong></p> <p>As part of a small, hardworking team of technicians and engineers, you will provide technical expertise and assist in the implementation of all environmental, health and safety programs at the Starship rocket development &amp; test site. The ideal candidate is highly skilled with both environmental and occupational safety fields, hands-on, and works well in a fast-paced environment. We work as a highly integrated team and job responsibilities will include helping other programs to ensure the overall success of SpaceX.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES: </strong></p> <ul> <li>Work closely with test engineers and technician teams to perform detailed safety reviews of complex hazardous operations to ensure safe execution</li> <li>Lead or assist in all aspects of incident investigations, including initial follow-up, root cause analysis, and corrective action development and closure</li> <li>Develop and maintain compliance with all applicable regulations and/or guidelines established by OSHA, NFPA, and NIOSH and other applicable regulatory agencies</li> <li>Collaborate with department leadership to complete job hazard assessments and implement health and safety policies and procedures</li> <li>Implement and develop safety and health programs including but not limited to:&nbsp; <ul> <li>OSHA general industry and construction standards</li> <li>HAZCOM, hazmat, cryogenics, compressed gases&nbsp;</li> <li>Confined space, fall protection and lock-out/tag-out</li> <li>Radiation and laser safety</li> </ul> </li> <li>Implement and develop environmental programs including but not limited to:&nbsp; <ul> <li>SPCC &amp; SWPPP&nbsp;</li> <li>Title V air permitting</li> <li>LQG hazardous waste management</li> </ul> </li> <li>Develop safety solutions to resolve EHS hazards/ concerns within cost and schedule constraints following a safety order of precedence to include elimination, substitution, engineering controls, work practice controls, training, and personal protective equipment (PPE) to ensure that safety of personnel, property, and the environment are within acceptable risk boundaries</li> <li>Monitor employee exposure to physical and chemical hazards</li> <li>Inspect facilities, machinery, and safety equipment to identify and correct potential hazards and ensure compliance with all applicable regulations</li> <li>Develop, implement, and maintain safety contingency plans (fires, spills, etc.)</li> <li>Develop and maintain compliance with all applicable regulations established by the EPA, CERCLA, RCRA, DOT, ATF, TCEQ, TRRC and other applicable regulatory agencies</li> <li>Perform environmental compliance and due diligence audits to ensure compliance with all applicable regulatory agencies</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree</li> <li>3+ years of experience in the design, development and operational oversight of environmental, health and safety disciplines</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in engineering with an emphasis in occupational health and safety and/or environmental engineering</li> <li>Demonstrated ability to research and apply the best industrial and working practices to provide effective services</li> <li>Knowledge of process safety management methods, pressure systems, and chemical delivery systems</li> <li>Strong knowledge and experience in interpreting, applying and documenting federal, state and local safety and environmental regulations</li> <li>Experience with emergency response communication and incident management in incidents involving hazardous and non-hazardous material releases to air, soil, and water</li> <li>Microsoft Office (Excel, PowerPoint, Word, Outlook)</li> <li>Strong organizational and communication skills&nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp;&nbsp;</li> <li>Experience and/or education in construction safety</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>This is&nbsp;<u>not</u> a remote or hybrid position and will require relocation if not already local to the Brownsville, TX area</li> <li>Position occasionally requires the ability to work extended hours and weekends when needed&nbsp; &nbsp;&nbsp;</li> </ul> <p>&nbsp;</p><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), title: Environmental Health & Safety Engineer (Construction Safety)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH &amp; SAFETY ENGINEER (CONSTRUCTION SAFETY)&nbsp;</strong></p> <p>As part of the SpaceX EHS Team, you will provide timely, clear, and high-quality technical expertise and assist in implementation of all environmental, health and safety programs for the <span data-teams="true">construction of Starbase's Starship and site development infrastructure</span>. The ideal candidate is highly skilled with both environmental and occupational safety fields, hands-on, and works well in a fast-paced environment. We work as a highly integrated team and job responsibilities will include helping other programs to ensure the overall success of SpaceX.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Oversee and own the day-to-day EHS site management of a fast-paced, high impact construction project including the responsibilities below: <ul> <li>Implement, enforce, and audit the site’s construction contractor EHS management program for SpaceX employees involved in or associated with contractor operations, ensuring requirements are understood and followed by contractors and subcontractors performing work for SpaceX</li> <li>Develop and maintain documented safety observations from regular hazard identification inspections of facilities, machinery, safety equipment, and on-site construction to identify, mitigate hazards, and ensure compliance with all applicable regulations and/or guidelines established by OSHA, NFPA and NIOSH and other applicable regulatory agencies</li> <li>Investigate and write corresponding reports for incidents, spills, injuries, or occupational diseases to determine root causes, establish corrective actions and preventive measures</li> <li>Develop and maintain compliance with all applicable regulations established by the EPA, RCRA, DOT and other applicable regulatory agencies</li> <li>Ensure that resources are allocated appropriately to safety-related items</li> </ul> </li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree</li> <li>1+ years of experience in the design, development and The ideal candidate is highly skilled in both environmental and occupational safety fields, hands-on, and works well in a fast-paced environment. We work as a highly integrated team, and job responsibilities will include helping other programs to ensure the overall success of SpaceX.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <p>Oversee and own the day-to-day EHS site management of a fast-paced, high-impact construction project, including the responsibilities below:</p> <ul> <li>Develop, implement, and enforce the site’s construction/contractor EHS management program, ensuring requirements are understood and followed by contractors and subcontractors performing work for SpaceX</li> <li>Develop and maintain safety observations from regular hazard identification inspections of facilities, machinery, safety equipment, and on-site construction activities</li> <li>Identify and mitigate hazards to ensure compliance with applicable regulations and guidelines established by OSHA, NFPA, NIOSH, and other applicable agencies</li> <li>Collaborate with department leadership to complete job hazard assessments, establish Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) requirements, determine safeguards, and implement health and safety policies and procedures to increase safety across all construction sites and projects</li> <li>Monitor and evaluate employee exposure to hazards during both nominal processes and emergencies</li> <li>Develop recommendations for remedial actions when safety policies are not met by employees and contractors</li> <li>Educate and provide necessary safety training to construction personnel</li> <li>Investigate and write corresponding reports for incidents, spills, injuries, or occupational diseases to determine root causes, establish corrective actions, and preventive measures</li> <li>Develop and maintain environmental compliance with all applicable regulations established by the EPA, RCRA, DOT, TECQ, and other applicable regulatory agencies</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree</li> <li>1+ years of experience in the design, EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in engineering with an emphasis in occupational health and safety</li> <li>Experience in health and safety with commercial/industrial construction title: Equipment Engineering Manager - Solar Cell Factory (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>MANAGER, EQUIPMENT ENGINEERING (SOLAR CELL MANUFACTURING</strong>)</p> <p>SpaceX is seeking a highly motivated Equipment Engineering Manager to lead the development, installation, qualification, and sustainment of advanced manufacturing equipment for our next-generation solar cell production lines. In this role, you will drive equipment strategy, reliability, and performance to enable high-volume, high-efficiency solar cell manufacturing that supports SpaceX’s energy goals. Your scope will span initial factory turn-on, execution of ambitious factory ramps, and driving of equipment strategy to support continuous solar cell technology and performance improvements.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Grow, lead, and mentor a team of equipment engineers responsible for solar cell manufacturing tools including wet chemical benches, PECVD deposition systems, PVD/sputtering tools, metrology/inspection systems, and beyond</li> <li>Own equipment lifecycle management from installation and process qualification through high-volume production, including preventive maintenance strategies, spare parts optimization, and continuous improvement of overall equipment effectiveness (OEE).</li> <li>Drive root-cause analysis and corrective actions for equipment downtime, yield excursions, and process drift using structured problem-solving methodologies (e.g., 8D, FMEA, DOE).</li> <li>Collaborate with process engineering, manufacturing, and facilities teams to define equipment specifications, acceptance criteria, and capacity expansion roadmaps for solar cell technologies</li> <li>Develop and execute equipment roadmaps that improve throughput, reduce cost per watt, and increase cell efficiency while maintaining world-class uptime</li> <li>Establish and enforce equipment safety, cleanroom protocols, and change control processes in a high-volume semiconductor-style manufacturing environment.</li> <li>Partner with vendors and internal SpaceX designers to evaluate, qualify, and integrate new equipment platforms and drive performance improvements on existing tools</li> <li>Track and report key performance metrics (MTBF, MTTR, yield impact, cost of ownership) to senior leadership and drive data-driven decisions</li> <li>Support new product introduction (NPI) activities by ensuring equipment is ready for pilot and ramp phases of next-generation cell architectures</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, chemical engineering, or materials science</li> <li>5+ years of experience in equipment engineering or maintenance in a high-volume manufacturing environment (semiconductor, solar, or related industry)</li> <li>5+ years of experience managing or leading a team of engineers</li> <li>Experience with thin-film deposition, vacuum systems, or wet processing equipment</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Experience specifically with silicon solar cell manufacturing equipment, processes, chemicals, and gases</li> <li>Strong background in semiconductor equipment (PECVD, PVD, ALD, etch, or CMP) or photovoltaic production lines</li> <li>Machine design and/or manufacturing background with proven track record of going from idea to working system</li> <li>Proven track record of improving equipment availability, reducing cost of ownership, and scaling manufacturing capacity</li> <li>Experience with statistical process control (SPC), data analytics platforms, and equipment automation (SECS/GEM, PLCs, SCADA)</li> <li>Knowledge of cleanroom operations, contamination control, and safety standards in a high-tech manufacturing setting</li> <li>Excellent leadership, communication, and cross-functional collaboration skills</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Must be willing to work extended hours and long weekends when needed to meet critical deadlines</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, title: Equipment Maintenance & Reliability Engineer, PCB (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>EQUIPMENT MAINTENANCE &amp; RELIABILITY ENGINEER, PCB (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>At SpaceX we’re leveraging our experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation and is providing fast, reliable internet to 10M+ users worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system – thousands of satellites, consumer receivers that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing, and the software that brings it all together. We’ve only begun to scratch the surface of Starlink’s potential global impact and are looking for best-in-class engineers to help maximize Starlink’s utility for communities and businesses around the world.</p> <p>The primary role of the Maintenance Engineer is to identify and manage asset reliability risks that could adversely affect factory or business operations. As production develops and increases rate, the Maintenance Engineer's primary goal is to achieve maximum asset and system up-time by implementing and executing plans to minimize production losses, unpredictable asset behavior, and unusually high costs for system maintainability. In addition, the Maintenance Engineer acts as the accountable engineering resource in driving the design, build, and installation stages of new and modified assets as well as provides technical support to maintenance management, technicians, and production personnel to prevent and mitigate operational issues of critical equipment.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Work with project engineering to ensure the reliability and sustainability of new and modified installations</li> <li>Guide efforts to ensure consistency and maintainability of critical equipment, processes, utilities, facilities, controls, and safety/security systems</li> <li>Own equipment improvement plans for more responsive and developed preventative maintenance strategies, equipment effectiveness, and minimization of production downtime</li> <li>Define, design, develop, monitor, and refine an asset maintenance plan that includes value-added preventive maintenance tasks, minimization of high-cost low-value repairs, effective utilization of predictive, and other non-destructive testing methodologies</li> <li>Prepare asset documentation package for review of system mechanical design, controls, and software</li> <li>Develop engineering solutions to repetitive failures and equipment-specific problems that adversely affect plant operations including capacity, quality, cost, or regulatory compliance issues</li> <li>Work with production to perform analyses of assets including asset utilization rate, overall equipment effectiveness, remaining useful life, operational restrictions, and other parameters that define the operating condition, reliability, and costs of assets</li> <li>Provide technical support to production, maintenance management, and technical personnel</li> <li>Manage production requests for asset improvement, control functions, and data collection</li> <li>Apply value analysis to repair/replace, repair/redesign, and make/buy decisions</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in mechanical, electrical, aerospace, systems, or manufacturing engineering</li> <li>1+ years of experience in an engineering role in manufacturing, integration, reliability, technical program management, and/or operations</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Advanced degrees in engineering with reliability analysis experience through research and/or internships</li> <li>2+ years of experience in a maintenance engineering role and reliability in a high-volume manufacturing, testing, or operational environment</li> <li>Hands-on experience with equipment control systems, machinery, and industrial automation</li> <li>Developed understanding of mechanical, fluid, and electrical components</li> <li>Ability to read and understand equipment schematics and OEM manuals</li> <li>Experience in using probability and statistical tools and methods</li> <li>Demonstrates critical thinking and problem-solving skills</li> <li>Detail-oriented, organized, and able to demonstrate a high sense of urgency</li> <li>Experience working with CMMS programs such as Maximo, SAP, Infor, etc.</li> <li>Certified reliability engineer (CRE) or maintenance &amp; reliability professional (CMRP)</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Physical effort including standing, lifting, and carrying equipment up to 25 lbs. unassisted</li> <li>Available to work extended hours and weekends as needed</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, State. Learn more about the ITAR <a href="https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/?id=ddtc_kb_article_page&amp;sys_id=24d528fddbfc930044f9ff621f961987">here</a>. &nbsp;</li> </ul> <p>SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.</p> <p>Applicants wishing to view a copy of SpaceX’s Affirmative Action Plan for veterans and individuals with disabilities, or applicants requiring reasonable accommodation to the application/interview process should reach out to&nbsp;<a href="mailto:EEOCompliance@spacex.com">EEOCompliance@spacex.com</a><em>.&nbsp;</em></p></div>

title: Equipment Maintenance Technician (Starship)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Enabled by a constellation of low Earth orbit satellites, Starlink will provide fast, reliable internet to populations with little or no connectivity, including those in rural communities and places where existing services are too expensive or unreliable. We are looking for talented, creative, and driven technicians to drive manufacturing output and yield.&nbsp;</p> <p>As a semiconductor equipment maintenance technician, you will be responsible for the upkeep, preventative, and unscheduled maintenance of the production equipment for the custom silicon packaging team at Starlink. This is a versatile and highly skilled, hands on manufacturing job. The position will require extensive collaboration and critical thinking to troubleshoot unique equipment issues and develop quick solutions in a demanding environment. The ideal candidate is comfortable working in a fast-paced cleanroom setting, has a wide array of complementary skills, and is motivated by Starlink’s mission to provide high speed, low latency connectivity across the globe.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Perform preventative maintenance and unplanned (Andon) maintenance repairs of production line equipment that includes photolithography, die prep, grind and polish, AOI, reflow, die bonding, compression molding, convection and vacuum curing ovens, tape mount, microsaw and die singulation equipment, physical <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Degree in electronics technology, mechanical engineering, or related field</li> <li>6+ years of direct experience in semiconductor title: Equipment Reliability Engineer (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>EQUIPMENT RELIABILITY ENGINEER (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>At SpaceX we’re leveraging our experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation and is providing fast, reliable internet to 4M+ users worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system – thousands of satellites, consumer receivers that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing, and the software that brings it all together. We’ve only begun to scratch the surface of Starlink’s potential global impact and are looking for best-in-class engineers to help maximize Starlink’s utility for communities and businesses around the world.</p> <p>The primary role of the Equipment Reliability Engineer is to identify and manage asset reliability risks that could adversely affect factory or business operations. As production develops and increases rate, the Equipment Reliability Engineer's primary goal is to achieve maximum asset and system up-time by implementing and executing plans to minimize production losses, unpredictable asset behavior, and unusually high costs for system maintainability. In addition, the Equipment Reliability Engineer acts as the accountable engineering resource in driving the design, build, and installation stages of new and modified assets as well as provides technical support to maintenance management, technicians, and production personnel to prevent and mitigate operational issues of critical equipment.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul>
