Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>EQUIPMENT RELIABILITY ENGINEER (STARSHIP)</strong></p> <p>As Starship production continues to push new bounds in order to satisfy the growing demands of the space industry, the complex and ever-evolving critical equipment required to build, integrate, and test our products must work harder than ever. Equipment Reliability Engineers hold the keys to the production machine; they not only help identify some of the most risk-heavy SpaceX production assets, but they technically diagnose, advise, implement, and execute a strategic path forward at the equipment-level to promote system reliability, minimize losses, and maximize critical asset efficiencies.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Own equipment improvement plans for maintenance strategies and equipment availability to maximize production equipment availability</li> <li>Define, develop, and refine equipment reliability programs that include:</li> <ul> <li>Preventive maintenance tasks performed by machine operators and experienced maintenance technicians</li> <li>Comprehensive BOM development and selection of critical spare parts</li> <li>Integration of existing equipment into SpaceX Internet of Things (IoT) to enable real time performance monitoring</li> <li>Design and integration of new sensors onto machines to set predictive and condition-based monitoring triggers</li> <li>Iterative design improvements</li> </ul> <li>Develop engineering solutions to repetitive or high consequence failures on critical equipment through Root Cause Analysis (RCA)</li> <li>Conduct Failure Mode Effects and Criticality Analysis (FMECA) to create proactive reliability programs for critical equipment</li> <li>Coordinate cross-functionally to drive process improvements, design iterations and complete equipment overhauls</li> <li>Integrate with internal tooling, automation and production teams to ensure maintainability of design is incorporated into new internally designed equipment</li> <li>Develop and implement maintenance and reliability Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) to drive equipment improvements and organizational efficiency</li> <li>Support onboarding and commissioning of newly purchased or fabricated equipment; release reliability programs prior to equipment entering production</li> <li>Provide technical support to production, maintenance management and technical personnel</li> <li>Manage production requests for asset improvements and data collection</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in an engineering discipline</li> <li>1+ years of experience in manufacturing, reliability, or operations</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>5+ years of experience in a maintenance engineering role and reliability in a high-volume manufacturing, testing or operational environment</li> <li>Hands-on experience with equipment control systems, machinery, tooling and industrial automation</li> <li>Developed understanding of mechanical, fluid, and electrical component functions</li> <li>Experience using Microsoft SQL and PowerBI</li> <li>Ability to read and understand equipment schematics, P&amp;ID, GD&amp;T and OEM manuals</li> <li>Familiarity with aerospace manufacturing and test equipment; title: Equipment Reliability Engineer, PCB Maintenance (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>EQUIPMENT RELIABILITY ENGINEER, PCB MAINTENANCE (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>At SpaceX we’re leveraging our experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation and is providing fast, reliable internet to 10M+ users worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system – thousands of satellites, consumer receivers that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing, and the software that brings it all together. We’ve only begun to scratch the surface of Starlink’s potential global impact and are looking for best-in-class engineers to help maximize Starlink’s utility for communities and businesses around the world.</p> <p>The primary role of the Maintenance Engineer is to identify and manage asset reliability risks that could adversely affect factory or business operations. As production develops and increases rate, the Maintenance Engineer's primary goal is to achieve maximum asset and system up-time by implementing and executing plans to minimize production losses, unpredictable asset behavior, and unusually high costs for system maintainability. In addition, the Maintenance Engineer acts as the accountable engineering resource in driving the design, build, and installation stages of new and modified assets as well as provides technical support to maintenance management, technicians, and production personnel to prevent and mitigate operational issues of critical equipment.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Work with project engineering to ensure the reliability and sustainability of new and modified installations</li> <li>Guide efforts to ensure consistency and maintainability of critical equipment, processes, utilities, facilities, controls, and safety/security systems</li> <li>Own equipment improvement plans for more responsive and developed preventative maintenance strategies, equipment effectiveness, and minimization of production downtime</li> <li>Define, design, develop, monitor, and refine an asset maintenance plan that includes value-added preventive maintenance tasks, minimization of high-cost low-value repairs, effective utilization of predictive, and other non-destructive testing methodologies</li> <li>Prepare asset documentation package for review of system mechanical design, controls, and software</li> <li>Develop engineering solutions to repetitive failures and equipment-specific problems that adversely affect plant operations including capacity, quality, cost, or regulatory compliance issues</li> <li>Work with production to perform analyses of assets including asset utilization rate, overall equipment effectiveness, remaining useful life, operational restrictions, and other parameters that define the operating condition, reliability, and costs of assets</li> <li>Provide technical support to production, maintenance management, and technical personnel</li> <li>Manage production requests for asset improvement, control functions, and data collection</li> <li>Apply value analysis to repair/replace, repair/redesign, and make/buy decisions</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in mechanical, electrical, aerospace, systems, or manufacturing engineering</li> <li>1+ years of experience in an engineering role in manufacturing, integration, reliability, technical program management, and/or operations</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> title: Factory Software Engineer (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>FACTORY SOFTWARE ENGINEER (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation and is providing fast, reliable internet to millions of users worldwide. Users can get online within minutes almost anywhere on the world. We design, build, manufacture, and operate all parts of the system including thousands of satellites and millions of consumer kits. We’ve only begun to scratch the surface of Starlink’s potential. We are looking for best-in-class engineers to help maximize Starlink’s utility for individuals, communities, and businesses.</p> <p>As a Factory Software Engineer, you will be solving challenges such as:</p> <ul> <li>Writing software that runs both on our servers and products during the manufacturing process</li> <li>Creating infrastructure and tools for rapid and reliable deployment of new software to the factory with minimal downtime</li> <li>Debugging software and hardware issues to improve factory output</li> </ul> <p>Our software engineers are responsible for the complete lifecycle of the software they create, including development, testing, and support.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Work with the Starlink factory engineering teams to manufacture devices in-house</li> <li>Invent new tools that enable more frequent and reliable software deployment, test execution, and data analysis as part of a continuous integration and release system</li> <li>Design and implement highly available, fault-tolerant systems that operate for long periods of time with minimal intervention</li> <li>Develop systems that allow for test execution across multiple environments such as virtualized hardware or real hardware-in-the-loop simulations</li> <li>Bringup and maintain servers and networking for use in the factory</li> <li>Participate in architecture, design, and code reviews</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in computer science, engineering, math, or a STEM discipline; OR 2+ years of professional experience in software engineering in lieu of a degree (internship experience is applicable)</li> <li>Development experience in Python, Golang, C++, or Rust</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Solid fundamental knowledge of networking protocols (TCP/IP etc.), electronics, radio frequency</li> <li>Creative approach to problem solving, exceptional analytical skills and engineering fundamentals</li> <li>Strong skills in debugging, performance optimization, and testing</li> <li>Experience with security issues associated with distributed systems and internet services</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Must be willing to work extended hours and weekends as needed</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. title: Failure Analysis Engineer, Microelectronics (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>FAILURE ANALYSIS ENGINEER, MICROELECTRONICS (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>Starlink is SpaceX’s ambitious goal to bring high-quality internet to the globe by building a constellation of thousands of satellites in low Earth orbit (LEO) using our Falcon 9 and Starship reusable rockets. We are developing millions of devices for end users to link our customers to our satellites.</p> <p>As a Failure Analysis Engineer on the Starlink team, you will perform detailed root cause failure analysis on microelectronic components and packaging to support high-volume manufacturing, qualification, and field returns. You will leverage advanced laboratory tools and physics-of-failure techniques to identify failure mechanisms and drive corrective actions that improve the reliability of our satellite constellation and user terminals.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Own end-to-end root cause failure analysis investigations on microelectronics failing in manufacturing, test, and field, from initial failure characterization through final corrective action verification</li> <li>Conduct advanced electrical fault isolation and characterization using curve trace, TDR, RF characterization, Lock-in Thermography, OBIRCH, EBIRCH, EBAC, nanoprobing, and related techniques to precisely localize defects in complex devices</li> <li>Perform advanced physical failure analysis using SEM, FIB, EDS, SAM, cross-sectioning, and related techniques to identify failure mechanisms in silicon, packaging, and interconnects</li> <li>Apply physics-of-failure principles and deep knowledge of semiconductor failure modes (electromigration, thermal fatigue, delamination, EOS/ESD, solder joint fatigue, etc.) to determine root causes</li> <li>Drive corrective actions by working directly with silicon design, packaging, and manufacturing teams to implement and validate design or process changes based on FA findings</li> <li>Author detailed technical reports documenting failure modes, root cause conclusions, supporting data, and corrective action effectiveness</li> <li>Develop and improve failure analysis techniques and workflows to support new packaging technologies and advanced materials</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in materials science, electrical engineering, physics, chemical engineering, or other STEM discipline&nbsp;</li> <li>2+ years of hands-on experience in microelectronics failure analysis or materials characterization (internship experience is applicable)</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Master’s or PhD in materials science, electrical engineering, physics, chemical engineering, or other STEM discipline with a focus on microelectronics or failure analysis</li> <li>Direct experience with failure analysis tools and techniques (SEM, FIB, EDS, cross-sectioning, fault isolation, or equivalent)</li> <li>Strong understanding of semiconductor physics and common microelectronics failure mechanisms (electromigration, thermal fatigue, delamination, solder joint fatigue, electrical overstress/ESD, etc.)</li> <li>Proficiency with advanced FA tools including SEM, FIB, SAM, and EDS</li> <li>Hands-on experience in electrical characterization and fault isolation techniques such as IV curves, RF/VNA measurement, LIT, OBIRCH, EBIRCH, EBAC, nanoprobing, photon emission, or voltage contrast</li> <li>Experience applying JEDEC and AEC reliability test standards and physics-of-failure methodologies to root cause investigations</li> title: Fluids Engineer (Starship)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>FLUIDS ENGINEER (STARSHIP)</strong></p> <p>Starship is the largest and most capable space launch system ever developed. With the capability to deliver in excess of 100 metric tons to Earth’s orbit, it will fundamentally change access to space, and is the technology that will be used to establish a self-sustaining city on Mars. We will ultimately need thousands of Starships to accomplish that feat.</p> <p>The production fluids team develops (1) machinery used for flight-like validation of all vehicles prior to flight, and (2) all gas generation farms to produce and distribute manufacturing and test gasses throughout the production site! We are looking for enthusiastic and creative individuals to pave the future of Starship production testing &amp; automation. As a Fluids Engineer, you will be responsible for developing systems from the ground-up using multidisciplinary skills. Specifically, this involves taking a problem, breaking it down to its core fundamentals, and designing / building / deploying a solution in the form a production-grade automated fluids system. We are looking for exceptional and aspirational engineers ready to take on this challenge.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Design, build, and deploy automated / manual fluids systems to support high-rate production vehicle performance validation testing</li> <li>Design, build, and deploy simple data acquisition and control systems for control and monitoring</li> <li>Own full integration, validation, and handoff to production of each test system at each deployed production cell</li> <li>Perform detailed fluids analysis to characterize and troubleshoot expected design performance</li> <li>Work closely with our in-house build shop to develop and own the scaling of the manufacturing line for your system</li> <li>Support critical vehicle test campaigns &amp; operations, provide troubleshooting and technical support</li> <li>Develop and maintain detailed timelines to capture and communicate project progress</li> <li>Make high-value decisions on the fly, use feedback to continuously iterate and develop both product and process</li> <li>Support critical vehicle tests &amp; operations, provide troubleshooting and technical support</li> <li>Develop build, maintenance, and upgrade plans for new and existing equipment to maximize up-time</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in aerospace engineering, manufacturing engineering, mechanical engineering, or other technical discipline</li> <li>Hands-on project experience with mechanical/electrical systems</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>2+ years of manufacturing design experience</li> <li>2+ years of professional experience in the field of aerospace/mechanical/ process engineering</li> <li>2+ years of experience with GD&amp;T concepts</li> <li>2+ years of experience with industrial waste/wastewater/chemical processing</li> <li>2+ years of experience with oil and gas operations or processing</li> <li>Ability to work effectively in a team environment</li> <li>Experience with mechanical design, including basic structures calculations and design considerations</li> <li>Experience with Siemens NX and Teamcenter CAD</li> <li>Experience with fluid system design, build and test</li> <li>Electrical schematic design experience</li> <li>Hands-on experience building and commissioning high quality electrical control panels</li> <li>Experience in fast-paced iterative design and manufacturing environments</li> <li>Experience solving complex problems with little to no supervision on schedule as an individual or as a member of an integrated team</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Ability to perform job duties that require standing, kneeling, crouching, twisting upper body, working in cramped positions in small openings and climbing hand over hand</li> <li>Typically exposed to work in outdoor environments – heat, cold, rain</li> <li>Schedule varies depending on site operational needs; title: Full-Stack Data Scientist, Hardware Reliability (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>FULL-STACK DATA SCIENTIST, HARDWARE RELIABILITY (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is leveraging our experience building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s largest satellite constellation and most advanced broadband internet system. We provide reliable and fast internet to millions of users worldwide, including populations with little or no connectivity, rural communities, aircraft, watercraft, and places where existing services are unreliable, too expensive, or disconnected by natural disasters. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system, thousands of satellites and millions of consumer antennae that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing. The Starlink team is seeking out the best-in-class professionals to maximize Starlink’s potential for communities and businesses around the globe.</p> <p>As a Full-stack Data Scientist on the Starlink Reliability team, you will build the data pipelines, models, and production scoring systems that improve the reliability of Starlink customer hardware (dishes, routers, power supplies, cables). You will work from telemetry, manufacturing, inventory, field-return, and unstructured support data (tickets, chats, images) through production pipelines and deployed models, put scores into the workflows that drive replacements and support decisions, and build LLM-backed tools — retrieval, tool calling, and agentic workflows — that engineers and operators run. You will measure whether those systems reduce failures as we launch new products and scale the network. title: Global Supply Manager, Capital Equipment & Construction (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><div> <p><strong>GLOBAL SUPPLY MANAGER, CAPITAL EQUIPMENT &amp; CONSTRUCTION (STARLINK)</strong></p> </div> <div> <p>SpaceX is on a fast track to become the market leader in various product categories like US based human spaceflight, rapid vehicle reusability, internet services through the Starlink constellation and others exciting projects. The SpaceX Supply Chain Department is a critical player in our operations. To capitalize on SpaceX’s technological and market changing successes, our team will be part of managing an agile yet robust supply chain that will enable a competitive advantage for the company. The functions within the department include procurement, planning and fulfillment, supplier development and quality, logistics and inventory. SpaceX Supply Chain will play a key role in enabling SpaceX to meet these ambitious growth targets and greatly contribute in making us a multi-planetary species.&nbsp;This individual will support construction projects and capital purchases for the construction and facilities organizations.</p> </div> <div> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> </div> <div> <ul> <li>Work directly with key internal stakeholders to develop and implement a comprehensive contract management process that ensures a successful project execution cycle</li> <li>Create sourcing strategies for assigned categories to reduce risk and meet targets for the purchasing department including, but not limited to, payment terms, cash targets, and cost savings</li> <li>Develop and maintain key internal stakeholder relationships to create strategic sourcing models that optimize the value of products and services that support business unit requirements to maintain continuous cost reduction programs for controllable expenditures</li> <li>Identify and execute cost reduction projects including planning, coordinating with stakeholders, estimating completion, and project updates</li> <li>Perform advanced quantitative and business process analyses to identify financial impacts of decisions, cost improvement, and performance for assigned categories</li> <li>Collaborate with stakeholders to define SLAs and KPIs for suppliers and measure the appropriate criteria such as delivery of business results, cost reduction, quality, and timeliness of delivery</li> <li>Conduct research, perform benchmarking, and gather market analysis for assigned categories</li> <li>Create contract documents in collaboration with the legal department</li> <li>Manage contracts to ensure the supplier's performance&nbsp;meets contract obligations</li> <li>Understand interrelationships between contracts and terms while applying creative solutions</li> <li>Maximize value and cost savings benefits while lowering risk through strategic negotiations</li> <li>Identify and drive year over year cost optimization through reducing usage and eliminating waste within our operations</li> <li>Establish preferred suppliers for assigned categories</li> <li>Create and implement management programs to develop, continuously improve, manage the performance of, and monitor KPIs of the supply base</li> <li>Place purchase orders and resolve blocked invoices related to assigned categories</li> <li>Develop and lead efforts to reduce number of transactions and for assigned categories</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> </div> <ul type="disc"> <li>Bachelor’s degree and 6+ years of experience working in one or more of the following; OR 10+ years of experience working in one or more of the following:</li> <ul type="circle"> <li>Engineering</li> <li>Purchasing</li> <li>Contract negotiation</li> <li>Material or production planning</li> <li>Operations or supply chain management</li> <li>Master production scheduling</li> <li>Construction, facilities, or industrial plant management</li> </ul> </ul> <div> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> </div> <div> <ul> <li>Strong technical background to speak the language of engineers and strong business background to deal with contracts and negotiations</li> <li>Construction project management experience and/or construction cost estimate experience</li> <li>Familiarity or experience in purchasing or similar procurement related experience</li> <li>Experience in industrial engineering, construction management, and/or facilities management</li> <li>Strong budget tracking and cost analytical skills</li> <li>Extensive project management and organizational skills</li> <li>Experience managing large scale industrial and commercial construction projects</li> <li>Strong contract negotiation and document management skills</li> <li>Remarkable problem-solving skills with a bias for speed</li> <li>Quick learner and ability to prioritize appropriately to meet customer and company needs</li> <li>Excellent customer service skills</li> <li>Effective written, verbal, and presentation communication skills</li> <li>Exceptional analytical and organizational skills</li> <li>Strong technical knowledge and skills in current technologies and applications (e.g. MS Office Suite, SQL, PowerBI, etc.)</li> <li>Ability to conduct all activities with the highest degree of integrity</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Ability to work extended hours and title: Global Supply Manager, Capital Equipment, Wastewater (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong data-olk-copy-source="MailCompose">GLOBAL SUPPLY MANAGER, CAPITAL EQUIPMENT, WASTEWATER (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>At SpaceX we’re leveraging our experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation and is providing fast, reliable internet to millions of users worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system – thousands of satellites, consumer receivers that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing, and the software that brings it all together. We’ve only begun to scratch the surface of Starlink’s potential global impact and are looking for best-in-class engineers to help maximize Starlink’s utility for communities and businesses around the world.</p> <p>This role will support the design, construction, commissioning, and operation of large-scale, state-of-the-art Ultrapure Water (UPW) and wastewater treatment plants that enable our high-volume manufacturing operations (including one of the largest PCB manufacturing lines in North America and major solar cell manufacturing facilities). You will work closely with the wastewater engineering team and construction/facilities stakeholders to drive capital equipment procurement and construction services for complex industrial water treatment systems, including Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) facilities.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Work directly with key internal stakeholders (wastewater engineering, construction, facilities, and operations) to develop and implement a comprehensive contract management process that ensures successful project execution for CAPEX and construction of wastewater and UPW systems</li> <li>Develop and execute equipment &amp; services procurement strategies focused on wastewater treatment plants, ultrapure water systems, and associated construction projects</li> <li>Perform market analysis to determine should-costs and achieve the best purchasing deals for specialized equipment (e.g., membrane systems, RO, EDI/IX, evaporators, crystallizers, chemical systems, solids handling) and construction services</li> <li>Own end-to-end sourcing strategy and performance for major utility water systems, including:</li> <ul> <li>Industrial water systems (raw water intake/treatment, process water, ultrapure/deionized water generation, cooling tower operations, and closed-loop hydronic systems)</li> <li>Wastewater collection, treatment, and discharge (industrial wastewater, process effluent, deluge water treatment, stormwater management, and compliance with environmental permits)</li> </ul> <li>Define and implement long-term sourcing strategies to ensure reliable water supply, capacity, and cost-effective availability of raw water, process water, and treatment systems</li> <li>Create and negotiate contract documents in collaboration with the legal department for capital equipment, EPC contractors, and construction services</li> <li>Track and report projected and actual spend, assess budgetary risk, and provide clear budgetary analysis to enable timely management decision-making on multi-million dollar wastewater CAPEX projects</li> <li>Manage vendor and contractor relationships, ensuring clear communication, adherence to contracts, and resolution of performance or delivery issues</li> <li>Present value propositions to SpaceX management related to contract awards, cost reviews, cost reduction strategies, and critical supply issues for wastewater infrastructure</li> <li>Identify and execute cost reduction projects including planning, coordinating with stakeholders, estimating completion, and providing project updates</li> <li>Perform advanced quantitative and business process analyses to identify financial impacts of decisions, cost improvement opportunities, and performance for assigned wastewater and construction categories</li> <li>Create and implement supplier management programs to develop, continuously improve, manage performance of, and monitor KPIs of the supply base supporting wastewater treatment and construction</li> <li>Lead and execute Requests for Proposals (RFPs) for capital equipment, construction packages, and specialized wastewater treatment systems</li> <li>Place purchase orders and resolve blocked invoices related to assigned categories</li> <li>Develop and lead efforts to reduce the number of transactions while maintaining control and compliance</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree and 5+ years of experience working in one or more of the following; OR 9+ years of experience working in one or more of the following in lieu of a degree:</li> <ul> <li>Purchasing/Procurement</li> <li>Engineering (chemical, environmental, or mechanical)</li> <li>Contract negotiation</li> <li>Operations or supply chain management</li> <li>Construction, facilities, or industrial plant management</li> <li>Wastewater treatment, water treatment, or industrial process systems</li> </ul> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Strong technical background to speak the language of engineers combined with strong business acumen for contracts and negotiations</li> <li>Experience with capital equipment procurement and/or construction project management for industrial water treatment, wastewater, or ultrapure water systems</li> <li>Knowledge of advanced wastewater treatment technologies (e.g., chemical precipitation, membrane filtration (TMF/UF/RO), EDI/IX, advanced oxidation, ZLD systems including evaporators and crystallizers)</li> <li>Construction project management experience and/or construction cost estimating experience, preferably on industrial or manufacturing facilities</li> <li>Experience managing large-scale industrial construction or CAPEX projects</li> <li>Strong budget tracking, cost analytical, and financial analysis skills</li> <li>Extensive project management and organizational skills</li> <li>Strong contract negotiation and document management skills</li> <li>Experience working with EPC contractors and multidisciplinary engineering teams</li> <li>Remarkable problem-solving skills with a bias for speed</li> <li>Quick learner with the ability to prioritize appropriately to meet customer and company needs</li> <li>Excellent customer service, written, verbal, and presentation communication skills</li> <li>Exceptional analytical and organizational skills</li> <li>Strong technical knowledge and skills in current tools (e.g., MS office suite, SQL, PowerBI, etc.)</li> <li>Ability to conduct all activities with the highest degree of integrity</li> <li>Detail-oriented, self-motivated, and able to respond quickly in a fast-moving and ever-changing environment</li> <li>Familiarity with environmental regulations and permitting related to industrial wastewater (EPA, NPDES, etc.) is a plus</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Ability to travel and communicate outside of work hours – up to 20% work week travel may be required, including international travel</li> <li>Willingness to work long hours and weekends when needed to meet critical deadlines</li> <li>This position is based in Bastrop, TX and requires being onsite</li> <li>Ability to work in industrial environments (as needed for site visits)</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> title: Global Supply Manager, Semiconductor Electronic Components (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong><span data-olk-copy-source="MessageBody">GLOBAL SUPPLY MANAGER, SEMICONDUCTOR ELECTRONIC COMPONENTS (STARLINK)</span></strong>&nbsp;</p> <p>We are seeking an experienced Global Supply Manager to own end-to-end sourcing strategy, supplier management, and delivery of leading-edge semiconductor components. In this role, you will partner directly with design engineering, to define commodity strategy, build multi-year technology roadmaps, establish and maintain the approved vendor list, and secure massive-scale supply at the record-breaking build speeds the SpaceXAI team is driving. You will negotiate transformative, high-value agreements, accelerate delivery timelines, actively manage inventory across the supply chain, and continuously optimize for cost, quality, speed, and supply chain resilience in one of the most competitive and dynamic AI infrastructure programs on the planet. The ideal candidate is a strategic leader who thrives in ambiguous, high-velocity environments, possesses exceptional commercial and technical acumen, and has a proven track record of delivering excellent results.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong>&nbsp;</p> <ul type="disc"> <li>Work directly with key internal stakeholders to develop/implement sourcing and cost management strategies; owning the semiconductor commodity</li> <li>Understand the technical aspects of electronic components to identify opportunities for design selection, cost, and reliability</li> <li>Own vendor management and negotiations to meet new product introduction (NPI) schedules</li> <li>Create and own supply strategy to ensure production clear to build readiness and supply risk mitigation</li> <li>Develop and manage supply base (domestic and international) for electronic components</li> <li>Work directly with key suppliers to develop and implement sourcing and cost management strategies that support existing platforms and new product development</li> <li>Evaluate demand while placing and managing purchase orders according to demand signals</li> <li>Track delivery and supplier delivery performance</li> <li>Provide guidance to internal engineering customers on recommended suppliers to use</li> <li>Act as the supplier interface for all RFIs, RFPs, and RFQs</li> <li>Monitor global industry trends, track technology roadmaps, and actively partner with the design teams to identify and mitigate supply and demand challenges</li> <li>Partner with internal resources to drive adoption of low-cost parts and avoidance of obsolescence</li> <li>Visit supplier facilities and accurately assess operational capability, financial health, and capacity to award contracts in support of new product development and long-term production</li> <li>Conduct comprehensive supplier analysis, including strategic direction, capacity, market and industry position, and risk assessment</li> <li>Manage costs to ensure alignment with program budget</li> <li>Present value propositions to executives, including those related to contract award, cost reviews, cost reduction strategies, and critical supply issues</li> <li>Work with supply chain engineers to develop requirements for both NPI and production phases</li> <li>Negotiate contracts to ensure continuity of supply and protect SpaceX interests</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong>&nbsp;</p> <ul type="disc"> <li>Bachelor’s degree and 6+ years of experience working in one or more of the following; or 10+ years of experience working in one or more of the following:&nbsp;</li> <ul type="circle"> <li>Engineering&nbsp;</li> <li>Purchasing&nbsp;</li> <li>Contract negotiation&nbsp;</li> <li>Material or production planning&nbsp;</li> <li>Operations or supply chain management&nbsp;</li> <li>Material cost control&nbsp;</li> <li>Master production scheduling&nbsp;</li> </ul> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong>&nbsp;</p> <ul type="disc"> <li>Technical procurement or planning experience with electronic components, PCBs, or PCBAs</li> <li>Experience in new product introduction (NPI) and mass production (MP)</li> <li>Experience reading technical drawings, data sheets, fabrication drawing, BOMs and all related files</li> <li>Drive piece price and tooling negotiation process to ensure that SpaceX’s commodity pricing meet best-in-class expectations, while meeting best-in-class quality, in addition to driving continual cost reduction and avoidance initiatives through ad-hoc price negotiations</li> <li>Address all areas of category management including category business plans, market conditions, technology roadmaps, cost modeling, and sourcing strategies</li> <li>Proven track record of taking ownership, successfully negotiating preferred pricing and driving results</li> <li>Detail-oriented, self-motivated, and able to respond quickly in a fast-moving and ever-changing environment</li> <li>Exceptional analytical, problem solving, and organizational skills</li> <li>Effective written, verbal, and presentation communication skills</li> <li>Conduct all activities with title: GNC Engineer - Embedded Controls, AI Satellites (Starmind)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>GNC ENGINEER - EMBEDDED CONTROLS, AI SATELLITES (STARMIND)</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is leveraging its experience deploying and operating the world’s largest satellite constellation to develop Starmind, a new constellation of satellites capturing solar energy in space to power low-cost, high-performance AI compute for Earth.</p> <p>The Starmind team is developing key technologies to power this satellite – massive solar power generation systems, active cooling, propulsion, and the highly reliable software stack that enables our vehicles to accomplish their mission safely and autonomously.</p> <p>As an Embedded Controls Engineer on the Starmind Guidance, Navigation, and Control team (GNC) team, you will apply a strong expertise in dynamics and closed loop controls to achieve robust and precise pointing on satellites, payloads, propulsion systems, and mechanisms. This is not just an analysis role – you will be responsible for vehicle design trades, simulation, flight software implementation, and ultimately deploying and operating your features in space.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Design, analysis, implementation of electromechanical control systems such as solar array actuators, antenna gimbals, and high bandwidth active optics.</li> <li>Design, analysis, implementation of satellite attitude control and momentum management systems.</li> <li>Design, analysis, implementation of fluid and power system controls for the Starlink hall thrusters.</li> <li>Optimal state estimation as applied to mechanical alignment and attitude determination.</li> <li>Hardware performance specification and sizing, support for hardware iteration and firmware bringup, design qualification, automated production screening, and performance monitoring in the fleet.</li> <li>Development and maintenance of high fidelity simulations using C++, python, matlab, integration of those simulations into collaborative analysis tools.</li> <li>Implementation, validation, unit testing, and deployment of production software (C++) pertinent to the systems described above.</li> <li>Provide engineering and data review support for hardware development, network level performance monitoring.</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in aerospace, physics or an engineering discipline.</li> <li>Software development experience in C++.</li> <li>Experience with design and analysis of closed loop control systems.</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Master's degree or PhD in physics or an engineering discipline.</li> <li>Very strong expertise and demonstrated project or professional experience in linear closed loop controls analysis and design, including state space and frequency domain methods.</li> <li>Experience with flexible body dynamics and reduced finite element models thereof in the context of closed loop control systems analysis.</li> <li>Expertise in state estimation, kalman filters, information filters, etc.</li> <li>Strong expertise in embedded C++, ideally in the context of electromechanical control systems firmware.</li> <li>Strong understanding of classical rigid body dynamics, orbital mechanics, modeling and simulation thereof.</li> <li>Direct experience with spacecraft operations and flight software development, testing, and deployment.</li> <li>Capable of identifying and solving complex problems in a self-directed manner.</li> <li>Passion for advancing the commercial space industry.</li> <li>Ability to work in a fast paced, autonomously driven, and demanding start-up atmosphere.</li> <li>Excellent communication skills both written and verbal.</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Must be willing to work extended hours and weekends as needed.</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>GNC ENGINEER (STARSHIP)</strong></p> <p>As a GNC Engineer, you will be responsible for pushing the technical boundaries of flight control systems for the world’s most advanced rockets, including our next-generation Starship vehicle, a fully reusable spacecraft capable of carrying humans to the Moon, Mars and beyond. You will work with a talented team of accomplished engineers to develop, analyze, and test vehicles and subsystems for highly reliable flight. You should thrive in fast-paced, dynamic environments where you adapt quickly and love to solve hard problems.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Develop innovative guidance, navigation, and control systems for Starship</li> <li>Engage in multi-disciplinary vehicle systems investigations and design work that define the systems architecture</li> <li>Implement new software or algorithms to enable mission unique capabilities and leading edge launch vehicle performance</li> <li>Develop 6-DOF dynamics simulation models used for GNC systems analysis and validation</li> <li>Analyze launch vehicle trajectories, performance dispersions, and flight stability</li> <li>Conduct post flight data review and correlation with analyses for continued improvement of predictions</li> <li>Support launch and mission operations of vehicles that you enabled</li> <li>Perform testing of GNC software utilizing hardware-in-the-loop testing, Monte Carlo analysis, and algorithm unit testing</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in physics or an engineering discipline</li> <li>Experience with control systems, orbital mechanics, classical dynamics, modeling, and simulation</li> <li>Experience with the software languages Python or C++</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Postgraduate degree in physics or an engineering discipline</li> <li>2+ years of professional experience in control systems, orbital mechanics, classical dynamics, aerodynamics, sensors and actuators, modeling and simulation, and the software languages C++ and Python</li> <li>Demonstrated project or professional experience in launch vehicle and/or spacecraft system</li> <li>Capable of solving complex problems with little to no supervision on schedule as an individual or as a member of an integrated team</li> <li>Passion for advancing the commercial space industry and human spaceflight</li> <li>Excellent communication skills both written and verbal</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Must be willing to work extended hours and/or weekends title: Hardware Development Engineer, Gateway Failure Analysis (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>HARDWARE DEVELOPMENT ENGINEER, GATEWAY FAILURE ANALYSIS (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is leveraging its experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation that provides fast, reliable internet to millions of users worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system – thousands of satellites, consumer receivers that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing, hundreds of gateway ground stations, and the software that brings it all together. We’ve only begun to scratch the surface of Starlink’s potential global impact. As we continue to upgrade and expand the constellation, we’re looking for best-in-class engineers to join the team.</p> <p>As a Hardware Development Engineer on Starlink, you’ll contribute to the design, build, and test electronics for the world's largest network of ground stations, which function as an intermediary between the satellites and our end-users to ensure smooth data transfer and transmission. You will sit at the intersection of electrical, mechanical, thermal analysis, software, and antenna engineering - ultimately ensuring that our ground antenna hardware can withstand the harshest environmental conditions while maintaining reliable communication with millions of users on a global scale. This is an opportunity to work on cutting edge R&amp;D technology, and some of the most complex applications of electrical and mechanical engineering in the industry.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Design, develop, and execute novel environmental, RF, mechanical, and electrical test solutions for our ground antenna electronics and payload</li> <li>Perform detailed failure analysis of ground antenna hardware, identifying root causes of failures and implementing corrective actions</li> <li>Select commercial-off-the-shelf hardware and/or design custom PCBAs to measure signals, apply flight-like loads, and power units under test</li> <li>Hands-on support of hardware through design qualification, production ramp, and ground network rollout</li> <li>Work closely with engineers from adjacent disciplines (mechanical, thermal, software, test engineering, supply chain, silicon design) to deliver tightly integrated, high-performance hardware</li> <li>Perform electrical bench testing of failures to replicate and inform mitigation of anomalies</li> <li>Drive continual improvements to our designs by building physical and digital tools to analyze data collected both in the field and in the lab</li> <li>Challenge assumptions and work to find simple solutions to complex problems</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, physics, or other STEM discipline</li> <li>1+ years of experience in hardware development, failure analysis, or reliability engineering (internships and co-ops acceptable)</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Master’s degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, physics, or other STEM discipline</li> <li>Experience with both electronics and mechanical design and analysis including knowledge of RF principles</li> <li>Experience analyzing circuits and PCBAs, and developing functional test plans</li> <li>Experience with test equipment and measurement techniques to verify and validate product requirements (oscilloscope, multimeter, electronic load, spectrum analyzer, network analyzer, vector signal generator, source measurement unit, etc.)</li> <li>Experience in environmental testing such as HALT/HASS, thermal, humidity, shock &amp; vibration</li> <li>Strong understanding of computers and programming languages (Python, C/C++)</li> <li>Thorough understanding of electronics reliability, manufacturing, and failure mechanisms</li> <li>Knowledge of quality tools such as Lean principles, Six Sigma, and root cause analysis methods</li> <li>Thorough understanding of metrology, sources of measurement error, and uncertainty analysis</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Ability to work extended hours or weekends as needed for mission critical deadlines</li> <li>Occasional travel to ground network sites to support root cause investigations</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, title: Hardware Engineer, Gateways & Customer Hardware (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>HARDWARE ENGINEER, GATEWAYS &amp; CUSTOMER HARDWARE (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>Starlink believes in providing fast, reliable internet to serve populations with little or no connectivity. We design, build, launch, and operate the world's largest constellation of satellites, enabling us to operate a global internet network unbounded by traditional ground infrastructure limitations. Starlink also designs, builds, and delivers high-volume consumer hardware that allows users to connect to these satellites within minutes of unboxing, as well as our advanced gateways that we deploy regionally throughout the world. The root of SpaceX’s success so far lies in our mission to keep all engineering and production in-house, which enables a tight feedback loop, nimble decision-making, and speedy deliverables. With millions of daily users worldwide already online, Starlink is truly a game-changer and levels the playing field for those who were previously unconnected.</p> <p>As an Hardware Engineer on the Starlink team, you will have complete ownership over the development of millions of customer-facing products and devices that we ship directly to end users (Starlink dishes/user terminals, Wi-Fi routers, etc.). Our customers currently include teachers in the most remote parts of the Amazon, researchers in Antarctica, digital nomads who travel via RV, emergency responders, commercial airlines, cruise lines, and residential users who live in more rural or developing areas. You will be responsible for the design, implementation, and verification of the entire electrical system for these products. You could also be responsible for the design and performance of next-generation gateways - ultimately ensuring that our ground station antenna hardware can withstand the harshest environmental conditions while maintaining reliable communication with millions of users on a global scale. You will interact regularly with partner teams including silicon, software, mechanical, and manufacturing engineering to steer this hardware from initial concept development to full-scale production.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Design, develop, and test highly reliable electronics for communicating with our satellites</li> <li>Partner with software, mechanical, thermal, manufacturing, and production test teams</li> <li>Drive system trades, requirements capture, component selection, analysis, schematic capture, PCB layout, prototyping, hardware bring-up, debugging, documentation, manufacturing, and test of complex electrical designs</li> <li>Get hands-on and support hardware through production, satellite integration, and flight</li> <li>Work closely with engineers from adjacent disciplines (mechanical, thermal, software, test engineering, supply chain, silicon design, etc.) to deliver tightly integrated, high-performance hardware</li> <li>Drive continual improvements to our designs by building physical and digital tools to analyze data collected on orbit and in the lab</li> <li>Challenge assumptions and work to find simple solutions to complex problems</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering or other engineering discipline</li> <li>1+ years of professional experience designing circuits, electronic products, or hardware</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Master’s degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, or similar engineering degree</li> <li>2+ years of professional experience rapidly designing and delivering highly reliable products</li> <li>2+ years of electronic product experience designing hardware from concept through production; strong emphasis on full life cycle development of new hardware products and not small incremental updates to legacy hardware</li> <li>2+ years of experience designing and implementing mixed-signal circuit boards from concept through production using processors, FPGAs, Ethernet, multi-GHz Serdes, DRAM interfaces (DDR4), I2C, SPI, operational amplifiers, analog to digital and digital to analog converters, and power supply components</li> <li>2+ years of professional experience testing, troubleshooting, and debugging electronics</li> <li>Strong understanding of computers and programming languages (Python, C/C++)</li> <li>Demonstrated ability to work in a highly cross-functional role</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Ability to work extended hours or weekends as needed for mission critical deadlines</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. title: Hardware Reliability Specialist (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong><span data-contrast="auto">HARDWARE RELIABILITY SPECIALIST (STARLINK)</span></strong></p> <p><span data-contrast="auto">SpaceX is leveraging our experience building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s largest satellite constellation and most advanced broadband internet system. We provide reliable and fast internet to millions of users worldwide, including populations with little or no connectivity, rural communities, aircraft, watercraft, and places where existing services are unreliable, too expensive, or disconnected by natural disasters. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system: thousands of satellites and consumer antennae that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing. The Starlink team is seeking out the best-in-class professionals to maximize Starlink’s potential for communities and businesses around the globe. </span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></p> <p><span data-contrast="auto">The success of Starlink depends on the quality, reliability, cost, manufacturability, throughput, and security of the products that you deliver. If you seek a fast-paced, dynamic environment; if you thrive on solving difficult problems where resolutions have high impact; and if you love the challenge of building something from scratch, then this role will be an ideal next career step. We’ve only begun to scratch the surface of Starlink’s potential global impact and are looking for best-in-class engineers to help maximize Starlink’s utility for communities and businesses around the world.</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></p> <p><span data-contrast="auto">This position will primarily support manufacturing and development of SpaceX’s Starlink product components alongside a strong group of manufacturing and process engineers. title: Instrumentation & Controls Technician
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>INSTRUMENTATION &amp; CONTROLS TECHNICIAN</strong></p> <p>The instrumentation &amp; controls technician will support the build-up and maintenance of our data and control systems. These systems consist of varying data acquisition and control hardware, wiring and interface harnesses, and a wide variety of instrumentation. The goal of this team is to meet a variety of test requirements to achieve safe, economical, and reliable access to space.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Maintain, calibrate, configure, monitor, test, troubleshoot, install, and repair instrumentation, process controls, data acquisition systems, and electrical systems</li> <li>Investigate, diagnose, correct, and document instrumentation or system malfunctions</li> <li>Lay out, build, test, troubleshoot, repair, and modify developmental and production electrical and electronic units, assemblies, components, parts, equipment, and systems.</li> <li>Perform wire terminations to a variety of instruments and verify sensor health: pressure transducers, thermocouples, valves, limits, and flow meters</li> <li>Adjust, calibrate, align, and modify circuitry and components, and record effects on unit performance</li> <li>Read and interpret planning documents, schematics, wiring diagrams, specifications, drawings, manuals, blueprints, and engineering sketches</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>High school diploma or equivalency certificate</li> <li>2+ years of experience working with instrumentation such as pressure transducers, thermocouples, valves, flow meters, multimeters, or oscilloscopes</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Experience working with any of the following instrumentation: resistance temperature devices (RTDs), silicon diode temperature devices, strain gauges, load cells, displacement transducers, pressure transducers, thermocouples, and flow meters (turbine, coriolis, and ultrasonic)</li> <li>IPC 620 spec for harness assembly&nbsp;</li> <li>Basic knowledge of Wheatstone Bridge Theory, ability to apply Ohm's Law, and an understanding of DC electronics</li> <li>Operational knowledge of an oscilloscope and multi-meter, soldering wires and connectors, operation of various crimping tools, wire stripping, continuity testing, pinning out a military type connector, routing and tie wrapping cables, drilling and tapping holes, and building junction boxes</li> <li>System-level troubleshooting skills and the ability to logically solve instrumentation system problems and determine corrective action</li> <li>Experience with Variable Frequency Drives and motor starters, and knowledge in troubleshooting</li> <li>Knowledge in signal conditioning concepts for various types of sensors, to include the following: thermocouple Types K, S, and E; TC bonding concepts: resistance weld on and adhesive bond on types; TC probes through thermowell sheaths; cold junction compensation concepts</li> <li>Background should include experience with the following devices: DC power supplies, DC-DC convertors, UPS installations, heat shrink tubing, cable harnessing, lacing, and proper strain relief concepts</li> <li>Working knowledge of transducers, operational amplifiers, and the knowledge of measurement techniques for temperature, pressure, flow, displacement, vibration, and the application of strain gauges are also highly desired. title: Instrumentation & Controls Technician, Solar Cells (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>INSTRUMENTATION &amp; CONTROLS TECHNICIAN, SOLAR CELLS (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>At SpaceX, we are building the next generation of space infrastructure to enable large-scale AI data centers in orbit. These orbital AI platforms require massive amounts of reliable, high-efficiency solar power, and we are standing up one of the largest solar cell manufacturing facilities in the world. The Instrumentation &amp; Controls Technician will provide hands-on support for the integration, commissioning, troubleshooting, and maintenance of automation and controls systems on our advanced solar cell production lines.</p> <p>This role focuses on safe, structured execution of repairs and recoveries that maximize uptime, wiring and building industrial control panels, supporting PLC/HMI/SCADA systems, and ensuring reliable operation of electromechanical, robotic, sensor, motion, and process-critical equipment while collaborating closely with Specialists and Engineers.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Support integration and commissioning of vendor/OEM equipment into centralized SCADA software (Ignition) and production line controls</li> <li>Perform safe controls and electrical work within LOTO, arc-flash, guarding, interlock, robot/AGV, bypass-control, and restart-verification requirements; identify hazards, verify zero energy, validate safety devices after repair, and escalate unsafe conditions or unauthorized changes</li> <li>Maximize uptime of automation assets through hands-on troubleshooting, basic repairs, and corrective actions on electromechanical, robotic, pneumatic, and control systems</li> <li>Wire, commission, validate, build, and maintain industrial control panels and field devices to NFPA 79 &amp; UL 508A standards; replace like-for-like components (power supplies, relays, fuses, terminal blocks, sensors, etc.), restore wiring condition, and create accurate redlines</li> <li>Navigate and diagnose PLCs, HMIs, alarms, permissives, sequences, I/O status, recipes, and logic behavior; clear approved alarms, perform basic recovery, capture evidence (screenshots, codes, states), and support minor authorized parameter/recipe adjustments with documentation</li> <li>Set up, diagnose, replace, and validate sensors, instrumentation, vision, barcode/RFID, encoders, IO-Link devices, and industrial networks; verify signals, alignment, scaling, and network health</li> <li>Support controls for VFDs, servo systems, motion axes, robots, conveyors, AGV/AMR interfaces, and controlled movement; perform documented resets, homing, recovery, and safe dry-cycle checks</li> <li>Provide controls support for process-critical solar cell equipment (e.g., deposition, chemical processing, printing, firing, testing, material transfer) and facilities/utility interfaces; protect product quality, recipe state, contamination control, and process stability during recovery</li> <li>Perform structured fault finding, root-cause support, and rapid corrective actions to minimize downtime on solar cell manufacturing equipment</li> <li>Collaborate with engineers, Instrumentation &amp; Controls Specialists, production, and maintenance teams to deliver safe, reliable solutions and continuous improvement</li> <li>Maintain accurate documentation, work tickets, and records; support 5S principles, inventory control, and a clean, organized workspace</li> <li>Ensure all work complies with safety protocols, cleanroom standards (as applicable), lock-out/tag-out, and regulatory requirements in a high-volume manufacturing environment</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>High school diploma or equivalency certificate</li> <li>2+ years of experience in a manufacturing and production environment with mechanical, electrical, pneumatic, or hydraulic systems; OR bachelor's degree in an engineering, math, or science discipline</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Strong working knowledge of NFPA 70 (National Electrical Code), NFPA 70E (Standard for Electrical Safety), NFPA 79, and UL 508A codes</li> <li>Demonstrated hands-on skill in fault finding, structured troubleshooting, electrical panel work, multimeter use, schematic reading, and problem resolution</li> <li>Ability to read, interpret, and redline electrical, hydraulic, and pneumatic schematics and drawings</li> <li>PLC and HMI experience or familiarization with Beckhoff TwinCAT, Siemens TIA Portal, and/or Allen-Bradley RSLogix/Studio 5000; ability to navigate alarms, I/O status, sequences, and basic diagnostics</li> <li>Experience with electrical control panel design, building, and wiring; sensors and instrumentation (photoeyes, proximity, pressure, vacuum, temperature, flow, encoders, vision, barcode/RFID, IO-Link)</li> <li>Experience with SCADA systems (Ignition preferred), sensors, actuators, servo drives, interlocks, production support devices, VFDs, robots, conveyors, AGVs/AMRs, and industrial networks</li> <li>Familiarity with process-critical controls, recipes, facilities/utility interfaces, hazardous gas/chemicals, cleanroom protocols, and product-protection practices</li> <li>Excellent skills in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint); detail-oriented with strong organizational, documentation, and communication skills</li> <li>Creative problem-solver with a high sense of urgency, ability to work independently or as part of a team, and flexibility in a fast-paced, high-stress production setting</li> <li>Experience with 5S, lean principles, CMMS/work ticket systems, and continuous improvement for uptime and reliability</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Must be willing to work overtime and/or weekends as needed</li> <li>Must be able to lift up to 25 lbs. unassisted</li> <li>Must be able to walk and stand for long periods of time</li> <li>Must be comfortable working in a production environment with extensive use of hazardous chemicals such as acids, alkalis, and solvents</li> <li>Must be able to wear appropriate PPE for lab and electro-chemical manufacturing environment</li> <li>Must be comfortable with climbing up and down ladders, grasping, standing, lifting, bending, pulling, pushing, stooping, stretching, carrying, crawling, and maneuvering in tight spaces</li> <li>Must be willing to train on 1st shift from 6:00 AM – 4:30 PM for initial 30 days</li> <li>Must be willing to work one or more of the following schedules:</li> <ul> <li>A-Shift: 5:00 AM - 5:00 PM (Sunday - Tuesday and every other Wednesday)</li> <li>B-Shift: 5:00 AM - 5:00 PM (Thursday - Saturday and every other Wednesday)</li> <li>C-Shift: 5:00 PM - 5:00 AM (Sunday - Tuesday and every other Wednesday)</li> <li>D-Shift: 5:00 PM - 5:00 AM (Thursday - Saturday and every other Wednesday)</li> </ul> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. title: Instrumentation & Controls Technician, Water Treatment (Starlink)

You will be the technical backbone of our critical water infrastructure, ensuring the reliability of Ultra-Pure Water (UPW), Industrial Wastewater (IWW), and Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) systems that support our manufacturing and testing operations.</p> <p>This is not a role for someone who prefers to sit at a desk. You will take ownership of the "eyes and ears" of our water systems, ensuring uptime for critical production lines and safety for the rest of the operations team.</p> title: Intelligence Analyst
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>INTELLIGENCE ANALYST</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is seeking a dynamic and driven individual with a demonstrated ability to work independently and as a member of a team in a fast-paced, high-tech environment. Our goal is to protect some of the world’s most advanced technologies, including rockets, Dragon capsules for human transport, inter-planetary transport vehicles, the world's largest satellite communications network, etc. As an industry leader, we attract foreign and domestic adversaries intent on impeding our progress and stealing our technology. The work we do will safeguard mankind as we become an interplanetary species.</p> <p>You will be responsible for the research, analysis, production, and dissemination of information relevant to protecting the security of personnel, global assets, and operations at SpaceX. You will use various collection methods and platforms to explore data, identify critical information, build queries, and assess risk to produce actional insights that drive informed business decisions.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Conduct in-depth research, evaluation, analysis, integration, and interpretation of information sourced from various open sources.</li> <li>Produce high-quality intelligence products on a daily, weekly, and monthly cadence, including data visualization, briefings, and analytic reports.</li> <li>Perform enhanced due diligence on companies and people within established tradecraft standards.</li> <li>Utilize data aggregators and OSINT tools to conduct open-source research, and leverage social media platforms, deep web, dark web, and breach data to identify hidden connections.</li> <li>Identify emerging risks to the company, our technology, and people and quickly synthesize information to share with relevant stakeholders.</li> <li>Communicate findings effectively and accurately to team members, leadership, and relevant stakeholders.</li> <li>Facilitate information sharing by fostering relationships and partnering with internal stakeholders as well as external local and federal law enforcement.</li> <li>Conduct intelligence analysis, threat assessments, and investigations on persons, companies, and organizations of interest.</li> <li>Develop risk mitigation strategies to address identified and work with internal teams to implement them.</li> <li>Manage and safeguard sensitive information, including case file and intelligence reports.</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree and 2+ years of professional experience in intelligence analysis, enhanced due diligence (EDD), third party risk management (TPRM), supply chain risk management (SCRM), and/or investigations; OR 4+ years of professional experience in the aforementioned areas in lieu of a degree.</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>2+ years of all-source intelligence experience in the military, intelligence community, federal law enforcement, or in the private sector at a high-tech company and/or US Government contractor.</li> <li>Familiarity with trade compliance regulations and restrictions, including export controls (ITAR, EAR, etc.) and import controls.</li> <li>Experience supporting trade compliance and/or supply chain teams and implementing TPRM and Denied Party Screening programs.</li> <li>Experience with open-source intelligence gathering tools/techniques for application/web-based social media platforms including web scraping, data parsing, and metadata extraction.</li> <li>Experience performing business process automation, constructing data pipelines, building dashboards, and developing robust queries and AI prompts.</li> <li>Ability to effectively communicate and collaborate with security and engineering teams on technical topics. This includes maintaining conceptual understandings of foundational topics related to data structures, databases, APIs, network infrastructure, and access controls.</li> <li>Strong analytical skills with the ability to analyze large data sets and draw actionable insights.</li> <li>Knowledge of analytic tradecraft standards, source validation, and disinformation detection.</li> <li>Excellent written and oral communication skills, with the ability to produce clear and concise research reports and briefings for a wide variety of internal and external audiences.</li> <li>Ability to work independently as well as collaboratively within a team environment in a fast-paced, high-tech environment.</li> <li>Highly organized with a strong attention to detail.</li> <li>Ability to adapt to changing priorities and deadlines.</li> <li>High degree of emotional intelligence and maturity.</li> <li>Strong critical thinking skills and a solutions-oriented mindset.</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Must be able to work extended hours and weekends as needed to support critical efforts and operations.</li> <li>Must be willing to travel ad hoc, although only minimal travel is expected at this time.</li> <li>Active TS/SCI clearance, or ability to obtain one. With an active clearance, candidates will be subject to pre-employment screening including background check and drug/alcohol test as well as random drug and alcohol testing during employment.</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. title: IT Network Administrator
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>IT NETWORK ADMINISTRATOR</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is looking for a network administrator with experience in networking technologies that support routing, switching, VoIP, and Wi-Fi. environment.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Procure, configure, and install network hardware: switches, access points, UPS, and PDUs.</li> <li>Troubleshoot and resolve network
