title: Manager, Starlink Engineering (Starlink PCBA SMT)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p class="xmsonormal"><strong>MANAGER, PCBA SMT ENGINEERING (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p class="xmsonormal">SpaceX is developing a low-latency, broadband internet system to meet the needs of people around the world. Enabled by a constellation of low Earth orbit satellites, Starlink will provide fast, reliable internet to populations with little or no connectivity, including those in rural communities and places where existing services are too expensive or unreliable. To enable our goal of “Connecting the Unconnected,” SpaceX is ramping up production of our User Terminal Kit manufacturing facility in Bastrop, Texas (Greater Austin), which will bring hundreds of high-skill manufacturing jobs to the area.</p> <p class="xmsonormal">SpaceX is also leveraging its experience deploying and operating the world’s largest satellite constellation to develop Starmind, a new constellation of satellites capturing solar energy in space to power low-cost, high-performance AI compute for Earth.</p> <p class="xmsonormal">We are looking for a hard-driving and well-rounded leader, capable of taking charge of a broad array of responsibilities associated with developing and growing a new production organization. You will be responsible for building out the production team that will operate and maintain this equipment. You will be responsible for establishing the standards by which this team operates, and shepherding the program from the startup phase into a disciplined production organization. This individual must have the capability to rapidly become a subject matter expert on multiple complex production operations. You must be capable of operating successfully within a chaotic startup environment while identifying and executing on actions needed to ensure mission success.</p> <p class="xmsonormal"><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul type="disc"> <li class="xmsonormal">Manage, recruit, and develop a team of manufacturing engineers, lead engineers, and specialists for Starlink PCBA manufacturing.</li> <li class="xmsonormal">Set technical standards and hold the team accountable for delivery.</li> <li class="xmsonormal">Lead manufacturing development strategy for SMT/PCBA, including capacity, line architecture, and process capability.</li> <li class="xmsonormal">Own quality, delivery, cost, yield, and equipment performance at high-volume throughput.</li> <li class="xmsonormal">Own factory layout, material flow, equipment, tooling, spares, and build-process strategy from receiving through test, including capital spend, vendor selection, and automation justified by ROI.</li> <li class="xmsonormal">Drive new products from design into production. Own NPI readiness, process qualification, and rate ramp, and influence design for manufacturability and testability (DFM/DFT).</li> <li class="xmsonormal">Align daily with production, design, test, supply chain, and quality. Serve as the escalation path for line issues and drive root cause to permanent corrective action.</li> <li class="xmsonormal">Define production data, SPC, and MES/MRP/ERP requirements. Keep process, equipment, and training records current.</li> <li class="xmsonormal">Ensure a strong focus on safety and ESD control and maintain an excellent safety record.</li> </ul> <p class="xmsonormal"><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul type="disc"> <li class="xmsonormal">Bachelor’s degree in an engineering discipline</li> <li class="xmsonormal">5+ years of experience in one or more of the following:</li> </ul> <ul type="disc"> <ul type="circle"> <li class="xmsonormal">Electronics development and/or production</li> <li class="xmsonormal">SMT production</li> </ul> </ul> <ul type="disc"> <li class="xmsonormal">2+ years of experience leading a team of 10+ individuals as direct reports</li> </ul> <p class="xmsonormal"><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul type="disc"> <li class="xmsonormal">Master's degree in an engineering discipline.</li> <li class="xmsonormal">Previous experience managing a team of high-performing manufacturing engineers and/or specialists.</li> <li class="xmsonormal">Proficiency in electronics manufacturing processes and equipment, including screen print, SPI, pick-and-place, reflow, AOI/AXI, selective solder or wave, coating, and test, plus a strong working knowledge of EEE piece parts, PCB, PCBA, and high-reliability electronics assemblies.</li> <li class="xmsonormal">Experience with design of experiments, gauge repeatability and reproducibility, and yield improvement.</li> <li class="xmsonormal">Ability to communicate clearly from the floor to senior leadership and to operate in a highly adaptive, iterative environment.</li> </ul> <p class="xmsonormal"><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:&nbsp;</strong></p> <ul type="disc"> <li class="xmsonormal">Must be willing to work extended hours and weekends as needed</li> <li class="xmsonormal">Able to travel up to 10% on an ongoing basis</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR <a href="https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/?id=ddtc_kb_article_page&amp;sys_id=24d528fddbfc930044f9ff621f961987">here</a>. &nbsp;</li> </ul> <p>SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.</p> <p>Applicants wishing to view a copy of SpaceX’s Affirmative Action Plan for veterans and individuals with disabilities, or applicants requiring reasonable accommodation to the application/interview process should reach out to&nbsp;<a href="mailto:EEOCompliance@spacex.com">EEOCompliance@spacex.com</a><em>.&nbsp;</em></p></div>

This is a dynamic position that requires the ability to monitor and create actions for key department metrics while managing production schedules, identifying risks, and clearly communicating them to key stakeholders. As a Manager, Production you will lead several complex, multi-disciplinary production teams/projects and will be required to dive into the unique engineering challenges we face daily in building rocket engine hardware.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Lead and manage a staff of 40+ employees per shift (up to 120 on 2 shifts)</li> <li>Manage modification, repair, title: Manager, Strategic Sourcing, Terafab Construction (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>MANAGER, STRATEGIC SOURCING, TERAFAB CONSTRUCTION (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is on a fast track to become the market leader in various product categories like US based human spaceflight, rapid vehicle reusability, internet services through the Starlink constellation and high performance compute. The SpaceX Supply Chain Department is a critical player in our operations. The functions within the department include procurement, planning and fulfillment, supplier development and quality, logistics and inventory. SpaceX Supply Chain will play a key role in enabling SpaceX to meet these ambitious growth targets and greatly contribute in making us a multi-planetary species.&nbsp;This individual will support construction projects and capital purchases for the construction and facilities organizations.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Manage a team of 5-10 buyers who are responsible for the purchase of all goods and services necessary for the construction of Terafab, including utilities and other infrastructure projects</li> <li>Work directly with key internal stakeholders to targets for the purchasing department including, but not limited to, payment terms, cash targets, and cost savings</li> <li>Develop and maintain key internal stakeholder relationships to create process analyses to identify financial impacts of decisions, cost improvement, and performance for assigned categories</li> <li>Collaborate with stakeholders to define SLAs and KPIs for suppliers and for assigned categories</li> <li>Create contract documents in collaboration with the legal department</li> <li>Manage contracts to ensure the supplier's performance&nbsp;meets contract title: Manager, Utilities Engineering and Operations (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>MANAGER, UTILITIES ENGINEERING AND OPERATIONS (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>The Manager of Utilities Engineering and Operations will lead the engineering, construction, operations, and maintenance of all critical utility systems at the Bastrop Manufacturing Site. The position ensures uninterrupted delivery and efficient use of utilities to support 24/7 mission-critical manufacturing operations in a highly dynamic environment. This position is based in Bastrop, Texas (Austin Area).</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Build and lead a multidisciplinary team of engineers, operators, technicians, and maintenance personnel responsible for the reliable operation of sitewide utility infrastructure.</li> <li>Own end-to-end performance of major utility systems, including: <ul> <li>Power generation and distribution (high-voltage switchgear, transformers, baseload and backup generation, grid elements, solar and other on-site power systems).</li> <li>Industrial water systems (raw water intake/treatment, process water, ultrapure/deionized water generation, cooling tower operations, and closed-loop hydronic systems).</li> <li>Wastewater collection, treatment, and discharge (industrial wastewater, process effluent, deluge water treatment, stormwater management, and compliance with environmental permits).</li> <li>Natural gas infrastructure (high-pressure supply lines, metering stations, regulators and safety systems)</li> </ul> </li> <li>Drive strategic planning, capital project execution, and expansion of utility infrastructure to match aggressive manufacturing ramp-up schedules, including new system design reviews, commissioning, and integration with production facilities.</li> <li>Establish and continuously improve preventive, predictive, and condition-based maintenance programs to achieve world-class uptime and minimal unplanned downtime.</li> <li>Ensure full compliance with all federal, state, and local environmental regulations, permitting requirements, and SpaceX internal standards.</li> <li>Manage operating budgets, utility cost forecasting, energy/water conservation initiatives, and vendor/service contracts.</li> <li>Partner closely with manufacturing, production engineering, environmental health &amp; safety, and facilities project teams to anticipate utility demands, resolve issues rapidly, and support new production lines.</li> <li>Lead root cause analysis (RCA) and corrective actions for any utility-related incidents, near-misses, or reliability events; implement lessons learned across the site.</li> <li>Foster a culture of ownership, rapid iteration, and first-principles problem solving within the utilities team while maintaining rigorous safety standards in high-hazard industrial environments.</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering, civil engineering, electrical engineering, environmental engineering, or other engineering discipline.</li> <li>8+ years of experience in utilities engineering, operations, or maintenance with industrial facilities.</li> <li>4+ years of direct people leadership experience managing engineers, operators, and technicians in 24/7 operational environments.</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Demonstrated hands-on experience with utility infrastructure and/or central utility plants in industrial environments.</li> <li>Proven track record leading utility system design, construction, commissioning, and ramp-up in fast-paced, high-growth industrial settings.</li> <li>Deep knowledge of industrial utility reliability best practices, including predictive maintenance technologies, SCADA/BMS systems, and automated monitoring/control platforms.</li> <li>Experience navigating complex environmental permitting and compliance for industrial wastewater, stormwater, and air emissions in regulated jurisdictions.</li> <li>Familiarity with high-reliability operations in mission-critical environments where downtime directly impacts production or safety (aerospace, semiconductor, or similar preferred).</li> <li>Strong project management skills with experience delivering multi-million-dollar utility capital projects on time and budget.</li> <li>Proficiency in reading/creating P&amp;IDs, utility flow diagrams, single-line electrical drawings, and equipment specifications.</li> <li>Ability to thrive in a high-intensity, iterative environment with evolving priorities and aggressive timelines.</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Ability to work at elevated heights, outdoor environments (heat, cold, rain, snow).</li> <li>Ability to work in an environment requiring exposure to fumes, odors, and noise.</li> <li>Must be available to work extended hours and weekends when needed based on site operational needs.</li> <li>Ability to provide on-call support in emergency situations.</li> <li>Demonstrated ability to work independently.</li> <li>Occasional travel may be required based on specific project tasks.</li> <li>Valid driver’s license.</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, title: Manufacturing Engineer - Supplier Development (Starlink Gateway)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>MANUFACTURING ENGINEER - SUPPLIER DEVELOPMENT (STARLINK GATEWAY)</strong></p> <p>This is a high-profile, cross functional position that plays an integral role in enabling development and production flow of our Starlink Gateways. You will work in close coordination with internal engineering and manufacturing departments as well as directly with suppliers to execute effective, creative and smart supply chain strategies to achieve production goals. title: Manufacturing Engineer, Blades and Vanes
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>MANUFACTURING ENGINEER, BLADES AND VANES</strong></p> <p>Working directly in the materials engineering group, this position owns equipment installation, commissioning, and process development for selected areas the blades and vanes investment casting line, from ceramic cores through wax, shell, and cast. A counterpart owns post-cast operations (shell removal through coating). Experience in any cores-through-cast area is welcome. The role starts with commissioning, then transitions to process ownership in the area where the engineer is strongest, always with a strong equipment foundation.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Lead commissioning, Factory Acceptance Tests (FAT), Site Acceptance Tests (SAT), supplier management, and customization of pre-cast equipment, including VIM furnaces, ceramic and wax injection machines, shell dip lines, and thermal systems (kilns, dewax autoclaves, burnout and preheat furnaces).</li> <li>Coordinate supplier-defined facilities and services: power, water, waste, controls, network, connectivity, and MES.</li> <li>After commissioning, take process ownership of assigned cores-through-cast operations, drive production-ready capability, and own cost, rate, yield, and quality.</li> <li>Specify, design, and implement tools, fixtures, process aids, and additional equipment to hit rate, quality, and yield targets.</li> <li>Develop and maintain work instructions, process specifications, PFMEAs, control plans, and change-control documentation.</li> <li>Own EHS and process safety for assigned equipment, including high-temperature, vacuum, pressure, and chemical operations.</li> <li>Troubleshoot equipment and process issues on the floor; lead root-cause analysis and implement robust corrections.</li> <li>Collaborate with Materials, Design, Quality, Facilities, Controls, Production, Maintenance/Reliability, and EHS, including technicians and operators.</li> <li>Lead technical projects and mentor junior engineers and technicians; provide technical guidance and promote skill growth and team cohesion. Senior individual-contributor role, not a people-manager position.</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in mechanical, manufacturing, industrial, electrical, chemical, materials science, or other engineering discipline.</li> <li>1+ years of equipment, manufacturing, or process engineering, including hands-on installation, commissioning, FAT/SAT, and supplier management.</li> </ul> <p><strong><span data-contrast="auto">PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</span></strong><span data-ccp-props="{&quot;134233117&quot;:false,&quot;134233118&quot;:false,&quot;335559738&quot;:240,&quot;335559739&quot;:240}">&nbsp;</span></p> <ul> <li>Experience in at least one major area of investment casting or a closely related high-temperature/precision process, and the ability to learn the full cores-through-cast flow.</li> <li>Strong mechanical aptitude with working knowledge of electrical, controls, automation, and facilities. Able to support or transition into maintenance and reliability for assigned equipment.</li> <li>Works independently, delivers under tight schedules, and communicates effectively with suppliers, technicians, and cross-functional partners.</li> <li>Direct experience with VIM furnaces, ceramic/wax injection, kilns/ovens, autoclaves, dip lines, core leachers, HIP, heat treat, AGVs, or related process equipment.</li> <li>Breadth across mechanical, electrical, materials, controls, and automation.</li> <li>Experience integrating equipment with MES and plant networks.</li> <li>Lean/Six Sigma or equivalent structured problem-solving.</li> <li>Prior mentoring of engineers and technicians, or technical leadership of project teams.</li> <li>Aerospace, energy, or other high-reliability casting or precision manufacturing.</li> <li>Hands-on maintenance, reliability, or equipment-sustainment experience.</li> </ul> <p><strong><span data-contrast="auto">ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</span></strong><span data-ccp-props="{&quot;134233117&quot;:false,&quot;134233118&quot;:false,&quot;335559738&quot;:240,&quot;335559739&quot;:240}">&nbsp;</span></p> <ul> <li>Travel approximately 15% for equipment commissioning and FATs; extended hours or weekends as required during commissioning and ramp.</li> <li>Ability to lift up to 25Ibs unassisted.</li> <li>Standing/walking for long periods of time.</li> <li>Willingness to work long hours and weekends as necessary to accommodate manufacturing and test campaigns.</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. title: Manufacturing Engineer, Tool & Die Machining
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>MANUFACTURING ENGINEER, TOOL &amp; DIE MACHINING (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is developing a low latency, broadband internet system to meet the needs of consumers across the globe. Enabled by a constellation of low Earth orbit satellites, Starlink will provide fast, reliable internet to populations with little or no connectivity, including those in rural communities and places where existing services are too expensive or unreliable.</p> <p>Working directly in the materials engineering group, this position is responsible for managing a technical project for the development and qualification of all equipment, tooling and manufacturing process technologies necessary to produce plastic injection molds and high pressure die cast tools. The correct individual will bring an open mindset, challenge the status quo with regards to traditional vs. emerging technologies and utilize a logical and disciplined approach to evaluate and select the correct set of solutions.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Develop machining capability in-house for the tool &amp; die team and deliver high-quality precision piece parts required to build internal tooling</li> <li>Analyze piece parts and assemblies for DFM to ensure that the parts are optimized for manufacturing and assembly</li> <li>Create collaborative business plans with design engineering, upstream production, and support teams and develop and maintain positive supplier/customer relationships</li> <li>Work between manufacturing and design engineers, machinists, technicians, and quality personnel to ensure processes are robust and any production problems are quickly solved</li> <li>Implement machining process controls that allow parts to run ‘lights out’. Leverage latest technologies and programming strategies to reduce in-cycle intervention</li> <li>Identify, recommend, procure, and install machine shop equipment as well as ensure all equipment is thoroughly maintained and calibrated</li> <li>Responsible for cost optimization and cost reduction initiatives associated with fabrication and processes</li> <li>Continually develop and manage engineering capacity, schedules, and project plans in order to support production manifest as well as a diverse and variable R&amp;D demand</li> <li>Research and identify new materials, manufacturing technologies and finishing options</li> <li>Inform estimations of prototype and production manufacturing costs - tooling, secondary assembly, secondary finishing and piece part</li> <li>Publish and maintain detailed schedules for each development project segment</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in mechanical, manufacturing, materials engineering, or other engineering discipline</li> <li>3+ years of experience with CNC machining</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Master’s degree or PhD in an engineering discipline</li> <li>Strong to expert level 3D CAD skills, including advanced surfacing and large assemblies</li> <li>Experience with Siemens NX</li> <li>Experience transitioning products from design to manufacturing and scaling to high volume as part of a cross-functional team</li> <li>Experience with manufacturing process like injection molding, CNC, die casting, stamping, assembly, and box build in a production setting and a good understanding of the costs and schedule and complexity associated with each process</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Willingness to travel to other SpaceX sites and/or vendors for significant/extended periods of time (~15% travel normally, more during urgent manufacturing and test campaigns)</li> <li>Ability to lift up to 25Ibs unassisted</li> <li>Standing/walking for long periods of time</li> <li>Willingness to work long hours and weekends as necessary to accommodate manufacturing and test campaigns</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. title: Manufacturing Engineering Specialist (Starlink) - 2nd Shift
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>MANUFACTURING ENGINEERING SPECIALIST (STARLINK) - 2ND SHIFT</strong></p> <p>At SpaceX we’re leveraging our experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation and is providing fast, reliable internet to millions of users worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system – thousands of satellites, consumer receivers that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing, and the software that brings it all together. We’ve only begun to scratch the surface of Starlink’s potential global impact and are looking for best-in-class engineers to help maximize Starlink’s utility for communities and businesses around the world.</p> <p>The success of Starlink depends on the quality, reliability, cost, manufacturability, throughput, and security of the products that you deliver. If you seek a fast-paced, dynamic environment; if you thrive on solving difficult problems where resolutions have high impact; and if you love the challenge of building something from scratch, then this role will be an ideal next career step. We are looking for talented manufacturing specialists to help establish new manufacturing and test processes and support full-scale production for the user terminal (a high-volume manufactured product that consumers will have in their homes).</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Troubleshoot automated equipment and recurring line issues, and implement fixes with engineering and maintenance</li> <li>Triage non-conforming products and drive resolution and preventative actions</li> <li>Identify continuous improvement opportunities for yield, performance, and cost</li> <li>Update work instructions and train teammates on the standard process, rework, and equipment tasks</li> <li>Perform process development and validation on new equipment alongside engineering</li> <li>Define maintenance schedules and support activities</li> <li>Drive area improvements involving layout, 5S, material flow, tooling, and operator safety&nbsp;</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>High school diploma or equivalency certificate and 2+ years of professional experience in a hands-on manufacturing environment; OR bachelor's degree in an engineering, math or science discipline</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Associate or bachelor's degree in an engineering, math, or science discipline&nbsp;</li> <li>Demonstrated experience working in a highly adaptive and iterative environment</li> <li>Experience in a high-volume commercial manufacturing environment</li> <li>Experience supporting new product introduction and the transition of products from development to volume production</li> <li>Experience supporting process validation or process qualification on production hardware</li> <li>Experience using production data or SPC to identify quality trends</li> <li>Experience operating and troubleshooting automated production equipment, including HMI issues and basic electrical, pneumatic, or mechanical faults</li> <li>Experience with electromechanical assembly or test on manual and automated processes</li> <li>Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings and recommend process or design improvements to engineering</li> <li>Experience using MES to document defects and non-conforming material, and familiarity with ERP or MRP systems</li> <li>Strong written and verbal communication, including updating work instructions and training others on the line&nbsp;</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Must be available one title: Manufacturing Technician
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>MANUFACTURING TECHNICIAN</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is leveraging our experience building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s largest satellite constellation and most advanced broadband internet system, providing fast, reliable internet to millions of users worldwide. Our Bastrop factory builds the technology behind Starlink across printed circuit boards, custom silicon, solar cells, and more. We are looking for talented, driven technicians to drive manufacturing output and yield across our production, maintenance, and facilities teams.</p> <p>This is a hands-on technician role. We are building a strong team of technicians who are trained into the team where they will have the greatest impact and clearest path to grow. This includes PCB production, machine and facilities maintenance, silicon packaging, gateway, solar, and satellite operations. The ideal candidate is comfortable in a fast-paced, metrics-driven manufacturing environment, learns quickly, works safely, and is motivated by SpaceX’s mission to provide high speed, low-latency connectivity across the globe.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Perform assigned technical tasks to written work instructions, procedures, and safety standards in a high-volume manufacturing environment</li> <li>Execute startup and shutdown procedures and operate production equipment; monitor process conditions and control systems</li> <li>Perform first-level troubleshooting on production equipment and tooling; provide feedback and work with maintenance and engineering teams to drive root cause of downtime</li> <li>Use hand and power tools, precision measurement instruments (calipers, micrometers), and common test equipment for calibration, inspection, and basic repair</li> <li>Read and interpret work instructions, mechanical/electrical/pneumatic schematics, drawings, and parts lists</li> <li>Read and safely execute lock-out/tag-out (LOTO) procedures and follow all Job Hazard Analyses (JHAs) for the assigned area</li> <li>Handle production and flight hardware correctly to prevent damage; perform quality inspections and identify defects and non-conformities</li> <li>Perform preventive maintenance and calibration of equipment and instruments; track schedule and maintain inventory of consumables</li> <li>Record work accurately in Warp, Factory Manual, and related manufacturing systems (travelers, tickets, work orders, logs)</li> <li>Support root cause analysis (e.g. 5-Why) for quality and process issues and implement corrective actions to improve overall equipment effectiveness (OEE)</li> <li>Recommend improvements to manufacturing processes with a focus on reducing cost and downtime and increasing yield</li> <li>Ensure 5S standards are upheld by maintaining a clean and organized work area</li> <li>Conduct or support training of production personnel; cross-train and rotate across tasks, stations, or lines as production demand shifts</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>High school diploma or equivalency certificate</li> <li>1+ years of hands on work experience</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Associate’s degree</li> <li>2+ years of hands-on experience in manufacturing, maintenance, facilities, skilled trades, automotive, military, or a technical/vocational school program</li> <li>Ability to read, interpret, and work from work instructions, layout drawings, mechanical/electrical/pneumatic schematics, and parts lists</li> <li>Familiarity with hand and power tools and basic precision measurement tools (calipers, micrometers, multimeters)</li> <li>Basic mechanical and/or electrical fundamentals (fasteners, pneumatics/hydraulics; Ohm’s law, multimeter use)</li> <li>Proficiently use a computer and the Microsoft Office suite</li> <li>Experience using production and inventory management software such as MES/ERP</li> <li>Experience with root cause analysis and problem solving (e.g. 5-Why, Fishbone, 8D)</li> <li>Strong interpersonal, verbal, and written communication skills to work closely with other technicians and cross-functional teams</li> <li>Ability to identify and maintain priorities while working independently in a high-paced environment with minimal oversight</li> <li>OSHA 10/30, forklift, or other relevant safety certifications</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Must be open to work all shifts, overtime, and/or weekends as needed</li> <li>Standing for long periods of time, climbing up and down ladders, bending, grasping, sitting, pulling, pushing, stooping, and stretching may be required to perform the functions of this position</li> <li>Must be comfortable working in a production environment, which may include loud areas, fumes/odors, and the handling of hazardous chemicals depending on the assigned team</li> <li>Must be able to wear appropriate PPE for the assigned manufacturing environment</li> <li>Must be able to lift up to 25 lbs. unassisted</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. title: Material Flow Engineer
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>MATERIAL FLOW ENGINEER (STARBASE)</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is currently seeking an experienced Material Flow Engineer to analyze, design and optimize the receiving, storage, movement, and presentation of materials at Starbase for all flight and non-flight programs to enable overall Starship objectives.</p> <p>Material Flow Engineers are responsible for developing and implementing material flow strategies that align with Starship production goals and drive operational excellence. This role involves using lean material flow principles, data analytics, problem solving, modeling, and project management skills to ensure the safe, efficient, and cost-effective movement of all materials.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Process Design and Optimization:</strong>&nbsp;Design and implement innovative strategies for efficient material flow from receipt to the lineside and any reverse logistics required. Understand critical part flow categories to develop specific plans that will allow Starbase to achieve significant scale. Use value stream mapping to ensure end-to-end process optimization.</li> <li><strong>Factory and Warehouse Layout Planning:</strong>&nbsp;Develop and implement conceptual and detailed layouts for material flow and storage to achieve targeted inventory levels. Ensure that storage strategies are aligned across the supply chain and achieve maximum desired part density considering all available facility volume. Build and use space capacity models to ensure we have adequate storage solutions.</li> <li><strong>Develop Materials Management Resource Plans:</strong>&nbsp;Using lean material flow principles and industry best practices, develop labor and equipment models to match the material flow strategies. Conduct time studies as needed to determine resource efficiency and implement procedures to track improvements. Ensure that all material handling equipment is optimized for the processes being supported.</li> <li><strong>Part Packaging and Rack Flow:</strong>&nbsp;Develop cost effective and sustainable packaging solutions for use between vendors and SpaceX and within Starbase facilities. Ensure that the packaging optimizes for total landed cost by considering logistics density and handling efficiency, while maintaining required quality standards. Work with external packaging and tooling vendors as well as internal teams to get right-sized packaging fleets built in time to support program targets.</li> <li><strong>Data Analysis and Reporting:</strong>&nbsp;Utilize data analysis tools (e.g., Excel, Tableau, SQL) to assess material flow performance metrics, identify issues, and develop data-driven solutions. Support the Materials Management operations teams as needed with decision making.</li> <li><strong>Safety and Training:</strong>&nbsp;Conduct risk assessments and implement measures to ensure that all Materials Management processes adhere to federal, state, local and SpaceX safety standards. Conduct periodic audits to ensure that safe conditions do not develop, all processes are being completed per design standards and any equipment in use remains adequate for the process it supports. Develop and lead training for new processes and equipment,</li> <li><strong>Project Collaboration:</strong>&nbsp;Collaborate with Engineering, Production and Supply Chain teams across SpaceX on critical projects to ensure stakeholder buy-in is achieved and everyone is working towards a common target state. As needed, conduct sessions to keep all cross-functional teams aligned.</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in an engineering discipline</li> <li>1+ years of engineering experience in a manufacturing environment (internship and school projects experience qualify)</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCES</strong></p> <ul> <li>Experience working directly on material flow engineering solutions</li> <li>Demonstrated leadership driving projects in an industrial environment</li> <li>Extensive analytical skills for performing detailed data analysis</li> <li>Experience with layout design in AutoCAD or similar, building both warehouse and manufacturing lineside layouts</li> <li>Experience with material handling equipment and packaging design and implementation</li> <li>Knowledge of Supply Chain planning design and warehousing requirements</li> <li>Experience solving challenging quantitative problems in fast paced environments</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS</strong></p> <ul> <li>Must be able to work extended hours and/or weekends as needed to meet major milestones</li> <li>This position is based in Starbase, TX and requires being onsite - remote work not considered</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. title: Materials Engineer (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>MATERIALS ENGINEER (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>Starlink is building the world's largest satellite constellation to deliver fast, reliable internet to people who need it most—and powering that constellation starts on the factory floor. We are insourcing solar cell manufacturing end-to-end, from crystal growth and ingot production through wafering and cell fabrication to drive performance, cost, and scale at every step. High-efficiency, high-reliability cells made in-house are the backbone of the Starlink network: more photons in means more data out to customers around the world.</p> <p>As a Materials Engineer, you will own the critical consumables that keep our ingot, wafer, and solar cell manufacturing lines running. You will take end-to-end ownership of materials used in production—partnering with supply chain on sourcing, driving material qualification, and handing off proven materials into high-volume manufacturing. We are looking for a general Materials Engineer who is excited about metals, polymers, crystals, and process consumables; solar experience is a plus, not a requirement. If you are passionate about solving hard problems, anchor your engineering judgment with first principles thinking, and are relentless about acting with urgency, this role is for you.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Own consumable materials used across ingot, wafer, and/or solar cell manufacturing lines—from initial sourcing and technical evaluation through qualification, production hand-off, and ongoing support.</li> <li>Partner closely with supply chain to identify, evaluate, and qualify suppliers for critical process materials.</li> <li>Define material requirements, specifications, and acceptance criteria in collaboration with process, quality, and production engineering teams.</li> <li>Plan and execute material qualification campaigns, including characterization, process trials, and production-readiness assessments before hand-off to manufacturing.</li> <li>Drive root cause to first principles and implement durable corrective actions.</li> <li>Build deep technical understanding of material chemistry, microstructure, and process interactions for metals, polymers, crystals, and other consumables used in high-volume manufacturing.</li> <li>Identify opportunities to improve material performance, cost, yield, and reliability through alternative materials, dual-sourcing strategies, or process changes.</li> <li>Document qualification results, material specifications, and best practices.</li> <li>Communicate status, risks, and recommendations clearly to cross-functional partners and leadership.</li> <li>Champion a culture of safety and quality in all materials handling, testing, and production support activities.</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in materials science, chemical engineering, or a STEM field.</li> <li>1+ years of experience in materials engineering, materials selection, process materials, or manufacturing materials support.</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Master’s degree or PhD in materials science, chemical engineering, or a related field.</li> <li>Hands-on experience with metals, polymers, crystals, ceramics, coatings, or other process consumables in a manufacturing or R&amp;D environment.</li> <li>Experience with material qualification, supplier development, or transitioning materials from development into production.</li> <li>Familiarity with materials characterization techniques (e.g., SEM-EDS, XRD, FTIR, optical microscopy, mechanical or chemical property testing).</li> <li>Experience working in a high-volume manufacturing environment and partnering with production, quality, and supply chain teams.</li> <li>Strong first-principles problem solving and a demonstrated ability to dig deep on ambiguous materials challenges.</li> <li>Passion for building, learning quickly, and owning outcomes end-to-end; thrives in a fast-paced, scrappy environment with tight timelines.</li> <li>Effective written and interpersonal communication skills; able to convey technical concepts across all levels of the organization.</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Willingness and ability to travel up to 25% time.</li> <li>Ability to lift up to 25 lbs unassisted.</li> <li>Ability to stand/walk for extended periods on the manufacturing floor.</li> <li>Willingness to work extended hours and weekends as needed.</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. title: Materials Engineer, AI Satellites (Starmind)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>MATERIALS ENGINEER, AI SATELLITES (STARMIND)</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is leveraging its experience deploying and operating the world’s largest satellite constellation to develop Starmind, a new constellation of satellites capturing solar energy in space to power low-cost, high-performance AI compute for Earth. Realizing this vision demands highly reliable, high performance electrical compute hardware, solar power systems, thermal radiators, and more. These systems must operate in the extreme environment of space while delivering the connectivity, control, power distribution, and processing needed for orbital AI inference.</p> <p>The Starmind team designs, builds, and operates the orbital compute fabric of the future. We develop nearly every key piece of technology in house – from the satellites’ flight computers and power systems to the fully custom compute electronics, memory, and networking that form the brain of our on-orbit data centers. As a Materials Engineer on the Starmind team, you’ll have ownership over the entire life-cycle of the hardware that enables advanced on-orbit AI processing and data center workloads. Your work sits at the intersection of process, packaging, mechanical, and thermal engineering. The Payload team is responsible for the design of industry-leading compute electronics, memory, and networking in order to achieve required domain sizes and processing workloads.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:&nbsp;</strong></p> <ul> <li>Rapidly develop high-reliability microelectronics packages, cooling systems, and radiator hardware for satellites.</li> <li>Own the full lifecycle of materials specification, validation, and process development— including device modeling, characterization of performance metrics, and materials failure analysis.</li> <li>Drive system trades, requirements capture, materials selection, prototyping, manufacturing, failure analysis.</li> <li>Build supply chains for build-up layers, plating chemicals, coatings, thermal interface materials, and other materials for compute and satellite manufacturing. Define incoming acceptance criteria for materials.</li> <li>Address materials and process challenges in advanced packaging while spearheading the development of next-generation TIM materials to improve packaging performance.</li> <li>Specify and implement in-process metrology tools for quality control. Design thermal test vehicles and test setups to evaluate material/electronic properties. Integrate simulation tools with experimental data to guide and drive targeted improvements via material or process changes.</li> <li>Work closely with engineers from adjacent disciplines (mechanical, thermal, electrical, software, test engineering, supply chain, silicon design, etc.) to deliver tightly integrated, high-performance hardware</li> <li>Challenge assumptions, question requirements, learn from your mistakes, and approach problems with an open mind</li> <li>Manage compliance risks related to materials and processes, ensuring safety and environmental compliance with industry standards.</li> <li>Collaborate closely with leadership and stakeholders across all departments—including design, reliability, production, and supply chain—to integrate materials innovations into product roadmaps and ensure accountability for operations and reliability.</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in materials science, mechanical engineering, or other engineering discipline</li> <li>Experience in microelectronics device research or manufacturing&nbsp;</li> </ul> <p><strong>&nbsp;</strong><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:&nbsp;</strong></p> <ul> <li>Master’s degree in materials science or similar field</li> <li>Internship, co-op, or early-career experience in hardware, robotics, automation, or manufacturing title: Materials Engineer, Solar Cell Characterization
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>MATERIALS ENGINEER, SOLAR CELL CHARACTERIZATION</strong></p> <p>Starlink is building the world's largest satellite constellation to deliver fast, reliable internet to people who need it most—and powering that constellation starts on the factory floor. We are insourcing solar cell manufacturing end-to-end, from crystal growth and ingot production through wafering and cell fabrication, to drive performance, cost, and scale at every step. High-efficiency, high-reliability cells made in-house are the backbone of the Starlink network: more photons in means more data out to customers around the world.</p> <p>As a Materials Engineer for solar cell characterization, you will own offline metrology and materials characterization of insourced solar cells—building the measurement capability, analysis methods, and physical understanding needed to raise cell performance and yield. You will turn electrical, optical, and materials data into root cause, and interface with process, production, and quality teams to lock in durable fixes. If you are passionate about solving hard problems, anchor your engineering judgment with first-principles thinking, and are relentless about acting with urgency, this role is for you.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Own characterization and metrology strategy for insourced solar cells across cell interfaces—from method development and tool qualification through production-ready measurement recipes</li> <li>Build and maintain a suite of offline electrical, optical, and materials characterization techniques to quantify cell performance, reliability, and yield-limiting defects (e.g., I-V, quantum efficiency, PL/EL imaging, lifetime, SEM-EDS, optical microscopy, spectroscopy, and related methods)</li> <li>Lead root cause analysis for performance and yield excursions: design experiments, execute failure analysis, correlate process history with metrology signatures, and drive corrective actions to first principles</li> <li>Define measurement requirements, sampling plans, gauge R&amp;R, calibration, and acceptance criteria in partnership with process, quality, and production engineering</li> <li>Stand up and develop processes for offline metrology equipment; own data integrity, tool matching, and measurement uncertainty so results can be trusted for process decisions</li> <li>Translate characterization results into clear material and process recommendations that improve efficiency, reliability, cost, and manufacturability</li> <li>Partner with process engineering on DOEs and golden-line development; provide rapid feedback loops during recipe, materials, and equipment changes</li> <li>Document methods, specifications, FA reports, and best practices; communicate status, risks, and recommendations clearly to cross-functional partners and leadership</li> <li>Champion a culture of safety and quality in all sample preparation, chemical handling, lab operations, and production support activities</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in materials science, materials engineering, chemical engineering, or a related technical discipline</li> <li>1+ years of professional experience in materials characterization, failure analysis, semiconductor/PV metrology, or a related laboratory or manufacturing role (internship and co-op experience applicable)</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Master's degree or PhD in materials science, materials engineering, chemical engineering, or a related technical discipline</li> <li>Hands-on experience characterizing photovoltaic devices, silicon wafers, thin films, or semiconductor devices</li> <li>Proficiency with solar cell and wafer metrology such as I-V, Suns-Voc, EQE/IQE, photoluminescence, electroluminescence, minority-carrier lifetime (QSSPC/PL), ellipsometry, four-point probe, and optical inspection</li> <li>Experience with materials analysis techniques including SEM-EDS, FIB cross-sectioning, AFM, XRD, FTIR, XPS, SIMS, ICP-MS, and optical microscopy</li> <li>Experience designing and implementing a laboratory inventory management system (including architecture, workflows, and user access), building automated pipelines to transfer metrology data from tools into the LIMS, and integrating SPC (control charts, dashboards, and alerts) on the collected data</li> <li>Demonstrated ability to lead structured root cause analysis (e.g., DOE, 5-why, fishbone, fault-tree) and convert findings into process or material improvements</li> <li>Experience qualifying metrology tools, writing measurement SOPs, and establishing statistical process controls or gauge capabilities</li> <li>Experience working in a high-volume manufacturing or fab environment and partnering with process, quality, and production teams</li> <li>Strong first-principles problem solving and a demonstrated ability to dig deep on ambiguous materials and device-performance challenges</li> <li>Comfortable with data analysis (Python, JMP, MATLAB, or equivalent) to correlate metrology, process, and electrical results</li> <li>Passion for building, learning quickly, and owning outcomes end-to-end; thrives in a fast-paced environment with tight timelines</li> <li>Effective written and verbal communication skills; able to convey technical concepts across all levels of the organization</li> <li>Self-motivated with strong organizational skills and a bias toward action</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> title: Mechanical Engineer
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>MECHANICAL ENGINEER</strong></p> <p>As a member of the construction projects team, you will work with engineers across multiple disciplines in the design, procurement, and build of infrastructure at our College Station facility. This is a hands-on role responsible for the planning and execution of new facility construction and renovation projects with emphasis on mechanical, piping, HVAC, and utility systems. You will work with construction project managers, facility engineers, designers, vendors, and internal partners/customers to support these goals. You will have the opportunity to drive positive change and own projects from start to finish with the goal of making the SpaceX campus a world-class facility. This position is based in College Station, TX.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Lead a project team of engineers, consultants, and contractors throughout the engineering, procurement, and construction process</li> <li>Manage the design, development, and issuance of drawings, documentation, and reports for large commercial or industrial-type facility and infrastructure projects</li> <li>Write, negotiate, and manage construction contracts with subcontractors across multiple disciplines from conceptual design through closeout and activation</li> <li>Lead and/or contribute to the design of HVAC systems for various facilities including office, warehouse, and industrial spaces</li> <li>Use fluid dynamics, thermodynamics, and heat transfer knowledge as required to design tubing and piping systems</li> <li>Prepare plans, details, specifications, and commercial bid documents for plumbing, heating, ventilating, air conditioning, and general piping systems</li> <li>Conduct research that tests and analyzes the feasibility, design, operation, and performance of equipment, components, and systems</li> <li>Recommend designs/modifications to eliminate machine or system malfunctions</li> <li>Estimate costs and submit bids for engineering and construction projects, and prepare contract documents</li> <li>Resolve design and construction conflicts in the field in real time with multiple parties</li> <li>Review and evaluate the work of consultants, contractors, and other external parties</li> <li>Responsible for planning, coordinating, and executing various construction projects simultaneously</li> <li>Accountable for accurate budgeting and cost forecasting</li> <li>Oversee project schedule accuracy and milestone reporting to engineers, contractors, fabricators, and project stakeholders</li> <li>Coordinate and schedule work with internal SpaceX teams and external general/sub-contractors</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, or other engineering discipline</li> <li>2+ years of professional experience with the design and build of large commercial or industrial-type projects</li> <li>Experience with mechanical/process piping/HVAC system design and/or project execution</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>5+ years of construction experience with working knowledge of mechanical, electrical, and plumbing</li> <li>Direct field experience with day-to-day management on a construction site</li> <li>Experience in conceptual design and budgeting</li> <li>Experience in contract management for large capital projects</li> <li>Experience in managing the engineering, procurement, and construction process for heavy industrial-type projects</li> <li>Experience with ASME B31.3 and B31.9 fluid systems</li> <li>Experience in managing multiple projects simultaneously</li> <li>Experience creating and implementing process/design solutions with minimal impact to business operations</li> <li>Able to quickly assess an issue and assist technicians with troubleshooting and repair</li> <li>Ability to work in a high-concentration, high-stress environment under possible extended work hours and tight deadlines</li> <li>Acute attention to detail and ability to see interactions with other systems to avoid problems</li> <li>Familiarity with National Electrical Code, ASHRAE, National Fire Protection Association, American Society of Mechanical Engineers (ASME), and International Building Code</li> <li>Competency with CAD programs (AutoCAD, Revit, Siemens NX, BIM/Navisworks or similar)</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Physical ability to perform hands-on work in various environments, including heat, cold, rain, and tight quarters</li> <li>Ability to work onsite at our College Station, TX facility (Remote work not considered)</li> <li>Ability to work extended hours and weekends as needed</li> <li>Ability to travel as needed</li> <li>Valid driver's license</li> <li>Ability to lift up to 25 lbs. unassisted</li> </ul><div title: Mechanical Engineer (Gas/Steam Turbines)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>MECHANICAL ENGINEER (<span data-teams="true">GAS/STEAM TURBINES</span>)</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is looking for a Mechanical Engineer who can support power plant development by owning the rotating equipment integration scope from technical specification through equipment selection, interface management, construction and into commissioning. You’ll work across gas turbines, steam turbines, and HRSGs. This is not a desk job. You will be constructing the power plant, owning commissioning in the control room during startup, and in the field troubleshooting.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:&nbsp;&nbsp;</strong></p> <ul> <li>Develop technical specifications for gas turbines, steam turbines, HRSGs, and associated auxiliaries (lube oil systems, gas fuel skids, SCR/CO catalyst systems)</li> <li>Lead technical evaluation of OEM proposals (GE, Siemens Energy, Mitsubishi Power, Doosan) and drive equipment selection recommendations</li> <li>Own mechanical interface management between major equipment packages — turbine, generator, HRSG, steam turbine, condenser, and balance of plant systems</li> <li>Review and approve OEM drawings, GA layouts, and P&amp;IDs for technical compliance and constructibility</li> <li>Support foundation and structural design coordination with civil/structural engineering, including dynamic loading and vibration criteria</li> <li>Work with EPC and OEM to resolve technical interface issues (piping stress, thermal expansion, casing supports, lube oil routing) before they hit the field</li> <li>Participate in factory acceptance testing (FAT) at OEM facilities</li> <li>Support commissioning and startup activities on-site, including mechanical checkout, alignment verification, and vibration baseline testing</li> <li>Develop technical basis for spare parts strategy and critical rotating equipment spares</li> <li>Travel to OEM factories, fabrication shops, and the construction site as needed</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:&nbsp;&nbsp;</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related engineering discipline</li> <li>2+ years of experience with utility-scale rotating equipment: gas turbines, steam turbines, HRSGs, or large industrial compressors/pumps</li> </ul> <p><strong><span data-contrast="auto">PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></strong></p> <ul> <li>Working knowledge of rotating equipment fundamentals: rotor dynamics, bearing design, lube oil systems, thermal expansion, and alignment</li> <li>Experience with mechanical specification development and technical bid evaluation for major equipment packages</li> <li>Direct experience with F-class or H-class gas turbines (GE 7/9FA/HA, Siemens SGT6/8, Mitsubishi M501/701, Doosan H-class)</li> <li>Experience with HRSG design review — drum internals, superheater/reheater arrangement, SCR integration</li> <li>Familiarity with API 611/612/616/617 standards for rotating equipment</li> <li>Experience with vibration analysis, rotor dynamics software, or finite element analysis for rotating machinery</li> <li>Factory acceptance test (FAT) experience at an OEM turbine or generator facility</li> <li>Field commissioning experience: alignment, mechanical run tests, vibration baselining</li> <li>Comfort working directly with OEM engineering teams to resolve technical disputes under schedule pressure</li> <li>Experience using SOLIDWORKS, Siemens NX, or similar CAD software</li> <li>Knowledge of engineering standards and best practices such as ASME B31.3, ASME BPV Code Section VIII, and AFSPCMAN 91-710</li> </ul> <p><strong><span data-contrast="auto">ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</span></strong><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></p> <ul> <li>Must be available to work extended hours and weekends when needed based on site operational needs; flexibility required</li> <li>Willingness to travel to job sites during construction, commissioning, and critical operational events</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under title: Mechanical Engineer (Starship)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>MECHANICAL ENGINEER (STARSHIP)</strong></p> <p>Our Starbase team is working on the toughest and most audacious project on our planet: making humanity multiplanetary. Our team is building high performance flight hardware, a high-volume rocket production line, and a launch system that can rapidly and reliably launch and land our rockets. Our mechanical engineers are responsible for designing, analyzing, and building all of the hardware across the Starship and Super Heavy vehicles. Expect a dynamic role doing what you’re best at. Whatever your skill set, you’ll be aligned to the part of the program you’re most effectively able to contribute to (design, analysis, test, structures, fluids, manufacturing, tooling, machine design, etc.). If you are a high performing engineer, want to immerse yourself in never-before-solved challenges, and are excited to put in the effort to make this goal a reality, we want to hear from you.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:&nbsp;</strong>&nbsp;</p> <ul> <li>Own the design and development of next generation launch vehicles, launch pad and production lines</li> <li>Transform system requirements into hardware concepts and trade implementation and architecture options</li> <li>Perform hand calculations and FEA to develop, assess, and optimize designs</li> <li>Rapidly iterate on manufacturing processes and development testing in a fast-paced environment&nbsp;</li> <li>Collaborate with interdisciplinary teams to ensure hardware integrates with all Starship systems and supports necessary mission operations</li> <li>Participate in design reviews internally and with suppliers and customers</li> <li>Partner with engineering and production teams to generate ideas, designs, and improvements for current and next-generation vehicles&nbsp;</li> <li>Own large business outcomes</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong>&nbsp;</p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in an engineering discipline or physics</li> <li>1+ years of mechanical or fluids design, analysis, or build experience (internship and school projects experience qualify)</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong>&nbsp;</p> <ul> <li>Master's or PhD in an engineering or physics discipline</li> <li>Strong ability to use data and analysis to make fast data-driven decisions</li> <li>Ability to perform trade studies and make clear recommendations using first principles and engineering fundamentals even with partial information. Strong understanding of engineering fundamentals</li> <li>Experience working at a nimble engineering organization or in a highly technical position that required a scrappy, entrepreneurial manner to accomplish tasks with tight time or budget constraints</li> <li>Excelled in ultra-competitive environments. title: Mechanical Engineer, AI Satellites (Starmind)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>MECHANICAL ENGINEER, AI SATELLITES (STARMIND)</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is leveraging its experience deploying and operating the world’s largest satellite constellation to develop Starmind, a new constellation of satellites capturing&nbsp;solar energy in space to power low-cost, high-performance AI compute for Earth.&nbsp;Realizing this vision demands highly reliable, high performance mechanical systems including large deployable solar, large radiators, and in space fluid distribution. We will build these satellites at a scale that far exceeds even Starlink. &nbsp;</p> <p>We are seeking talented Mechanical Engineers to own the full lifecycle of the hardware that make Starmind possible.</p> <p>We will be developing</p> <ul> <li>Large, fluid-based deployable radiator</li> <li>Biggest deployable solar arrays flown on SpaceX satellites</li> <li>Packaging at high volume for compute trays</li> <li>Satellite mechanisms + other high power satellite payloads</li> <li>Optical and networking payloads</li> </ul> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong>&nbsp;</p> <ul> <li>Own hardware from conceptual design through high volume production and on-orbit operation for the Starmind constellation&nbsp;</li> <li>Develop design criteria, collaborate on requirements, and drive system-level optimization&nbsp;</li> <li>Rapidly iterate on designs and analysis to inform high level systems trades and steer overall product direction&nbsp;</li> <li>Design for extreme high volume - drive holistic DFM to create elegant designs with a focus on piece part and process count reductions, error proofing at every step of fabrication and integration, and consistent performance and production metrics</li> <li>Establish an efficient product lifecycle starting in the supply chain all the way through final integration that balances cost, complexity, and quality; work closely with partner teams to design and realize an efficient in-house production line</li> <li>Perform environmental and performance testing on hardware to validate analysis and demonstrate compliance to design criteria</li> <li>Own product delivery timeline through conception, design, assembly, and launch</li> <li>Demonstrate extreme ownership of product outcomes at every stage of development and production&nbsp;</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong>&nbsp;</p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in an engineering discipline&nbsp;</li> <li>Experience with CAD and FEA software packages&nbsp;</li> <li>1+ years of professional experience (including internships) with mechanical/electromechanical design, analysis, testing, and/or manufacturing</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong>&nbsp;</p> <ul> <li>Master’s degree in engineering or a related technical discipline</li> <li>3+ years of professional experience in mechanical design and analysis</li> <li>2+ years of hands-on project experience with complex mechanical systems, preferably as a team lead</li> <li>Proficient in 3D CAD (NX preferred)</li> <li>Solid understanding and application of GD&amp;T</li> <li>Demonstrated understanding of structural analysis and failure modes of complex mechanical systems</li> <li>Prior ownership of a complex component or assembly from initial design through high-volume production ramp</li> <li>Self-motivated with strong organizational, written, and oral communication skills&nbsp;</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS</strong></p> <ul> title: Mechanical Engineer, Cabin Structures (Crew Starship)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>MECHANICAL ENGINEER, CABIN STRUCTURES (CREW STARSHIP)</strong></p> <p>After 50 years, humankind will once again return to the surface of the moon using SpaceX’s new vehicle, Crew Starship (also known as HLS or the Human Landing System) – this time for good. Starship will usher in the next era of crewed spaceflight and exploration, ultimately allowing us to establish permanent communities on the Moon, Mars, and beyond. As a Mechanical Engineer on the Crew Starship team, you will design and build spacecraft systems that are critical to the success and safety of future astronauts. Disciplines within this team include primary and secondary structures, mechanisms, and crew-interfacing hardware. Your design solutions will be driven by all future Crew Starship missions (Lunar, Mars, etc.). This role requires full hardware ownership, from initial design requirements and concepts all the way through design, analysis, prototype, qualification, and integration.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Own the design and development of next generation structures, mechanisms, or interior systems for Crew Starship vehicles</li> <li>Perform hand calculations and FEA to develop, assess, and optimize designs</li> <li>Rapidly iterate on manufacturing processes and development testing in a fast-paced environment</li> <li>Collaborate with interdisciplinary teams to ensure hardware integrates with Starship systems and supports necessary mission operations</li> <li>Lead design reviews internally and externally with suppliers and customers (e.g., NASA)</li> <li>Negotiate complex trade studies to optimize for cost, schedule, safety, and performance, among other considerations</li> <li>Be responsible for project delivery timeline from early design through production, launch, and recovery</li> <li>Exemplify technical excellence and be accountable for your work</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS </strong></p>
