title: Mechanical Engineer, Hardware Reliability (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>MECHANICAL ENGINEER, HARDWARE RELIABILITY (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is leveraging our experience building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s largest satellite constellation and most advanced broadband internet system. We provide reliable and fast internet to millions of users worldwide, including populations with little or no connectivity, rural communities, aircraft, watercraft, and places where existing services are unreliable, too expensive, or disconnected by natural disasters. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system, thousands of satellites and consumer antennae that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing. The Starlink team is seeking out the best-in-class professionals to maximize Starlink’s potential for communities and businesses around the globe.</p> <p>The Hardware Reliability Team at Starlink is an interdisciplinary team that is committed to the reliability of the mechanical and electrical hardware required to connect our customers to our satellites.&nbsp;Your breadth of exposure will span across dozens of areas (mechanical, electrical, RF, software, test, etc.) as you collaborate with core groups at SpaceX to bring hardware from initial concept development to full-scale high-volume production.</p> <p>You will use data to understand the factors that drive process and product reliability in design and manufacturing. You will dive deep into the details to identify, understand, and solve difficult technical problems to influence product design and manufacturing processes. You will be exposed to a hands-on environment that will enable you to spend time on the factory floor and in the test lab to improve the reliability of hardware and, ultimately, the user experience.&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Develop and implement reliability test strategies for new products and their subcomponents to maximize field life and minimize early life failures</li> <li>Develop, implement, and validate test and inspection processes for new and existing products and production processes, ensuring that criteria are objective and that reliability goals are consistently met</li> <li>Design and execute novel environmental, RF, mechanical, and electrical testing techniques tailored to the product and its functions</li> <li>Write test programs to exercise the functionality of the product over various conditions and environments</li> <li>Automate reliability test initiatives and reporting using proper data visualization techniques and thorough knowledge of the product and its functions</li> <li>Define the ongoing reliability testing strategy to monitor the manufacturing process and screen for long-term reliability defects caused by process and component variability</li> <li>Monitor product and process quality through production ramp-up using a suite of analysis tools, and drive improvements to areas that are under-performing&nbsp;in terms of key quality metrics</li> <li>⁠Investigate failures in production and test, identifying and mitigating the immediate and underlying root causes in order to reduce risk and improve reliability of designs and processes</li> <li>⁠Contain suspect or known non-conforming product, providing guidance to production representatives and engineers to assist in quarantining and rework activities</li> <li>Work closely with hardware, software, manufacturing, and network engineering teams to maximize reliability across all disciplines</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering or other engineering discipline</li> <li>1+ years of experience in test, analysis, manufacturing, or hardware development (internship and project experience is applicable)</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Experience with both electronics and mechanical design and analysis including knowledge of RF principles</li> <li>Programming experience in Python, C, and SQL with an emphasis on data analysis and automation</li> <li>Demonstrated capability to think creatively and solve complex problems with little to no supervision and on schedule, both as an individual or as a member of an integrated team</li> <li>Experience in a fast-paced, iterative design environment within the consumer electronics, mobile handset, medical devices, aerospace, marine, or automotive industries</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Ability title: Mechanical Engineer, Machine Design (Starship)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>MECHANICAL ENGINEER, MACHINE DESIGN (STARSHIP)</strong></p> <p>As a member of the Starship Tooling team, you will work with a team of elite engineers across multiple disciplines to design, build, and activate critical production assets required to build the Starship launch vehicle. This position is based at our&nbsp;Starship production facility in Brownsville, Texas but may involve work on designs that are implemented across all of SpaceX’s sites supporting the Starship program.&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:&nbsp;</strong></p> <ul> <li>Design, build, and activate custom machinery and infrastructure to enable the production and handling of Starship launch vehicles</li> <li>Develop the Starfactory and Gigafactory of the future to enable rapid build, test, and operation of our transport architectures</li> <li>Collaborate with vehicle engineers to influence vehicle design and manufacturing processes to maximize production rate</li> <li>Use your technical knowledge to execute on structural sizing, mechanism design, hardware fabrication, and activation testing to deliver results on projects</li> <li>Create detailed models and engineering prints in NX</li> <li>Perform engineering hand calculations and analysis to size structures and mechanisms.</li> <li>Create manufacturing planning for scope performed by internal welding and toolmaking teams.</li> <li>Support machine activation with controls engineering team and perform development testing with production engineering team.</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in an engineering discipline</li> <li>Experience using a CAD software design package (e.g. Solidworks, NX, CATIA, or ProE)</li> <li>1+ years of total experience in one or more of the following: involvement with an outside&nbsp;of the classroom project designing and building mechanical structures; academic research on mechanical structures; professional experience designing and analyzing mechanical structures</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Ability to prioritize and execute tasks in a fast-paced, dynamic environment</li> <li>Ability to work in a collaborative team environment, including daily interactions with engineers, technicians, suppliers, and leadership</li> <li>Experience working in a production facility with equipment and machinery</li> <li>Experience managing large CAD assembly models and drawings</li> <li>Experience with finite element analysis</li> <li>Experience designing and fabricating mass efficient welded structures</li> <li>Experience designing and testing mechanisms</li> <li>Strong understanding and application of GD&amp;T</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Ability to pass Air Force background check for Cape Canaveral</li> <li>Ability to work extended hours and weekends as necessary</li> <li>Willing to travel to other SpaceX locations as necessary</li> <li>Work schedule may vary depending on site operational needs, and flexibility is required</li> <li>Lifting, standing, climbing, bending, grasping, sitting, pulling, pushing, stooping, stretching, and carrying are generally required to perform the functions of this position</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. title: Mechanical Engineer, Mechanisms (Crew Starship)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>MECHANICAL ENGINEER, MECHANISMS (CREW STARSHIP)</strong></p> <p>After 50 years, humankind will once again return to the surface of the moon using SpaceX’s new vehicle, Crew Starship (also known as HLS or the Human Landing System) – this time for good. Starship will usher in the next era of crewed spaceflight and exploration, ultimately allowing us to establish permanent communities on the Moon, Mars, and beyond. As a Mechanical Engineer on the Crew Starship team, you will design and build spacecraft systems that are critical to the success and safety of future astronauts. Disciplines within this team include primary and secondary structures, mechanisms, and crew-interfacing hardware. Your design solutions will be driven by all future Crew Starship missions (Lunar, Mars, etc.). This role requires full hardware ownership, from initial design requirements and concepts all the way through design, analysis, prototype, qualification, and integration.&nbsp;</p> title: Mechanical Engineer, Tower/Launch and Test
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>MECHANICAL ENGINEER, TOWER/LAUNCH AND TEST</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is committed to developing revolutionary space technology, with the ultimate goal of enabling people to live on other planets. As a mechanical and/or fluids engineer on the starship launch pad and test site, you will support the development of SpaceX's Starship Tower, Launch Mount, and test stands, part of a fully reusable transportation system designed to launch both crew and cargo to Earth orbit, the Moon, Mars, and beyond.</p> <p>Engineers in this role are responsible for hardware development from initial system architecting through the design, analysis, manufacturing, integration, activation, and operational phases. Mechanical engineers design welded structures, large-scale mechanisms, electromechanical &amp; fluid power actuation systems, and fluid systems, including hydraulic and cryogenic.&nbsp;These systems are involved with performing proof and static fire testing of individual Starship stages<em>, </em>stacking the vehicle on the launch pad, loading propellant before launch, releasing fluid and structural connections at T-0, catching both stages when they return to the launch site, and configuring the vehicles to a safe state post-catch so they can be rapidly reflown. The Starship program is focused on rapid iteration and improvement, which enables engineers to continuously innovate and advance technology throughout the life of the program. The overarching goal of the launch mount team is to get to a ZERO refurbishment state where the pad can launch one vehicle and immediately be ready to launch again.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Drive hardware development for systems within the Starship tower, launch mount and test stands from basic architecture through design, analysis, scheduling, manufacturing, activation, and operational phases</li> <li>Own design and manufacturing of mechanisms, actuation systems, fluid systems, and large structures</li> <li>Perform structural, dynamic, thermal, and fluids analysis as necessary to determine requirements and to optimize the design of these systems &nbsp;</li> <li>Work closely with software and operation engineers to develop the concept of operations for launch mount systems with the goal of developing robust, fault tolerant systems and software that perform every time in the varying extreme conditions of a launch environment</li> <li>Collaborate with engineers designing the Starship and Super Heavy vehicles to determine how the tower, launch mount, and vehicle can work together most effectively</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in an engineering discipline</li> <li>1+ years of experience with CAD and FEA software packages</li> <li>1+ years of experience with mechanical or fluid systems design, analysis, and hands-on assembly (internship or project team experience qualify)</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Master’s degree in engineering or a related technical discipline</li> <li>3+ years of professional experience in mechanical design and analysis</li> <li>2+ years of hands-on project experience with complex mechanical systems, preferably as a lead</li> <li>Solid understanding and application of GD&amp;T and manufacturing techniques</li> <li>Demonstrated understanding of structural analysis and failure modes of complex mechanical systems and weldments</li> <li>Self-motivated with strong organizational, written, and oral communication skills</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Tower and launch mount hardware is typically built in tight quarters at high elevations, and physical dexterity is required</li> <li>Ability to work extended hours and weekends as necessary</li> <li>Stand: Up to 6 hours per day</li> <li>Sit: Up to 6 hours per day</li> <li>Push/Pull: Up to ≤ 50 lbs. title: Mechanical Process Engineer, PCB (Starlink/Starmind)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>MECHANICAL PROCESS ENGINEER, PCB (STARLINK/STARMIND)</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is leveraging our experience building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s largest satellite constellation and most advanced broadband internet system. We provide reliable and fast internet to millions of users worldwide, including populations with little or no connectivity, rural communities, aircraft, watercraft, and places where existing services are unreliable, too expensive, or disconnected by natural disasters. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system, thousands of satellites and consumer antennae that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing. The Starlink team is seeking out the best-in-class professionals to maximize Starlink’s potential for communities and businesses around the globe.</p> <p>As a Mechanical Engineer on Starlink, you will spearhead state-of-the-art production processes for our printed circuit boards (PCBs). This position is responsible for the development and implementation of all equipment, facilities, tooling, and manufacturing process technologies necessary to scale production to high volumes. You will design and implement advanced manufacturing processes and automation, owning your projects from conception and factory design through machine installation, commissioning, factory ramp, and process optimization. You will design and run large, hands-on process Design of Experiments (DOE), optimize complex mechanical and chemical process equipment, and interact regularly with senior leadership during critical design phases. By the end of this year, the Starlink factory in Bastrop will be the largest PCB manufacturing facility, by volume, in North America.</p> <p>Your work will form the backbone for millions of next generation consumer-facing devices that we ship directly to customers and businesses all over the world. From private homes, RVs, planes, or boats, this team plays an instrumental role in leveling the playing field for high-speed connectivity.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Develop, implement, and maintain new and/or improved manufacturing processes, equipment, technologies, and facilities; examples could include laser and mechanical Computer Numerical Control (CNC) drilling machines, advanced inductive lamination machines, plasma etching chambers, screen printing and inkjet printing adhesives, automation cells, copper etching and plating lines, etc.</li> <li>Analyze production processes and machinery from a first principles, physics-based approach</li> <li>Lead Design of Experiments (DOE) to establish a stable and robust process that can be handed off to production personnel; perform defect characterization and analysis to determine root cause and develop action plans to improve yields</li> <li>Develop project plans, budgets, and cost/benefit analysis for implementation of new processes or machines</li> <li>Own and perform machine activation and testing with a small team of engineers and technicians</li> <li>Solve technical and emergent issues from manufacturing (part quality, machine reliability, process instability, etc.)</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in engineering discipline</li> <li>1+ years of experience with fluids, mechanical, electromechanical design, and/or analysis (internship or project team experience is applicable)</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Master’s degree in engineering or a related technical discipline</li> <li>2+ years hands-on project experience with complex fluid or mechanical based production systems in a professional setting, preferably as a lead</li> <li>3+ years of professional experience in design and analysis</li> <li>Experience with taking products from research and development into production.</li> <li>Experience with PCB manufacturing processes like metal plating, chemical etching, CNC drill equipment, lamination presses, cleanroom equipment, etc.</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS</strong></p> <ul> <li>Willingness to travel to other SpaceX sites and/or vendors for potentially extended periods of time including international</li> <li>Ability to lift 25 lbs. unassisted</li> <li>Lifting, standing, climbing, bending, grasping, sitting, pulling, pushing, stooping, stretching, and carrying are generally required to perform the functions of this position</li> <li>Willing to work onsite; remote work is not considered</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. OPERATIONS)</strong></p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES</strong></p> <ul> <li>Serve as Launch Weather Officer (LWO) for orbital launch, return-to-launch-site, re-entry, recovery, and test operations—owning weather workflows from forecast, balloon, and sensor data through countdown, launch commit criteria, contingency response, and post-flight data review</li> <li>Develop new decision-support forecast tools, integrate probabilistic forecast information into operator tools, and train operators and end-users of forecasts</li> <li>Improve launch availability by developing new weather tools, improving launch commit criteria, and coordination with SpaceX launch operations and the external weather stakeholders that support launch and re-entry operations</li> <li>Lead projects on weather-sensor architecture, numerical weather prediction tools, launch commit criteria, including NASA LLCCs, and marine/recovery weather</li> <li>Generate rocket launch, landing, and recovery forecasts against vehicle constraints, NASA Lightning Launch Commit Criteria (NASA-STD-4010), and 14 CFR Part 450 weather requirements</li> <li>Conduct numerical weather prediction analysis and testing; interpret model guidance (NBM, GFS, RRFS, CMC, ECMWF, GraphCast, HAFS, and other AI and ensemble variants) against measured conditions and communicate results to launch/flight control, pad operations, recovery, and leadership</li> <li>Drive requirements, procurement, calibration, installation, quality control, and operational use of mesonets, electric-field mills, radar, weather balloons, and related instrumentation</li> <li>Integrate the weather sensor suite and gridded model data into automation, dashboards, and decision-support tools</li> <li>Collaborate closely with peers, operators, Range, Recovery, Flight Safety, and external stakeholders to ensure reliable launch-weather support and drive initiatives that support Starship launch-rate growth</li> <li>Support Dragon undock, re-entry, and splashdown weather, and marine forecasts for Atlantic, Gulf, and Pacific recovery and vessel operations</li> <li>Provide nowcasts and alerts for hazardous weather including severe thunderstorms, lightning, tropical cyclones, flooding, marine, and heat risks</li> <li>Represent SpaceX with NASA, United States Space Force range weather organizations, National Weather Service, and other core partners</li> <li>Interface with NASA Lightning Advisory Panel, FAA Common Standards Working Group, and other university research to operations groups to drive improvement in LLCC constraints for all launch and re-entry vehicles</li> <li>Travel to and operate from Cape Canaveral, Vandenberg, Starbase, Hawthorne, and other launch/test/development sites as EXPERIENCE</strong></p> <ul> <li>Experience as a Launch Weather Officer, range weather officer, or equivalent for orbital launch, aviation, or marine weather operations</li> <li>Experience presenting executive leadership and key decision-makers; includes hurricanes, severe weather, launch forecasting, flooding, and other Impact-based Decision Support Services (IDSS) functions</li> <li>Combination of training and experience that has led to qualification as a forecaster by the National Weather Service or a U.S. or NATO military authority</li> <li>Familiarity with NASA Lightning Launch Commit procurement, installation, calibration, and operational use</li> <li>Experience conducting model and forecast verification and familiarity with probabilistic modeling techniques</li> <li>Familiarity with Linux, Python, JavaScript, InfluxDB, Grafana, or similar tools, and the ability to integrate gridded model data into weather communication tools</li> <li>AI-assisted programming or scripting associated with weather-sensor integration and automation</li> <li>Marine forecasting experience, including routing or recovery decision support</li> <li>Background coordinating multi-vehicle or briefings for operators and external stakeholders; comfort owning documentation and process reliability</li> <li>Experience building training or qualification programs for operations personnel</li> onboarding programs for Launch Weather Officers and meteorology support, including off-nominal, severe-weather, and hurricane operations</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS</strong></p> <ul> title: New Graduate Engineer, Civil/Structural (Starship)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>NEW GRADUATE ENGINEER, CIVIL/STRUCTURAL (STARSHIP)</strong></p> <p>Our Starbase team is working on the toughest and most audacious project on our planet: making humanity multiplanetary. Our team is designing, building, and activating the civil and structural infrastructure that enables high-volume rocket production, launch pad operations, and Starbase's growth as a world-class facility. Our civil and structural engineers design, analyze, and deliver steel and concrete structures, site development, utilities, and launch infrastructure across the Starship program. Expect a dynamic role where you do what you’re best at. Whatever your skill set, you’ll be aligned to the part of the program you’re most effectively able to contribute to (structural design and analysis, civil site development, construction management, drafting, or field engineering). If you are a high-performing engineer, want to immerse yourself in never-before-solved challenges, and are excited to put in the effort to make this goal a reality, we want to hear from you.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Own the design and development of civil and structural systems for next-generation launch pads, production facilities, and site infrastructure</li> <li>Develop and issue drawings, design documentation, and reports for aerospace, industrial, commercial, and residential-type projects</li> <li>Perform civil and structural design and analysis calculations for structural steel and concrete</li> <li>Perform calculations necessary for grading and drainage, stormwater control facilities, water quality, domestic water distribution, and other underground utilities</li> <li>Collaborate with interdisciplinary teams to ensure civil and structural designs integrate with all Starship systems and support necessary mission operations</li> <li>Provide direct onsite engineering inspections and field observations; design switching power converters, signal conditioning, filters, and high-integrity layouts; support hardware through production, integration, and flight while collaborating across teams (EEE, EMI, radiation, propulsion, structures, GNC, etc.)</li> <li>Rapidly develop high-reliability avionics components (sensors, power systems, network interfaces, propulsion interfaces, data acquisition); drive system trades, requirements, component selection, schematic capture, prototyping, bring-up, debugging, analysis, testing (acceptance/qualification), documentation, manufacturing support, and flight support</li> <li>Participate in conceptual development of automated equipment and processes for Starship production</li> <li>Troubleshoot issues hands-on, support technicians, and ensure safe, efficient operation of systems in dynamic environments</li> <li>Design, build, operate, and maintain the various microgrids that comprise Starbase, TX</li> <li>Create and maintain sitewide power budgets, monitoring, and metering for mission-critical assets to optimize visibility and efficiency</li> <li>Ensure compliance with NFPA 70, 70B, 70E, NESC, and IEEE standards, prioritizing safety and engineering excellence</li> <li>Develop and implement protective relay settings and schemes for high-voltage equipment</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Graduating with a bachelor’s degree, master’s degree or PhD in 2027</li> <li>Degree in an electrical engineering, computer engineering, or other engineering discipline</li> <li>1+ years of electrical experience with power systems, automation &amp; This is a fast-paced, hands-on, constantly evolving, real-as-it-gets engineering environment for the ambitious. Some engineering groups design, build, activate, modify, and maintain the fluid and mechanical systems that power, restrain, and measure the most powerful high-volume rocket engines in the world, while others&nbsp;specialize in the design and execution of unique tests for engines, components, and spacecraft on an accelerated schedule.&nbsp;From thousands of gallons per minute of cryogens to tens of pounds per second of high-pressure gas, we develop clever solutions to meet the needs of a demanding test program both today and in the future.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> Our electrical engineers build some of the most advanced electronics ever flown in space, at a cost and rate previously considered unthinkable in the space industry. Become a part of this fast-moving and world-class electrical team. You’ll work with motivated engineers to achieve truly audacious goals. If you’re ready for a challenge and would like to help make our civilization multi-planetary, then you’ve come to the right place!</p> <p>Your placement on these teams will be determined throughout the interview process after factoring in technical fit, expertise, and your personal preference. Sub-teams include, but are not limited to:</p> <ul> <li>Avionics: robust electronics for sensors, power, networking, and data acquisition that fly on the world’s most powerful rocket</li> <li>Automation &amp; We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system – thousands of satellites, consumer receivers that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing, and the software that brings it all together. We’ve only begun to scratch the surface of Starlink’s potential global impact and are looking for best-in-class engineers to help maximize Starlink’s utility for communities and businesses around the globe.</p> <p>As arguably SpaceX's most complex software engineering challenge, Starlink offers a variety of areas within software engineering that you can focus. As a Software Engineer on the Starlink program, you will be solving challenges underpinning every aspect of the program’s growth. The teams and areas you could have an impact on could include, but are not limited to:</p> <ul> <li>Next generation networking technologies to direct data through an ever-changing network of satellites, ground stations, planes and users.</li> <li>Firmware, embedded and controls software running on custom hardware that flies the world’s largest fleet of spacecraft.</li> <li>Infrastructure and tools to enable rapid development and reliable deployment of our code to dynamic production environments.</li> <li>Measurement system software and hardware, supporting our in-house RF Silicon designs.</li> <li>Physic based software engineering to design and simulate the orbital life cycle of the Starlink constellation.&nbsp;</li> <li>Develop software running on custom hardware that is deployed to millions of devices around the world</li> <li>Create infrastructure and tools for rapid and reliable deployment of our code to our customers no matter where they are</li> <li>Write software for Starlink’s custom phased array and modem silicon</li> </ul> <p>Our software engineers are responsible for the complete lifecycle of the software they create, including development, testing, and support. title: Operations Analyst, Reliability (Starship)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>OPERATIONS ANALYST, RELIABILITY (STARSHIP)</strong></p> <p>At SpaceX, the Build and Flight Reliability team ensures hardware—from engines to fully integrated vehicles—is built to the highest standards and performs flawlessly on missions to make humanity multiplanetary. This team bridges manufacturing excellence with mission-critical reliability, developing data-driven tools and processes to identify, mitigate, and prevent risks from factory floor to flight. As a Reliability Analyst, you'll develop and maintain data-driven tooling and infrastructure to guide decisions, with a focus on identifying AI opportunities, defining and leading AI-driven solutions for predictive analytics, automation, and risk mitigation. You'll drive sustainable improvements to reduce build failures and boost vehicle performance, partnering with software engineering for AI workflow deployment into agents or enterprise systems.</p> <p>In this role, you'll collaborate across teams to turn production and test data into insights, own build-to-flight metrics, and drive improvements in a fast-paced environment.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:&nbsp;</strong></p> <ul> <li>Identify opportunities in reliability processes (e.g., predictive modeling, anomaly detection); define problems, develop prompts/workflows using LLMs or generative AI, evaluate outputs, monitor performance, provide go-live support, and create operational protocols—partnering with software engineering to define implementation direction while maintaining ownership of outcomes.</li> <li>Design, implement, and maintain dashboards (e.g., Grafana, PowerBI, Tableau, SQL reports) for monitoring build metrics (defect rates, tolerances, nonconformances) and flight indicators.</li> <li>Maintain and optimize dashboards and tools for ongoing accuracy and usability, including troubleshooting issues, updating data feeds, and ensuring seamless integration with user workflows across production, quality, and reliability teams.</li> <li>Improve data infrastructure (pipelines, ETL, schemas) for scalability, integrity, and real-time use, with ownership of data integrity to support reliable AI tools and initiatives.</li> <li>Develop/track KPIs for build health and flight risk, including yields, pass rates, traceability, and predictive models to inform decisions and actions.</li> <li>Analyze datasets (SQL, Python) to find root causes of anomalies, correlate build/flight data, and recommend solutions; use AI for pattern recognition and forecasting.</li> <li>Collaborate with production, design, reliability, and software teams to define data requirements for emerging use cases, such as integrating build data with flight test results, and develop automation scripts to mitigate risks, streamline reporting, and enhance efficiencies.</li> <li>Create ad-hoc queries, reports, and simulations for workflows, nonconformances, constraints, and gaps.</li> <li>Standardize data capture for manufacturing processes (e.g., welding, assembly, NDE, and checkouts), ensuring comprehensive traceability and feedback loops that capture lessons learned from builds and flights to prevent repeat issues.</li> <li>Train users/leaders on tools, data interpretation, AI workflows, and best practices; share knowledge to build expertise in analytics and AI.</li> <li>Actively contribute creative thinking and leadership to solving complex problems under tight deadlines, with a focus on "reliability by any means necessary" to align production scaling with mission success.</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree.</li> <li>1+ years in building and operating metric based dashboards.</li> <li>1+ years of experience building data structures and query optimizations.</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Experience in a manufacturing or engineering environment.</li> <li>Experience working in in a factory or production environment.</li> <li>3+ years of experience with SQL, Python, C++, Tableau, or PowerBI.</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Ability to work extended hours, weekends, and offsite as needed.</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. title: Operations Engineer (Starship)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. We design, build, activate, and improve the fluid systems that fuel Starship. Development is the job: hardware you design can be made, installed, and tested the same day. From tens of thousands of gallons per minute of cryogen to tens of pounds per second of high-pressure gas, you’ll solve real pad problems every day for a demanding launch and test program.</p> title: Operations Engineer, Starbase Infrastructure
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>OPERATIONS ENGINEER, STARBASE INFRASTRUCTURE</strong></p> <p>Starbase infrastructure — site power, HVAC, facilities, production fluids, industrial gas, water, and wastewater — is run by technician shops. This Operations Engineer standardizes how those shops plan, execute, and close work so the site runs as one operating system. Match existing SpaceX / site standards where they work; write a unique process only when the circumstances require it, and say why. When something is broken or slow, pick the lever: a tool (including software and AI), a physical change, or a people standard. Warp work orders, PMs, punch lists, and labor hours should mean the same thing in every shop. You write WOs for the initiatives you own; supervisors and leads own the daily flow.&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:&nbsp;</strong></p> <ul> <li>Standardize how work is requested, planned, executed, and closed across all infrastructure shops. One WO / PM / estimate / closeout standard, with documented exceptions where a system (MV electrical, TCEQ water, cryogenic gas, etc.) requires them</li> <li>Adopt company and site standards (Warp, Foundation, LOTO, MOC, commissioning turnover) and pull in processes from other SpaceX plants where they fit</li> <li>Choose the fix: software / AI / data, a physical or tooling change, or a personnel skill and behavior standard. Be explicit which lever you are using and why it is the right one for that problem</li> <li>Define and improve the work-management system: Warp / Foundation work orders, PM and PdM backlog, kitting, as-found / as-left closeout, critical spares. Write WOs to support the initiatives you are driving; supervisors and engineering own daily WO writing and planning releases</li> <li>Give shops visibility they can staff against: time estimates vs actuals, remaining hours, and which jobs are blocking a customer</li> <li>Own commissioning and operational-readiness for new or modified systems: punch lists, first PMs, mBOM / spare setup, procedures, and trained turnover to operations</li> <li>Translate design packages (one-lines, P&amp;IDs, vendor submittals, construction RFPs) into isolation plans, LOTO, work instructions, and hold points the floor can execute</li> <li>Stand up asset identity for equipment that is still informal: what it is, what feeds it, what PM it gets, where the WO lives</li> <li>Put numbers on the shops: availability, PM compliance, WO aging, estimate accuracy, contractor vs in-house mix; brief supervisors and site leadership</li> <li>Write the procedures the shops actually use and teach leads and technicians the standard — you succeed when the shop runs it without you in the room, including the cases that stay unique on purpose&nbsp;</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:&nbsp;</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in an engineering discipline</li> <li>1+ years of professional experience in industrial plant, central plant, utilities, facilities, power generation, process operations, or maintenance engineering&nbsp;</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:&nbsp;</strong></p> <ul> <li>2+ years in a process plant, municipal or industrial utility, semiconductor or data-center facilities, shipyard, or similar 24/7 plant</li> <li>Hands-on work management: Warp, Foundation, Maximo, SAP PM, or equivalent CMMS; you can write and close a work order to support an initiative</li> <li>Experience reading P&amp;IDs, electrical one-lines, and OEM manuals, and writing a procedure a technician can follow on night shift</li> <li>Experience commissioning or standing up operational-readiness of new equipment (punch list through first PMs and spare setup)</li> <li>Working knowledge of LOTO, MOC, confined space, and energized / pressurized systems</li> <li>Familiarity with at least two of: medium-voltage or industrial electrical; HVAC / BMS; industrial gas or compressed air; water / wastewater; rotating equipment</li> <li>TCEQ public water / wastewater or similar permitted-plant exposure</li> <li>Practical use of SQL, Power BI, scripting, or AI to remove clerk work from WOs, PMs, and reports, with judgment for when the right answer is a technician skill</li> <li>Experience overseeing contractors and vendors on a live industrial site</li> <li>Ability to work well in an integrated collaborative team environment, including frequent interactions with technicians, engineers, and leadership</li> <li>Internships, clubs, or other hands-on extra-curricular activities qualify&nbsp;</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:&nbsp;</strong></p> <ul> <li>Ability to work extended hours, weekends, and offsite as needed</li> <li>Must be able to work in extreme outdoor environments when needed — heat, cold, wind, rain</li> <li>Must be able to lift 25 lbs. unassisted, climb ladders, and walk the plants and shops you support</li> <li>This position is based in Starbase, TX (Brownsville / Boca Chica) and requires being onsite – remote work not considered</li> <li>Must be willing to travel to other SpaceX sites when needed (up to 15%)&nbsp;</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. title: Paint & Coatings Technician
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>PAINT &amp; COATINGS TECHNICIAN</strong></p> <p>As a member of the construction projects and facilities team, the paint &amp; coatings technician mixes, strips, paints, and details advanced paint systems, prepares metallic substrates via abrasion and etchants, applies sealants/adhesives, maintains spraying equipment, and uses precision tools like calipers while supporting safety, quality, and delivery improvements. You will have the opportunity to drive positive changes in a fast-paced, low-drag environment. This technician owns tasks and projects from start to finish, with the goal of making the SpaceX campus a world-class test facility that can support the mission of enabling life beyond Earth.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Manage and coordinate ticket system requests for paint projects across the site to ensure timely and quality execution of work</li> <li>Prepare, prime, sand, seal, patch, and paint steel surfaces, buildings, and fixtures utilizing all types of painting materials such as varnish, lacquer, shellac, enamel, latex, epoxy, waterproofing, and heat-resistant finishes</li> <li>Tape, float, paint, and repair wall finishes and apply texture</li> <li>Operate, clean, and maintain all painting equipment, including brushes, rollers, sprayers, electrostatic sprayers, and pumps</li> <li>Safely store and label all materials on a daily basis</li> <li>Erect scaffolding, rigging, and ladders as necessary in a manner consistent with safety codes</li> <li>Operate and use required tools and equipment skillfully and safely</li> <li>Apply finishes to a wide variety of surfaces</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>High school diploma or equivalency certificate</li> <li>1+ years of experience as a painter in a residential, commercial, industrial, or manufacturing environment</li> <li>Experience painting projects indoors and outdoors</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Experience in commercial and industrial painting practices and processes, including the properties and application of paints, varnishes, lacquers, enamels, epoxies, paint removers, and related materials</li> <li>Familiarity with applicable code requirements, methods and practices for maintaining tools, machinery, and equipment</li> <li>5+ years of experience as a painter in a residential, commercial, industrial, or manufacturing environment</li> <li>Experience painting internal and external surfaces</li> <li>Ability to safely operate aerial platforms, lifts, man lifts, and heavy equipment</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Role may require extended hours, weekend work and shift schedules, that vary depending on site operational needs; flexibility required</li> <li>Physical dexterity and the ability to lift heavy objects are required in this position (up to 25lbs unassisted)</li> <li>Ability to perform job duties that require standing, kneeling, crouching, twisting the upper body, working in cramped positions in small openings, and climbing hand over hand</li> <li>Ability to work at elevated heights</li> <li>Typically exposed to work in extreme outdoor environments – heat, cold, rain</li> <li>Work performed in an environment title: PCB Technician (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>PCB TECHNICIAN (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is leveraging our experience building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s largest satellite constellation and most advanced broadband internet system. We provide reliable and fast internet to millions of users worldwide, including populations with little or no connectivity, rural communities, aircraft, watercraft, and places where existing services are unreliable, too expensive, or disconnected by natural disasters. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system, thousands of satellites and consumer antennae that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing. The Starlink team is seeking out the best-in-class professionals to maximize Starlink’s potential for communities and businesses around the globe.</p> <p>As a PCB Technician, you will be working on the many processes within printed circuit board manufacturing in the Starlink factory. This is a versatile and highly skilled, hands-on manufacturing job that includes operating production equipment, performing quality inspections, performing chemical analysis and additions, and handling chemical materials to meet the goals for output and quality. The ideal candidate is comfortable working in an electro-chemical manufacturing environment and is motivated by Starlink’s mission to provide high speed, low-latency connectivity across the globe.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Execute startup and shutdown procedures for production equipment</li> <li>Monitor process conditions, equipment, and control systems for state-of-the-art PCB manufacturing which may include metal plating lines, copper etching lines, soldermask printers, water treatment systems, plasma etching systems, laser or mechanical drilling machines, and lamination ovens</li> <li>Perform necessary interventions to maintain process parameters, including chemical analysis, additions, recipe changes, and machine adjustments</li> <li>Perform first-level troubleshooting, provide feedback, and work with maintenance and engineering teams to drive root cause of equipment downtime</li> <li>Track schedule and perform preventive maintenance and calibration of equipment and instruments</li> <li>Perform dispositions and rework for nonconforming PCBs</li> <li>Provide feedback on failure modes and support engineering to drive root cause of yield title: PECVD Process Engineer, Solar Cells (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong><span data-contrast="auto">PECVD PROCESS ENGINEER, SOLAR CELLS (STARLINK) </span></strong><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></p> <p><span data-contrast="auto">Starlink believes in providing fast, reliable internet to those that need it most. We design, build, and launch the world's largest and most advanced satellite constellation that is capable of delivering high-speed internet to even the most remote locations.&nbsp;</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></p> <p><span data-contrast="auto">As a solar cell process engineer on Starlink, you will spearhead state of the art production processes for an internal solar cell production line, providing high efficiency and high-quality solar cells for both our latest generation Starlink satellites and for Starship missions to the Moon and Mars. You will work through the life cycle of setting up a greenfield solar cell production plant, including equipment procurement, plant design/layout, equipment commissioning and ramp-up, recipe and process development, and working to develop a world-class production team and environment.</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></p> <p><span data-contrast="auto">As a PECVD Process Engineer, you will own the development, optimization, and scaling of Plasma-Enhanced Chemical Vapor Deposition (PECVD) processes critical for depositing the intrinsic and doped hydrogenated amorphous and nanocrystalline silicon layers that passivate the wafer surface and form the carrier-selective contacts of high-efficiency SHJ cells. You will develop and iterate on the manufacturing processes and recipes to achieve a state-of-the-art silicon cell efficiency, low defect rate and cost, and high reliability cell for space-based applications. Your work will form the backbone of the Starlink network (photons of sunlight in is directly proportional to photons of data out to customers!) and help provide internet to tens of millions of customers all around the world.&nbsp;</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></p> <p><strong><span data-contrast="auto">RESPONSIBILITIES:</span></strong><span data-contrast="auto"> </span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></p> <ul> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Design, qualify, and optimize PECVD processes for SHJ intrinsic passivation layers and p-type/n-type doped layers, ensuring film thickness uniformity, passivation quality (minority carrier lifetime, implied Voc), doping efficiency, and contact resistivity at GW-scale volumes</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Lead process development for new toolsets and materials, including gas chemistry, plasma power and frequency, pressure, temperature, and electrode gap optimization to support state of the art efficiency cells</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Own chamber conditioning strategy, including seasoning, in-situ/remote plasma clean recipes, and clean intervals, to control particles, cross-contamination, and run-to-run drift while maximizing tool uptime</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Partner closely with the CVD Equipment Engineering team on tool qualification, chamber matching, preventive maintenance recovery, and throughput (UPH) improvements</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Responsible for developing, implementing, and maintaining new and/or improved manufacturing processes, equipment, technologies, and facilities</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Analyze production processes and machinery from a first principles, physics-based approach</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Develop experiments to diagnose and correct manufacturing problems, utilizing robust DOE and statistical methodologies. Optimize process conditions and materials to improve the optical and electrical quality of solar cells</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Perform defect characterization and analysis to determine root cause and develop action plans to improve yields</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Develop project plans, budgets, and cost/benefit analysis for implementation of new processes or machines</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Own and perform machine activation and testing with a small team of engineers and technicians</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Prepare detailed content for technical design reviews. Demonstrate extreme ownership of the production outcome of the Starlink solar factory across yield, uptime, and cost</span></li> </ul> <p><strong><span data-contrast="auto">BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</span></strong><span data-contrast="auto"> </span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></p> <ul> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Bachelor’s degree in an engineering discipline</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">1+ years of experience in system design, analysis, and/or system implementation (internship and extracurricular experience is applicable)</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></li> </ul> <p><strong><span data-contrast="auto">PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</span></strong><span data-contrast="auto"> </span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></p> <ul> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Master’s degree or Ph.D. in chemistry, chemical engineering, materials science, physics, or related technical discipline</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">5+ years of hands-on experience in PECVD process engineering, preferably in SHJ/HJT or TOPCon solar, semiconductor, or display manufacturing</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Proven track record of scaling PECVD processes to high-volume production (&gt;1GW/year equivalent)</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Strong understanding of vacuum systems, plasma physics, gas-phase and surface chemistry, and thin-film growth of amorphous and nanocrystalline silicon</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Deep understanding of SHJ surface passivation and carrier-selective contacts, including epitaxial growth suppression, hydrogen content and bonding, and band alignment at the a-Si:H/c-Si interface</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Hands-on experience with thin-film and PV characterization techniques (e.g., spectroscopic ellipsometry, FTIR, Raman crystallinity, dark/photo conductivity, Sinton lifetime, PL/EL)</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Experience safely handling pyrophoric, toxic, and flammable process gases (e.g., silane, phosphine, diborane)</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Experience with SPC, DoE, and lean manufacturing principles</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Ability to work in a cleanroom environment</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Hands-on experience working with complex fluid or mechanical based production systems in a professional setting</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Experience transitioning products from design to manufacturing and scaling to high volume as part of a cross-functional team</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Self-motivated with strong organizational, written, and oral communication skills</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Experience with solar cell manufacturing equipment, such as wet chemical processing equipment, PE-CVD equipment, PVD machines, metallization and final test equipment, and wafer inspection equipment. Experience in hot-wire CVD, evaporation tools, and ALD tools are a plus.&nbsp;</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Experience or expertise with perovskite solar cells or perovskite tandem solar cells</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Experience with micro-structure analysis tools (SEM, TEM, EDX, SIMS, etc.) and optical/electrical characterization tools (UV-VIS, I-V, Resistance, etc.)</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Familiarity with large-area, high-throughput PECVD platforms (in-line and cluster/batch) and automation/integration for inline production</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Proficiency in data analysis/scripting (Python, R, SQL) and plasma or device simulation tools (e.g., COMSOL, Quokka, AFORS-HET)</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Experience in cost-of-ownership modeling, capex justification, and fab ramp-ups to multi-GW scales</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Passion for sustainable energy and space technology; prior work in photovoltaics at GW-scale a plus</span></li> </ul> <p><strong><span data-contrast="auto">ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</span></strong><span data-contrast="auto"> </span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></p> <ul> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Ability to travel frequently for work, potentially for extended periods of time during machine buyoffs and startup</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Ability to lift 25 lbs. unassisted</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Lifting, standing, climbing, bending, grasping, sitting, pulling, pushing, stooping, stretching, and carrying are generally required to perform the functions of this position</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Must be willing to work extended hours and weekends as needed</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. title: Piping Technician (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>PIPING TECHNICIAN (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is developing a low latency, broadband internet system to meet the needs of consumers across the globe. Enabled by a constellation of low Earth orbit satellites, Starlink will provide fast, reliable internet to populations with little or no connectivity, including those in rural communities and places where existing services are too expensive or unreliable. We are looking for talented, creative, and driven technicians to drive manufacturing output and yield. You will have ownership of one or more process areas and will have the opportunity to directly impact Starlink’s products. You will have frequent interaction with engineering teams and leadership and will participate in developing and validating new equipment, processes, and technologies. The success of Starlink depends on the quality, reliability, cost, manufacturability, throughput, security, and user experience of the products that you will manufacture.&nbsp;</p> <p>As a Piping Technician at&nbsp;Starlink, you will take ownership of state-of-the-art piping systems that support our&nbsp;Starlink User Terminal Production Facility—supporting our PCB operations (largest printed circuit fab in North America!) and our Chip Packaging Plant (featuring a&nbsp;state-of-the-art&nbsp;panel level packaging process). You will install, maintain, and repair&nbsp;all piping systems&nbsp;to ensure reliable water quality and system uptime for our partner teams in a fast-paced, innovative manufacturing environment.&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong>&nbsp;</p> <ul> <li>Install, assemble, modify, and maintain PVC piping systems, including solvent welding, threading, and mechanical joining for UPW and wastewater treatment processes</li> <li>Read and interpret P&amp;IDs, blueprints, isometric drawings, and technical specifications to route and install piping systems&nbsp;</li> piping modifications, as-built drawings, and spare parts inventory&nbsp;</li> <li>Safely handle and transport piping materials, fittings, and chemicals&nbsp;</li> <li>Ensure 5S standards are upheld by maintaining a clean and organized work area&nbsp;</li> <li>Perform other related duties, as assigned, for the purpose of ensuring an efficient and effective work environment&nbsp;</li> </ul> title: Power Electronics Engineer, AI Satellites (Starmind)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>POWER ELECTRONICS ENGINEER, AI SATELLITES (STARMIND)</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is leveraging its experience deploying and operating the world’s largest satellite constellation to develop Starmind, a new constellation of satellites capturing solar energy in space to power low-cost, high-performance AI compute for Earth. Realizing this vision demands highly reliable, high performance electrical hardware ranging from power electronics, high speed digital systems, mixed signal designs, robust avionics, networking, and custom compute electronics. These systems must operate in the extreme environment of space while delivering the connectivity, control, power distribution, and processing needed for orbital AI inference.</p> <p>Our Power Electronics team designs and develops the power conversion and control systems at the heart of Starmind satellites and orbital data centers — enabling the reliable, high-efficiency power delivery required for massive on-orbit AI compute. As a member of the team, your designs will run the gamut from low voltage to kV range, and powers from 1W to many kW (applications include high-density compute power delivery, battery systems, motors/actuators, propulsion, laser optical links, and other vehicle systems critical to orbital AI platforms).</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Provide engineering expertise in design, analysis, and testing of DC-DC power converters for harsh environments</li> <li>Work on electrical power system and sub-system level design trades and develop requirements</li> <li>Define and perform electrical power system verification testing and analysis</li> <li>Work with multidisciplinary teams of design, test, and production engineers to create new power electronics hardware</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, physics, or other STEM discipline</li> <li>1+ years of professional related field</li> <li>Strong grasp of analog control and discrete logic design</li> <li>Experience in modeling, simulation, and testing of power electronics</li> <li>Working experience in voltage and current mode control and compensation design</li> <li>Experience with AC-DC converters and power factor correction</li> <li>Strong grasp of DC-DC topologies, with ability to select optimal architectures and components</li> <li>Understanding of design for fault tolerance and reliability</li> <li>Familiar with failure mode effects and criticality analysis</li> <li>Familiarity with design loop-gain measurement</li> <li>Familiarity with spacecraft electrical power systems and knowledge of radiation effects</li> <li>Familiarity with lithium-ion battery handling, safety, and usage</li> jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong><span data-contrast="auto">POWER ELECTRONICS ENGINEER, CONSUMER HARDWARE &amp; GATEWAYS (STARLINK)</span></strong><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></p> <p><span data-contrast="auto">Starlink believes in providing fast, reliable internet to serve populations with little or no connectivity. We design, build, launch, and operate the world's largest constellation of satellites, enabling us to operate a global internet network unbounded by traditional ground infrastructure limitations. The root of SpaceX’s success so far lies in our mission to keep all engineering and production in-house, which enables a tight feedback loop, nimble decision-making, and speedy deliverables. With millions of daily users worldwide already online, Starlink is truly a game changer and levels the playing field for those who were previously unconnected.</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></p> <p><span data-contrast="auto">As a Power Electronics Engineer on Starlink in Bastrop, you could be responsible for the design and performance of next-generation gateways power electronics - ultimately ensuring that our ground station antenna hardware can withstand the harshest environmental conditions while maintaining reliable communication with millions of users on a global scale. These are challenging high power multi kW systems needing high performance and reliability. Alternatively, you could spearhead the design and development of the power supply for millions of consumer-facing devices that we ship directly to customers and businesses all over the world. Our customers currently include teachers in the most remote parts of the Amazon, researchers in Antarctica, digital nomads who travel via RV, emergency responders, commercial airlines, cruise lines, and residential users who live in more rural or developing areas. You will own hardware from cradle to grave and will interact regularly with senior leadership during critical design phases.</span><span title: Power Generation Engineer (Starship)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>POWER GENERATION ENGINEER</strong></p> <p>Join the Power Systems Engineering team at SpaceX to pioneer the design, build, operation, and maintenance of advanced power generation, transmission, and distribution systems for Starship's launch, production, propellant generation, and the city of Starbase, TX. As a power systems engineer, you'll work with a team to scale high-capacity electrical infrastructure for the world's most powerful rocket, ensuring seamless energy flow for groundbreaking missions. The position is based at Starbase, TX, with potential travel to other SpaceX facilities.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES</strong></p> <ul> <li>Design, build, operate, and maintain the various microgrids that comprise Starbase, TX.</li> <li>Collaborate with cross-functional teams; lead projects; and drive rapid, continuous improvements at Starbase launch sites.</li> <li>Be responsible for infrastructure upgrades to dynamically scale systems for Starship's production rate targets.</li> <li>Create and maintain sitewide power budgets, monitoring, and metering for mission-critical assets to optimize visibility and efficiency.</li> <li>Develop and execute asset strategies for high-power launch and grid infrastructure.</li> <li>Develop standardized designs for launch, propellant generation, and power delivery facilities.</li> <li>Performs detailed design on all aspects of electrical power systems: one-lines, three-lines, control/relaying schematics, wiring diagrams, SCADA, conduit/cable sizing/routing, grounding design, general arrangement, etc.</li> <li>Develops and implements protective relay settings and schemes for high voltage equipment.&nbsp;</li> <li>Maintain organized design and asset documentation for all Starbase launch and power facilities.</li> <li>Ensure compliance with NFPA 70, 70B, 70E, NESC, and IEEE standards, prioritizing safety and engineering excellence.</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, physics, or another engineering discipline.</li> <li>1+ years of experience in power systems design, analysis, and build, with a focus on high-power, high-voltage systems.</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCES</strong></p> <ul> <li>3+ years of professional experience in a similar role.</li> <li>Professional Engineering license or intention to actively seeking PE license.&nbsp;</li> <li>Experience with power systems analysis software and tools: ETAP, SKM, EasyPower, PowerWorld, Matlab, PSCAD, PSEE, Simulink, etc.</li> <li>Experience performing basic load flow, short-circuit, arc-flash, coordination, and transient stability studies.</li> <li>Familiarity with industrial power systems up to 345 kV, including switchgear, transformers, BESS, VFDs, motors, distribution systems, UPS/emergency backups, power generation, relaying, metering, protective devices, and networking.</li> <li>Familiarity with industrial communications protocols and networking: Modbus, IEEE C37.115, IEEE C37.111, DNP3, etc.</li> <li>Experience with CAD software: Revit, AutoCAD, NX, etc.</li> <li>Demonstrated initiative, creative problem-solving, and strong analytical/engineering fundamentals.</li> <li>Excellent written and verbal communication skills.</li> <li>Proven ability to lead teams, work independently, and thrive in dynamic, high-stress environments with tight deadlines.</li> <li>Strong organizational skills to prioritize, schedule, and implement solutions with minimal operational impact.</li> <li>Ability to quickly troubleshoot issues and support technicians hands-on.</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS</strong></p> <ul> <li>Perform hands-on work in all environments (heat, cold, rain), in tight quarters or at heights.</li> <li>Work extended hours and weekends as needed to support launch operations.</li> <li>Remain focused in hazardous environments while wearing appropriate PPE.</li> <li>Lift up to 25 lbs. unassisted.</li> <li>Provide 24/7 on-call support for emergencies.</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. Learn more about the ITAR <a href="https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/?id=ddtc_kb_article_page&amp;sys_id=24d528fddbfc930044f9ff621f961987">here</a>. &nbsp;</li> </ul> <p>SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.</p> <p>Applicants wishing to view a copy of SpaceX’s Affirmative Action Plan for veterans and individuals with disabilities, or applicants requiring reasonable accommodation to the application/interview process should reach out to&nbsp;<a href="mailto:EEOCompliance@spacex.com">EEOCompliance@spacex.com</a><em>.&nbsp;</em></p></div>

title: Power Plant Engineer
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>POWER PLANT ENGINEER</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is building and operating combined-cycle gas turbine power plants that must come online, stay online, and perform. This role owns the design and build of the full power plant: gas turbines, mechanical and electrical balance of plant, and everything else that keeps the plant running at rated output, day after day. This is not a desk job. You will be constructing the power plant, owning commissioning in the control room during startup, and in the field troubleshooting.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Support the full lifecycle of gas turbine power generation assets — installation, commissioning, startup, operations, and long-term maintenance</li> <li>Lead or support commissioning activities including combustion tuning, control system checkout, protective relay testing, and performance/reliability run verification</li> <li>Own root-cause analysis and corrective action for turbine trips, forced outages, and performance degradation; drive fixes that prevent recurrence</li> <li>Develop and refine operating procedures, startup/shutdown sequences, and abnormal operating condition playbooks</li> <li>Interface directly with OEMs (GE, Siemens Energy, Mitsubishi Power, Doosan) on warranty issues, LTSA scope, outage planning, and technical issues</li> <li>Plan and execute major/minor inspections, hot gas path outages, and combustion inspections in line with OEM maintenance intervals</li> <li>Analyze turbine performance data (heat rate, capacity factor, degradation curves) to identify efficiency losses and recommend corrective action</li> <li>Coordinate with balance-of-plant teams (HRSG, steam turbine, cooling systems, water treatment) to ensure integrated performance</li> <li>Build and maintain relationships with EPC contractors during construction handoff to ensure a clean transition from construction to commercial operation</li> <li>Develop spare parts strategy, critical spares inventory, and maintenance budgets</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. This is a hands-on role supporting day-to-day operations, maintenance, and troubleshooting at a power generation facility. You will inspect running equipment, respond to issues as they come up, restore systems, and keep generation and balance-of-plant online. You will work across mechanical, electrical, and controls equipment — pumps, piping, chillers, cooling towers, HVAC, generators, motors, water systems, UPS, switchgear, and plant control systems — following procedures and engineering direction in a fast-paced environment.</p> <p>This position entails ownership of equipment performance and reliability by monitoring process parameters and maintaining components, with a keen eye for leading indicators of instability or malfunction, and a drive to correct those issues in advance of undesirable events. Ideally, the operator has experience working with industrial processes that utilize engines, motors, fluid piping, electrical equipment, and instrumented controls.</p> self-report problems before they affect generation</li> <li>Identify equipment and process deviations and perform corrective actions</li> <li>Troubleshoot and repair operational issues found during interpret P&amp;IDs, schematics, data sheets/manuals, drawings, and equipment documentation</li> <li>Work with engineers and technicians to create operating procedures</li> <li>Write, follow, and execute MOPs, SOPs, and EOPs, and learn and run standard operating procedures on the machinery</li> <li>Support lockout/tagout, hot work, confined space, and site safety and environmental requirements</li> <li>Coordinate and support scheduled system shutdowns, outages, and utility events as directed</li> <li>Support commissioning by witnessing equipment start-up, assisting with jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not.
