title: Sr. Antenna Engineer (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>SR. ANTENNA ENGINEER (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is leveraging our experience building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation that provides fast, reliable internet to millions of users worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system – thousands of satellites, consumer receivers that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing, and the software that brings it all together. We’ve only begun to scratch the surface of Starlink’s potential global impact and are looking for best-in-class engineers to help maximize Starlink’s utility for communities and businesses around the globe.</p> <p>As a Sr. Starlink Antenna Engineer, you will have full ownership of all phased array, Wi-Fi, and other RF systems for this customer-facing hardware. Our customers currently include teachers in the most remote parts of the Amazon, researchers in Antarctica, digital nomads who travel via RV, emergency responders, commercial airlines, cruise lines, and residential users who live in more rural or developing areas. In addition, you will own advanced parabolic antenna systems for our gateways/ground stations, which we deploy regionally throughout the world. You will design, implement, and verify small router antennas, phased arrays, and reflector antenna systems. You will interact regularly with senior leadership to influence the fundamental operation of our constellation and network while collaborating with electrical, silicon, software, mechanical, and manufacturing teams to steer this project from initial concept development to full-scale production.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Design, fabricate, and characterize prototypes of antennas, feed systems, and RF front ends for next-generation phased arrays, gateways, and consumer wireless products</li> <li>Create electromagnetic simulation models of hardware (antennas, filters, PCB layout) to design and evaluate performance</li> <li>Work in close collaboration with electrical, mechanical, digital signal processing, and software engineering teams to design and validate RF systems</li> <li>Create and test phased array alignment solutions</li> <li>Rapidly develop design, validation, and production test solutions for our high-volume consumer products and gateway antennas</li> <li>Write automation software in python to interact with units under test, test equipment, instrumentation, and documentation systems</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering or other engineering discipline</li> <li>5+ years of professional experience with antennas or communication systems</li> <li>5+ years professional experience with radio test equipment such as spectrum analyzers, vector signal analyzers, vector signal generators, and network analyzers</li> <li>5+ years of professional programming experience in Python, C#, C++, or MATLAB</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Master’s degree or PhD in electrical engineering with emphasis in RF/antenna engineering</li> <li>Experience designing wireless communications systems</li> <li>Experience with basic principles of antenna theory</li> <li>Understanding of link budgets and analysis related to communications</li> <li>Thorough understanding of RF active and passive components</li> <li>Experience characterizing radio performance at microwave frequencies</li> <li>Experience title: Sr. Automation & Controls Engineer, Solar Cell Factory
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>SR. AUTOMATION &amp; CONTROLS ENGINEER, SOLAR CELL FACTORY (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>At SpaceX we’re leveraging our experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation and is providing fast, reliable internet to millions of users worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system – thousands of satellites, consumer receivers that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing, and the software that brings it all together. We’ve only begun to scratch the surface of Starlink’s potential global impact and are looking for best-in-class engineers to help maximize Starlink’s utility for communities and businesses around the globe.&nbsp;</p> <p>The Solar Cell team is revolutionizing power generation for space applications through advanced solar cell manufacturing. We're scaling production of high-efficiency solar cells to support sustainable energy solutions for Starlink constellations, launch vehicles, and beyond. As a Solar Cell Factory Sr. Automation and Controls Engineer, you will design, build, and optimize controls and automation systems for the production of solar cell manufacturing equipment and material movement mechanisms. This role requires a detail-oriented engineer passionate about safe electrical design, writing robust and elegant control code, and taking on total ownership of existing systems for optimization in addition to development of novel equipment, all while minimizing risks and maximizing efficiency in our cutting-edge solar cell factory.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES: &nbsp;</strong></p> <ul> <li>Design, develop, and manage automation projects - including initial factory ideation, machine commissioning, proof of rate capability, and eventual hand-off to operational teams &nbsp;</li> <li>Architect, write, and debug PLC code with an emphasis on generating code that is organized, structured, documented, maintainable, and reusable for high-volume manufacturing applications &nbsp;</li> <li>Keep our factory safe and reliable by implementing ANSI/RIA15.06/OSHA compliant systems for robots, gantries, conveyors, and other manufacturing equipment&nbsp;</li> <li>Generate aesthetically simple HMI screens to make complex machines easy to understand, operate, and troubleshoot&nbsp;</li> <li>Integrate individual equipment pieces into master SCADA and MES systems</li> <li>Design electrical systems compliant to NEC, NFPA, &amp; UL508A regulations&nbsp;</li> <li>Stay organized by creating schedules and budgets, and then motivate the team to achieve them &nbsp;</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS: &nbsp;</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in engineering, physics, or chemical discipline &nbsp;</li> <li>5+ years of experience with high-speed manufacturing, controls and automation, and/or programming&nbsp;</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE: &nbsp;</strong></p> <ul> <li>Excited by a quick and iterative design and manufacturing role&nbsp;</li> <li>Proven ability to solve complex problems with simple solutions in both design and implementation stages&nbsp;</li> <li>Excellent communication skills both written and verbal, with the ability to make plans and directional recommendations collaboratively and cross-functionally&nbsp;</li> <li>Ability to engineer creative, new approaches to problems while adhering to ANSI/RIA15.06/OSHA safety requirements to keep a factory safe &nbsp;</li> <li>Hazardous process expertise in an aerospace, oil and gas, or chemical industry where high pressure or hazardous systems for fluids or gasses were in use</li> <li>Experience with at least one of the specific disciplines listed below. The ideal candidate is interested in learning at least the fundamentals of the other areas they are not yet strong in</li> </ul> <p><em>Electrical/Industrial Controls: &nbsp;</em></p> <ul> <li>Electrical sizing of motors, valves, pneumatics, cables, circuit protection, VFDs, motor starters, various other motion systems &nbsp;</li> <li>Design of fail-safe electrical circuits using both safety logic controllers and safety-rated relays &nbsp;</li> <li>Hands-on experience troubleshooting industrial electrical systems using tools like multimeters, oscilloscopes, EMI probes&nbsp;</li> title: Sr. BIM Specialist
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>SR. BIM SPECIALIST&nbsp;</strong></p> <p>Building on the rapid advancement of the Starlink program, we are moving into a new phase of facility and infrastructure growth. We are currently seeking a Sr. BIM Specialist to lead the integration and coordination of Building Information Modeling (BIM) across fast-paced multidisciplinary projects, ensuring project objectives are met through effective model management and collaboration. This position will serve as a key technical resource, supporting project teams and fostering strong BIM practices throughout the project lifecycle.&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Develop and maintain detailed 3D BIM models using industry-standard software (Revit, Navisworks, AutoCad) for architectural, structural, mechanical, electrical, plumbing (MEP), and other engineering disciplines</li> <li>Perform clash detection, model coordination, and constructability reviews to identify and resolve conflicts early in the design and construction phases</li> <li>Lead BIM coordination efforts for multi-disciplinary projects, ensuring the seamless integration of models and data. Specifically, this will be a mix of in-house processes/elements and external design consultants throughout the whole project lifecycle</li> <li>Collaborate closely with project stakeholders to establish and maintain BIM standards, protocols, and workflows</li> <li>Act as the primary BIM resource for team members, internal customers and external design consultants, addressing technical issues and optimizing BIM processes for project success</li> <li>Work with with the design and construction teams to keep a living model that will culminate in an as-built of the facility at hand</li> <li>Lead the transition of BIM workflows from third-party providers to in-house operations, including data migration, process documentation, and training of team members</li> <li>Generate accurate construction documentation, quantity takeoffs, and visualizations to support project bidding, procurement, and on-site execution</li> <li>Troubleshoot technical issues in BIM environments and recommend software/tools/process improvements to enhance efficiency</li> <li>Participate in cross-functional meetings, providing BIM expertise to inform design decisions and mitigate risks</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in architecture, engineering or construction management</li> <li>6+ years of hands-on experience as a BIM specialist or Modeler in a construction or engineering environment</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>8+ years of professional experience in BIM coordination, with multidisciplinary experience on high rise projects</li> <li>Experience modeling multiple disciplines (e.g., architecture, structural, MEP).</li> <li>Exposure to high rise construction projects is strongly preferred. The ideal candidate will have owned BIM coordination through construction administration on multiple large scale projects and have a solid understanding of means and methods of construction</li> <li>Experience in aerospace, high-tech manufacturing, or mission-critical facilities projects.</li> <li>Proficiency in BIM authoring and coordination tools, including Revit (advanced level), Navisworks, and related plugins; familiarity with Dynamo or similar scripting for automation.</li> <li>Strong understanding of interdisciplinary coordination workflows, clash detection, and federated modeling in large-scale projects.</li> <li>Demonstrated expertise in architectural, engineering or MEP-focused BIM workflows, with the ability to drive project success through effective model coordination and communication.</li> <li>Certification in BIM (e.g., Autodesk Certified Professional in Revit for Architectural Design/Structure/MEP, or AGC BIM Certificate).</li> <li>Knowledge of advanced BIM integrations, such as reality capture (e.g., laser scanning with Trimble or Leica), VR/AR visualizations, or cloud-based collaboration platforms (e.g., Autodesk BIM 360/ACC).</li> <li>Design experience in architecture, engineering or a related field</li> <li>Familiarity with structural analysis tools and integration of BIM data for structural engineering applications.</li> <li>Experience with Siemens NX</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Must be available to work extended hours and weekends when needed, based on site operational needs; employment law (Texas, Florida, Washington State also helpful)</li> <li>Excellent written and verbal communication skills</li> <li>Prior experience—either in-house or through client relationships—representing high-growth companies</li> <li>Demonstrated ability to work cross-functionally and build strong relationships with other business groups and/or clients</li> <li>Proven ability to work both collaboratively and independently in a fast-paced and constantly changing environment</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Willingness to travel not considered</li> <li>Must be able to work extended hours and weekends as needed</li> </ul> <p><strong>COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:</strong><br><br>Pay Range:<br>Level 4: $245,000.00 - $305,000.00</p> <p>Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.</p> <p>Base salary is just one part of your total rewards package at SpaceX. You may also be eligible for long-term incentives, in the form of company stock or long-term cash awards, as well as potential discretionary bonuses and the ability to purchase additional stock at a discount through an Employee Stock Purchase Plan. You will also receive access to comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short and long-term disability insurance, life insurance, paid parental leave, and various other discounts and perks. You may also accrue 3 weeks of paid vacation and will be eligible for 10 or more paid holidays per year. Employees accrue paid sick leave pursuant to Company policy which satisfies or exceeds the accrual, carryover, and use requirements of the law.</p><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. ELECTRICAL HARDWARE ENGINEER, AI SATELLITES (STARMIND)</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is leveraging its experience deploying and operating the world’s largest satellite constellation to develop Starmind, a new constellation of satellites capturing solar energy in space to power low-cost, high-performance AI compute for Earth. Realizing this vision demands highly reliable, high performance electrical hardware ranging from power electronics, high speed digital systems, mixed signal designs, robust avionics, networking, and custom compute electronics. These systems must operate in the extreme environment of space while delivering the connectivity, control, power distribution, and processing needed for orbital AI inference.</p> <p>The Starmind team designs, builds, and operates the orbital compute fabric of the future. We develop nearly every key piece of technology in house – from the satellites’ flight computers and power systems to the fully custom compute electronics, memory, and networking that form the brain of our on-orbit data centers. As a Senior Electrical Design Engineer on the Starmind Payload Engineering team, you’ll have ownership over the entire life-cycle of the hardware that enables advanced on-orbit AI processing and data center workloads. Your work sits at the intersection of electrical, mechanical, thermal, and software engineering. The Payload team is responsible for the design of industry-leading compute electronics, memory, and networking in order to achieve required domain sizes and processing workloads.</p> ELECTRICAL TEST AND RELIABILITY ENGINEER, GATEWAYS (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is leveraging its experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation that provides fast, reliable internet to millions of users worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system – thousands of satellites, consumer receivers that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing, hundreds of gateway ground stations, and the software that brings it all together. We’ve only begun to scratch the surface of Starlink’s potential global impact. As we continue to upgrade and expand the constellation, we’re looking for best-in-class engineers to join the team.</p> <p>As a Sr. Electrical Test and Reliability Engineer on Starlink, you’ll contribute to the design, build, and test electronics for the world's largest network of ground stations, which function as an intermediary between the satellites and our end-users to ensure smooth data transfer and transmission. You will sit at the intersection of electrical, mechanical, thermal analysis, software, and antenna engineering - ultimately ensuring that our ground antenna hardware can withstand the harshest environmental conditions while maintaining reliable communication with millions of users on a global scale. This is an opportunity to work on cutting edge R&amp;D technology, and some of the most complex applications of electrical and mechanical engineering in the industry.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Design, develop, and execute novel environmental, RF, mechanical, and electrical test solutions for our ground antenna electronics and payload</li> <li>Perform detailed failure analysis of ground antenna hardware, identifying root causes of failures and implementing corrective actions</li> <li>Select commercial-off-the-shelf hardware and/or design custom PCBAs to measure signals, apply flight-like loads, and power units under test</li> <li>Hands-on support of hardware through design qualification, production ramp, and ground network rollout</li> <li>Work closely with engineers from adjacent disciplines (mechanical, thermal, software, test engineering, supply chain, silicon design) to deliver tightly integrated, high-performance hardware</li> <li>Perform electrical bench testing of failures to replicate and inform mitigation of anomalies</li> <li>Drive continual improvements to our designs by building physical and digital tools to analyze data collected both in the field and in the lab</li> <li>Challenge assumptions and work to find simple solutions to complex problems</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC failure analysis, or reliability engineering&nbsp;</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Master’s degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, physics, or other STEM discipline</li> <li>Experience with both electronics and mechanical design and analysis including knowledge of RF principles</li> <li>Experience analyzing circuits and PCBAs, title: Sr. Facilities Engineer, Solar Cell Factory (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>SR. FACILITIES ENGINEER, SOLAR CELL FACTORY (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>At SpaceX, we are building the next generation of space infrastructure to enable large-scale AI data centers in orbit. These orbital AI platforms require massive amounts of reliable, high-efficiency solar power to support intensive computing workloads in space. To make this possible, we are standing up one of the largest solar cell manufacturing facilities in the world. We are seeking a Sr. Facilities Engineer to oversee the maintenance, performance, and continuous improvement of facility systems (power, ultrapure water, exhaust, bulk gases) that support high-volume solar cell manufacturing. This high-impact role offers the opportunity to build and shape the organization from the ground up while directly enabling SpaceX’s ambitious vision for AI data centers in space.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Oversee the maintenance, performance, and continuous improvement of facility systems including power distribution, ultrapure water, exhaust systems (acidic, caustic, harmful gas, VOC, and general heat), bulk gases, chilled water, and process cooling systems that support high-volume solar cell manufacturing</li> <li>Collaborate with engineers, technicians, production teams, and leadership to maintain systems in peak operating condition and develop detailed work instructions for preventative maintenance to ensure zero unplanned interruptions</li> <li>Monitor and optimize utility systems supporting wet chemistry texturing, PECVD, PVD, metallization, and cleaning processes</li> <li>Perform failure assessments, root cause analysis, and implement corrective actions for facility systems</li> <li>Ensure work and materials comply with manufacturer specifications, industry standards, and all applicable safety, environmental, and building regulations</li> <li>Read and interpret P&amp;IDs, schematics, OEM manuals, and construction drawings for assembly, repair, and optimization</li> <li>Present equipment and system performance statuses to internal customers and leadership</li> <li>Track and resolve electronic work tickets, manage priorities with minimal guidance, and take on additional responsibilities as needed</li> <li>Drive continuous improvement initiatives for reliability, uptime, yield, and cost in a high-volume production environment</li> <li>Operate forklifts, scissor lifts, boom lifts, and other equipment as required</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in mechanical, electrical, chemical, or related engineering discipline</li> <li>5+ years of professional experience in facilities engineering or sustaining engineering for a manufacturing environment</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>7+ years of experience with cleanroom facility systems, ultrapure water, exhaust abatement, bulk gas delivery, and/or process utility systems supporting semiconductor or solar manufacturing</li> <li>Knowledge of high-pressure gases, flammable gases, hazardous chemicals, and associated safety systems</li> <li>Proficiency reading and interpreting P&amp;IDs, schematics, and technical drawings</li> <li>Experience with continuous improvement, root cause analysis, and implementing preventative maintenance programs</li> <li>Ability to troubleshoot mechanical, electrical, and controls systems down to the component level</li> <li>Familiarity with commercial building codes, OSHA, EPA, and NFPA standards</li> <li>Strong interpersonal and communication skills with the ability to work in a fast-paced, high-stress environment balancing multiple projects</li> <li>Proficiency with Microsoft Office tools and computerized maintenance management systems</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Ability to travel internationally (20%)</li> <li>Ability to stand up to 6 hours, lift up to 25 pounds unassisted, and maneuver around equipment in a factory setting</li> <li>Ability to work in industrial environments with fumes/odors, noise, hazardous chemicals, and confined spaces</li> <li>Must be available to work extended hours and weekends as needed</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, State. title: Sr. Failure Analysis Engineer, Microelectronics (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>SR. FAILURE ANALYSIS ENGINEER, MICROELECTRONICS (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>Starlink is SpaceX’s ambitious goal to bring high-quality internet to the globe by building a constellation of thousands of satellites in low Earth orbit (LEO) using our Falcon 9 and Starship reusable rockets. We are developing millions of devices for end users to link our customers to our satellites.</p> <p>As a Sr. Failure Analysis Engineer on the Starlink team, you will perform detailed root cause failure analysis on microelectronic components and packaging to support high-volume manufacturing, qualification, and field returns. You will leverage advanced laboratory tools and physics-of-failure techniques to identify failure mechanisms and drive corrective actions that improve the reliability of our satellite constellation and user terminals.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Own end-to-end root cause failure analysis investigations on microelectronics failing in manufacturing, test, and field, from initial failure characterization through final corrective action verification</li> <li>Conduct advanced electrical fault isolation and characterization using curve trace, TDR, RF characterization, Lock-in Thermography, OBIRCH, EBIRCH, EBAC, nanoprobing, and related techniques to precisely localize defects in complex devices</li> <li>Perform advanced physical failure analysis using SEM, FIB, EDS, SAM, cross-sectioning, and related techniques to identify failure mechanisms in silicon, packaging, and interconnects</li> <li>Apply physics-of-failure principles and deep knowledge of semiconductor failure modes (electromigration, thermal fatigue, delamination, EOS/ESD, solder joint fatigue, etc.) to determine root causes</li> <li>Drive corrective actions by working directly with silicon design, packaging, and manufacturing teams to implement and validate design or process changes based on FA findings</li> <li>Author detailed technical reports documenting failure modes, root cause conclusions, supporting data, and corrective action effectiveness</li> <li>Develop and improve failure analysis techniques and workflows to support new packaging technologies and advanced materials</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in materials science, electrical engineering, physics, chemical engineering, or other STEM discipline&nbsp;</li> <li>5+ years of hands-on experience in microelectronics failure analysis or materials characterization (internship experience is applicable)</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Master’s or PhD in materials science, electrical engineering, physics, chemical engineering, or other STEM discipline with a focus on microelectronics or failure analysis</li> <li>10+ years of hands-on experience in microelectronics failure analysis or materials characterization</li> <li>Direct experience with failure analysis tools and techniques (SEM, FIB, EDS, cross-sectioning, fault isolation, or equivalent)</li> <li>Strong understanding of semiconductor physics and common microelectronics failure mechanisms (electromigration, thermal fatigue, delamination, solder joint fatigue, electrical overstress/ESD, etc.)</li> <li>Proficiency with advanced FA tools including SEM, FIB, SAM, and EDS</li> <li>Hands-on experience in electrical characterization and fault isolation techniques such as IV curves, RF/VNA measurement, LIT, OBIRCH, EBIRCH, EBAC, nanoprobing, photon emission, or voltage contrast</li> <li>Experience applying JEDEC and AEC reliability test standards and physics-of-failure methodologies to root cause investigations</li> <li>Experience analyzing complex datasets with Python, JMP, or similar tools</li> <li>Excellent problem-solving, communication, and technical writing skills</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Ability to work overtime and weekends as needed</li> <li>Ability to work in a cleanroom or ESD-controlled environment when required</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR <a href="https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/?id=ddtc_kb_article_page&amp;sys_id=24d528fddbfc930044f9ff621f961987">here</a>. &nbsp;</li> </ul> <p>SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.</p> <p>Applicants wishing to view a copy of SpaceX’s Affirmative Action Plan for veterans and individuals with disabilities, or applicants requiring reasonable accommodation to the application/interview process should reach out to&nbsp;<a href="mailto:EEOCompliance@spacex.com">EEOCompliance@spacex.com</a><em>.&nbsp;</em></p></div>

Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>SENIOR FIRE PROTECTION ENGINEER</strong></p> <p>The Senior Fire Protection Engineer provides advanced design and operations engineering support and subject matter expertise in fire protection, life safety, building and fire codes, fire hazard and risk assessment of materials and processes, fire and smoke spread, fire detection, alarm and sprinkler system design, industrial fire hazards, fire investigation support, and other fire and life safety topics. This role leads complex design-evaluations, mentors junior engineers, and delivers robust solutions for SpaceX including large scale manufacturing environments.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Lead engineering design, analysis, calculations, and specifications for facility fire and life safety systems</li> <li>Develop building and fire code compliance documents and fire life safety designs for SpaceX facilities</li> <li>Develop AM&amp;M (Alternate Means &amp; Methods) to local AHJ to support performance-based design criteria that meet the intent of code</li> <li>Perform and oversee hazardous material analysis for code compliance, including chemical classification, chemical maximum allowable quantity analysis, chemical inventory management, and related system design support</li> <li>Support facility construction and operations teams to develop field solutions and resolve technical issues</li> <li>Support and lead aspects of commissioning activities during pre-test and AHJ testing phases for launch site facility builds</li> <li>Conduct fire/life safety code reviews and analyses</li> <li>Prepare and present technical reports and presentations</li> <li>Review and comment on shop drawing design packages developed by contractors/engineering firms</li> <li>Mentor junior engineers and contribute to project team leadership</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree</li> <li>5+ years of experience in the design and construction of fire protection systems and/or fire protection consulting</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li><span data-teams="true">Bachelor’s degree in an engineering discipline</span></li> <li>Working knowledge of Building &amp; title: Sr. Full Stack Engineer (Application Software)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>SR. FULL STACK ENGINEER (APPLICATION SOFTWARE)</strong></p> <p>The application software team is the central nervous system of SpaceX – we create mission critical applications that are used throughout SpaceX to accelerate launch vehicle production and flight as well as systems that allow Starlink to grow into a worldwide fast, reliable Internet service. We are looking for engineers who treat fellow teammates with fairness, respect, and support.</p> <p>Our team is currently creating and evolving systems to enable rapid build and reuse of Starship as well as designing the next generation manufacturing software that will be used in high throughput factories for Starlink. Other applications range from platforms that support concurrent streams of data from many always-on assets to manage the world’s largest satellite constellation to public facing systems where customers can join our Starlink network globally. We work closely with engineers throughout the company to create and update our systems with respect to crewed launches, Starship flights, changes to the Starlink network and much more.</p> <p>Aerospace experience is not required to be successful here - rather we look for smart, motivated, respectful, collaborative engineers who love solving problems and want to make an impact on a super inspiring mission. You will have full ownership of challenging problems, working with a team of enthusiastic engineers with diverse perspectives to design and produce solutions that enable SpaceX to move towards our goals at a rapid pace. The success of the missions at SpaceX depends on the software that you and your team produce.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Develop highly reliable software solutions that are used across SpaceX</li> <li>Create new applications that improve how SpaceX operates</li> <li>Build prototypes to prove out key design concepts and quantify technical constraints</li> <li>Own all aspects of software engineering and product development</li> <li>Deep dive into your users’ problems to find and create efficient solutions</li> <li>Bring your voice to the table in team collaborations on architecture, design, and code reviews</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, math, or scientific discipline and 5+ years of professional experience in software development; OR 7+ years of professional experience building software in lieu of a degree</li> <li>3+ years of professional experience in full stack development</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Programming experience in Python, C#.NET, Go, Scala, Java, or similar object-oriented language</li> <li>1+ years of rigorous experience building single page web applications</li> <li>Experience with version control, continuous integration, and continuous delivery concepts</li> <li>Expertise in designing software systems</li> <li>Deep understanding of testing, continuous integration, build, deployment &amp; monitoring</li> <li>Expertise in profiling and improving application performance</li> <li>Experience with build systems (Make, Bazel/Pants/Buck, Gradle) and package management tools (pip, npm)</li> <li>Experience with UNIX-like operating systems and tools like Terraform, Ansible, Puppet for managing them</li> <li>Experience working with in-stream data processing&nbsp;using Apache Kafka, RabbitMQ, ActiveMQ, or similar technologies</li> <li>Production experience with Docker and Kubernetes</li> <li>Front-end experience in Angular, React, or similar JavaScript framework</li> <li>Database experience with PostgreSQL, SQL Server, or similar database technologies</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>You may be asked to work extended hours/weekends dependent on launch cadence</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>Sr. GLOBAL OPERATIONS ENGINEER (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>Starlink is leveraging SpaceX’s experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy the world’s most advanced broadband internet system and largest satellite constellation. In this role, you will partner directly with design engineering, &nbsp;to define commodity strategy, build multi-year technology roadmaps, establish and maintain the approved vendor list, and secure massive-scale supply at the record-breaking build speeds the SpaceXAI team is driving. You will negotiate transformative, high-value agreements, accelerate delivery timelines, actively manage inventory across the supply chain, and continuously optimize for cost, quality, speed, and supply chain resilience in one of the most competitive and dynamic AI infrastructure programs on the planet. The ideal candidate is a strategic leader who thrives in ambiguous, high-velocity environments, possesses exceptional commercial and technical acumen, and has a proven track record of delivering excellent results.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul type="disc"> <li>Partner with engineers and platform teams to define commodity strategy, align multi-year technology roadmaps, and maintain approved vendor lists</li> <li>Orchestrate demand forecasting and allocation across SpaceXAI companies to ensure balanced supply support for all programs</li> <li>Own global sourcing, including supplier qualification, multi-sourcing strategies, and performance management to meet build schedules and reduce lead times</li> <li>Negotiate agreements focused on competitive pricing, volume commitments, and preferential allocation, using creative approaches where needed to secure supply at reasonable cost</li> <li>Align internal roadmaps with key vendors and collaborate on capacity planning and technology development</li> <li>Monitor supply chain risks and implement mitigation plans to protect build schedules</li> <li>Drive cost reduction through should-cost analysis, long-term agreements, and value engineering while meeting quality and reliability requirements</li> <li>Build strong supplier relationships through regular reviews and joint projects</li> <li>Track KPIs for cost, quality, delivery, and resilience; report progress to leadership</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul type="disc"> <li>Bachelor’s degree and 8+ years of experience working in one or more of the following; or 12+ years of experience working in one or more of the following in lieu of a degree:</li> <ul type="circle"> <li>Business</li> <li>Supply Chain</li> <li>Engineering</li> </ul> <li>7+ years of experience in global supply chain, procurement, sourcing, or commodity management with a focus on semiconductors, memory, storage, or datacenter infrastructure</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul type="disc"> <li>Deep technical understanding of semiconductor architectures (ASICs, FPGAs, GPUs/AI accelerators, memory, power, RF, and analog/mixed-signal)</li> <li>Proven experience in fast-paced, high-growth technology or hyperscale environments with direct responsibility for large-scale sourcing</li> <li>New product introduction (NPI) supply chain planning and procurement, from prototype through production ramp</li> <li>Previous experience at hyperscalers, memory/storage OEMs (e.g., Micron, SK hynix, Samsung), AI infrastructure companies, or semiconductor supply organizations</li> <li>Demonstrated success negotiating and managing complex, high-value supplier relationships in volatile, supply-constrained markets</li> <li>Strong negotiation, analytical, project management, financial modeling, communication, and cross-functional leadership skills</li> <li>Familiarity with commodity to the fastest AI infrastructure builds on Earth</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul type="disc"> <li>Willingness to travel domestically and internationally as needed to title: Sr. Hardware Development Engineer, Gateway Failure Analysis (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>SR. HARDWARE DEVELOPMENT ENGINEER, GATEWAY FAILURE ANALYSIS (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is leveraging its experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation that provides fast, reliable internet to millions of users worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system – thousands of satellites, consumer receivers that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing, hundreds of gateway ground stations, and the software that brings it all together. We’ve only begun to scratch the surface of Starlink’s potential global impact. As we continue to upgrade and expand the constellation, we’re looking for best-in-class engineers to join the team.</p> <p>As a Sr. <span class="job-application-title">Hardware Development Engineer </span>on Starlink, you’ll contribute to the design, build, and test electronics for the world's largest network of ground stations, which function as an intermediary between the satellites and our end-users to ensure smooth data transfer and transmission. You will sit at the intersection of electrical, mechanical, thermal analysis, software, and antenna engineering - ultimately ensuring that our ground antenna hardware can withstand the harshest environmental conditions while maintaining reliable communication with millions of users on a global scale. This is an opportunity to work on cutting edge R&amp;D technology, and some of the most complex applications of electrical and mechanical engineering in the industry.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Design, develop, and execute novel environmental, RF, mechanical, and electrical test solutions for our ground antenna electronics and payload</li> <li>Perform detailed failure analysis of ground antenna hardware, identifying root causes of failures and implementing corrective actions</li> <li>Select commercial-off-the-shelf hardware and/or design custom PCBAs to measure signals, apply flight-like loads, and power units under test</li> <li>Hands-on support of hardware through design qualification, production ramp, and ground network rollout</li> <li>Work closely with engineers from adjacent disciplines (mechanical, thermal, software, test engineering, supply chain, silicon design) to deliver tightly integrated, high-performance hardware</li> <li>Perform electrical bench testing of failures to replicate and inform mitigation of anomalies</li> <li>Drive continual improvements to our designs by building physical and digital tools to analyze data collected both in the field and in the lab</li> <li>Challenge assumptions and work to find simple solutions to complex problems</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, physics, or other STEM discipline</li> <li>5+ years of experience in hardware development, failure analysis, or reliability engineering&nbsp;</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Master’s degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, physics, or other STEM discipline</li> <li>Experience with both electronics and mechanical design and analysis including knowledge of RF principles</li> <li>Experience analyzing circuits and PCBAs, and developing functional test plans</li> <li>Experience with test equipment and measurement techniques to verify and validate product requirements (oscilloscope, multimeter, electronic load, spectrum analyzer, network analyzer, vector signal generator, source measurement unit, etc.)</li> <li>Experience in environmental testing such as HALT/HASS, thermal, humidity, shock &amp; vibration</li> <li>Strong understanding of computers and programming languages (Python, C/C++)</li> <li>Thorough understanding of electronics reliability, manufacturing, and failure mechanisms</li> <li>Knowledge of quality tools such as Lean principles, Six Sigma, and root cause analysis methods</li> <li>Thorough understanding of metrology, sources of measurement error, and uncertainty analysis</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Ability to work extended hours or weekends as needed for mission critical deadlines</li> <li>Occasional travel to ground network sites to title: Sr. Manager, Power Plant (Starship)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>SENIOR MANAGER</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is building and operating combined-cycle gas turbine power plants that must come online, stay online, and perform. This role owns the design and build of the full power plant: gas turbines, mechanical and electrical balance of plant, and everything else that keeps the plant running at rated output, day after day. This is not a desk job. You will be constructing the power plant, owning commissioning in the control room during startup, and in the field troubleshooting.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Build, lead, and develop a multi-disciplinary power plant team spanning gas turbines, mechanical and electrical balance of plant, controls, and commissioning</li> <li>Own the full lifecycle of gas turbine power generation assets — installation, commissioning, startup, operations, and long-term maintenance — and be accountable for plant availability, reliability, and performance</li> <li>Set technical direction and execution plans for commissioning, including combustion tuning, control system checkout, protective relay testing, and performance/reliability run verification</li> <li>Own root-cause analysis and corrective action for turbine trips, forced outages, and performance degradation; drive fixes that prevent recurrence and hold the team to a no-repeat standard</li> <li>Establish and continuously improve operating procedures, startup/shutdown sequences, and abnormal operating condition playbooks</li> <li>Serve as the primary technical and commercial interface with OEMs (GE, Siemens Energy, Mitsubishi Power, Doosan) on warranty issues, LTSA scope, outage planning, and technical issues</li> <li>Plan, staff, and execute major/minor inspections, hot gas path outages, and combustion inspections in line with OEM maintenance intervals; own outage cost, duration, and quality of return-to-service</li> <li>Drive turbine performance analysis (heat rate, capacity factor, degradation curves) to identify efficiency losses and convert findings into funded corrective action</li> <li>Coordinate across balance-of-plant teams (HRSG, steam turbine, cooling systems, water treatment) to deliver integrated plant performance, not siloed subsystem success</li> <li>Own the construction-to-operations handoff with EPC contractors; ensure a clean transition from construction to commercial operation</li> <li>Develop and own spare parts strategy, critical spares inventory, and maintenance budgets; manage spend against reliability and availability targets</li> <li>Hire, coach, and retain engineers and technicians; set performance standards and grow the next generation of plant leadership</li> <li>Represent the power plant organization to internal stakeholders (operations, grid interconnection, commercial, construction) and make timely field decisions under pressure</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree and 10+ years of experience working in one or more of the following; or 14+ years of experience working utility-scale gas turbines in commissioning, operations, maintenance, or plant engineering roles</li> <li>2+ years of project management experience leading operations</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Working knowledge of combined-cycle plant systems: gas turbines, HRSGs, steam turbines, generators, and balance-of-plant equipment</li> <li>Experience reading and interpreting P&amp;IDs, single-line diagrams, and turbine control logic</li> <li>Direct commissioning or operations leadership experience with GE 7/9HA, Siemens Energy SGT6/8-8000H, Mitsubishi M501/701JAC, or Doosan H-class turbines</li> <li>Experience with DCS/turbine control platforms (Mark VIe, SPPA-T3000, or equivalent)</li> <li>Familiarity with LTSA structures, OEM contract negotiation, and outage scope development</li> <li>Background in root-cause failure analysis (RCA/5-Why/Fishbone) for rotating equipment</li> <li>Experience with performance monitoring tools and heat balance modeling</li> <li>Exposure to grid interconnection requirements, PPA performance obligations, or capacity market rules</li> <li>Experience integrating power generation with co-located industrial or data center loads</li> <li>Proven ownership of plant or fleet reliability metrics (availability, forced outage rate, heat rate) and of the budgets that fund them</li> <li>Experience standing up a new plant, commissioning organization, or operations team from construction through commercial operation</li> <li>A bias toward action: comfortable making a call in the field without waiting for a committee</li> <li>Demonstrated ability to work under pressure during startup, outages, or unplanned events, with a sense of urgency and ownership over outcomes</li> <li>Experience using SOLIDWORKS, Siemens NX, or similar CAD software</li> <li>Knowledge of engineering standards and best practices such as ASME B31.3, ASME BPV Code Section VIII, and AFSPCMAN 91-710</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. title: Sr. Manager, Product Growth Strategy (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>SR. MANAGER, PRODUCT GROWTH STRATEGY (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>Starlink is scaling consumer broadband worldwide. As Sr. Manager, Product Growth Strategy, you will lead the Starlink product growth team that takes service programs and offering changes to market, and you will be accountable for their growth impact.</p> <p>The team owns how we deploy programs such as plan and offer mechanics, referral programs, and market-specific value proposition work. You plan and product selection experiences and service programs work for markets, in partnership with global go-to-market teams. You organize how we ship changes to the product offering, new features, and new functionality across the service suite: launch coordination, impact planning, and prioritization.</p> <p>Direction comes from Consumer Growth leadership, the broader growth team, and go-to-market. This is not an order-taking seat. The team is expected to bring ideas, justify them, vet them, test them, and take them to market. The work is high impact and closely reviewed. You need to be strong enough to stand behind the choices the team makes, read back in-market performance, and iterate or stop.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Lead the product growth team: set the bar, assign ownership, and hold the team to launch quality, timeline, and growth impact</li> <li>Own how service programs and offering changes go to market (multi-family, community access, cash referral, market-specific value propositions, and similar programs), including what is in the offer, where it launches, and what GTM needs in each market</li> <li>Organize deployment of product offering changes, new features, and new functionality across the service suite: roadmap, sequencing, launch coordination, and readiness with product, engineering, marketing, and in-market GTM</li> <li>Partner with global go-to-market teams so online experiences and service programs actually work in market (positioning, eligibility, in-store activation, onboarding, ops handoff, and local constraints)</li> <li>Drive impact planning and prioritization: size the growth case, sequence work against Consumer Growth goals, and kill or re-scope what will not move the number</li> <li>Be accountable for program and offering growth impact: get work executed, read back performance after launch, and use that feedback to iterate, scale, or stop</li> <li>Bring a point of view. Source ideas, justify them with data and GTM input, vet feasibility, run tests, and take winners to market. Do not wait to be assigned a list</li> <li>Represent product growth in Consumer Growth and GTM forums: defend the plan, surface tradeoffs early, and keep US and in-market teams aligned through launch</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree</li> <li>8+ years of experience in product, growth, go-to-market, consumer programs, or a related role in a technical or consumer business</li> <li>3+ years of direct people leadership</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>10+ years in product growth, consumer subscription, telecommunications, broadband, or marketplace businesses</li> <li>5+ years leading a team that shipped programs or product changes into market</li> <li>Demonstrated ownership of launch coordination across product, engineering, marketing, and in-country GTM</li> <li>Experience taking service plans, promotions, or packaging changes live, then reading impact and iterating or killing</li> <li>Experience making digital purchase and onboarding experiences work across multiple countries or languages</li> <li>Comfort with market-specific value proposition work (including high-context markets such as Japan)</li> <li>Strong analytical chops: sizing, prioritization, experiment design, and post-launch readouts (Excel required; SQL or BI tools preferred)</li> <li>Experience in a fast-paced, high-scrutiny environment where you are expected to have a point of view and stand behind it</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Ability to travel as needed to support global go-to-market teams</li> <li>Must be able to work extended hours and weekends as needed</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. title: Sr. Manufacturing Engineer, Tool & Die Machining (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. MANUFACTURING ENGINEER, TOOL &amp; DIE MACHINING (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is developing a low latency, broadband internet system to meet the needs of consumers across the globe. Enabled by a constellation of low Earth orbit satellites, Starlink will provide fast, reliable internet to populations with little or no connectivity, including those in rural communities and places where existing services are too expensive or unreliable.</p> <p>Working directly in the materials engineering group, this position is responsible for managing a technical project for the development and qualification of all equipment, tooling, and manufacturing process technologies necessary to produce plastic injection molds and high pressure die cast tools. The correct individual will bring an open mindset, challenge the status quo concerning traditional vs. emerging technologies, and utilize a logical and disciplined approach to evaluate and select the correct set of solutions.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Lead a project focused on the development of technologies relating to plastic injection molding and high pressure die title: Sr. Materials Engineer, AI Satellites (Starmind)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>SR. MATERIALS ENGINEER, AI SATELLITES (STARMIND)</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is leveraging its experience deploying and operating the world’s largest satellite constellation to develop Starmind, a new constellation of satellites capturing solar energy in space to power low-cost, high-performance AI compute for Earth. Realizing this vision demands highly reliable, high performance electrical compute hardware, solar power systems, thermal radiators, and more. These systems must operate in the extreme environment of space while delivering the connectivity, control, power distribution, and processing needed for orbital AI inference.</p> <p>The Starmind team designs, builds, and operates the orbital compute fabric of the future. We develop nearly every key piece of technology in house – from the satellites’ flight computers and power systems to the fully custom compute electronics, memory, and networking that form the brain of our on-orbit data centers. As a Materials Engineer on the Starmind team, you’ll have ownership over the entire life-cycle of the hardware that enables advanced on-orbit AI processing and data center workloads. Your work sits at the intersection of process, packaging, mechanical, and thermal engineering. The Payload team is responsible for the design of industry-leading compute electronics, memory, and networking in order to achieve required domain sizes and processing workloads.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:&nbsp;</strong></p> <ul> <li>Rapidly develop high-reliability microelectronics packages, cooling systems, and radiator hardware for satellites.</li> <li>Own the full lifecycle of materials specification, validation, and process development— including device modeling, characterization of performance metrics, and materials failure analysis.</li> <li>Drive system trades, requirements capture, materials selection, prototyping, manufacturing, failure analysis.</li> <li>Build supply chains for build-up layers, plating chemicals, coatings, thermal interface materials, and other materials for compute and satellite manufacturing. Define incoming acceptance criteria for materials.</li> <li>Address materials and process challenges in advanced packaging while spearheading the development of next-generation TIM materials to improve packaging performance.</li> <li>Specify and implement in-process metrology tools for quality control. Design thermal test vehicles and test setups to evaluate material/electronic properties. Integrate simulation tools with experimental data to guide and drive targeted improvements via material or process changes.</li> <li>Work closely with engineers from adjacent disciplines (mechanical, thermal, electrical, software, test engineering, supply chain, silicon design, etc.) to deliver tightly integrated, high-performance hardware</li> <li>Challenge assumptions, question requirements, learn from your mistakes, and approach problems with an open mind</li> <li>Manage compliance risks related to materials and processes, ensuring safety and environmental compliance with industry standards.</li> <li>Collaborate closely with leadership and stakeholders across all departments—including design, reliability, production, and supply chain—to integrate materials innovations into product roadmaps and ensure accountability for operations and reliability.</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in materials science, mechanical engineering, or other engineering discipline</li> <li>5+ years of experience in microelectronics device research or manufacturing&nbsp;</li> </ul> <p><strong>&nbsp;</strong><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:&nbsp;</strong></p> <ul> <li>Advanced degree in materials science or similar field</li> <li>Experience in hardware, robotics, automation, or manufacturing environments</li> MATERIALS ENGINEER, CORROSION CONTROL AND FLUID COMPATIBILITY (STARMIND)</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is leveraging its experience deploying and operating the world’s largest satellite constellation to develop Starmind, a new constellation of satellites capturing solar energy in space to power low-cost, high-performance AI compute for Earth. Realizing this vision demands highly reliable, high performance electrical compute hardware, solar power systems, thermal radiators, and more. These systems must operate in the extreme environment of space while delivering the connectivity, control, power distribution, and processing needed for orbital AI inference.</p> <p>The Starmind team designs, builds, and operates the orbital compute fabric of the future, developing key in-house technologies from satellites’ flight computers and power systems to custom compute electronics, memory, and networking for on-orbit data centers. As a Senior Materials Engineer, you will serve as the technical owner for corrosion control, chemical resistance, liquid coolants and long-term material compatibility - defining and maintaining specifications for base fluids, additives, and wetted materials (including contaminant limits and compatibility criteria), while building and driving a comprehensive testing program evaluating coolant quality, contamination, and materials reliability.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Own design criteria, selection, and reliability evaluations of materials used in liquid title: Sr. Materials Engineer, Electronic Materials
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. MATERIALS ENGINEER, ELECTRONIC MATERIALS</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is leveraging its experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world's most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world's largest satellite constellation, providing fast, reliable internet to 10M+ users worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system - thousands of satellites, consumer receivers that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing, and the software that brings it all together. We've only begun to scratch the surface of Starlink's potential global impact. As we continue to upgrade and expand the constellation, we are looking for the best-in-class engineers to join the team.<br>&nbsp;<br>We are seeking a Sr. Materials Engineer to join our Bastrop, TX team, where we are advancing materials technologies to support the deployment of Starlink, the world's most advanced broadband internet system. The ideal candidate will bring deep expertise in semiconductor device physics and device fabrication, along with hands-on industry experience in at least one of the following domains—solar cell development, panel-level packaging, or printed circuit board (PCB) manufacturing—to drive material and process innovations across all three areas. This position requires a technical expert who delivers thoughtful leadership, collaborates with stakeholders to execute strategies aligned with Starlink's business objectives, budget, and priorities, while orchestrating end-to-end equipment and process development. You will push material and device performance limits to enable high-efficiency, reliable systems for space and terrestrial applications.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Lead the development and optimization of CVD recipes and device fabrication processes to boost solar cell efficiency.</li> <li>Own the full lifecycle of equipment specification, validation, and process development— including device modeling, characterization of performance metrics, and materials failure analysis.</li> <li>Build supply chains for wafers, gases, chemicals, and equipment for solar cell manufacturing. Define incoming acceptance criteria for materials (e.g. silicon wafers, conductive pastes).</li> <li>Address material and process challenges in panel-level packaging while spearheading the development of next-generation dielectric materials to improve packaging performance and scalability.</li> <li>Specify and implement in-process metrology tools for quality control. Design wafer-level test structures to evaluate material/electronic properties. Integrate simulation tools with experimental data to guide and drive targeted improvements via material or process changes.</li> <li>Drive end-to-end material and process R&amp;D programs, from concept through product implementation, to drive cost down, efficiency improvements, and reliability in electronic systems.</li> <li>Collaborate closely with leadership and stakeholders across all departments—including design, reliability, production, and supply chain—to integrate materials innovations into product roadmaps and ensure accountability for operations and reliability.</li> <li>Manage compliance risks related to materials and processes, ensuring safety and environmental compliance with industry standards.</li> <li>Mentor and develop engineers, providing technical guidance and project oversight.</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in materials science, electrical engineering, or an engineering degree.</li> <li>5+ years of experience in microelectronics device research or manufacturing.</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Master’s degree or PhD in materials science, electrical engineering, or a related field.</li> <li>Strong background in semiconductor device physics with extensive hands-on CVD, PVD and related device fabrication experience; preferred background in photovoltaics.</li> <li>Expertise in electrical device testing methods (IV, CV, Hall effect, TLM) and optical device characterization (ellipsometry, UV-VIS-IR spectroscopy, PL, EL, QSSPC).</li> <li>Proficiency in microscopy and analytical techniques (SEM/EDS, Raman, XRD, AFM, XPS, SIMS, FTIR, DMA, DSC).</li> <li>Proven cross-functional leadership skills, with experience aligning diverse teams to achieve shared technology goals.</li> <li>Strong communication skills for presenting to stakeholders as well as guiding and mentoring junior engineers.</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Must be available to work extended hours and weekends as needed.</li> <li>Willingness and ability to travel up to 25% time.</li> <li>Work performed in an environment requiring exposure to fumes, odors, and noise.</li> <li>Comfort occasionally working in tight or confined spaces.</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. title: Sr. Materials Engineer, Thin Films
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>SR. MATERIALS ENGINEER, THIN FILMS</strong></p> <p><span data-contrast="none">Starlink is building the world's largest satellite constellation to deliver fast, reliable internet to people who need it most—and powering that constellation starts on the factory floor. We are insourcing solar cell manufacturing end-to-end, from crystal growth and ingot production through wafering and cell fabrication, to drive performance, cost, and scale at every step. High-efficiency, high-reliability cells made in-house are the backbone of the Starlink network: more photons in means more data out to customers around the world.</span></p> <p><span data-contrast="none">As a Sr. Materials Engineer for thin films, you will partner with solar cell process engineering on PECVD-deposited films that set the optical and electrical performance of insourced cells. You will build deep understanding of film chemistry, microstructure, interfaces, and failure modes, then work with process, production, and quality teams to turn that insight into higher efficiency, yield, reliability, and cost. You will operate as a technical expert for the team: setting priorities from program needs, solving poorly defined materials problems autonomously, and raising the bar for how we specify, evaluate, and improve thin-film materials. If you are passionate about solving hard problems, anchor your engineering judgment with first principles thinking, and are relentless about acting with urgency, this role is for you.</span></p> <p><span data-contrast="none"><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></span></p> <ul> <li><span data-contrast="none"> Partner with solar cell process engineering on PECVD thin films (e.g., passivation, anti-reflection, and related dielectric or semiconductor layers), developing materials requirements, film-property targets, and the physical understanding of how deposited films perform in the cell</span></li> <li>Build deep technical understanding of plasma-deposited film materials: composition, hydrogen content, density, stress, optical constants, passivation quality, interfaces, and reliability; translate that understanding into clear recommendations that improve cell performance and manufacturability</li> <li>Operate as the technical expert for thin-film materials: independently apply advanced materials concepts to highly complex issues, develop new characterization or evaluation methods where they do not already exist, and make high-impact materials decisions with limited tactical guidance</li> <li>Set your own priorities from program needs; execute multiple complex, multi-month materials projects in parallel (new film stacks, materials qualification, yield or reliability recovery, supplier materials) and come to leadership with solved problems and already-implemented solutions</li> <li>Partner with process engineering on DOEs and process trials: define materials-relevant responses, interpret how plasma, chemistry, and hardware changes affect film properties and cell results, and recommend durable improvements</li> <li>Define film material requirements, specifications, and acceptance criteria; qualify precursors, consumables, and film stacks so materials used in production are understood, controlled, and scalable</li> <li>Lead structured root cause analysis for materials-limited performance, yield, and reliability issues (film defects, interface failure, contamination, stoichiometry, stress, delamination); correlate process history with metrology (ellipsometry, lifetime, FTIR, SEM, I-V, and related methods) and drive corrective actions to first principles</li> <li>Influence cross-functional decisions with process, equipment, quality, production, and characterization teams; challenge assumptions that do not serve cell performance or manufacturability; create materials methods, specifications, and tools that raise the bar for others</li> <li>Identify and drive path-finding for advanced thin-film materials, stacks, or precursor chemistries that deliver measurable gains in efficiency, reliability, or cost</li> <li>Coordinate with suppliers on precursors, consumables, and film materials to reduce supply-chain risk and ensure long-term scalability</li> <li>Mentor engineers, new hires, and interns on thin-film materials, PECVD-relevant materials science, and first-principles problem solving; generate and share high-quality engineering content, specifications, and best practices</li> <li>Champion a culture of safety and quality in all vacuum, plasma, pyrophoric/toxic gas, chemical handling, lab, and production support activities</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li><span data-contrast="none"> Bachelor's degree in materials science, chemical engineering, electrical engineering, physics, or a STEM discipline</span></li> <li>5+ years of professional experience with thin films, PECVD or other vacuum-deposited coatings, or electronic materials in a manufacturing or R&amp;D environment</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li><span data-contrast="none">Master’s degree or PhD in materials science, chemical engineering, electrical engineering, physics, or a STEM discipline</span></li> <li>Hands-on experience with PECVD-deposited films in semiconductor or solar cell manufacturing</li> <li>Experience working closely with process engineering on PECVD or other vacuum deposition processes in a manufacturing or development environment</li> <li>Proficiency with thin-film and solar-cell metrology such as spectroscopic ellipsometry, reflectance, FTIR, minority-carrier lifetime (QSSPC/PL), SEM-EDS, XPS, four-point probe, film stress, and optical inspection</li> <li>Deep understanding of film growth mechanisms, precursor chemistry (e.g., SiH4, NH3, N2O, TMB, PH3), plasma/vacuum processing, and how film properties couple to solar-cell passivation and optics</li> <li>Demonstrated ability to lead structured root cause analysis (e.g., DOE, 5-why, fishbone, fault-tree) and convert findings into durable material or process recommendations</li> <li>Experience writing material specifications, qualifying precursors or film stacks, and establishing materials-related process-control or acceptance criteria</li> <li>Experience working in a high-volume manufacturing or fab environment and partnering with process, equipment, quality, and production teams</li> <li>Track record of owning complex, ambiguous materials problems end-to-end, setting priorities with limited supervision, and delivering results on tight timelines</li> <li>Experience mentoring engineers, technicians, interns, or new Realizing this vision demands highly reliable, high performance electrical compute hardware, solar power systems, thermal radiators, and more. These systems must operate in the extreme environment of space while delivering the connectivity, control, power distribution, and processing needed for orbital AI inference.</p> <p>The Starmind team designs, builds, and operates the orbital compute fabric of the future. We develop nearly every key piece of technology in house – from the satellites’ flight computers and power systems to the fully custom compute electronics, memory, and networking that form the brain of our on-orbit data centers. PCB DESIGNER (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is leveraging its experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation and is providing fast, reliable internet to millions of users worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system – thousands of satellites, consumer receivers that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing, and the software that brings it all together. We’ve only begun to scratch the surface of Starlink’s potential global impact. As we continue to upgrade and expand the constellation, we’re looking for best-in-class engineers to join the team.</p> <p>As a Sr. PCB Designer at SpaceX, you’ll be responsible for creating the layout for all our in-house board designs. You’re not just connecting the dots. Here you’ll partner closely with Hardware Development Engineers as they develop their schematics, providing your expertise and recommendations at each design review, and iterating your designs to come up with the best possible solutions. You’ll contribute to a variety of design mixes from radio phased arrays to solar power converters and more.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Determine layer stackup, perform component package selection, component placement, routing feasibility studies, and signal routing of digital, analog, RF, and power conversion of printed circuit boards (PCB)</li> <li>Library creation title: Sr. Process Controls Engineer, Solar Cell Factory (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not.
