title: Starlink Development Lead, Solar Ingot & Wafer
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>STARLINK DEVELOPMENT LEAD, SOLAR INGOT &amp; WAFER</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is developing a low-latency, broadband internet system to meet the needs of consumers across the globe. Enabled by a constellation of low Earth orbit satellites, Starlink will provide fast, reliable internet to populations with little or no connectivity, including those in rural communities and places where existing services are too expensive or unreliable.</p> <p>As the development lead, you will be responsible for factory acceptance tests, equipment readiness, process development, trials, and production launch for silicon ingot growth and wafering. Additionally, you will be the day-to-day link between OEMs, development, operations, quality, equipment, and suppliers, moving new recipes, tools, and process changes from trial to stable production with clear documentation, yield targets, and a schedule.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES: </strong></p> <ul> <li>Plan, schedule, and run development trials on ingot pullers, crop and square, multi-wire saws, cleaning, and related metrology</li> <li>Turn engineering intent into trial plans: DOE, recipe versions, material lots, fixtures and consumables, and success criteria (yield, TTV, warp, resistivity, lifetime, breakage, kerf)</li> <li>Define process windows (pull rate, rotation, hot zone, slurry or diamond wire, tension, coolant, clean chemistry) and track KPIs such as kg/pull, wafer yield, kerf loss, downtime, scrap, and first-pass yield</li> <li>Coordinate tool time, material readiness, operator coverage, fixtures, hot-zone parts, wires, slurry and coolant, crucibles, and other consumables with production, maintenance, quality, EHS, and supply chain</li> <li>Track status, blockers, and results; escalate schedule, quality, or safety risks with options and owners; and give leadership concise updates</li> <li>Collect trial data and support root cause on trial and early-production issues (ingot defects, saw marks, TTV, warp, stains, lifetime)</li> <li>Own trial reports, work instructions, travelers, checklists, training notes, and revision control of recipes, fixtures, and consumable specs</li> <li>Initiate and track ECOs and process changes, including training and first-article or first-lot verification before release</li> <li>Partner with quality and metrology on incoming silicon, in-process checks, and outgoing wafer specs, and support vendor trials and incoming qualifications of new materials or tools</li> <li>Lead pilot-to-production transfer (standard work, operator training, control and reaction plans), support the ramp until rate and quality are stable, and capture lessons learned</li> <li>Enforce EHS requirements for high temperature, chemicals, slurry, wafer handling, lockout, PPE, and clean-area rules</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in materials science, chemistry, mechanical engineering, industrial engineering, or a STEM field</li> <li>5+ years in manufacturing process development or production coordination (semiconductor, PV, crystal growth, precision machining, or injection molding/process engineering strongly preferred)</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Experience in Czochralski ingot growth, wafering (wire saw), or a photovoltaic or semiconductor wafer fabrication line</li> <li>Familiarity with silicon specifications, including resistivity, lifetime, oxygen, and geometry (TTV, bow and warp, and thickness)</li> <li>Working knowledge of MES and QMS, change control, and basic CAD or process mapping</li> <li>Experience working with equipment teams and suppliers</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS: </strong></p> <ul> <li>Extended hours and weekend work may be required to support critical project and mission milestones</li> <li>Up to 10% travel is expected</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR <a href="https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/?id=ddtc_kb_article_page&amp;sys_id=24d528fddbfc930044f9ff621f961987">here</a>. &nbsp;</li> </ul> <p>SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.</p> <p>Applicants wishing to view a copy of SpaceX’s Affirmative Action Plan for veterans and individuals with disabilities, or applicants requiring reasonable accommodation to the application/interview process should reach out to&nbsp;<a href="mailto:EEOCompliance@spacex.com">EEOCompliance@spacex.com</a><em>.&nbsp;</em></p></div>

title: Starlink Production Associate
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>STARLINK PRODUCTION ASSOCIATE</strong></p> <p>One of the most ambitious missions that SpaceX has undertaken to date, the Starlink satellite constellation is our solution to providing fast and reliable internet to the entire world. This facility in Bastrop, TX manufactures the high-volume consumer products that we ship directly to customers. Our customers currently include teachers in the most remote parts of the Amazon, researchers in Antarctica, digital nomads who travel via RV, emergency responders, commercial airlines, cruise lines, and residential users who live in more rural or developing areas.</p> <p>This Production Associate position supports the Starlink product factory and manufacturing operation, which continues to grow as demand for Starlink increases globally. This is a hands-on position that operates light equipment and performs basic assembly tasks in an organized and efficient manner. We are looking for motivated and well-rounded workers to help ensure the productivity and reliability of our manufacturing facility, ultimately ensuring that we can produce thousands of Starlink kits every day.&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Support the development of prototype manufacturing and test capabilities</li> <li>Mechanical/electrical assembly of user terminal components, subassemblies, and final assembly according to instructions</li> <li>Operate light equipment such as drills, custom build tooling, crimpers, and presses</li> <li>Program, load, operate, and troubleshoot automated equipment</li> <li>Execute equipment maintenance and calibration schedules</li> <li>Maintain consumables inventory</li> <li>Assist engineers with development builds and other tasks</li> <li>Help develop and optimize production line stations and processes</li> <li>Keep a clean, organized, and thoroughly maintained workspace</li> <li>Ensure product quality and conformance to design requirements</li> <li>Put safety as number one priority</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>High school diploma or equivalency certificate</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>2+ years of mechanical or electrical assembly experience</li> <li>Demonstrated ability to read, interpret, and work from drawings and controlled documentation such as: layout drawings, mechanical drawings, assembly procedures/work instructions, schematics, engineering drawings, and parts lists</li> <li>Able to proficiently use a PC, Microsoft Windows, and Microsoft Office suite</li> <li>Experience working in an electro-mechanical manufacturing company, a precision manufacturing company, or high-volume manufacturing company</li> <li>Experience with electrical wiring</li> <li>Electro-mechanical assembly and prototype development experience</li> <li>Experience setting up and running tests and experiments</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Must be available to work at least one of the following shifts: <ul> <li>A Shift: 5 AM - 5:30 PM (Sunday through Tuesday and every other Wednesday)</li> <li>B Shift: 5 AM - 5:30 PM (Thursday through Saturday and every other Wednesday)</li> <li>C Shift: 5 PM - 5:30 AM (Sunday through Tuesday and every other Wednesday)</li> <li>D Shift: 5 PM - 5:30 AM (Thursday through Saturday and every other Wednesday)</li> </ul> </li> <li>Able to work all shifts, overtime and weekends as needed. Shifts are subject to change, we have multiple shifts, including late afternoons/nights</li> <li>Standing for long periods of time, climbing up and down ladders, bending, grasping, sitting, pulling, pushing, stooping, and stretching may be required to perform the functions of this position</li> <li>Able to lift up to 25lbs. unassisted</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. title: Starship Engineer, FOD Control
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>STARSHIP ENGINEER, FOD CONTROL</strong></p> <p>As a Starship Engineer specializing in FOD Control, you will own Foreign Object Debris (FOD) prevention and elimination across Starship Production while developing engineering and manufacturing processes that maximize quality at high rate. You will employ root cause investigations and data review to deploy robust fabrication methods, work instructions, tooling design, inspection and cleaning measures. Engineering design, process, facility and supply chain controls will all be areas of ownership.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:&nbsp;</strong></p> <ul> <li>Own FOD control strategy and execution for Starship Production; ensure facilities and processes comply with AS9146 (Foreign Object Debris Prevention Program) and related aerospace/defense standards.</li> <li>Partner with design engineering to apply Design for Manufacturability (DFM) and design-for-cleanliness principles—sealing machined areas, eliminating hidden cavities where debris can lodge, and enabling clean assembly line layouts—while influencing flight design and vehicle architecture.&nbsp;</li> <li>Develop and enforce manufacturing, integration, assembly, welding, NDE, cleanliness, and checkout processes across work centers, including Clean-As-You-Go methodologies, tool accountability tracking, and hardware kitting protocols.&nbsp;</li> <li>Design and implement precision tooling and poka-yoke systems for work access, build fixturing, lifting &amp; rigging, fluids, and mechanical/avionics/propulsion testing to eliminate assembly error, prevent FOD introduction, improve quality, and minimize cycle time.&nbsp;</li> <li>Develop, qualify, and automate manufacturing processes and in-situ inspection techniques to enable high-rate, repeatable production with higher yield and lower takt time.&nbsp;</li> <li>Evaluate and integrate automated FOD detection systems, millimeter-wave radar, and specialized mechanical sweeping equipment into production and integration environments.&nbsp;</li> <li>Define inspection requirements, author planning/test plans/work instructions, and create training for production and inspection—including FOD awareness—ensuring stable quality as volume scales.&nbsp;</li> <li>Contain non-conforming hardware with quality, production, and design; conduct build quality and FOD audits to identify high-impact issues; drive corrective action and manage fleet risk.&nbsp;</li> <li>Challenge and simplify requirements where design intent, cleanliness, and production rate conflict; manage transition of parts and assemblies from development to high-rate production with FOD controls built in.&nbsp;</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering, aerospace engineering, materials engineering, manufacturing engineering, chemical engineering, electrical engineering, engineering physics, or other engineering discipline.</li> <li>1+ years in manufacturing, quality, process design, and/or design engineering (student project team or internship experience qualifies).</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Master's degree in an engineering discipline.&nbsp;</li> <li>Experience developing or leading FOD prevention, cleanliness, contamination control, or AS9146 (or equivalent) programs.&nbsp;</li> <li>Hands-on experience with high-rate or mixed value stream manufacturing, focused on yield, rate, and process control.&nbsp;</li> <li>Experience building, assembling, or integrating aerospace hardware (structures, avionics, propulsion, fluids, valves, actuators, thermal protection, or similar).&nbsp;</li> <li>Mechanical tooling or component design with strong DFM; proficiency in assembly methods, testing, FMEA, and troubleshooting.&nbsp;</li> <li>Proficiency with 3D CAD (NX, SolidWorks, or CATIA).&nbsp;</li> <li>Knowledge of welding (MIG, TIG, laser, stud, spot, or robot) and NDT (visual, penetrant, x-ray, EMAT, or other); experience improving weld processes and inspection, including automation.&nbsp;</li> <li>Knowledge of metallic manufacturing processes (machining, forming, casting, additive, fastening, drilling, bonding).&nbsp;</li> <li>Experience evaluating or deploying automated inspection, sensing, detection, or shop-floor cleanup technology.&nbsp;</li> <li>Proficiency with SQL, Power BI, or similar tools to prioritize work and measure performance.&nbsp;</li> <li>Collegiate or hobby design project experience (Formula SAE, rocketry, etc.); thrives hands-on on the shop floor.&nbsp;</li> <li>Strong interpersonal skills and ability to collaborate across diverse engineering disciplines.&nbsp;</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Ability to work extended hours, weekends, and offsite as needed; schedule varies with site operational needs.&nbsp;</li> <li>Flexibility to travel to remote build sites, up to 10%.&nbsp;</li> <li>Flight hardware is built in tight quarters; physical dexterity required. Duties may include standing, kneeling, crouching, twisting, working in cramped openings, and climbing (including ladders/stairs up to 6 hours/day).&nbsp;</li> <li>Work may involve extreme outdoor environments (heat, cold, rain), temperatures over 80°F for 6+ hours/day, and exposure to fumes, odors, and noise.&nbsp;</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR <a href="https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/?id=ddtc_kb_article_page&amp;sys_id=24d528fddbfc930044f9ff621f961987">here</a>. &nbsp;</li> </ul> <p>SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.</p> <p>Applicants wishing to view a copy of SpaceX’s Affirmative Action Plan for veterans and individuals with disabilities, or applicants requiring reasonable accommodation to the application/interview process should reach out to&nbsp;<a href="mailto:EEOCompliance@spacex.com">EEOCompliance@spacex.com</a><em>.&nbsp;</em></p></div>

title: Strategic Connectivity Manager (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>STRATEGIC CONNECTIVITY&nbsp;MANAGER&nbsp;(STARLINK)&nbsp;</strong></p> <p>Starlink, our revolutionary satellite constellation, is delivering low-latency broadband internet around the world. In addition to the current use cases Starlink is serving in masse – such as residential, maritime, aviation, fixed site enterprise – there are many other uses cases and applications for Starlink that help social and economic development that require development or modification of existing capabilities and thinking. Examples include serving anchor institutions (schools, clinics, libraries, community centers, etc.), refugee camps, securing development bank funding, and supporting unique philanthropic efforts.&nbsp;</p> <p>The Strategic Connectivity Projects team is charged with identifying and enabling these projects by assessing the potential positive impact of projects, thinking creatively, applying excellent business judgement, and having a bias for action.&nbsp;</p> <p>We are searching for&nbsp;someone&nbsp;to apply additional focus to these projects&nbsp;in the APAC, Middle East, and Central Asia region =, to increase the pace of progress and scale the impact by orders of magnitude. Our ideal candidate is a self-starter that has a passion for expanding connectivity access, building excellent teams, sharing the stories of how Starlink can positively impact social and economic development, and managing complex cross-functional projects.&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:&nbsp;</strong></p> <ul> <li>Scale the use of Starlink in projects that have significant positive social and economic impact around the world&nbsp;</li> <li>Develop and execute strategies that align with Starlink business goals as well as team-specific goals&nbsp;</li> <li>Manage and grow capabilities to enable embracing projects of all sizes&nbsp;</li> <li>Select, establish, and maintain key relationships that align with the strategy and mission, such as influential individuals, philanthropic entities, non-governmental organizations, and development banks&nbsp;</li> <li>Measure and report progress towards goals, establishing new tracking methods if required&nbsp;</li> <li>Maintain a strong grasp of standard Starlink product offerings and business processes&nbsp;</li> <li>Apply excellent business judgement on if, when, and how to deviate&nbsp;</li> <li>Ensure Starlink products, processes and capabilities develop with social and economic development project use cases in mind by identifying and justifying necessary changes or deviations&nbsp;</li> title: Structural Welder, Massey's Test Site - Night Shift
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>STRUCTURAL WELDER, MASSEY’S TEST SITE - NIGHT SHIFT</strong></p> <p>As a structural welder on our ground support equipment team, you'll fabricate and repair the robust stands and structures that support Starship's historic launches and tests. Join a dynamic night shift crew in a high-energy environment where your precision welding directly enables reusable rocketry and rapid innovation.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Execute welding assignments and procedures for constructing and repairing site structural stands, delivering high-quality results on time, safely, and professionally to support mission-critical timelines</li> <li>Cut, trim, or scarf metal objects; fit and fabricate components to precise dimensions for assembling test site structural forms that withstand extreme launch conditions</li> <li>Under lead welder supervision, interpret engineering drawings and specifications to plan operations, filling procedural gaps and driving efficient problem-solving</li> <li>Operate hand welding and flame-cutting equipment to join metal components, assembling durable structural forms essential for ground support reliability</li> <li>Visually inspect welds to AWS D1.1 and ASME B31.3 standards (for normal and high-pressure service), maintaining top-tier quality with proper training</li> <li>Secure and maintain internal licenses, operator permits, or certifications as needed to uphold safety and compliance</li> <li>Continuously optimize operations: reduce turnaround times, streamline processes, and collaborate across teams to accelerate program goals</li> <li>Thrive in a fast-paced setting with shifting priorities, adapting to evolving program needs while performing related duties to foster an efficient work environment</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>High school diploma or equivalency certificate</li> <li>2+ years of hands-on experience with flux-cored arc welding (FCAW)</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>5+ years in shielded metal arc welding (SMAW), gas metal arc welding (GMAW), flux-cored arc welding (FCAW), oxy-acetylene cutting, fitting, and arc gouging</li> <li>Strong knowledge of welding title: Supervisor, Hardware Reliability
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>SUPERVISOR, HARDWARE RELIABILITY (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>At SpaceX we’re leveraging our experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation and is providing fast, reliable internet to millions of users worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system – thousands of satellites, consumer receivers that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing, and the software that brings it all together. We’ve only begun to scratch the surface of Starlink’s potential global impact and are looking for best-in-class engineers to help maximize Starlink’s utility for communities and businesses around the globe.</p> <p>As a Supervisor on the Starlink Hardware Reliability team, you will lead a group of technicians and specialists responsible for root causing production failures on Starlink hardware. You will own the day-to-day operations of the production root cause lab and drive improvements that directly enhance product reliability and manufacturing quality.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES</strong>:</p> <ul> <li>Lead, mentor, and develop a team of reliability technicians and specialists performing root cause analysis on electrical systems and PCBAs</li> <li>Drive root cause findings into actionable improvements with manufacturing and design teams to reduce failure rates and improve yield</li> <li>Own day-to-day operations of the production root cause lab, including technician scheduling, equipment maintenance, lab organization (5S), and resource planning</li> <li>Develop and implement new processes and tools that improve the team’s ability to efficiently and accurately root cause electrical failures</li> <li>Establish clear priorities across multiple shifts and ensure timely communication of findings and recommendations to production stakeholders</li> <li>Define and track team performance metrics and key indicators, holding the team accountable to measurable outcomes</li> <li>Identify development opportunities for team members that align with both individual growth and Starlink program goals</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>High school diploma or equivalency certificate</li> <li>3+ years of quality or reliability experience in a manufacturing environment</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in electrical, mechanical, manufacturing, aerospace engineering, or related technical field</li> <li>Demonstrated experience performing root cause analysis on electrical systems and PCBAs with expertise in diagnosing and resolving issues related to solder joint quality, component failures, and manufacturing/assembly defects</li> <li>Experience training, mentoring, and developing technicians or junior engineers</li> <li>Proven ability to work in a fast-paced, highly iterative environment with rapidly changing priorities</li> <li>Strong track record of influencing cross-functional teams through data-driven analysis and clear communication</li> <li>Demonstrated ability to organize, prioritize, and drive completion of work across a team</li> <li>Experience jumping into ambiguous problems and driving them to resolution</li> <li>Excellent verbal and written communication skills</li> <li>Experience in consumer electronics, aerospace, automotive, or other high-volume hardware manufacturing environments</li> <li>Familiarity with quality management systems (ISO 9001 or equivalent)</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Ability to work extended hours, weekends, and offsite as needed</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) Our goal is to become a leader in logistics performance with high on time delivery rates. The Supervisor will be responsible for managing the day-to-day activities and exceeding customer expectations by leading continuous improvement to improve all aspects of logistics management.</p> title: Supervisor, Hospitality
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>HOSPITALITY SUPERVISOR</strong></p> <p>The SpaceX Hospitality team serves all employees, customers, government partners, potential clients and/or visitors with everything from snacks to daily meals to full-service events. The Hospitality Supervisor supports the direction and management of the organization’s food/beverage operations and is directly responsible for the quality of service throughout one or more of our food service outlets/catering locations. This role assists in developing and implementing effective customer service strategies and training programs. Duties include, but are not limited to, coordinating service operations; monitoring, positioning, and motivating staff; ensuring excellent customer service; engaging with customers; hiring, onboarding, and developing talent; maintaining team compliance with mandatory trainings; handling scheduling and payroll; and setting/upholding customer service principles. Additionally, maintaining food safety and sanitation standards is of utmost importance and necessity to protect the health of all served individuals, comply with regulations, and uphold the organization's commitment to excellence. The Hospitality Supervisor supports SpaceX’s mission by overseeing day-to-day hospitality functions and providing quality food/beverage options. This creates&nbsp;exemplary, professional and welcoming service&nbsp;environments that enhance productivity and morale.&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong>&nbsp;</p> <ul> <li>Set and enforce standards for hospitality operations and guest interactions</li> <li>Support conceptualization and implementation of new services, offerings, and training programs</li> <li>Oversee day-to-day operations through one or more food service outlets/catering locations</li> <li>Manage direct reports, including hiring, performance evaluations, development opportunities, 1:1 meetings, responsibility assignment, communication facilitation, and feedback documentation</li> <li>Assist with organizing and coordinating events, including large onsite/offsite gatherings and catering requests</li> <li>Enforce food safety practices and maintain clean, safe workstations</li> <li>Coordinate and enhance team time management</li> <li>Train staff on customer service expectations, menu knowledge, allergen, and nutritional awareness; create and maintain in-person and online training materials</li> <li>Manage and monitor product quality, consistency, service, menu accuracy, and inventory levels; address issues as needed</li> <li>Monitor financial activities, support scheduling, sales data collection/reporting, and other administrative tasks</li> <li>Communicate with vendors for orders, deliveries, and product quality issues</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong>&nbsp;</p> <ul> <li>High school diploma or equivalency certificate&nbsp;</li> <li>6+ years of within the food service industry&nbsp;</li> <li>Experience opening new operations and/or creating operations procedures from the ground up</li> <li>Experience managing a team in fine dining, upscale, casual and quick service restaurants</li> <li>Excellent interpersonal, oral and written communication skills&nbsp;</li> <li>Excellent time management skills&nbsp;</li> <li>Excellent understanding of food safety and sanitation practices</li> <li>Excellent knowledge of food service systems, ordering and inventory</li> <li>Advanced computer skills including Microsoft Office</li> <li>Advanced knowledge with allergen identification and dietary restrictions</li> <li>Advanced knowledge of beverage service including beer, wine and spirits</li> <li>Showcases high level of professionalism</li> <li>Experience in a corporate environment</li> <li>Proficient knowledge of HR best practices</li> <li>Experience leading groups in large team settings of 10 or more staff members</li> </ul> title: Supervisor, IT Network Infrastructure - 1st Shift
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>SUPERVISOR, IT NETWORK INFRASTRUCTURE - 1ST SHIFT</strong></p> <p>SpaceX technical teams work in a complex environment supporting a variety of critical production, launch and landing activities. The Network Infrastructure team installs and supports the low voltage used for all types of telecommunications in support of the production and launch vehicles and spacecraft.&nbsp; This includes but not limited to installation and support of the layer 1 fiber and copper data network cabling infrastructure, support of mission video, ground-side vehicle and payload interface systems, ground stations, telemetry and optical tracking systems, marine communications, readiness testing, and other systems involved in real-time communications and operations for Falcon, Dragon, Starship and other missions.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Supervise technician teams to install and maintain mission critical communication systems</li> <li>Prioritize and schedule work to meet required timelines</li> <li>Provide feedback and progress updates to project stakeholders</li> <li>Evaluate, diagnose, troubleshoot cabling infrastructure systems and perform repairs as necessary</li> <li>Coordinate with other contractors and project teams as needed</li> <li>Collaborate with the communication engineers and telecommunication specialist in system designs, selection of materials, and creation of documentation</li> <li>Interface with external carriers (private and government) at cross-connect facilities, and transition points</li> <li>Provide superior customer service to SpaceX launch customers</li> <li>Provide QA and auditing before and after work</li> <li>Maintain the integrity of the documentation of all installations including assets, locations, connectivity, and the patch record databases&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</li> <li>Assist with the creation of local and companywide installation and workmanship standards</li> <li>Provide ongoing feedback, periodic review, and corrective action to direct reports</li> <li>Review timesheets, manage overtime and time off requests</li> <li>Verify compliance with OSHA regulations and SpaceX safety requirements</li> <li>Assist in the evaluation and selection of candidates for open positions in the team</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>High school diploma or equivalency certificate</li> <li>5+ years of telecommunications systems experience</li> <li>2+ years prior leadership experience (leading teams, projects or people)</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Technical expertise in the installation, termination, testing of low voltage cables and fiber optical cables to include twisted pair, coaxial, stranded and solid conductor low voltage cables, single mode and multi-mode fiber optical cables</li> <li>Strong knowledge of industry standards (BICSI, NEC, TIA/EIA); different types of fiber (MM, SM) for interior and exterior usage; Cat5E, Cat6 and Cat6A data cabling; and cable pathways such as conduit, fire penetrations and cable trays</li> <li>Knowledge of the telecom network best practices and concepts including network security, network architecture design, technical standards and deliverables, troubleshooting tools (e.g., line analyzers, breakout boxes, and network traces), software and hardware installation and configuration, network hardware, and protocols (e.g., TCP/IP, DLC, and ASYNC)</li> <li>Working knowledge of audio, video, and wireless systems and corresponding physical means of delivery (analog, digital, AoIP, VoIP, etc.)</li> <li>Operational knowledge of oscilloscopes and multi-meters, soldering wires and connectors, various crimping tools, wire stripping techniques, Ohm’s law, continuity testing, pinning out a military type connector, routing and tie wrapping cables, drilling and tapping holes, and building junction boxes&nbsp;</li> <li>Experience with DC power supplies, DC-DC converters, heat shrink tubing, cable harnessing, lacing, and proper strain relief concepts</li> <li>Experience with IP and HD-SDI video cameras and infrastructure</li> <li>Comprehension of modern networking architecture and what is necessary for physical layer inter-connectivity</li> <li>Experience operating articulating boom lifts, fork lifts, scissor lifts, and other work site machinery</li> <li>Proficient in the use of Visio or other CAD software to read and develop system documentation</li> <li>Experience in the installation and operation of RF communication systems</li> <li>IP and HD-SDI Video cameras and infrastructure</li> <li>Comprehension of modern networking architecture and what is necessary for physical layer inter-connectivity</li> <li>Working knowledge of electrical systems including UPS and standby power systems</li> <li>Sound knowledge of computer skills, MS Words, Excel, and Power Point</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Must be able to work 1st shift: Monday-Friday, 5:30AM-3:30PM</li> <li>Ability to distinguish between different colors and possess manual dexterity to complete fine motor tasks</li> <li>Ability to work at elevated heights and/or tight spaces</li> <li>Physical effort including standing, lifting and carrying moderately heavy materials (up to 25 lbs unassisted) or equipment&nbsp;</li> <li>Regularly exposed to work in extreme outdoor environments – heat, cold, rain</li> <li>Work occasionally performed in an environment requiring exposure to fumes, odors, and noise</li> <li>Willingness to work long hours, some nights and weekends when need to meet critical deadlines</li> <li>Ability to travel (up to 25%) as required to common destinations including Hawthorne, CA (SpaceX headquarters); McGregor, TX (SpaceX test site); Vandenberg, CA (SpaceX west coast launch site); Cape Canaveral, FL (SpaceX east coast launch site)</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR <a href="https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/?id=ddtc_kb_article_page&amp;sys_id=24d528fddbfc930044f9ff621f961987">here</a>. &nbsp;</li> </ul> <p>SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.</p> <p>Applicants wishing to view a copy of SpaceX’s Affirmative Action Plan for veterans and individuals with disabilities, or applicants requiring reasonable accommodation to the application/interview process should reach out to&nbsp;<a href="mailto:EEOCompliance@spacex.com">EEOCompliance@spacex.com</a><em>.&nbsp;</em></p></div>

title: Supervisor, Machining & Fabrication
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>SUPERVISOR, MACHINING &amp; FABRICATION (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is developing a low latency, broadband internet system to meet the needs of consumers across the globe. Enabled by a constellation of low Earth orbit satellites, Starlink provides fast, reliable internet to populations with little or no connectivity, including those in rural communities and places where existing services are too expensive or unreliable.</p> <p>We are looking for an organized, creative, technically sharp, and driven Supervisor to lead the Machining &amp; Fabrication team. This is a group of highly skilled technicians and automation specialists. As the team Supervisor, you and your team will be at the center of fabricating all engineering R&amp;D and factory build-outs supporting exciting programs like high volume Starlink User Terminal assembly line technologies, PCB manufacturing, silicon packaging, and brand new products yet to be dreamed of.</p> <p>You will manage a diverse team of fabrication, assembly, electrical, and automation experts in close partnership to key engineering leaders across Starlink, with expectation to grow the capabilities, skills, and output of a fast-growing team and Bastrop site. Your ability to lead in a highly dynamic environment will have immense impact on the output of Starlink products being distributed to the entire world.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Build and lead a group of technicians and specialists that fabricate, build, integrate, and deploy Starlink factory equipment and tooling</li> <li>Collaborate with the broader development operations and automation teams to achieve factory infrastructure deployment targets and milestones</li> <li>Manage tooling/testing equipment and infrastructure required to support engineering, automation, and product development projects</li> <li>Manage the parts inventory used to build standard factory assets, set targets for the team, and drive continuous improvement</li> <li>Provide mentorship to technicians/specialists and assist with design decisions, project strategies, and technical problems</li> <li>Provide technical support and feedback to engineering groups on tooling, fabrication, testing, and maintenance</li> <li>Ensure technicians and specialists on the team have the training, tools, and materials needed to carry out their duties – including creating and giving safety trainings to all members of the team</li> <li>Identify and execute on projects that improve overall program success and progress</li> <li>Take input from partner teams to align team priorities with broader program priorities</li> <li>Improve factory safety and efficiency through regular auditing and continuous improvement</li> <li>Enforce area standards and rules (including bi-annual reviews, disciplinary action, and time management)</li> <li>Report on project status and critical path items to management and key stakeholders for alignment</li> <li>Provide surge support and leadership as needed by traveling to other SpaceX sites to deploy factory assets</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree and 2+ years of professional experience in machining, maintenance, or production/manufacturing; OR 5+ years of professional experience in machining, maintenance, or production/manufacturing in lieu of a degree</li> <li>2+ years of professional experience managing a team or leading projects</li> </ul> <p><strong>&nbsp;PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Comprehensive knowledge of conventional machining, CNC programming, machining operations, and quality inspection procedures</li> <li>Experienced in welding techniques, fabrication processes, and precision mechanical assembly operations</li> <li>Experience managing large scale electromechanical projects by coordinating resources appropriately and collaborating with cross functional teams to achieve program objectives</li> <li>Knowledge of electrical theory, power distribution (both low and high voltage) and pneumatics</li> <li>Experience working with electrical/pneumatic/hydraulic schematics</li> <li>Familiar with NFPA 70 (National Electrical Code), NFPA 70E (Standard for Electrical Safety), NFPA 79, and/or UL 508A standards</li> <li>Demonstrable hands-on skill in fault finding and technical problem resolution</li> <li>Ability to bring multiple departments with different priorities together and support them in achieving common goals</li> <li>Ability to coordinate multiple projects on a large scale with multiple stakeholders and deliver on schedule</li> <li>Ability to work in a fast-paced environment and adjust team priorities as broader program priorities shift</li> <li>Strong communication skills both written and verbal</li> <li>Proficient in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Smartsheet (or equivalent)</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Must be willing to work extended hours and/or weekends as needed</li> <li>Standing for long periods of time, climbing up and down ladders, bending, grasping, pulling, pushing, and stretching may be required to perform the functions of this position</li> <li>Ability to lift 30lbs. unassisted</li> <li>Willing to travel up to 20% of the time to support business needs</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR title: Supervisor, Materials Management (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>SUPERVISOR, MATERIALS MANAGEMENT (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p><span class="ui-provider ec bwu bgd bwv bww bwx bwy bwz bxa bxb bxc bxd bxe bxf bxg bxh bxi bxj bxk bxl bxm bxn bxo bxp bxq bxr bxs bxt bxu bxv bxw bxx bxy bxz bya">At SpaceX we’re leveraging our experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation and is providing fast, reliable internet to millions of users worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system – thousands of satellites, consumer receivers that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing, and the software that brings it all together. We’ve only begun to scratch the surface of Starlink’s potential global impact and are looking for best-in-class engineers to help maximize Starlink’s utility for communities and businesses around the world.&nbsp;</span></p> <p>This role will involve the supervision of a team of hourly employees operating within SpaceX’s materials management organization. The team is responsible for all activities from the point that hardware is deemed acceptable from our quality inspections to the moment hardware is handed off to the production organization. Our goal is to become a leader in materials management performance with high inventory efficiency/accuracy and industry-leading customer service while maintaining a safe work environment that utilizes the latest in applicable technologies. This supervisor will also be responsible for leading and driving continuous improvement throughout all aspects of their operations.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Manage an hourly workforce by assessing employee performance, providing positive/constructive feedback, facilitating conflict resolution, and addressing repeat issues with corrective actions, performance improvement plans, or through disciplinary means</li> <li>Lead by setting an example, taking feedback from all levels of the organization, and motivating your organization to achieve the highest level of results</li> <li>Monitor and improve operations, ensuring a safe work environment – with the goal of zero OSHA recordable annually</li> <li>Ensure business practices are being followed to not only guarantee the processing of products in a quality manner but also meet those needs outlined in AS9100 and customer flow-down requirements</li> <li>Manage the incoming acceptance, storing, and issuing of a wide variety of parts, details, and hardware into inventory</li> <li>Manage operations that provide industry-leading levels of customer service in all operations: recognizing the needs of the business and adapting to support our mission</li> <li>Lead cost-saving opportunities, identifying internal/external cost reductions and optimization opportunities</li> <li>Ensure cycle counting procedures are routinely followed to meet both our internal and external audit requirements</li> <li>Assist in the control of a fleet of vehicles, ensuring the necessary preventative maintenance, upkeep, and enhancements are made to service the customer</li> <li>Develop and maintain the appropriate service routes and material replenishments to deliver material to internal customers at agreed-upon service levels</li> <li>Supervise the local shipping and receiving operation; coordinating movements into and out of the local facility, along with critical point-to-point movements outside of the local facility</li> <li>Drive projects and changes that contribute to materials management’s ongoing improvement</li> <li>Ensure procedures are routinely being followed for shelf-life storage and maintain proper rotation of stock, FIFO</li> <li>Ensure the appropriate environmental controls are continuously effective, depending on the material requirements of the items being stored</li> <li>Actively monitor and grow the workforce, ensuring team members are challenged and performing at the expected standards</li> <li>Monitor and approve employee time-keeping records</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree and 2+ years of professional experience in materials management, supply chain, or production/manufacturing; OR 4+ years of professional experience in materials management, supply chain, or production/manufacturing</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in supply chain, business, science, engineering, or similar technical discipline</li> <li>Completion of a leadership or rotational development program</li> <li>The Association for Operations Management (APICS) certification – CPIM or CSCP</li> <li>Lean/6-Sigma experience (Green/Black Belt certifications)</li> <li>Excellent communication and team-building skills</li> <li>Organized and self-driven, capable of working independently with little direction</li> <li>Ability to work in a fast-paced /cross-functional environment</li> <li>Experience within an aerospace, aviation, or automotive manufacturing environment</li> <li>Computer Skills – Microsoft Office applications, SQL and PowerBI</li> </ul> <p><strong>&nbsp;ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>A Shift – 5:00am-5:00pm, Sunday-Wednesday</li> <li>B Shift – 5:00am-5:00pm, Wednesday-Saturday</li> <li>Must be willing to work extended hours and/or weekends as needed</li> <li>Lifting, standing, climbing, bending, grasping, sitting, pulling, pushing stooping, stretching and carrying are generally required to perform the functions of this position</li> <li>Must be able to operate forklift equipment</li> <li>Must be able to work in areas that require using a ladder (20 feet)</li> <li>Must be able to relocate to the Bastrop, TX area if not already local. title: Supervisor, Spaceport Operations
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>SUPERVISOR, SPACEPORT OPERATIONS</strong></p> <p>The role of Spaceport Operations Supervisor will be to provide the management of the organization’s housing accommodations, transportation, site amenities, and customer service. You will help develop and implement effective customer service strategies and training programs. The duties of Spaceport Operations Supervisor will include but are not limited to: coordinating service operations, monitoring and motivating staff, ensuring excellent customer service, engaging with customers, creating and implementing processes to improve the growing operation, ensuring team is current with all mandatory company trainings, scheduling and payroll, interviewing, hiring and onboarding of new staff, setting and upholding customer service principles. The Spaceport Operations Supervisor will support the mission by providing a foundation of understanding for excellent customer service and quality of living and visiting accommodations that boost morale and productivity within SpaceX.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Oversee Spaceport operations including strategy and execution leasing/traveler housing program, transportation and amenities</li> <li>Monitor quality and consistency of Spaceport operations by setting and enforcing standards, inspecting and routinely walking areas of responsibility</li> title: Supplier Development Engineer (Materials Engineering)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><span data-teams="true"><strong>SUPPLIER DEVELOPMENT ENGINEER (MATERIALS ENGINEERING)</strong></span></p> <p>SpaceX demands a new type of supply chain. We require our suppliers to provide premium quality with rapidly evolving designs at increasingly ambitious volumes. We are actively looking for candidates who possess comprehensive knowledge of manufacturing and quality tools and have unrelenting motivation to enable suppliers for success. This position will support our Starship program and requires a combination of proven leadership and technical capabilities.</p> <p>This is a highly technical position that requires practical experience in manufacturing engineering and new product development through to stabilized production for an array of fabrication processes (components and assemblies) used in rockets and rocket engines.&nbsp;The ideal candidate will have a broad and thorough understanding of propulsion/fluid system component fabrication including extrusions, draw forming, welded and seamless tubing, cutting, and assembly, along with associated processes. This candidate should have the desire and capability to take on new challenges in unfamiliar areas to help enable our mission to Mars.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Serve as the technical point of contact for assigned parts and assemblies of the rocket, solving emergent challenges at suppliers, and mitigating risk to the manifest by addressing high-impact manufacturing and quality challenges</li> <li>Own the new product introduction of new assemblies on the rocket, including determining the ideal manufacturing method, identifying suppliers, and developing a reliable process for ramping to rate. This individual is expected to be the extreme owner for the process at suppliers for new parts, drawing changes, or when re-sourcing existing parts to a new supplier</li> <li>Conduct design for manufacturing (DFM) reviews to ensure parts are manufacturable at early stages, preferably prior to sourcing</li> <li>Work with procurement to find exceptional suppliers and vet them appropriately for quality and ability to meet our aggressive takt times</li> <li>Create and develop specifications as needed to flow down quality and manufacturing requirements to the supply base</li> <li>Scope out new forming, cutting, and inspection technologies and suppliers that may be employed to improve rate/quality/efficiency</li> <li>Review issues on assigned parts and solve to the root cause, implementing changes at the supplier, at SpaceX or both, as appropriate, drive further actions to closure, and re-source to new suppliers where appropriate</li> <li>Create and disposition issue tickets where needed, working with engineering counterparts to implement, but not limited to, required re-work, repair or use as-is disposition</li> <li>Become thoroughly familiar with your assigned parts and the processes that make up the overall assembly and become the primary point of contact for supply chain related defects on your parts</li> <li>Demonstrate innovation, technical excellence, attention to detail, self-direction and courage to push the technical envelope which is conventionally held in the industry.</li> <li>Lead containment activities on assigned parts, working with cross-functional counterparts to agree on scope, path forward and ultimate resolution</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in an engineering discipline&nbsp;</li> <li>1+ years of experience with manufacturing and/or inspection of mechanical products in a production environment</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Master’s degree in engineering or business</li> <li>Fundamental understanding of propulsion/fluid systems and the respective component manufacturing processes including: raw materials, draw forming, extrusions, seamless and welded tubing, pipe manufacturing, bending, welding, proof/pressure testing, and other forming &amp; assembly processes.</li> <li>Fundamental understanding of sheet metal forming, cutting, and assembly processes, particularly in stretch forming (longitudinal and transverse), stamping (progressing and transfer), spin forming, roll forming, roll bending, press brake forming, hydroforming and tube forming/bending of primarily, but not limited to, stainless and carbon steels.</li> <li>Experience with machining and ancillary operations such as milling, turning, and tube cutting of materials</li> <li>Experience with engineering drawings, modeling, GD&amp;T, etc.</li> <li>General familiarity with welding (TIG, MIG and orbital tube welding) of stainless and carbon steels is a plus</li> <li>Knowledge of supplier quality processes (production part approval process, advanced product quality planning, first article inspection reports, etc.)</li> <li>Knowledge of statistical techniques and methods, e.g., design of experiments, Lean, Six Sigma, etc.</li> <li>Experience with quality systems (ISO 9000/TS/AS9100/NADCAP) and MRP/ERP systems</li> <li>Disciplined approach to problem solving - 8D</li> <li>Proficient in MS Office and Excel applications and report writing</li> <li>Experience with sharing information and influencing others across organizational lines, internally and externally</li> <li>Experience with PPAP and related elements (PFD, PFMEA, control plan, process capability, etc.)</li> <li>Experience leading containments of discrepant product</li> <li>Experience in manufacturing with different grades of stainless steel</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Ability to work extended hours, some nights and/or weekends when needed</li> <li>Ability to travel: up to 40-50% work week travel</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. title: Supplier Development Engineer, Assembly Processes (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>SUPPLIER DEVELOPMENT ENGINEER, ASSEMBLY PROCESSES (STARLINK)&nbsp;</strong></p> <p>Starlink User Terminal business is experiencing exponential growth across consumer, retail, enterprise, and mobility applications. This rapid expansion requires a highly resilient and scalable supply chain with world-class precision assembly processes at contract manufacturers.&nbsp;The role entails early engagement in supplier selection, equipment selection, and process engineering to set programs up for success in high-volume manufacturing by ensuring material and process corners are fully completed. The role also includes ownership to deliver on time, monitor field performance, react to issues, and feed lessons learned back to engineering teams for iterative improvement.</p> <p>We are seeking a technically strong Supplier Development Engineer to drive equipment bring-up and process development for critical joining, dispensing, and inspection technologies. This role focuses on developing robust, high-volume manufacturing processes for hardware to be manufactured at contract manufacturers, with emphasis on plastic and metal joining methods, precision material dispensing, and automated quality inspection.&nbsp;The Supplier Development Engineer, Assembly Processes will be responsible for end-to-end process development and qualification of joining, dispensing, and inspection systems. This position demands deep manufacturing process expertise and extreme ownership from early equipment selection through process characterization, line qualification, and field performance feedback.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Own end-to-end process development, equipment bring-up, and qualification for precision assembly technologies at contract manufacturers, spanning strategic supplier selection, new product introduction (NPI), and high-volume production</li> <li>Engage early with suppliers on equipment selection, tooling design, and process engineering to properly set up high-volume manufacturing programs by ensuring material and process corners are fully characterized and completed</li> <li>Lead development of ultrasonic welding processes, including amplitude, force, energy, weld time, and trigger optimization, as well as horn design, joint geometry, and weld strength validation for both metal and thermoplastic components</li> <li>Develop hot plate welding and vibration welding processes for plastic housings and enclosures, focusing on temperature uniformity, platen design, melt displacement control, weld pressure profiles, and long-term joint durability</li> <li>Optimize heat staking and hot riveting processes for plastic boss forming, including temperature control, pressure profiling, staking tool design, and dimensional stability validation</li> <li>Develop and qualify precision dispense processes for thermal interface materials (TIM), adhesives, and sealants, including rheological characterization, volumetric vs. time-pressure dispensing, needle selection, vision-guided positioning, and repeatable bead or dot formation</li> <li>Establish and optimize automated optical inspection (AOI) systems, including multi-angle lighting techniques, high-resolution imaging, algorithm development, false call reduction, and integration with deep learning-based defect detection</li> <li>Design and execute comprehensive design of experiments (DOE) and corner case studies (material and process windows) to define robust parameter ranges and ensure process capability across environmental and material variations</li> <li>Lead line qualification activities at contract manufacturers, including equipment installation qualification (IQ), operational qualification (OQ), performance qualification (PQ), gauge repeatability and reproducibility (GR&amp;R), and production part approval process (PPAP)</li> <li>Develop detailed process control plans, failure mode and effects analysis (FMEA), statistical process control (SPC) limits, and reaction plans to sustain high process capability in mass production</li> <li>Perform reactive quality engineering support, including rapid containment, root cause analysis using eight disciplines (8D) and five-whys (5-Why) methodologies, and corrective actions for quality escapes, field returns, and production issues</li> <li>Own on-time delivery of process qualification and production ramp activities while continuously monitoring field performance, reacting quickly to issues, and feeding lessons learned from field data back to design and process engineering teams for iterative improvement</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering, manufacturing engineering, materials science, or other engineering discipline</li> <li>1+ years of experience in precision joining, dispensing, and automated inspection process development for consumer electronics or complex hardware&nbsp;</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Strong technical background in ultrasonic welding, hot plate welding, vibration welding, precision dispensing, and automated optical inspection</li> <li>Hands-on experience bringing up and qualifying ultrasonic welding, hot plate welding, vibration welding, and heat staking processes in high-volume production environments</li> <li>Deep expertise in thermal interface material (TIM) and sealant dispensing, including viscosity control, dispense valve technology, and closed-loop feedback systems</li> <li>Strong experience developing automated optical inspection (AOI) systems, including illumination optimization, image processing, and defect classification algorithms</li> <li>Expertise in statistical methods including design of experiments (DOE), statistical process control (SPC), process capability analysis (Cp/Cpk), and measurement system analysis (MSA)</li> <li>Experience leading full line qualification (IQ/OQ/PQ) and production part approval process (PPAP) at contract manufacturers</li> <li>Knowledge of relevant standards including IPC-A-610, IPC-J-STD-001, ISO 9001, and AS9100</li> <li>Strong problem-solving skills using structured root cause analysis methods and statistical tools such as Minitab and design of experiments (DOE)</li> <li>Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to distill complex technical topics into clear one-pagers, process characterization reports, and executive presentations</li> <li>Demonstrated ability to influence cross-functional teams and contract manufacturers in a fast-paced, high-growth environment</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Ability to travel up to 30% of the time, both domestically and internationally</li> <li>Position may require extended working hours and occasional weekends to support equipment bring-up and production ramps</li> <li>This position is based in Bastrop, TX and requires being onsite</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR <a href="https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/?id=ddtc_kb_article_page&amp;sys_id=24d528fddbfc930044f9ff621f961987">here</a>. &nbsp;</li> </ul> <p>SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.</p> <p>Applicants wishing to view a copy of SpaceX’s Affirmative Action Plan for veterans and individuals with disabilities, or applicants requiring reasonable accommodation to the application/interview process should reach out to&nbsp;<a href="mailto:EEOCompliance@spacex.com">EEOCompliance@spacex.com</a><em>.&nbsp;</em></p></div>

This rapid expansion requires a highly resilient and scalable supply chain for Power over Ethernet (PoE) cables, AC power cords, and associated connectivity components.&nbsp;The role entails early engagement in supplier selection, equipment selection, and process engineering to set programs up for success in high-volume manufacturing by ensuring material and process corners are fully completed. The role also includes ownership to deliver on time, monitor field performance, react to issues, and feed lessons learned back to engineering teams for iterative improvement.</p> <p>We are seeking a technically strong Supplier Development Engineer to drive end-to-end supplier development for the PoE and AC cable portfolio — from strategic supplier selection and new product introduction (NPI) through high-volume production scaling and reactive quality support. The ideal candidate will bring deep expertise in cable design, manufacturing processes, and quality systems.&nbsp;The Senior Supplier Development Engineer, Cables will be responsible for executing supplier strategies focused on Power over Ethernet (PoE) cables, AC power cords, and critical connectivity components. This position will have significant technical influence across Starlink engineering, quality, and supply chain teams.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Own end-to-end supplier development for the PoE, AC cable, and power cord portfolio within the Starlink User Terminal Bill of Materials, spanning strategic supplier selection, new product introduction (NPI), qualification, production ramp, and reactive quality support</li> <li>Engage early with suppliers on selection, equipment selection, and process engineering to properly set up high-volume manufacturing programs by ensuring material and process corners are fully characterized and completed</li> <li>Assess supplier manufacturing capabilities, process controls, and technical readiness for high-volume production of PoE and AC cables, including conductor stranding, extrusion, shielding, termination, crimping, and connector molding processes</li> <li>Lead new product introduction (NPI) activities, production part approval process (PPAP), first article inspections (FAI), production rate ramps, and reliability campaigns to enable full-rate, high-volume manufacturing</li> <li>Develop and execute robust qualification plans tailored to cable commodities, including temperature rise testing under PoE load, bundle heating validation, flex-life cycling, insulation resistance, hi-pot testing, and electromagnetic interference and electromagnetic compatibility (EMI/EMC) compliance</li> <li>Create and standardize qualification protocols across the cable supply base, including equipment buy-off checklists, factory acceptance tests (FAT), site acceptance tests (SAT), and consistent reliability demonstration methods</li> <li>Drive supplier performance improvement through Lean methodologies, supplier scorecards, process audits, and systematic problem solving to deliver measurable gains in quality, cost, and on-time delivery</li> <li>Perform root cause analysis and lead corrective actions for quality issues, with focus on common cable failure modes such as insulation cracking, conductor fatigue and breakage, poor crimp termination, increased contact resistance, PoE-related overheating in bundles, shield discontinuities, and strain relief failures</li> <li>Perform reactive quality engineering support, including rapid containment, root cause analysis using eight disciplines (8D) and five-whys (5-Why) methodologies, and corrective actions for quality escapes, field returns, and production issues</li> <li>Own on-time delivery of qualification and production ramp activities while continuously monitoring field performance, reacting quickly to issues, and feeding lessons learned from field data back to design and process engineering teams for iterative product and process improvement</li> <li>Partner closely with Cable Design Engineering, Test Engineering, and Production teams to ensure supplier processes and manufacturing capability align with Starlink’s high-volume product requirements and performance goals</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, materials science, or a other engineering discipline</li> <li>1+ years of experience in cable engineering, quality engineering, reliability engineering, or supplier development (internship and extracurricular experience is applicable)</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>3+ years of experience in cable engineering, quality engineering, reliability engineering, or supplier development</li> <li>Strong technical background in Power over Ethernet (PoE) standards, AC cord requirements, cable construction, termination processes, and high-volume manufacturing</li> <li>Hands-on knowledge of high-volume cable manufacturing processes including wire drawing, stranding, extrusion, braiding, automated crimping, and connector molding</li> <li>Experience with production part approval process (PPAP), advanced product quality planning (APQP), design failure mode and effects analysis (DFMEA), process failure mode and effects analysis (PFMEA), and first article inspection (FAI) specifically for cable and power cord commodities</li> <li>Deep familiarity with relevant standards including Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE) 802.3af/at/bt (PoE standards), Underwriters Laboratories (UL) 444, UL 817, International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) 60228, IEC 61156, TIA/EIA-568, IPC/WHMA-A-620 (Class 2/3), and AS9100</li> <li>Practical experience qualifying Cat5e, Cat6, and Cat6A cables for PoE applications, AC cords (NEMA and IEC 60320), conductor sizing, insulation and jacket materials, and thermal/electrical performance under load</li> <li>Strong understanding of manufacturing capability evaluations, including capacity analysis, process capability indices (Cp/Cpk), process window validation, and scalability for high-volume cable production</li> <li>Strong problem-solving skills using structured root cause analysis methods and statistical tools such as Minitab, design of experiments (DOE), and Six Sigma</li> <li>Knowledge of reliability engineering practices such as accelerated life testing, flex-cycle testing, thermal aging, humidity exposure, and cable-specific failure mechanism analysis</li> <li>Ability to read and interpret two-dimensional drawings, cable specifications, pair balance requirements, and connector datasheets</li> <li>Experience with Lean manufacturing concepts, supplier scorecard systems, and high-volume process capability</li> <li>Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to distill complex technical topics into clear one-pagers and presentations</li> <li>Demonstrated ability to influence cross-functional teams and suppliers in a fast-paced, high-growth environment</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Ability to travel up to 25% of the time, both domestically and internationally</li> <li>Position may require extended working hours and occasional weekends to support production ramps and critical issue resolution</li> <li>This position is based in Bastrop, TX and requires being onsite</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR
