jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>SUPPLIER DEVELOPMENT ENGINEER, ELECTRICAL (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is developing a low latency, broadband internet system to meet the needs of consumers across the globe. Enabled by a constellation of low Earth orbit satellites, Starlink will provide fast, reliable internet to populations with little or no connectivity. We are looking for talented, creative, and driven electrical engineers to develop, drive, and maintain suppliers, from initial concept development to full scale production.</p> <p>This is a high-profile, cross functional position that plays an integral role in enabling development and production of Starlink products. You will drive end-to-end supplier development for the electromechanical portfolio — from strategic supplier selection and new product introduction (NPI) through high-volume production scaling. Need to work in close coordination with internal engineering, manufacturing, and reliability teams as well as directly with suppliers to execute effective, creative and smart supply chain strategies to achieve production goals.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Analyze manufacturing processes and electromechanical assemblies from a first principles, physics-based approach with focus on electrical domain</li> <li>Experience with taking products from concept and development into high-volume production</li> <li>Work closely with engineers from adjacent disciplines (mechanical, thermal, software, test engineering, supply chain, etc.) to deliver tightly integrated, high-performance hardware</li> <li>Develop part qualification criteria, collaborate on functional and reliability requirements, and drive system-level optimization for high-volume production</li> <li>Lead Design of Experiments (DOE) to develop supplier production processes for high-rate, high-yield, and reliable parts</li> <li>Lead hardware failure investigations, defect characterization and analysis to determine root causes to improve manufacturing yields</li> <li>Direct the supplier process modifications while ultimately responsible for approving first article inspection (FAI) reports, and Production Part Approval Process (PPAP) reports</li> <li>Collaborate with design, materials, and manufacturing engineers to gain an in-depth knowledge of electrical parts, assembly, metrology, and sub-system design intent</li> <li>Create and define supplier technical and quality requirements based on NPI lifecycle, production phases, and program requirement</li> <li>Demonstrate a strong sense of ownership, proactivity, technical excellence, creativity, self-direction, and courage</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in electrical engineering</li> <li>2+ years of professional experience in electrical engineering, electronics manufacturing, quality engineering, reliability engineering (internship and extracurricular experience is applicable)</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Master's degree in electrical engineering</li> <li>5+ years of professional experience in consumer electronics</li> <li>Experience troubleshooting electronics hardware and/or RF communication systems</li> <li>Hands-on knowledge of high-volume electromechanical manufacturing processes including motors, sensors, robotics, automation lines etc.</li> <li>Strong understanding of manufacturing capability evaluations, including capacity analysis, process capability indices (Cp/Cpk), process window validation, and scalability for high-volume electronics production</li> <li>Strong problem-solving skills using structured root cause analysis methods and statistical tools such as Minitab, design of experiments (DOE), and Six Sigma</li> <li>Knowledge of reliability engineering practices such as accelerated life testing, flex-cycle testing, thermal aging, humidity exposure, and electrical-specific failure mechanism analysis</li> <li>Ability to read and interpret two-dimensional drawings, electrical specifications, pair balance requirements, and connector datasheets</li> <li>Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to distill complex technical topics into clear one-pagers and presentations</li> <li>Experience in a fast-paced, iterative design environment within the consumer electronics, mobile handsets, medical devices, aerospace, or automotive industries</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Position is based in Bastrop, TX and requires being onsite - remote work not considered</li> <li>Position internationally</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or title: Supplier Development Engineer, Mechanical Metrology (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>SUPPLIER DEVELOPMENT ENGINEER, MECHANICAL METROLOGY (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>Starlink User Terminal business is experiencing exponential growth across consumer, retail, enterprise, and mobility applications. This rapid expansion requires a highly resilient and scalable supply chain with world-class precision measurement capabilities for high-tolerance mechanical components.&nbsp;The role entails early engagement in supplier selection, equipment selection, and process engineering to set programs up for success in high-volume manufacturing by ensuring material and process corners are fully completed. The role also includes ownership to deliver on time, monitor field performance, react to issues, and feed lessons learned back to engineering teams for iterative improvement.&nbsp;</p> <p>We are seeking a Metrology Engineer with strong technical and leadership skills to drive supplier development, metrology strategy, and AI-enabled measurement systems for mechanical parts in high-volume production.&nbsp;The Supplier Development Engineer, Mechanical Metrology will be responsible for executing end-to-end supplier strategies focused on precision mechanical components and their associated metrology processes. This position will have significant technical and leadership influence across Starlink engineering, quality, and supply chain teams.&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:&nbsp;</strong></p> <ul> <li>Own end-to-end supplier development for mechanical metrology and high-precision mechanical components within the Starlink User Terminal Bill of Materials, spanning strategic supplier selection, new product introduction (NPI), qualification, production ramp, and reactive quality support&nbsp;</li> <li>Engage early with suppliers on selection, equipment selection, and process engineering to properly set up high-volume manufacturing programs by ensuring material and process corners are fully characterized and completed&nbsp;</li> <li>Provide technical guidance on mechanical metrology methods, Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing (GD&amp;T) implementation, datum scheme development and best practices, PC-DMIS programming, surface texture and surface technology standards, and measurement system analysis (MSA) while driving adoption of AI-powered metrology solutions&nbsp;</li> <li>Design, develop, and qualify precision measurement fixtures, including fixture concept design, datum scheme optimization, repeatability studies, and qualification to ensure measurement system stability and accuracy&nbsp;</li> <li>Assess supplier manufacturing and metrology capabilities, including capacity, process windows, gage repeatability and reproducibility (GR&amp;R) performance, uncertainty budgets, datum scheme robustness, and scalability for high-volume production of tight-tolerance mechanical parts&nbsp;</li> <li>Indirectly manage internal metrology lab activities and technicians by setting technical direction, prioritizing work, and ensuring consistent execution of measurement standards and best practices&nbsp;</li> <li>Implement artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning solutions for metrology, including automated vision inspection, predictive analytics on measurement trends, anomaly detection, and intelligent data interpretation systems&nbsp;</li> <li>Lead Production Part Approval Process (PPAP), First Article Inspections (FAI), gage repeatability and reproducibility (GR&amp;R) studies, and production rate ramps to enable full-rate, high-volume manufacturing&nbsp;</li> <li>Develop and execute robust qualification plans including dimensional validation, surface finish and texture analysis, coordinate measuring machine (CMM) and optical measurement correlation, and environmental stability testing&nbsp;</li> <li>Drive supplier performance improvement through Lean methodologies, supplier scorecards, process audits, and systematic problem solving to deliver measurable gains in quality, cost, and delivery&nbsp;</li> <li>Perform reactive quality engineering support, including rapid containment, root cause analysis, and corrective actions for measurement escapes, dimensional non-conformances, and field issues&nbsp;</li> <li>Own on-time delivery of qualification and production ramp activities while continuously monitoring field performance, reacting quickly to issues, and feeding lessons learned from field data back to design and process engineering teams for iterative improvement&nbsp;</li> <li>Ensure internal customers are highly satisfied by delivering not only precise measurement data but clear engineering inferences, trend analysis, and actionable recommendations derived from metrology results&nbsp;</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:&nbsp;</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering, metrology, industrial engineering, or a other engineering discipline&nbsp;</li> <li><span data-teams="true">1+ years of experience in mechanical metrology, precision manufacturing, or supplier development (internship and extracurricular experience is applicable)&nbsp;</span></li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCES:&nbsp;</strong></p> <ul> <li><span title: Supplier Development Engineer, PCB (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>SUPPLIER DEVELOPMENT ENGINEER, PCB (STARLINK) </strong></p> <p>Starlink User Terminal business is experiencing exponential growth across consumer, retail, enterprise, and mobility applications. This rapid expansion requires a highly resilient and scalable supply chain for printed circuit boards (PCBs) that form the foundation of our User Terminals. We are seeking a technically strong engineer to drive supplier selection, development, qualification, and scaling specifically for the PCB portfolio in high-volume production.</p> <p>The ideal candidate will bring deep expertise in PCB manufacturing processes, materials, quality systems, and reliability, combined with practical experience developing suppliers for high-volume electronics. This role demands a strong balance of hands-on technical capability, understanding of manufacturing capability, and the ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams to mature suppliers rapidly to support Starlink’s aggressive growth targets.</p> <p>The Supplier Development Engineer will be responsible for executing supplier strategies focused on bare PCBs, multilayer boards, high-frequency/RF PCBs, including and not limited to raw materials used in PCB fabrications. This position will have significant technical influence across Starlink engineering, quality, and supply chain teams. Success requires solid engineering judgment, strong communication skills, and the ability to turn suppliers into reliable, high-volume production partners.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Own supplier development activities for the PCB portfolio within the Starlink User Terminal Bill of Materials, with primary focus on managing incoming PCB supply chain quality and reliability.</li> <li>Build and maintain a resilient, high-quality, and scalable supply base capable of supporting high-volume production ramp and sustained growth of the Starlink User Terminal business.</li> <li>Assess supplier manufacturing capabilities, including production capacity, process stability, equipment suitability, process windows, material control, and overall technical readiness for high-volume PCB fabrication (lamination, drilling, plating, etching, solder mask, surface finishes, impedance control, and automated optical/electrical testing).</li> <li>Lead Production Part Approval Process (PPAP), First Article Inspections (FAI), production rate ramps, and reliability campaigns to enable high-volume manufacturing.</li> <li>Develop and execute robust qualification plans tailored to PCBs, including dimensional and electrical verification, RF performance testing, thermal/mechanical reliability demonstration, and compliance to applicable standards.</li> <li>Create and standardize qualification protocols across the PCB supply base, including equipment buy-off checklists, Factory Acceptance Tests (FAT), Site Acceptance Tests (SAT), and consistent reliability demonstration methods.</li> <li>Drive supplier performance improvement through Lean methodologies, supplier scorecards, process audits, and systematic problem solving to deliver measurable gains in quality, cost, and on-time delivery.</li> <li>Perform root cause analysis and lead corrective actions for quality issues, with focus on common PCB defect modes and failure mechanisms such as delamination, plating voids or thin plating, open/short circuits, warpage, copper thickness variation, solder mask defects, impedance drift, CAF (conductive anodic filament), pad cratering, and material-related reliability issues.</li> <li>Partner closely with Design Engineering, Reliability Engineering, RF/Electrical teams, and Production to ensure supplier processes and manufacturing capability align with Starlink’s high-volume product requirements and performance goals.</li> <li>Support continuous improvement of supplier quality systems and manufacturing processes to meet escalating volume, cost, and reliability targets for both standard and high-frequency/RF PCBs used in indoor and outdoor-rated products.</li> <li>Qualify new suppliers and manage ongoing performance of the incoming PCB supply base.</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Material Science, RF Engineering, or a related engineering discipline.</li> <li>3+ years of experience in PCB engineering, quality engineering, reliability engineering, or supplier development.</li> </ul> APQP, PFMEA, DFMEA, and First Article Inspection specifically for PCBs and electronic interconnects.</li> <li>Deep familiarity with relevant IPC standards (e.g., IPC-A-600, IPC-6012, IPC-6013, IPC-4101, IPC-4552, IPC-TM-650) as well as related quality and reliability standards.</li> <li>Strong understanding of PCB reliability, common defect modes, failure analysis techniques, and material science aspects of laminates, copper foils, and finishes.</li> <li>Practical experience qualifying rigid, flex, rigid-flex, and high-frequency/RF PCBs for high-volume production, including controlled impedance, high-speed digital, and RF performance requirements.</li> <li>Strong understanding of manufacturing capability evaluations, including capacity analysis, Cp/Cpk process capability studies, process window validation, and scalability for high-volume PCB production.</li> <li>Strong problem-solving skills using 8D, 5-Why, fishbone analysis, and statistical methods (JMP, Design of Experiments, Six Sigma).</li> <li>Knowledge of reliability engineering practices such as accelerated life testing, thermal cycling, humidity exposure, thermal shock, CAF testing, and PCB-specific Lean manufacturing concepts, supplier scorecard systems, and high-volume process capability (Cp/Cpk).</li> <li>Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to distill complex title: Supplier Development Engineer, Reliability (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. This rapid expansion demands exceptional product reliability to meet high consumer expectations. We are seeking a Supplier Development Engineer, Reliability to own end-to-end reliability activities — from developing reliability plans and models to executing test programs at the supply base, bringing up test, implementing ongoing reliability testing, and driving failure analysis to closure. The ideal candidate will bring strong first-principles thinking, deep expertise in reliability physics, and the ability to deliver statistically sound reliability programs at scale. This role requires a strong combination of technical depth in reliability engineering, statistical rigor, and the ability to influence suppliers and cross-functional teams in a high-volume consumer electronics environment.</p> <p>The Supplier Development Engineer, Reliability will be responsible for creating and executing comprehensive reliability strategies across the full product lifecycle. This position carries significant technical authority and will have broad influence across design, test, quality, and supply chain organizations. Success requires excellent engineering judgment, strong logical reasoning in sampling and failure analysis, and the ability to translate reliability data into actionable product improvements.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Own end-to-end hardware reliability for Starlink consumer electronics products, from early reliability plan development through new product introduction, mass production, and field performance</li> <li>Develop comprehensive reliability plans, accelerated life test plans, and reliability demonstration test protocols</li> <li>Build and We are looking for talented, creative, and driven engineers to develop, drive, and maintain suppliers, from initial concept development to full scale production.<strong><br></strong><br>As a Supplier Development Engineer focused on Surface Mount Technology (SMT) for Starlink, you will play a critical role in ensuring the quality, reliability, and scalability of PCBA (Printed Circuit Board Assembly) manufacturing at our global suppliers. This position requires deep technical expertise in SMT processes, hands-on experience with PCBA manufacturing, and the ability to collaborate with cross-functional teams and suppliers worldwide. Based in Bastrop, Texas, you will report to the Supplier Development Engineering team lead and contribute to the rapid iteration and production scaling of Starlink hardware.</p> jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>TEST ENGINEER, COMPUTE PAYLOAD (STARMIND)</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is leveraging its experience deploying and operating the world’s largest satellite constellation to develop Starmind, a new constellation of satellites capturing solar energy in space to power low-cost, high-performance AI compute for Earth. Realizing this vision demands highly reliable, high performance compute hardware systems which must operate in the extreme environment of space.</p> <p>The Starmind team designs, builds, and operates the orbital compute fabric of the future. We develop nearly every key piece of technology in house – from the satellites’ flight computers and power systems to the fully custom compute electronics, memory, and networking that form the brain of our on-orbit data centers. As a Test Engineer on the Starmind Compute Payload team, you’ll have ownership over how we validate the hardware that enables advanced on-orbit AI processing and data center workloads.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES: </strong></p> <ul> <li>Design and implement test processes which seamlessly integrate into electro-mechanical assembly line with rapid iteration</li> <li>Manage physical infrastructure of test integration and operations</li> <li>Interface with engineers, specialists and technicians to optimize testing operations</li> <li>Collaborate with the mechanical design team and end users to incorporate designs for test optimization</li> <li>Lead development tests ensuring incremental milestones for the production ramp are met</li> <li>Track manufacturing system key metrics around rate, cost, and quality</li> <li>Identify tooling and hardware requirements, design and implement them into production processes. Rapidly iterate by evaluating non-conformances to determine root cause and drive test optimization</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in an engineering discipline</li> <li>1+ years of experience in a manufacturing or test environment via professional work experience, project/research-based student experience, or a combination of both</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Demonstrated experience working in a highly adaptive and iterative environment</li> <li>Experience with integration and testing of propulsion, thermal, electrical and/or structural systems</li> <li>Experience transitioning products from design to manufacturing and test validation, and scaling to high volume as part of a cross-functional team</li> <li>Proficiency in NX/CATIA/SolidWorks or any industry standard CAD design tools</li> <li>Experience with process qualifications</li> <li>Ability to design tooling for high-volume manufacturing</li> <li>Demonstrated experience implementing automation into test processes</li> <li>Experience working with and defining requirements for ERP, MRP, and MES systems</li> <li>Knowledge and experience with testing of pressurized fluid/gas systems</li> <li>Experience with instrumentation and data acquisition</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Must be available to work extended hours and weekends as needed</li> <li>Ability to lift up to 25lbs.</li> <li>Ability to travel for short and extended trips as needed - title: Test Stand Maintenance Technician
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>TEST STAND MAINTENANCE TECHNICIAN</strong></p> <p>Maintenance technicians at the Rocket Development and Test Facility work in a fast-paced testing environment, where the extraordinary becomes the everyday. This role helps with the build, activation, modification, and improvement of fluid and mechanical systems that test the most powerful high-volume rocket engines in the world. With a focus on repairs and reliability, maintenance technicians are expected to use every tool they have to keep the rocket development and production test stands working well. This work includes performing corrective, preventive, and predictive maintenance on test systems, troubleshooting mechanical and electrical hardware, and giving operations and design feedback to drive improvements across our entire test site.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Modify and maintain test stands and ground support equipment that support testing of fully integrated flight vehicles, individual rocket engines, and various rocket components</li> <li>Troubleshoot, diagnose, and repair hardware associated with rocket test stand systems, typically part of fluid, structural, and mechanical subsystems</li> <li>Maintain structural/mechanical systems and related components such as rollers, bearings, rams, and similar items</li> <li>Maintain fluid systems and related components such as process piping, pumps, valves, filters, and similar items</li> <li>Collaborate with design and operations engineers to maintain systems in peak operating condition, provide feedback on designs and operations, and promote continual improvement of ground support equipment</li> <li>Develop novel methods to streamline and increase the reliability of internal processes across the entire test site</li> <li>Follow all regulations and appropriate SpaceX procedures, including quality policies, safety policies, Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH), National Fire Protection Association (NFPA), American Society of Mechanical Engineers (ASME), National Electrical Code (NEC), and other standards</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>High school diploma or equivalency certificate</li> <li>3+ years of experience working with hydraulic, pneumatic, mechanical, electrical, cryogenic, high-pressure gas, or data systems</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>5+ years of experience working as a maintenance technician, service technician, field service engineer, or mechanic</li> <li>Strong experience with schematics and diagrams for fluid routing, instrumentation, and electrical components</li> <li>Experience working in a fast-paced production environment in fields such as power generation, oil and gas, aerospace, automotive, or electronics</li> <li>Knowledge of vacuum systems, heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) systems, process piping inspections and operations, tubing and pipe fittings, rotating machinery (pumps, air compressors), and a wide variety of mechanical fasteners</li> <li>Knowledge of high-pressure gas, hydraulic, cryogenic, flammable, hypergolic, and pyrophoric systems</li> <li>Experience with heavy equipment or industrial operations and maintenance</li> <li>Experience in equipment maintenance and calibration, instrumentation troubleshooting, process controls, and data and control systems</li> <li>Operational knowledge of process instrumentation (pressure transducers, thermocouples, resistance temperature detectors (RTDs), load cells, flow meters, and similar items)</li> <li>Operational knowledge of basic electrical theory and system (CMMS) or enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems such as Maximo, SAP, Oracle, and others</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Ability to rapidly change roles and responsibilities while keeping a high sense of urgency in a fast-paced, challenging work environment</li> <li>Ability to work both independently and as part of a team, take individual initiative, and communicate effectively with peers, leadership, and customers</li> <li>Ability to perform job duties that require standing, kneeling, crouching, twisting the upper body, working in cramped needed (up to 25 percent of the time)</li> <li>Ability to work in tight quarters that require physical dexterity</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> title: Test Stand Maintenance Technician - 2nd Shift
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>TEST STAND MAINTENANCE TECHNICIAN - 2ND SHIFT</strong></p> <p>Maintenance technicians at the Rocket Development and Test Facility work in a fast-paced testing environment, where the extraordinary becomes the everyday. This role helps with the build, activation, modification, and improvement of fluid and mechanical systems that test the most powerful high-volume rocket engines in the world. With a focus on repairs and reliability, maintenance technicians are expected to use every tool they have to keep the rocket development and production test stands working well. This work includes performing corrective, preventive, and predictive maintenance on test systems, troubleshooting mechanical and electrical hardware, and giving operations and design feedback to drive improvements across our entire test site.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Modify and maintain test stands and ground support equipment that support testing of fully integrated flight vehicles, individual rocket engines, and various rocket components</li> <li>Troubleshoot, diagnose, and repair hardware associated with rocket test stand systems, typically part of fluid, structural, and mechanical subsystems</li> <li>Maintain structural/mechanical systems and related components such as rollers, bearings, rams, and similar items</li> <li>Maintain fluid systems and related components such as process piping, pumps, valves, filters, and similar items</li> <li>Collaborate with design and operations engineers to maintain systems in peak operating condition, provide feedback on designs and operations, and promote continual improvement of ground support equipment</li> <li>Develop novel methods to streamline and increase the reliability of internal processes across the entire test site</li> <li>Follow all regulations and appropriate SpaceX procedures, including quality policies, safety policies, Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH), National Fire Protection Association (NFPA), American Society of Mechanical Engineers (ASME), National Electrical Code (NEC), and other standards</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>High school diploma or equivalency certificate</li> <li>3+ years of experience working with hydraulic, pneumatic, mechanical, electrical, cryogenic, high-pressure gas, or data systems</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>5+ years of experience working as a maintenance technician, service technician, field service engineer, or mechanic</li> <li>Strong experience with schematics and diagrams for fluid routing, instrumentation, and electrical components</li> <li>Experience working in a fast-paced production environment in fields such as power generation, oil and gas, aerospace, automotive, or electronics</li> <li>Knowledge of vacuum systems, heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) systems, process piping inspections and operations, tubing and pipe fittings, rotating machinery (pumps, air compressors), and a wide variety of mechanical fasteners</li> <li>Knowledge of high-pressure gas, hydraulic, cryogenic, flammable, hypergolic, and pyrophoric systems</li> <li>Experience with heavy equipment or industrial operations and maintenance</li> <li>Experience in equipment maintenance and calibration, instrumentation troubleshooting, process controls, and data and control systems</li> <li>Operational knowledge of process instrumentation (pressure transducers, thermocouples, resistance temperature detectors (RTDs), load cells, flow meters, and similar items)</li> <li>Operational knowledge of basic electrical theory and electrical troubleshooting (multimeter fault finding, soldering and connecting, operation of various crimping tools, and similar items)</li> <li>Experience with computerized maintenance management system (CMMS) or enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems such as Maximo, SAP, Oracle, and others</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Anticipated hours for this position are 1:30 p.m. - 12:00 a.m.</li> <li>Schedule varies depending on site operational needs; flexibility required</li> <li>Ability to rapidly change roles and responsibilities while keeping a high sense of urgency in a fast-paced, challenging work environment</li> <li>Ability to work both independently and as part of a team, take individual initiative, and communicate effectively with peers, leadership, and customers</li> <li>Ability to perform job duties that require standing, kneeling, crouching, twisting the upper body, working in cramped positions in small openings, and climbing hand-over-hand</li> <li>Ability to work at elevated heights (up to 300 feet) with proper personal protective equipment (PPE)</li> <li>Ability to lift heavy objects (up to 25 pounds) without help</li> <li>Ability to respond to emergencies to support priority projects, missions, and launches</li> <li>Ability to work extended hours and weekends as needed with flexibility</li> <li>Ability to work in extreme outdoor environments when needed, including heat, cold, wind, rain, and similar conditions</li> <li>Ability to travel to other SpaceX locations as needed (up to 25 percent of the time)</li> <li>Ability to work in tight quarters that require physical dexterity</li> </ul> <p>&nbsp;</p><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR <a href="https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/?id=ddtc_kb_article_page&amp;sys_id=24d528fddbfc930044f9ff621f961987">here</a>. &nbsp;</li> </ul> <p>SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.</p> <p>Applicants wishing to view a copy of SpaceX’s Affirmative Action Plan for veterans and individuals with disabilities, or applicants requiring reasonable accommodation to the application/interview process should reach out to&nbsp;<a href="mailto:EEOCompliance@spacex.com">EEOCompliance@spacex.com</a><em>.&nbsp;</em></p></div>

Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>THERMAL CONTROL AND LIFE SUPPORT HARDWARE ENGINEER (CREW STARSHIP)</strong></p> <p>After 50 years, humankind will once again return to surface of the moon using SpaceX’s Crew Starship (also known as HLS or the Human Landing System) – this time for good. Leveraging the lessons learned from our flight proven Dragon spacecraft and Falcon rocket, Starship will usher in the next era of crewed spaceflight and exploration, ultimately allowing us to establish permanent communities on the Moon, Mars, and beyond.</p> <p>As a Thermal Control and Life Support Engineer, you will have the opportunity to utilize your knowledge, experience, and creativity to develop novel solutions at the cutting edge of space technology. This team develops the necessary hardware to maintain environmental and thermal control as well as support life onboard the Starship spacecraft. The role requires attentiveness across disciplines, as it involves design, analysis, testing, and manufacturing of components that are critical to the safety of future astronauts and passengers.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Own the conceptualization, design, and build of creative life support and thermal control systems for all Crew Starship missions, including Mars missions, across disciplines such as fans and air distribution, air sanitation, water collection and reclamation, waste management, fire suppression, and active thermal control</li> <li>Rapidly iterate on manufacturing processes and development testing in a fast-paced environment</li> <li>Be responsible for project delivery timeline from early design through production, launch, and sustained operations.</li> <li>Lead design reviews internally and externally with suppliers and customers</li> <li>Work with interdisciplinary customers to ensure the component will integrate with the necessary avionics, software, mission operations, etcetera</li> <li>Ensure designs are manufacturable and reliable</li> <li>Exemplify technical excellence and be accountable for your own work</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in an engineering or science discipline</li> <li>1+ years of experience working with fluid systems, mechanical systems, environmental control systems, or components (internship and project team experience is applicable)</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Ability to perform trade studies using first principles and engineering fundamentals to make clear recommendations even with partial information</li> <li>Experience with rotating machinery</li> <li>Experienced in NX</li> <li>Solid understanding and application of geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&amp;T) and tolerance stack-up analysis</li> <li>Experience with structural analysis methods (hand calcs, ABAQUS, ANSYS) in order to optimize hardware to strength requirements as well as to evaluate for life and fracture</li> <li>Knowledge of metallic and fluid system manufacturing techniques, processes, equipment, and other processes such as machining, welding, brazing, tube bending, etc.</li> <li>Experience with selection of materials considering engineering properties, manufacturing, and fluid compatibility</li> <li>Able to work well in an integrated collaborative team environment, including frequent interactions with technicians, other engineers, and managers</li> <li>Highly self-motivated with strong organizational and written/oral communication skills – able to prioritize and execute tasks in a high-pressure environment with the&nbsp;ongoing drive for continuous improvement in all aspects of work</li> <li>Master’s degree in engineering discipline</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Must be willing to work long hours and weekends as needed to support critical milestones</li> <li>Ability to pass Air Force background checks for Cape Canaveral</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To title: Thermal Engineer, AI Satellites (Starmind)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>THERMAL ENGINEER, AI SATELLITES (STARMIND)</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is leveraging its experience deploying and operating the world’s largest satellite constellation to develop Starmind, a new constellation of satellites capturing solar energy in space to power low-cost, high-performance AI compute for Earth. Scaling AI in space is a thermal problem as much as a power and processing problem. With a dense compute payload dissipating hundreds of kilowatts, the thermal system must efficiently transfer heat to large radiators that reject it to space, under solar load, eclipse, and multi-mode AI duty cycles.</p> <p>You will join the Starmind Thermal team, which owns the satellite cooling stack end-to-end. Rejecting hundreds of kilowatts of accelerator waste heat to space is limited by high-flux loads transferring heat to massive deployable radiators. No capable cooling architecture has been flown at this scale. As a Senior Thermal Engineer focused on fluids analysis, you own conjugate heat transfer and thermal-fluid analysis of cold plates, heat exchangers, and radiator channels and manifolds, and the system 0-D/1-D thermal-fluid network that sets flow split, ΔP budget, loop ΔT, and pump operating point. You co-evolve geometry and flow path with mechanical and fluid-systems owners under tight feedback from manufacturing and test. You sit where the local physics is hardest and the design decisions stick: predictions that close margins, ground in test, and drive rate-production hardware.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Own conjugate heat-transfer (CHT) and thermal-fluid analysis of high-performance cold plates, heat exchangers, and radiator channels for STARMIND satellites</li> <li>Own the system 0-D/1-D thermal-fluid network that sizes and balances the cooling loop: flow split, ΔP budget, loop ΔT, pump operating point</li> <li>Drive cooling-loop architecture trades with hardware and vehicle-level thermal teammates</li> <li>Co-evolve geometry, materials and processes with hardware owners to find mass producible, efficient thermal solutions</li> <li>Predict component and system performance under wide range of flow and thermal conditions</li> <li>Own pre-test prediction, test design, and model-test correlation for fluid component and integrated thermal tests</li> <li>Automate analysis workflows for re-running trades as designs and boundary conditions change</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in mechanical, aerospace, or a related engineering discipline</li> <li>1+ years of professional experience in fluids, CFD, or thermal analysis</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND packaging process engineers, hardware design teams, production operations, and quality to integrate test insights into product development and production ramp&nbsp;</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC title: Trajectory Analysis Engineer (Starship)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>TRAJECTORY ANALYSIS ENGINEER (STARSHIP)</strong></p> <p>As a Trajectory Analysis Engineer, you will be responsible for finding creative analysis solutions to enable the world’s most advanced rockets, including our next-generation Starship vehicle, a fully reusable spacecraft capable of carrying humans to Mars and beyond. You will work with a talented team of accomplished engineers to iterate on mission objectives for upcoming and future flights to ensure flight safety objectives are met. You should thrive in fast-paced, dynamic environments where you adapt quickly and love to solve hard problems.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Analyze launch vehicle trajectories and vehicle performance in the presence of faults</li> <li>Find creative flight plan solutions to enable mission objectives, while maintaining safe vehicle operation</li> <li>Generate and submit flight safety deliverables</li> <li>Produce and present trajectory analysis products for internal and external partners</li> <li>Interface with internal operations teams, flight reliability teams, hardware teams, and external regulatory partners such as the FAA.</li> <li>Engage in multi-disciplinary vehicle systems investigations to motivate mission design, vehicle architecture, and analysis methodologies</li> <li>Develop and evaluate flight termination system mission rules</li> <li>Support launch and mission operations of vehicles that you enabled</li> <li>Conduct flight data review</li> <li>Automate mission-to-mission trajectory analysis product generation</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in physics or an engineering discipline</li> <li>1+ years experience with orbital mechanics, classical dynamics, modeling, and simulation (via project team, research, internships, and/or professional experience)</li> <li>1+ years experience with the software languages Python or C++ (via project team, research, internships, and/or professional experience)</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Demonstrated project or professional experience in launch vehicle and/or spacecraft systems</li> <li>Capable of solving complex problems with little to no supervision on schedule as an individual or as a member of an integrated team</li> <li>Experience with system trades and first-hand knowledge of how requirements tie hardware to larger systems</li> <li>Passion for advancing the commercial space industry and human spaceflight</li> <li>Excellent communication skills both written and verbal</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Must be willing to work extended hours and/or weekends as needed</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>TRANSPORT TECHNICIAN</strong></p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Lead the safe transport of flight hardware and modules between SpaceX facilities (Hawthorne, CA; McGregor, TX; Cape Canaveral, FL; and Vandenberg, CA), including all transit and hand-off operations</li> <li>Supervise the entire transport crew, including SpaceX logistics technicians, tiller operators, spotters, and contracted vendors (truck drivers, pole car operators, and escorts)</li> <li>Review all transportation documentation (permits, route surveys, height checklists, pre-trip and post-trip inspections) prior to departure and develop contingency plans to mitigate risk</li> <li>Travel with assigned flight hardware at all times during long-haul transports</li> <li>Serve as the primary point of contact for all in-transit decisions, including route adjustments, repairs, additional escorts, or driver changes</li> <li>Provide technical input on Department of Transportation (DOT) and Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) requirements to the Logistics and Manufacturing teams for the continuous improvement of transport hardware, procedures, and processes</li> <li>Utilize heavy equipment (forklifts, spotters, overhead cranes) to safely load, unload, and stage flight hardware and ground support equipment</li> <li>Coordinate with the master production schedule (MPS) to ensure required resources, personnel, and transport equipment are available and aligned with program needs</li> <li>Oversee the completion and quality of all daily pre-trip and post-trip inspections, security briefings, permit reviews, and procedural documentation</li> <li>Develop and maintain work instructions, transport procedures, and best practices in collaboration with logistics leadership</li> <li>Track and report key performance metrics, including on-time delivery, safety incidents, and transport efficiency</li> <li>Identify and implement improvements to transportation systems, processes, and hardware to increase safety, reliability, and efficiency</li> <li>Identify various lifting hardware (shackles, slings, chain hoists, wire ropes, D-rings, web straps)</li> <li>Assist with planning and performing lift procedures</li> <li>Assist with crane operations and rigging under supervision</li> <li>Assist in maintaining transport equipment and materials needed for operational success</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>High school diploma or equivalency certificate</li> <li>1+ years of experience working with load transport and inventory processes</li> <li>1+ years of hands-on experience with preparing loads, rigging, and packaging</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>1+ years of hands-on experience with overhead cranes and general lifting procedures</li> <li>Knowledge and experience in transport equipment (tractor and trailer) design and maintenance</li> <li>Experience with scheduling and production work instructions to manufacture hardware</li> <li>Advanced skills with Microsoft Office Suite</li> <li>Experience working with and troubleshooting high-pressure systems</li> <li>Experience working in a challenging and fast-paced environment</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Must be available to work all shifts, overtime, and weekends as needed based on operational needs; flexibility required</li> <li>Must be available to travel up to 40% of the time</li> <li>Valid driver’s license</li> <li>Must be bridge (overhead) crane certified within the first 180 days</li> <li>Ability to successfully pass U.S. Air Force background checks required for access to Cape Canaveral, Florida, and Vandenberg, California</li> <li>Must be able to lift 25 pounds unassisted and perform physical activities such as stooping, bending, crawling, and maneuvering in tight or confined spaces</li> <li>Ability to safely work in confined spaces and operate heavy equipment and machinery</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or title: Utility Operator Specialist - Level 4/5
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>UTILITY OPERATOR SPECIALIST - LEVEL 4/5</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is seeking utility operators for its Starbase, TX facility. Ideally, the operator has experience working with industrial processes that utilize engines, motors, fluid piping, electrical equipment, and instrumented controls. This position entails ownership of equipment performance and reliability by monitoring process parameters and maintaining components, with a keen eye for leading indicators of instability or malfunction, and a drive to correct those issues in advance of undesirable events.&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES: </strong></p> <ul> <li>Identify equipment and process deviations and perform corrective actions</li> <li>Troubleshoot, maintain, and calibrate a variety of process equipment including centrifugal and reciprocating compressors, gas analyzers, control systems, instrument electrical systems and process control valves</li> <li>Work with engineers, technicians, and fabricators to implement fluid and mechanical designs in the field</li> <li>Work with engineers and technicians to create operating procedures</li> <li>Coordinate across multiple disciplines to ensure that required resources are available to complete builds</li> <li>Use knowledge of systems and existing documentation like schematics and parts lists to create and maintain a mature and efficient hardware inventory system – including procurement of critical spares&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</li> <li>Learn and run standard operating procedures on the machinery</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Associate degree in mechanical or electrical engineering technology and 4+ years of experience working with automated processes in one of the following areas; OR a high school diploma or equivalency certificate and 6+ years of experience in one of the following areas: <ul> <li>Control room operations</li> <li>Plant operations</li> <li>Mechanic/millwright support</li> <li>Instrumentation/electrical operations</li> </ul> </li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li><span data-teams="true">Holds a Class B or higher Water Operator and/or Wastewater Operator license through TCEQ or equivalent</span></li> <li>Basic understanding of process parameters and engineering units for temperature, pressure, flow, and power</li> <li>Ability to read and understand P&amp;ID and schematic wiring diagrams</li> <li>Familiar with mechanical equipment and systems requiring the isolation of the malfunction, disassembly of industrial machinery and repair/replacement of bearings, gears, structural components</li> <li>Familiar with lock out tag out, job hazard analysis, hot work permitting</li> <li>Familiar with 120V, 480V, and 4160V electrical switchgear and components</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Willing and able to work outside with hand tools, which includes the ability to stand, walk, climb, and work with objects overhead</li> <li>Required to climb ladders to elevated platforms and operate man-lifts at elevations in excess of 100 feet</li> <li>Must be willing to work all shifts, overtime and weekends as needed</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. title: Wastewater Treatment Supervisor (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>WASTEWATER TREATMENT SUPERVISOR (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is developing a low latency, broadband internet system to meet the needs of consumers across the globe. Enabled by a constellation of low Earth orbit satellites, Starlink will provide fast, reliable internet to populations with little or no connectivity, including those in rural communities and places where existing services are too expensive or unreliable. We are looking for talented, creative, and driven supervisors to drive manufacturing tools and processes, from initial concept development to full scale production. You will drive the relationship between engineering, development, and production teams and will interact regularly with department leadership. The success of Starlink depends on the quality, reliability, cost, manufacturability, throughput, security, and user experience of the products that you deliver.</p> <p>As a Starlink Wastewater Treatment Supervisor, you will manage a team of technicians while working closely with specialists and engineers, driving the operationalization and ramp of a 24/7 state-of-the-art wastewater treatment plant with the mission of recycling process water from various Starlink production lines. The supervisor will also drive progress on an hour-by-hour and day-by-day basis by effectively using labor resources, prioritizing work, and setting goals. For this role specifically, it is highly important that the supervisor is an inspiring leader, frequently working side-by-side with their team.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Lead and manage a team of technicians, including performance management related tasks</li> <li>Supervise shop floor activity, including daily schedules and workflow</li> <li>Effectively organize, assign, and track work/deliverables for the team, ensuring seamless progression through multi-shift work schedules</li> <li>Prioritize work based on production schedule and organizational goals</li> <li>Support transitioning equipment from engineering development to full rate production</li> <li>Develop standard work instructions and PM schedules</li> <li>Identify training needs and develop a training program</li> <li>Provide required data and reporting to support department metrics and improvements</li> <li>Maximize productivity, efficiency, and quality</li> <li>Maintain tooling and consumable supply inventory</li> <li>Continuously improve people, process, and equipment</li> <li>Identify and mitigate risks to production schedules and targets</li> <li>Coordinate efforts to minimize production interruptions</li> <li>Ensure process quality and conformance to specifications</li> <li>Improve area safety and efficiency through regular auditing and continuous improvement</li> <li>Use root cause analysis and implement corrective and preventive actions</li> <li>Initiate and foster a spirit of cooperation within and between departments</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree or 5+ years of professional experience in a water treatment or wastewater treatment plant in lieu of degree</li> <li>1+ years of experience leading a team or project</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>2+ years of experience leading a team or project</li> <li>Lean manufacturing training and experience</li> <li>Demonstrated ability to read and interpret controlled documentation such as wiring diagrams, layout drawings, mechanical drawings, GD&amp;T, assembly procedures/work instructions, schematics, engineering drawings, and parts lists</li> <li>Familiarity with Design for Manufacturability, Kaizen, Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, and Failure Mode Effects Analysis</li> <li>Able to adapt to constant changing work assignments and fast-paced work environment</li> <li>Proficient with computers, the ability to use MS Office, shop floor management software (ERP) and related software</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Must be available for one of the following shifts (start and end times are approximate):</li> <ul> <li>A Shift – 5:00am-5:00pm, Sunday-Wednesday</li> <li>B Shift – 5:00am-5:00pm, Wednesday-Saturday</li> <li>C Shift – 5:00pm-5:00am, Sunday-Wednesday</li> <li>D Shift – 5:00pm-5:00am, Wednesday-Saturday</li> </ul> <li>Ability to travel on an ongoing basis (up to 10%)</li> <li>Ability to stand up to 6 hours, lift 25 pounds unassisted, and maneuver around equipment in a factory setting</li> <li>Lifting, standing, climbing, bending, grasping, sitting, pulling, pushing, stooping, stretching, and carrying are required to perform the functions of this position</li> <li>Ability to work in cleanroom and industrial environments with fumes/odors, noise, hazardous chemicals, and confined spaces</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR <a href="https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/?id=ddtc_kb_article_page&amp;sys_id=24d528fddbfc930044f9ff621f961987">here</a>. &nbsp;</li> </ul> <p>SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.</p> <p>Applicants wishing to view a copy of SpaceX’s Affirmative Action Plan for veterans and individuals with disabilities, or applicants requiring reasonable accommodation to the application/interview process should reach out to&nbsp;<a href="mailto:EEOCompliance@spacex.com">EEOCompliance@spacex.com</a><em>.&nbsp;</em></p></div>

<p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Perform at least two of the following processes, depending upon the needs of the business: Flux-Cored Arc Welding (FCAW), Shielded Metal Arc title: Principal Software Engineer, Continuous Integration (Starship)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>PRINCIPAL SOFTWARE ENGINEER, CONTINUOUS INTEGRATION (STARSHIP)</strong></p> <p>As a Principal Software Engineer on the Starship Continuous Integration team, you will own the tools that power Starship software development. You will design, maintain, and scale the systems which enable hundreds of engineers to integrate their changes and deliver reliable software to all Starship vehicles and launch pads on a continuous basis. This is a high-autonomy role and we are looking for people who want to work closely with peers, identify the biggest problems facing the team, and own solutions from start to finish!</p> <p>Aerospace experience is not required to be successful here - rather we look for smart, motivated, collaborative engineers who love solving problems and want to be a force multiplier for building world class software that is critical to SpaceX’s mission to make life multiplanetary.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Invent tools and processes which enable fast and correct software development.</li> <li>Hands-on integration and troubleshooting across the entire Starship software stack.</li> <li>Collaborate with counterpart teams to design, maintain, and continuously improve a dedicated pool of on-premises compute.</li> <li>Identify areas for improvement and create innovative solutions that enable the software team to tackle all challenges facing the Starship program as we develop the world’s first fully reusable rocket and spacecraft.</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>7+ years of software engineering experience and a Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, math, or STEM discipline; OR 9+ years of professional experience in software development in lieu of a degree</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Skill with Bazel or similar build systems</li> <li>Fluency in Python, C++, Rust, or Go</li> <li>Experience building tools and infrastructure that impacts hundreds of engineers daily</li> <li>Experience with AI-assisted development tools and interest in applying AI to improve code quality, testing, and development workflows</li> <li>Strong critical thinking and first-principles problem-solving skills</li> <li>Excellent written and verbal communication skills</li> <li>Able to work effectively in a dynamic environment while assuming high levels of responsibility and demonstrating accountability for software outcomes</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Willing to work long hours and weekends as needed</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR <a href="https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/?id=ddtc_kb_article_page&amp;sys_id=24d528fddbfc930044f9ff621f961987">here</a>. &nbsp;</li> </ul> <p>SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.</p> <p>Applicants wishing to view a copy of SpaceX’s Affirmative Action Plan for veterans and individuals with disabilities, or applicants requiring reasonable accommodation to the application/interview process should reach out to&nbsp;<a href="mailto:EEOCompliance@spacex.com">EEOCompliance@spacex.com</a><em>.&nbsp;</em></p></div>

Starlink brings an unprecedented opportunity to significantly impact communities, businesses, and governments worldwide. The role requires personal drive to identify opportunities in your region, develop the necessary relationships, and ultimately sign deals that will have immediate impact. </p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong>&nbsp;</p> <ul> <li>Grow and build the enterprise&nbsp;sales&nbsp;function within Starlink</li> <li>Meet your revenue targets – you should always be looking for opportunities for Starlink to make an impact and always be closing</li> <li>Identify&nbsp;and secure new enterprise customers directly. title: Director, Security - Gulf Coast
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>DIRECTOR, SECURITY – GULF COAST (STARBASE, TX)&nbsp;</strong></p> <p>Help SpaceX protect life and property anywhere company assets are deployed. The Director, Security is a highly trained professional who will provide coordination for Contracted Guard Force, Physical Security, Automated Access Control System, Intrusion Detection System, and CCTV System. This individual will have access to cutting edge technology in order to provide the best possible protection for the employees and assets of SpaceX.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES: </strong></p> <ul> <li>Develop and communicate the overall strategy for site security, aligning it with SpaceX’s business objectives</li> <li>Become the trusted security advisor to senior management and leaders across the organization through high-level communication and excellent briefing skills</li> <li>Establish procedures and protocols to assess, identify, and mitigate any security vulnerabilities or gaps</li> <li>Maintain a positive, professional environment in full compliance with applicable laws, regulations, policies and procedures; ensure that all team members understand and comply with those laws, regulations, policies and procedures</li> <li>Identify, prioritize, develop, and implement security measures, emergency preparedness and response plans, and security protocols and strategies</li> <li>Participate in local, state, and federal working or advisory groups to stay updated on security-related information</li> <li>Maintain security equipment such as cameras, alarms, and access control systems</li> <li>Assess systems, alarms, and other physical security measures for effectiveness</li> <li>Make effective decisions in both routine and crisis situations</li> <li>Take personal initiative in developing efficient work processes</li> <li>Address and resolve security issues promptly, effectively, and independently</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>High school diploma or equivalency certificate</li> <li>12+ years of experience in the field of security</li> <li>7+ years of security management experience supervising and directing staff across a wide range of operating functions</li> <li>Experience with International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR)</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university</li> <li>Exceptional track record in managing security operations, special events, and risk mitigation to critical infrastructure</li> <li>Prior experience directing large teams in all areas of security management</li> <li>Established skills in strategic and critical thinking, decision-making, communications, and relationship-building</li> <li>Highly organized, detail oriented, and possess a proven ability to thrive under pressure and to execute on a number of projects simultaneously</li> <li>Successful experience working in a fast-paced, dynamic, results-oriented team environment</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Must be willing to work all shifts, extended hours, and/or weekends as needed</li> <li>Must be willing to travel up to 15%</li> <li>Must be able to obtain and maintain an FAA Part 107 Drone license&nbsp;</li> <li>Ability to pass Air Force background checks for Cape Canaveral and Vandenberg</li> <li>Must be able to obtain a TS/SCI clearance</li> <li>An active clearance may provide the opportunity for you to work on sensitive SpaceX missions; if so, you will be subject to pre-employment drug and random drug and alcohol testing</li> <li>Position is subject to pre-employment enhanced screening, including a background check, psychological test, bi-annual physical fitness test, and a drug and alcohol test</li> <li>Position is subject to random drug and alcohol testing</li> </ul> <p>&nbsp;</p><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR title: Director, Starlink Production (Assembly)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>DIRECTOR, STARLINK PRODUCTION (ASSEMBLY)</strong></p> <p>We are seeking a highly motivated and achievement-oriented leader to own Starlink Product Assembly Production in Bastrop, TX—scaling high-volume manufacturing to fuel global connectivity for millions. This includes oversight and responsibility for Assembly, Test, Manufacturing Engineering, Automation, and Maintenance across high-rate automated mechanical/pick &amp; place, SMT/PCBA, and large electromechanical build production lines. This position plays a critical role in achieving rapid user expansion required for the success of the organization. Ideal candidates have a successful track record of scaling complex operations, leading 200+ person teams, and building cross-functional partnerships.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES: </strong></p> <ul> <li>Oversee the strategic &amp; tactical execution of Starlink Product Production</li> <li>Lead 250+ staff (multiple direct reports) across engineering and operations.</li> <li>Lead and mentor high-performing teams of manufacturing, process, and automation engineers to operationalize and continuously improve production.</li> <li>Implement a development program to enhance the capability of all team members while improving quality and reducing lead time &amp; cost.</li> <li>Partner with Responsible Engineering teams to embed manufacturability into the design of new products and production lines.</li> <li>Ensure a strong focus is placed on safety and maintain an excellent safety record.</li> <li>Champion continuous improvement projects using appropriate metrics &amp; data.</li> <li>Use quality metrics to continually improve the quality output of the operation.</li> <li>Manage resource levels to ensure optimum performance of the team.</li> <li>Monitor and communicate area status/readiness and risks to leadership.</li> <li>Monitor and maintain compliance with internal quality and customer contractual requirements.</li> <li>Foster a spirit of cooperation and collaboration within and between departments.</li> <li>Meet tight production schedules to achieve high-rate production, while adapting to changing priorities in a fast-moving environment.</li> <li>Think creatively and drive innovation; question the status quo, while following documentation and maintaining prescribed quality standards.</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in a STEM or engineering discipline OR 7+ years of production/manufacturing experience.</li> <li>5+ years of experience in production/manufacturing/operations.</li> <li>5+ years of experience in people leadership.&nbsp;</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Experience managing large teams comprised of engineering and operations.</li> <li>Thorough knowledge of electronics manufacturing and test techniques.</li> <li>Experience monitoring cost and quality (ISO 9000, AS9100) standards.</li> <li>Experience developing and delivering continuous improvement projects within a production environment.</li> <li>Experience in fast-paced iterative design environments within the consumer electronics, mobile handset, medical devices, or automotive industries.</li> <li>Able to communicate complex concepts, problems, and solutions clearly and effectively to all levels within the organization.</li> <li>Demonstrated ability to act and execute in a scrappy, entrepreneurial manner against tight timelines and aggressive schedules.</li> <li>Strong desire to mentor and grow employees and manage out poor performers.</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Willing to work extended hours and/or weekends as needed.</li> <li>Willing to travel as needed, up to 25%.</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. title: Principal Design Verification Engineer (Silicon Engineering)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>PRINCIPAL DESIGN VERIFICATION ENGINEER (SILICON ENGINEERING)</strong></p> <div> <p>At SpaceX we’re leveraging our experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. title: Principal Mechanical Engineer (Starship)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>PRINCIPAL MECHANICAL ENGINEER (STARSHIP)</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is looking for a Principal Mechanical Engineer to help build the infrastructure behind power generation and supercompute at Starbase. You will own mechanical scope from concept through design, fabrication, construction, and commissioning. The work can span power generation, fluid and cooling systems, and the structures and equipment that production depends on. You will set the technical direction, work across engineering, construction, and operations, and see your decisions show up in hardware that has to perform in the field.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Develop design concepts from a clean sheet and size infrastructure systems based on operational loads, site conditions, and how the facility will actually run</li> <li>Collaborate with peers across disciplines to develop designs that balance cost, schedule, reliability, and capability</li> <li>Create detailed designs and generate CAD models for components, assemblies, and integration into the larger site</li> <li>Build analysis models to assess your designs in detail and confirm they meet the needs of the system</li> <li>Apply first-order hand calculations and empirical formulas to assess and iterate on your designs rapidly</li> <li>Validate your designs through development hardware, mockups, or first articles, and test critical joints, components, and design elements</li> <li>Support testing and commissioning of subsystems and full installations</li> <li>Partner with construction, build engineers, and technicians to improve your designs</li> <li>Support installation of your hardware in the field, witness your designs being built and brought online, and see them go into service</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in an engineering discipline</li> <li>7+ years of experience with mechanical design and analysis</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Experience designing, analyzing, building, and testing high performance, mechanical systems</li> <li>Experience working within interdisciplinary teams to develop solutions to challenging and complex problems</li> <li>Experience with FEA or multiphysics simulation package (e.g. NASTRAN, ABAQUS, ANSYS)</li> <li>Experience designing and executing qualification
